docs.title: Bharat Agentic Commerce Protocol
docs.text:
BACP lets an AI agent discover, negotiate, buy, pay for, return and raise grievances about goods and services in India, on behalf of a person or a business, within limits that person or business has signed.

Version 2026-10-18

BACP 2026-10-18 is the first dated release of the specification, and implementers can target it. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. The conformance test suite is not yet published, so no participant can hold a conformance attestation yet. BACP is an independent proposal: it is not issued or endorsed by NPCI, ONDC, RBI or any other public body. Send feedback on GitHub.

Read the specification Core concepts View on GitHub

docs.title: Why BACP
docs.text:
India already has the rails that agentic commerce needs. ONDC and Beckn provide an open commerce network with order, cancel, return and grievance flows. UPI moves money at population scale and already has standing-authority primitives such as UPI Circle, Reserve Pay and AutoPay. Account Aggregator consent shows how to make permission explicit, purpose-bound and revocable. The DPDP Act sets the rules for personal data.

As of 17-10-2026, none of these rails has a published, standard way to identify agents. A network message identifies the buyer app, not the agent that acted. A payment carries no record of what the user allowed the agent to do. Nothing standard says whether a human was present, how a user revokes an agent, or how a dispute can reconstruct what the agent was told.

Global agentic-commerce protocols solve parts of this problem, but, as of 17-10-2026, they are built mainly around cards and around single merchants. None of them defines how to use UPI, cash on delivery, GST, Indian-language voice or the ONDC network.

BACP is a thin agent layer over the Indian rails. It replaces none of them. It adds four things to every transaction:

  • who the agent is, as a signed and registered credential;
  • on whose authority it acts, and within what limits, as a signed mandate;
  • whether a human was present when it acted;
  • what the user agreed to share, as a DPDP consent receipt.

Every step leaves verifiable evidence, so that a dispute can be traced from the user's instruction to the UPI reference number.

docs.title: What the first release covers
docs.text: BACP 2026-10-18 leads with marketplace and quick commerce (b2c.ecom), and launches with kirana khata, subscriptions and ticketing. These four trade profiles are stable. Distributor schemes and B2B procurement, services and social commerce are in the release as proposed profiles: attestable, but their rules MAY change in a later dated release. GeM, agri and mandi trade, cross-border trade, high-value purchases, rentals and assisted rural commerce are in review: described so that readers can comment, outside the conformance scope of this release, and open to change or removal. Trade profiles lists the maturity of each.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text: You are What BACP gives you An agent builder One way to discover, check out, negotiate, pay and raise grievances across the ONDC network, over REST, MCP or A2A, without a separate integration for each seller. A buyer app (BAP) A gateway model for hosting agents safely: a deterministic mandate verifier, signed agent requests, and idempotency and replay protection on top of Beckn. A seller or seller app (BPP) Agent orders you can trust: a declared and signed agent, a mandate reference, a hash of the cart the user approved, and structured negotiation that never leaks the buyer's walk-away price. A PSP, bank or issuer A clean binding between an agent mandate and the UPI and other Indian payment primitives you already run, with a basket-blind payment leg and signed receipts. A regulator or policy team A concrete, reviewable proposal for how agent commerce can meet RBI authentication rules, DPDP consent, e-commerce consumer protection and grievance timelines.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Mandate-bound agents

    An agent acts only under a signed mandate, open or closed, with budgets, allow-lists, step-up thresholds and fast revocation. The agent is never an authentication factor.

    Mandates and consent →

  • Native UPI and all Indian rails

    Open mandates bind to UPI Circle, Reserve Pay, AutoPay and One-Time Mandate. (As of 17-10-2026, NPCI lists AI-driven payments through UPI Circle as a closed-user-group pilot.) A registry of payment handlers covers cards, net banking, wallets, BBPS, e-RUPI, NACH, cash on delivery and B2B credit.

    Payments →

  • Built on ONDC/Beckn

    BACP rides on Beckn's search, select, init, confirm, cancel, update and IGM flows. Agent data travels in a namespaced extension that existing network participants can ignore.

    Beckn / ONDC binding →

  • Negotiation the way India trades

    Mol-bhav, B2B price rounds, RFQs, reverse auctions and schemes. The language model proposes and a deterministic guard decides. The reservation price never leaves the buyer's side.

    Negotiation →

  • DPDP-grade consent

    Mandates follow Account Aggregator consent semantics: immutable, purpose-bound, use-counted and revocable. Every data share produces a consent receipt in the user's language.

    Security and privacy →

  • Verifiable evidence and IGM

    A hash-chained instruction log and rail-anchored receipts link the prompt, intent, cart, mandate and UPI RRN. Agents raise grievances through ONDC IGM with that evidence attached.

    Evidence →

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U["User"] -->|"approves mandate on the Trusted Surface"| MM["Mandate Manager"]
    A["Agent"] -->|"signed request with mandate"| G["BACP gateway<br/>in a buyer app"]
    MM -.->|"mandate status"| G
    G -->|"Beckn with context.bacp"| S["Seller apps on ONDC"]
    G -->|"basket-blind payment leg"| P["Payer PSP and UPI"]
    P -->|"signed receipt with RRN"| G
    G -->|"instruction log and receipts"| E["Evidence bundle"]

Core concepts explains each part. BACP and India's DPI explains what BACP takes from each rail, and BACP and other protocols explains how it relates to UCP, AP2, ACP, A2A and MCP.

docs.title: An independent, open proposal
docs.text:
BACP is an independent open proposal. It is not issued, endorsed or operated by NPCI, ONDC, RBI or any other public body. As of 17-10-2026, no production deployments have been announced. Where it relies on a rail or a regulation, it describes that rail as publicly documented and leaves the rail's own rules in charge.

The specification, schemas and tools are developed in the open at github.com/bacp-dev/bacp under the Apache License 2.0. See Status and Roadmap for what comes next.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text:
This page defines what it means to conform to BACP: the conformance levels a participant can claim, the requirements each role MUST meet, the invariants that must hold after every interaction, and how conformance is tested and attested.

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

Testing status

The levels and checklists on this page are normative for BACP 2026-10-18. As of 17-10-2026, the automated conformance suite and the reference implementation are not yet published. Until they are, conformance is self-declared against these checklists.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
BACP treats conformance as data, not as code. A conformance rule that lives only inside a test tool cannot be read, compared between versions or signed on its own, and a validator that fails open, or checks only logs, proves little. So:

  1. Declarative cases. Every conformance case MUST be data: a manifest entry naming its fixture, its steps as request templates, and its expected outcomes (HTTP status, error code, resolution, resulting state, and invariants). The test runner interprets the manifest; it is never the place where a rule is defined.
  2. Fail closed. The runner MUST fail a case, and the level, on an unknown assertion kind, a missing expectation, a skipped case, an unregistered error code or an exception. A level is attested only if every required case passes. There is no "warn and continue" mode.
  3. Live and log. Cases MUST drive the system under test live, with signed requests and mock counterparties, and check the resulting artefacts: the instruction-log chain, receipts, the Beckn message trace and webhooks. Checking logs alone is not sufficient.
  4. Invariants after every case. The runner MUST evaluate the global invariants after every case of a level, not only in dedicated cases.
  5. Stable ids and traceability. Each case has a stable case id and an expected verdict. Requirement ids and specification sections are carried as data, so the traceability matrix is generated rather than hand-written.
  6. Versioned and signed. The manifest is versioned with the specification (see Versioning). A run produces a published report, and a conformance authority on the public list may sign a conformance attestation listing the levels passed.
  7. Portable. Schemas are resolved by their $id from the published schema bundle, never from a local path.
  8. Every required code is tested. Every registered error or message code that a level requires MUST have at least one conformance case before that level can be attested.

docs.title: Conformance levels
docs.text: Level id Name Requires Scope bacp.core.1 Core — Identity and request signatures (tags, purposes, replay), idempotency, resource limits, the mandate schema and deterministic verification (including the positive-amount rule and atomic reservation), the session state machine and payment saga, post-order writes, IGM grievances, the instruction log and evidence bundle, field-scoped webhooks, and conformance to the REST contract. Exercised against a reference mock rail. bacp.pay.upi.1 Payments-UPI Core Live UPI standing authorities and human-present PIN payments: Reserve Pay (one block per seller, fail-safe notice from the second debit), UPI Circle caps (per transaction, monthly, first 24 hours, at most five devices), AutoPay (24-hour pre-debit notice and opt-out), AFA at ₹15,000, UPI 123PAY caps, the basket-blind payment leg, and RRN/UTR receipts. bacp.pay.all.1 Payments-All Payments-UPI, and in this version the negotiation endpoint (because handler intersection takes a negotiation_id unless the gateway lists in.bacp.payment_plan, Q-45) The full handler registry and binding classes O, C, A, D and N; alias resolution; cards (e-mandate AFA, card-not-present disabled, cross-border card-not-present AFA, refund consent states); PPIs and gift instruments; net banking presence rules; COD and return-to-origin; credit (key fact statement offer list, human-present acceptance, cooling-off, repayment to the lender); eNACH caps; split tender; refunds to source; the FX disclosure view. bacp.neg.1 Negotiation Core (and Payments-UPI for the hand-off from negotiation to payment) The separate negotiation mandate, term sheets, signed offers, the offer and negotiation state machines, the withdraw/accept crossing rule, the negotiation guard with atomic exposure checks, the validators that apply to bilateral bargaining, escalation with the diff card on the Trusted Surface only, protection of reservation values, and handling of untrusted counterparty text. bacp.b2b.1 B2B Negotiation, Payments-All RFQs (sealed, deposits, response_by, landed-cost comparison), purchase orders via confirm, the MSMED credit-days cap, document gates (e-invoice IRN, e-way bill), schemes, the bacp.credit_ledger (two-party header, hash chain, acknowledgement, rail-evidenced settlement), eNACH B2B subscriptions and maker–checker approval. bacp.ts.1 Trusted Surface — Requirements TS-1 to TS-6 of a Mandate Manager's or payer PSP's Trusted Surface (Human participants): signed and templated content only, decline as easy as approve, language and modality, no urgency, a recorded Presentation, rendering only to the principal or payer that the render names, the typed ts_render and render_required[], the language fail-safe, the TS-drawn voice challenge with keypad equal to speech, no PIN on a call the Trusted Surface places, and the assisted announcement. Exercised with system_under_test: trusted_surface. bacp.auction.1 Auctions Negotiation A neutral auctioneer, a signed and frozen auction specification, anti-sniping, commit–reveal with deposits and forfeits, reverse (L1), English and Dutch rules, retraction rules, shill-bid refusal, and award rules.

docs.title: Profile maturity
docs.text:
Each trade profile carries a maturity label (as of 18-10-2026). The label changes no case. It says whether a conformance attestation can cover the profile.

Maturity Profiles Conformance scope of this release launch b2c.ecom (marketplace and quick commerce), kirana.khata, subscription, ticketing Stable. An attestation MAY cover the levels the profile needs. proposed fmcg.distribution, b2b.procurement, services, social In the release. An attestation MAY cover the levels the profile needs, and the rules MAY change in a later dated release. experimental gem, agri, crossborder, high_value, c2c.rental, assisted.rural Outside the scope. No attestation covers the profile, and a verifier MUST NOT treat a claim of one of these profiles as conformance. A party MAY refuse it with capabilities_incompatible, reason profile_not_supported.

docs.title: Claiming a level
docs.text:
• A participant declares the levels it claims in its profile and carries them in its conformance credential. An AgentCredential carries them in conformance.levels[], using the level ids above, with the signed attestation in conformance.attestation (see Identity and Request Signing).
  • A participant that claims a level MUST pass every case of that level and of every level it requires.
  • A gateway MAY offer a payment handler whose registry status is pilot only if its conformance attestation lists that pilot in pilots[] and has not expired.
  • Counterparties MAY check a participant's attestation at registry lookup (see Registry lookup).

docs.title: Conformance attestation
docs.text:
A conformance attestation is a compact JWS issued after a conformance run (see Principles, item 6). A gateway publishes its attestation in its profile (conformance.attestation), and an AgentCredential carries the agent's in conformance.attestation.

The payload is defined by conformance-attestation.json. The JOSE header typ MUST be bacp-conformance+jwt (RFC 8725 section 3.11); an attestation with any other typ is refused. All fields below are REQUIRED, and no other claim is allowed.

Field Content iss The ca_id of the entry in the conformance-authority list whose key signed the attestation. sub The participant the attestation is about: the gateway's subscriber id, the agent id or the Mandate Manager's registry id. For a trusted_surface, the subscriber id of the Mandate Manager or payer PSP that operates the Trusted Surface. subject_role gateway, agent, mm or trusted_surface. trusted_surface is the Trusted Surface of a Mandate Manager or a payer PSP, attested at level bacp.ts.1 (system_under_test: trusted_surface). Only a gateway may list pilot handlers: for agent, mm and trusted_surface, pilots[] is empty. scope The constant bacp-protocol-conformance. It states that the attestation covers BACP protocol conformance and nothing else. iat, exp Issue and expiry time, as NumericDates (seconds since the epoch; NumericDate is defined in RFC 7519 §2, exp in §4.1.4 and iat in §4.1.6). exp is at most 180 days after iat. After exp, no verifier may rely on the attestation. jti The attestation's unique id (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$). A mandate's rail_binding.conformance records it, and a pause for a lapsed attestation logs it. bacp_version, registry_version The dated BACP release whose cases were run, and the dated release of the handler registry that the run used. levels[] The level ids passed. pilots[] The canonical ids of the pilot payment handlers whose cases the gateway passed and that it may offer. Empty when there are none. A legacy alias is not a canonical id. manifest_digest sha-256: digest of the conformance-case manifest that was run. report_digest sha-256: digest of the published, reproducible run report behind the attestation. status Where the attestation's revocation status is published: {"status_list": {"uri": …, "idx": …}}, the same shape as an AgentCredential's status (Identity and Request Signing).

The attestation is a statement that the subject passed BACP protocol tests. It MUST NOT be offered or accepted in place of any rail onboarding, permission or certification, and MUST NOT be presented as approval by NPCI, RBI, ONDC or any public body. A gateway or agent that shows it to a principal says "passed BACP protocol tests" (and the same in hi-IN, in Devanagari) and MUST NOT use the words "certified", "approved", "verified" or "accredited", or their hi-IN equivalents, or any logo of NPCI, RBI or ONDC, and MUST NOT show kind to a principal.

docs.title: Conformance-authority list
docs.text:
The conformance-authority list is the only way to admit a signer of conformance attestations. It is a public, dated list that each dated BACP release publishes as source/registry/conformance-authorities.json, and whose digest the release manifest source/handlers/release.json records; its schema is conformance-authority-list.json. The registry role conformance_authority (Identity and Request Signing) names a key that signs attestations and nothing else, and only a key of a listed entry qualifies.

  • The list ships empty in 2026-10-18. No key qualifies until an entry is added, so a Mandate Manager still refuses open mandates on every pilot handler, as it did before this list existed. Adding an entry needs the further approval that GOVERNANCE.md requires.
  • Who may be listed. An independent test laboratory (kind: lab) or a rail-sponsor bank (kind: rail_sponsor). kind is for display and grants no extra power. A bank is listed only at its own request and is never the required signer. Every entry names its operator (legal name and id), its funders[], its keys[], the report_uri_template of its published run reports, its validity period and a status pointer.
  • Every entry is scoped. scope.levels[] and scope.pilots[] (at least one handler) bound what the authority may attest. A pilot outside the entry's scope.pilots is refused.
  • A Mandate Manager may only narrow the list. It MAY publish an exclusion list (excluded_attesters[] in its profile) and MUST NOT accept a signer that the public list does not contain.
  • A conformance authority only signs and revokes. It never routes, holds or settles funds. The project's interim maintainer never holds, operates or funds an authority key (GOVERNANCE.md).
  • Separation is checked per mandate. The Mandate Manager compares the entry's operator and funders[] with the operators of the attested subject, of the payer PSP and of itself (Rules).
  • Fees and reports. Every entry carries fee_model{basis: per_run | subscription, outcome_contingent: false, terms_uri}, so that no fee depends on whether the subject passes, and publishes_all_runs: true, so that the report of every run, passes and failures, is published. No fee is payable to the project for a list entry (GOVERNANCE.md). A run report carries a conflict_declaration{sponsor_of_subject, other}, which report_digest covers: sponsor_of_subject is true when the authority, its operator or a funder sponsors the attested subject, and other states any other relationship, or none.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• At issuance. Before a Mandate Manager issues an open payment mandate on a handler whose registry status is pilot, it MUST verify the gateway's attestation, which the gateway forwards in the mandate request (gateway_attestation). The Mandate Manager MUST refuse issuance with rail_binding_not_open_eligible (Handler binding) when any of these holds:
    • the JOSE typ is any value other than bacp-conformance+jwt;
    • the signing key, selected by the kid of the JOSE header, is not in the keys[] of an entry of the conformance-authority list of the latest publication of the registry files (the highest registry_serial of the release manifest); the time of the check is outside the entry's valid_from to valid_until; or the entry's status is revoked; while the list has no entry, no key qualifies, so a Mandate Manager refuses open mandates on every pilot handler, including in.upi.circle and in.card.agentic;
    • the entry is in the Mandate Manager's published exclusion list (reasons: [attester_not_accepted]);
    • a pilots[] member is outside the entry's scope.pilots, or the handler is not in pilots[];
    • exp is passed, or exp − iat is over 180 days (JSON Schema cannot compare the two, so a conformance case tests it);
    • the status is revoked (reasons: [binding_ineligible]);
    • the copy of the status list is more than 24 hours old, or the list is unreachable (reasons: [attestation_status_stale], resolution: recoverable);
    • the report at the entry's report_uri_template for this jti is absent, or does not hash to report_digest;
    • registry_version is older than the registry release in which the bound handler's status, binding or mandate_primitives last changed;
    • sub is not the subscriber that the signing key of the forwarded request resolves to in the registry (the Mandate Manager does not take sub from a body field);
    • the entry's operator, or any of its funders, is the same operator as sub, as the payer PSP in rail_binding.psp_id or as the issuing Mandate Manager, or any of those operators is unknown (reasons: [attester_not_independent]). A participant's operator is the operator of its registry record with assertion: registry: a profile, a request body, the attestation or an operator whose assertion is declared never supplies it, and an absent or declared operator is unknown. Two operators are the same when they share a CIN, an LLPIN or a PAN, or a group_id; a GSTIN alone never decides it, because one entity can hold several. The entry's operator.id and the id of each of its funders[] are compared with the entity_ids[] of the other operators, and so is each of its funder_ids[]. When the entry names a group_id, a compared record that has none is unknown.
  • Binding. The Mandate Manager MUST write rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti} on every open payment mandate bound to a pilot handler. The schema leaves the object optional, because a live handler needs none; this rule makes it REQUIRED for pilot bindings.
  • At complete. On a pilot handler the gateway MUST refuse (400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible) when rail_binding.conformance is absent or its sub is not itself. It MUST re-check, at every complete, the gateway's current attestation for the pilot: the bound jti, or after a lift the newer attestation from the same authority that lifted the pause, whose sub is itself and whose pilots[] lists the bound handler, under the same 24-hour rule. rail_binding.conformance records the attestation verified at issuance and is not rewritten; the InstructionLog entry for a lift records the new jti. It MUST also check, under the same 24-hour rule, that rail_binding.conformance.iss is still an entry of the list, within its validity and not revoked, that the attestation's key is still in its keys[], and that the bound handler is still in its scope.pilots. An entry that is removed, lapsed or revoked, or a key that is removed, is a lapse of the attestation: the gateway adds binding_ineligible with cause attestation. While Q-77 is open, it refuses every human-not-present complete under an open mandate on in.upi.circle with 400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible.
  • Freshness. An attestation status list that is more than 24 hours old, or unreachable, is refused for issuance and for a human-not-present complete on a pilot handler, and the complete returns reasons: [attestation_status_stale] with resolution: recoverable and no pause. An agent that receives attestation_status_stale tells the principal that human-not-present payment on this handler is unavailable for now, and offers the human-present step. It never blocks a status check, a reversal, a refund or a post-order write. A revoked or expired attestation, at a re-check, pauses the mandate (Handler binding).
  • Test fixtures. The fixture typ bacp-conformance-test+jwt MUST be refused by every Mandate Manager outside a conformance harness.
  • No other use. A conformance authority only signs and revokes; the attestation MUST NOT be offered or accepted in place of any rail onboarding, permission or certification, and MUST NOT be presented as approval by NPCI, RBI, ONDC or any public body.
  • Unchanged for in.upi.circle. Listing Circle in an authority's scope and in an attestation does not open the human-not-present path on in.upi.circle (UPI Circle).

No open question blocks a conformance level of 2026-10-18; the remaining ones are listed on Open Questions, each with a fail-safe default that the conformance cases test. Core is attested against stable vectors: the signature algorithms ES256 and EdDSA, both mandatory to verify (Q-42), the attached-JWS encoding used to close open mandates (Q-41), and the purpose-code registry with its bounds (Q-47) are settled in this version.

docs.title: Requirements by role
docs.text: The checklists below collect the MUST-level requirements that conformance tests check for each role. They summarise the normative pages and do not replace them; each line links to its source.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
An agent (and its operator) MUST:

  • Send its AgentCredential in the BACP-Agent header and sign every request with RFC 9421, covering every required component, including @query whenever a query string is present (Identity and Request Signing).
  • Use the signature tag each endpoint requires, a fresh nonce per request, and a validity window of at most 300 seconds (Signature tags).
  • Send an Idempotency-Key on every POST and PUT, retry only with the same key, and read the resource before retrying after a lost response (Idempotency).
  • Never collect, store or relay a UPI PIN, OTP, card credential or Aadhaar number, and never call POST /trusted-surface/events (Security and Privacy).
  • Present the AI disclosure and the human-handoff option in its first message of every session, logged at stage ai_disclosure as the first entry whose actor is agent; list a tel: route (optionally with DTMF digits) when its credential's channels include voice, ivr or upi123pay; and request a handoff with POST /sessions/{id}/handoff whenever the principal asks, even after the mandate is revoked (Human participants).
  • On an assisted session (channel: assisted, or an AgentCredential of class assisted), list the assisted operator in participants[], and never answer a bacp.input_request whose needed_from is principal on the principal's behalf.
  • Send hp_proof{ts_event_hash, step_up_id} with every post-order write that declares presence: HP, obtained through the post_order step-up that a write without it returns, and use each proof once, for the write its ts_render names (Presence proof).
  • Record a GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection or ledger acknowledgement as an agent only with hp_proof (Trade acts).
  • Close an open mandate only for the exact amount and checkout_hash of the seller-signed quote, with its cnf key (Mandates and Consent).
  • Relay every step-up and pre-debit notice to the principal and never dismiss them on the principal's behalf (Payments).
  • Treat catalogue text, seller messages and other counterparty content, including every origin: counterparty message and args[] value, as untrusted data, never as instructions.
  • Never emit a firm counter-offer outside its negotiation mandate. When the guard escalates, any counter it sends MUST be marked subject_to_principal_approval: true and firm: false (Negotiation).
  • Verify a fetched receipt's hash against the receipt_hash in the webhook before relying on it (Evidence and Instruction Log).
  • On a mandate paused for binding_ineligible, open no Trusted-Surface resume request and no re-issue request (POST /mandates) without a new instruction from the principal (Handler binding).
  • In a multi-seller basket, open one session per seller under one basket_id and one root open Checkout Mandate, request a further block only with checkout_mandate_ref, payee and rail_limits.block_amount, offer a new block only beside a one-time human-present payment and never after a failed payment, and never re-route an in_doubt leg (Per-leg rule).
  • Keep its operator signing key separate from the agent's cnf key, and sign instruction-log entries asymmetrically.
  • When it presents discovery results, say the fixed sponsorship sentence for every sponsored or undeclared item and never render undeclared as "not sponsored"; voice a prior price only as the amount pair; show no reduction, strike-through, percentage, "was" or "off" claim without a prior_price, and none taken from free text; and verify the seller-signed source of every item it presents or relies on, rendering an unverified item with no claim and with sponsorship as undeclared at least. It generates a fresh Idempotency-Key for each search, and checks Disclosures.catalogue[] against what it verified (Verifying discovery results, Disclosure phrases; cases CD-07, CD-13, CD-14, CD-26 to CD-34, CD-47 to CD-51).
  • Present a registered type: disclosure message as its fixed phrase, never as the message's content, and not hand over a step-up whose catalogue_disclosure[] does not match Disclosures.catalogue[] (Message object; cases CD-41, CD-R09, CD-R10).
  • Submit no affiliate code of its operator when no human is present, and tell a present principal before it submits one (Discounts; case CD-50).
  • Learn the ts_event_hash of a post-order approval only from GET /step-ups/{step_up_id} or step_up.updated, check the host of a trusted_surface_url against StepUp.surface, keep its voice channel off the Trusted Surface's call leg, and never send afa_ref, ref_verification: verified or confirmation_floor (Presence proof; cases T6-14, T6-19, T6-38, T6-42, T6-47c).

docs.title: Gateway
docs.text:
A BACP gateway MUST:

  • Publish a valid profile at /.well-known/bacp, including message_id_namespace.
  • Decide a withdraw and accept crossing only by transcript positions inside the loser's own chain, return a CounterSignaturePayload in the synchronous response to every firm message within 5 seconds of the sender's dispatch on the sender's monotonic clock, return a byte-identical receipt on re-delivery, treat an unprovable order as crossing_contested and never as a breach, raise a contested crossing to its own principal without auto-confirming (a seller gateway too), keep one linearisable chain per negotiation_id, and fill sender_log_seq, sender_log_prev and protocol_terms itself (Signed seller acceptance and clock skew; cases T5-07 to T5-17, T5-19 to T5-24, T5-42, T5-45, T5-50).
  • Raise a negotiation step-up only on an outgoing accept or firm-counter attempt, treat an absent accept_confirmation as ask, honour autonomous only with a usable notice_route, deliver the notice of an autonomous act through that route and not through the agent, accept a purchase-offer withdrawal, and accept a decline of an AGREED or BOUND deal only as the Trusted Surface event (cases T5-03, T5-29 to T5-40).
  • Refuse request bodies over 256 KiB with 413, then verify signatures on the raw bytes before parsing, in the specified order, with the replay cache and the 5-second skew (Identity and Request Signing).
  • Verify each AgentCredential against the registry and its status list, and enforce that the tag is allowed for the endpoint and listed in the credential's purposes.
  • Implement idempotency exactly as specified, including per-agent quotas, Idempotent-Replayed, never storing 5xx, and failing closed with 503 when the store is unavailable (Idempotency).
  • Run the deterministic mandate verifier on every complete, fail closed, reject unknown constraints, and reject non-positive payable amounts (Mandates and Consent).
  • Re-check the open mandate's handler binding (status, conformance attestation and rail_binding.primitive) against the current registry on every complete, taken from the dated release; adopt a status downgrade within 24 hours of its published_at, refuse an HNP complete on a handler whose descriptor copy is more than 24 hours old (reasons: [registry_copy_stale], resolution: recoverable, no pause), serve GET /payment-handlers with a Cache-Control max-age of at most 86400, and add the pause reason binding_ineligible, with the registry_version and registry_serial that caused it, to every affected mandate when a registry or attestation change makes its binding ineligible. Keep pause reasons as a set: keep a mandate PAUSED while any reason remains, remove only binding_ineligible and only on a strictly newer registry version in which the binding is eligible, pause a legacy mandate with reissue_required and never remove it, and write every addition and removal to the InstructionLog with the registry_version (Handler binding).
  • On a pilot handler, refuse a complete whose mandate has no rail_binding.conformance or names another gateway, re-check the bound attestation's jti (expiry, pilots[] and status) at every complete, pause the mandate with binding_ineligible (cause attestation, the jti logged) when it is revoked or expired, and for a status that is more than 24 hours old or unreachable refuse an HNP complete with reasons: [attestation_status_stale], resolution: recoverable and no pause (Conformance attestation; cases S-F1, S-F1-missing, S-F7, CA-04b, CA-07).
  • Evaluate budgets, usage, rail caps and split-order detection inside one atomic section keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate against a reservation ledger, reserve every tender of a split-tender plan in that one section, decrement budgets only from PSP-signed receipts, and leave no reservation behind once every payment has resolved.
  • Never rely on rail limits to bound BACP budgets.
  • Count every Reserve Pay block as reserved spend at its full attested amount until its revocation is confirmed or it expires, also against any new root of the same principal; apply the activation of a sibling block inside the root's atomic section and refuse it (403 mandate_exhausted) when the block no longer fits the headroom of every budget window; hold the seller's BPP-signed payment terms (the raw on_init body and its Beckn Authorization header) for every Reserve Pay block before the request reaches the Trusted Surface, or refuse it (400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible); where the payer PSP attests a block-debit feed, count an unmatched debit as settled spend and add the pause reason unmatched_rail_debit, which only the principal removes (Usage ledger).
  • For a multi-seller basket: refuse a basket_id shared across principals, presence or root open Checkout Mandates (400 invalid_request at $.basket_id) and never send it to the network or the PSP; plan every leg under the per-leg rule, log chosen and skipped rungs in comparison[], run the headroom check on every block and raise any rail_fallback step-up before the first debit; consume each covers[] entry once in the root-Checkout-Mandate atomic section; never let one payment span sellers; and never re-route an in_doubt leg (Multi-seller basket).
  • Move a session to requires_escalation for every step-up, with a Trusted Surface link valid for at most 15 minutes (at least 5 for ivr_callback and assisted), and complete only after a signed approval from the Trusted Surface (Sessions and Checkout).
  • Sign a ts_render once for every step-up, never change it, and serve it by step_up_id only to the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP (Step-up signers: for a session step-up, the PSP in rail_binding.psp_id of the open Payment Mandate under the session's mandate; for a post_order step-up, the PSP in auth_binding.psp_id of the order's closed Payment Mandates) (404 not_found to any other registry key, 429 above a rate limit counted per caller key before the lookup); refuse an approval from any other registry key (404 not_found), without presentation, without presentation.checkout_hash or with user_action: decline (400 invalid_request), with a content_hash that is not the hash of the ts_render (403 ts_render_mismatch), acted on after expires_at (step_up_expired), or, on an assisted session, without the principal's own factor or an assisted_by that is an assisted operator of the session (403 presence_not_proven); and skip evaluation step 8 only while the session's checkout_hash equals the approval's (Human participants).
  • Accept a post-order write (cancel, return, raise issue, issue action) with presence: HP and a valid hp_proof on an order whose mandate is REVOKED, PAUSED (for every pause reason), EXPIRED or EXHAUSTED, and refuse it without HP with 403 presence_not_allowed; let a status check, a reversal and a refund to the original source of a debit that is in the ledger proceed under a binding pause, and refuse a refund to any other destination (cases T2-OPS-01 to T2-OPS-03, S-F6b; Post-order gate).
  • Refuse every post-order write with presence: HP that lacks a valid hp_proof (403 presence_not_proven, with a post_order step-up when the proof is missing) before any network message; accept a proof only for the action, order and issue its ts_render names (for an issue action, only while the issue's resolution still hashes to its subject_hash), and consume it once inside the atomic section keyed on the order's root Checkout Mandate; keep at most one pending post_order step-up per (order_id, action, issue_id), return it again on a repeat, and rate-limit their creation (429) (Post-order gate).
  • Accept POST /sessions/{id}/handoff in every state and after revocation; refuse the agent's PUT and complete in human_handoff with 409 session_state_conflict, and hold every Trusted Surface approval until release; set handoff.accepted_by only from a support operator key under tag bacp-handoff; accept action: release only from that key, or from the agent while accepted_by is absent, and then return the session to incomplete; run accept and release as compare-and-set on accepted_by and ended_at, and refuse an accept after ended_at with 409 session_state_conflict; and refuse POST /sessions for an assisted session with no assisted_operator participant (Human handoff).
  • Never put counterparty text in a gateway-written message content; carry it in args[] with origin: counterparty, and label it visibly in every text rendering (Messages).
  • Over MCP, signal a step-up by URL-mode elicitation when the client declared it, and insufficient_scope otherwise; never treat an elicitation accept as an approval (MCP and A2A).
  • Apply every fail-safe default as stated in the release it claims, never a relaxed form (Fail-safe defaults).
  • Debit at most once per closed payment mandate and per checkout_hash; handle in_doubt without a new debit and debited_not_confirmed with an immediate refund to source (Payments).
  • Send the PSP only payee, amount, rail reference, mandate reference and checkout hash: never the basket.
  • Verify, before money moves, that the collecting party is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank.
  • Remove pre-ticked add-ons, flag drip pricing, and refuse to reach ready_for_complete while a required disclosure is missing.
  • Refuse to share personal data outside the mandate's data_scopes or not covered by a consent receipt.
  • Add context.bacp to every BACP-originated network message, with ai_disclosure: true, mandate_ref on init, confirm, update, cancel and IGM issue, and the instruction-log head on every committing message, and mirror ai_disclosure into the bacp tag group (Beckn / ONDC Binding).
  • Put every signed Trusted Surface event of a transaction, verbatim, in the evidence bundle's trusted_surface_events[], and the ts_render of every step-up event, byte-identical, in ts_renders[] (Evidence bundle).
  • Send acting_for.gstin and acting_for.display_name to a seller only when the mandate's data_scopes include ACTING_FOR (Mirroring).
  • Derive Beckn message_ids deterministically and bind each callback to its request (Network leg signing).
  • On mandate revocation, cancel open sessions and refuse new commitments, while still allowing cancel, return and grievance on existing orders.
  • Sign webhooks, embed only receipt references (never signed receipts), and never send personal data outside the agent's data_scopes or any negotiation bound.
  • Accept POST /trusted-surface/events only from the registry key of the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP, signed under bacp-ts with no BACP-Agent header.
  • Return errors through the two-channel model with registered codes, and document every status each operation can return (Errors).
  • Run the negotiation guard on every outgoing firm counter-offer, ACCEPT, bid and award, and never reveal the reservation price or total_max (Negotiation level and above).
  • Refuse a firm offer without acceptance_revocation and never insert a value; refuse allowed_until_receipt on every leg, incoming or in the principal's own draft (capabilities_incompatible); apply the value rules by leg and session, with the profile fixed at session open and the acting_for cross-check for consumer sessions; accept a waived offer without the principal only against a basis document obtained from the principal before the offer arrived; on a Beckn leg excuse no schema error other than a missing waiver_basis; release exposure once per reservation; refuse every accept_revoke with accept_revoke_not_allowed; apply the tag and presence rules for accept_revoke; and accept a negotiation approval only as negotiation.step_up.approved whose presentation.offer_hash equals the ts_render's and the offer's (403 ts_render_mismatch) (Acceptance revocation; cases T3-01 to T3-30 outside the Proposed (sunset) block).
  • Return sponsorship on every discovery item with the monotone OR rule, relay the seller's prior_price, mrp, tax_inclusive and sponsorship unaltered, never create a prior_price, drop an invalid one with prior_price_invalid, state ranking.sponsored as the OR of the items, give every results[] entry the source_digest of one signed callback, keep and serve those callbacks, and sign the POST /discover response (Catalogue disclosures; cases CD-02 to CD-06, CD-09 to CD-12, CD-15, CD-20 to CD-22, CD-32).
  • Report discovery_price_changed (escalating only for an item shown with a prior_price), fill Disclosures.catalogue[], emit the registered type: disclosure messages, carry catalogue_disclosure[] on session step-ups, and refuse a step_up.approved whose presentation.renders lacks it (Sessions and Checkout, Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface; cases CD-16 to CD-19, CD-35, CD-40, CD-R11).
  • Apply discounts only from the seller-signed quote, never submit a code the agent did not send, report each rejected code, rate-limit rejected codes, and refund from the seller-signed revised quote (Discounts; cases CD-42 to CD-46, CD-52, CD-R13 to CD-R18).
  • Mint a trusted_surface_url only on an origin of the step-up's signer, push content-free through ts_notify_url or answer 503 trusted_surface_unavailable; refuse voice_confirm_plus_device on rail_auth and on a debit-releasing confirm; bind a handoff to the session's agent operator's support operator key; serve GET /step-ups/{step_up_id} to the issuing credential only; match a RETURN or CANCEL field by field with an overlap rule; and apply the decline cool-off, the re-prompt cap and the declared limits (Human participants; cases T6-05 to T6-09, T6-15 to T6-30, T6-33b, T6-35 to T6-42, T6-44b, T6-46 to T6-49).
  • Refuse an open mandate at a gateway that is not its agent.bap_id, take the principal section before the root section (K1 before K2), write a firm commitment into the root's ledger keyed by offer_hash, allow one debit per checkout_hash per root inside the root's section, send a signed MandateEvent to the audit_uri for each use, relinquishment and gateway-originated pause change, apply a receipt only when the PSP of the debit signed it, release a budget only on the refund evidence of the usage ledger, hold human-not-present payment to a seller with an unresolved reversal, and state the reversal_basis and refund_route of a debited_not_confirmed payment (cases T7-01, T7-02, T7-07 to T7-14, T7-18 to T7-31, T7-36 to T7-38, T7-44).
  • Pass the binding cases for every one of in.bacp.payment_plan, in.bacp.ledger, in.bacp.trade_document and in.bacp.ucp_checkout that its profile lists, and, whatever it lists, the transport cases that bind every gateway (cases BND-TAG-01, BND-TAG-02, BND-MCP-STDIO-01, BND-MCP-ARGS-01, BND-MCP-IDEM-01).
  • Refuse, and never ignore, a request member that a capability owns when its profile does not list that capability (400 capability_unsupported at the member's path, nothing created or changed), publish a closed MCP inputSchema generated from the capabilities it lists, and, on the UCP projection, refuse a buyer-consent, loyalty or cart_id member (cases T8-CAP-01, T8-CAP-03 to T8-CAP-05); require BACP-Version as a covered component when its profile lists more than one version, pin a session to its version, put the version in the idempotency fingerprint, run the protective checks of the newest version for bacp-pay and bacp-post-order, and never fetch an extension schema (cases T8-CAP-02, T8-VER-01 to T8-VER-06, T8-EXT-01 to T8-EXT-03, T8-FETCH-01 to T8-FETCH-04); refuse an off-increment quantity, an unoffered fulfilment option and a basket below min_order, refuse an upward weight adjustment that no band allows, accept no substitute without a new checkout_hash, assign added_by itself, and report every marketing purpose as not granted without a receipt (cases T8-QTY-01, T8-QTY-02, T8-ADJ-01 to T8-ADJ-03, T8-SUB-01, T8-FO-01, T8-MIN-01, T8-POL-01, T8-LINE-01 to T8-LINE-03, T8-GST-01, T8-GST-02, T8-MKT-01, T8-MKT-02, T8-LINK-01, T8-LOY-01).

docs.title: Seller (BPP)
docs.text:
A seller app that does not implement BACP needs no change: it ignores context.bacp. A BACP-aware BPP MUST:

  • Reject a duplicate message_id within its ttl with a NACK.
  • Refuse (NACK) an init, confirm, update, cancel or IGM issue that lacks context.bacp.mandate_ref, and verify the kb_jwt when one is present.
  • Return a signed quote in on_init, with the required disclosures.
  • Send bacp.disclosure tags only with values that are true: a prior_price only for a reduction it announced, as the lowest price in the 30 days before announced_on, and sponsored only as the fact of a paid placement (Catalogue disclosure mapping).
  • In negotiation, sign every message with its registry key, give every firm offer an absolute expiry, verify only the buyer's within_bounds attestation, and never request the buyer's bounds.
  • Respond to IGM issues whose complainant is an AI agent (an actors[] entry with type = AI_AGENT, Proposed: Q-11) as to any other complainant.

docs.title: Mandate Manager
docs.text:
A Mandate Manager MUST:

  • Write process.accept_confirmation on every negotiation mandate it issues, present ask and autonomous with equal weight and preselect neither, capture process.notice_route, show the current-stage charge before the factor of a decline of an AGREED or BOUND deal, and show every time in IST (cases T5-30, T5-38, T5-47).

  • Activate a mandate only after an explicit, affirmative approval by the principal on the Trusted Surface. An agent can never activate one.

  • Run its Trusted Surface to TS-1 to TS-6 and send a Presentation with every mandate.activated, step_up.approved, loan.accepted and payment.afa_completed event (Human participants).
  • State each catalogue_disclosure[] entry of a step-up render before the total, in the fixed sentences and with the item name as labelled seller text, and report it in Presentation.renders (Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface; cases CD-37, CD-39).
  • Reject, before anything reaches the Trusted Surface, a mandate request outside its purpose's bounds, and reject any mandate whose constraints exceed the limits of its rail binding.
  • Refuse to issue an open payment mandate whose rail_binding.primitive is not in the handler descriptor's binding.open_primitives, whose handler is not open-eligible, or whose handler is pilot without a verified gateway conformance attestation listing it. Take the registry from the dated release, never from a gateway endpoint, and record its version in rail_binding.registry_version.
  • Verify the gateway's attestation under every rule of Conformance attestation (signer in the public list and not excluded, scope, typ, 180-day validity, 24-hour status freshness, sub equal to the signing gateway, separation of operators), write rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti} on every pilot binding, refuse any in.upi.circle open mandate request while Q-77 is open, read the attestation's status list itself, and refuse the fixture typ outside a harness (cases T0-RT-11b, CA-01 to CA-15).
  • For a Reserve Pay mandate, require payee{vpa, bpp_id} equal to the seller's BPP-signed payment terms and rail_limits.block_amount, and refuse a buyer-app payee for HNP; for a request with checkout_mandate_ref, build only a Payment Mandate under that ACTIVE root of the same principal; keep the block amounts under a root, the requested one included, within its smallest budget max; refuse an attested block larger than requested or expiring after the root's valid_until, and revoke at the rail any block created for a request it then refuses, reporting rail_revocation; key the parallel-root rule on the principal's account behind every pairwise principal.ref and refuse a new root while another is ACTIVE unless its notice states every other root's budgets and the combined total; show the requested block amount, each budget's remaining amount and, without an attested block-debit feed, the unseen-draw statement in the issuance notice; when a root ends in any way, revoke each block at the rail and send one mandate.revoked per sibling with cascade_of and rail_revocation; and be the only key that fetches and answers a summary step-up (Sibling Payment Mandates).
  • Copy agent.bap_id from the verified AgentCredential, accept supersedes only from the Trusted Surface and sign carried_exposure from its own use events, accept a MandateEvent only from the BAP of agent.bap_id, record event_gap on a missing seq, refuse an attested credit funding (an overdraft without a deposit attestation, or a missing funding) without credit_funding_allowed, refuse a gift PPI without principal-side custody, and compare operators only from the registry record's operator with assertion: registry (cases T7-03 to T7-06, T7-11, T7-12, T7-16, T7-17, T7-34).
  • Sign mandates as immutable artefacts. Open mandates carry cnf, data_scopes, audit_uri, a data-retention period and at least one budget or max_executions.
  • Issue a consent receipt per recipient, in the principal's language, with the withdrawal and grievance routes, and list ACTING_FOR in a per-seller receipt before the gateway tells that seller whom the agent acts for.
  • Render a step-up only for a mandate of the principal who is logged in (TS-6), keep the principal's confirmation_floor and device_jkt[] under the principal's own control on the Trusted Surface, and read the floor in full in the activation notice (bacp.ts.1; cases T6-02, T6-46, T6-47).
  • Publish mandate status in a status list and send signed status events (activation, pause, revocation) to the gateway within 60 seconds.
  • Remain data-blind: store mandates and logs only, never order or payment payloads.
  • Issue a within_bounds attestation only for an ACCEPT inside the negotiation mandate, or after the principal approves on the Trusted Surface (Negotiation level and above).

docs.title: PSP and rail
docs.text:
A payer PSP MUST:

  • Run, or integrate with, a non-agentic Trusted Surface, and take the PIN or biometric only there, on its own app or on a call that the principal places to the PSP's published number, never on a web page and never on a call that the Trusted Surface places (PIN rule).
  • Render a step-up only to the principal or payer that the render names (TS-6), draw its own voice challenge, accept a keypad answer as speech, refuse an unknown listed render_required[] name and a JWS without typ: bacp-ts-render+jws, and render no other language than the step-up's unless the principal chooses it (bacp.ts.1; cases T6-02, T6-03, T6-11 to T6-13, T6-32 to T6-34, T6-43 to T6-45).
  • Render a step-up only from the ts_render fetched by step_up_id and its own templates, with counterparty text only in counterparty_text, decline no harder than approve, nothing preselected, no urgency text, the principal's language and modality, and audio read in full before the factor; record a Presentation whose content_hash is the hash of the ts_render; on an assisted session, take only the principal's own PIN or enrolled biometric and name the operator in assisted_by, taken from ts_render.assisted_operators[] (Human participants).
  • Create the standing authority (block, delegation or mandate) on a primitive listed in the handler's binding.open_primitives, and sign a rail_binding attestation of its reference, type, primitive, limits, expiry, payee and funding (deposit or credit); create no Reserve Pay block larger than the requested rail_limits.block_amount; never fetch or answer a summary step-up over a basket.
  • Refuse a second debit for the same closed payment mandate or checkout_hash, refuse any payment request that carries a basket, and refuse a Reserve Pay debit to any payee other than the block's.
  • Sign every payment and refund receipt with the rail evidence its handler requires (for UPI, a 12-digit RRN), name the original payment and the refund_state on refunds, and never include a PIN, OTP, card number, CVV, expiry or Aadhaar number.
  • Refund to the original source.
  • Send signed revocation, pre-debit notice and opt-out events to the gateway, and reject debits on a revoked authority.

docs.title: Verifier
docs.text:
A verifier of an evidence bundle (a grievance officer's tool, an ODR body, a PSP or a seller) MUST:

  • Treat two receipts at one log_seq for different entries, a received_at that decreases along a chain without clock_step_observed, a CounterSignaturePayload with a missing member and a negotiation step-up event with no ts_render in ts_renders[] as evidence_unverifiable, and compare times as instants (cases T5-04, T5-06, T5-17, T5-45, T5-49).

  • Run the six verification steps and the chain check, and report evidence_unverifiable on any failure, including a payment receipt whose payee VPA differs from checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms where the bundle carries them, a Reserve Pay payment whose bundle lacks those terms or whose terms' Beckn Authorization header does not verify over their body, a covered leg whose covers[] entry (or ts_render_digests[] entry, whose render_hash must equal the event's content_hash) differs from the leg's quote or payee, a step-up entry without a matching signed Trusted Surface event, an approval without a Presentation, a step-up event whose ts_render is missing from ts_renders[] or differs from the BPP-signed quote in total, payee or checkout_hash, or from the disclosures hash in price_breakup_hash, a step-up render whose catalogue_disclosure[] differs from the bundle's Disclosures.catalogue[], omits a qualifying entry or names an item other than the quote's, a Disclosures.catalogue[] entry whose source_digest the agent's discover log entry does not list or whose signed source fails (cases CD-36, CD-38, CD-R03, CD-R10), and a log whose first agent entry is not ai_disclosure (Evidence bundle), a negotiation step-up whose ts_render or presentation carries an offer_hash or an acceptance_revocation that differs from the signed offer, and a negotiation transcript in which a later entry has an earlier received_at (Clock skew).

  • Accept a step_up.* or negotiation.step_up.* event only from a key that Step-up signers derives from the bundle's mandates (case T6-01).
  • Never accept a summary rendered under in.bacp.evidence.summary.1 as evidence (Evidence summary).

docs.title: Operator
docs.text:
These are duties of the operator of an agent, gateway or Mandate Manager as a Data Fiduciary under the DPDP Act and Rules. They sit outside the protocol, so the conformance runner does not test them: an operator that claims a level attests to them. Each applies from 13-05-2027 (Commencement).

An operator MUST:

  • Engage a Data Processor, including a model or LLM host, only under a valid contract (Act s.8(2)) that requires reasonable security safeguards (DPDP Rule 6(1)(f)), and cause the processor to erase personal data whenever the operator must erase it (Act s.8(7)(b)) (Retention).
  • If it is, or belongs to a class notified as, a Significant Data Fiduciary: carry out a Data Protection Impact Assessment and an audit once in every twelve months and have the report of significant observations furnished to the Board (Rule 13(1)–(2)), and verify with due diligence that its algorithmic software, including the agent's models, is not likely to pose a risk to Data Principals' rights (Rule 13(3)). The AgentCredential's model_family and build feed this inventory (Identity and Request Signing).
  • If it is an e-commerce entity with at least two crore registered users in India: erase a Data Principal's personal data three years after she last approached it or exercised her rights (except what she needs to reach her user account or a stored virtual token), and tell her at least 48 hours before the erasure (Rules 8(1)–(2) and the Third Schedule, item 1). Data that another law requires to be kept is kept (Retention).

docs.title: Global invariants
docs.text:
These invariants MUST hold after every conformance case:

Invariant Rule INV-ONE-DEBIT-PER-CHECKOUT At most one money-moving rail transaction per checkout_hash. INV-NO-WRONG-AMOUNT Every debit equals the amount of the session that owns its checkout_hash. INV-EVIDENCE-5-OF-5 Every completed order's evidence bundle passes the five AP2 verification steps and step 6 (Trusted Surface events), with a valid instruction-log chain and bundle signature. The id is kept from earlier versions. INV-GUARDED-COMMITMENT No firm counter-offer, ACCEPT or bid leaves the gateway without a guard pass or a signed step-up approval. INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEAK No reservation price or total_max value appears in any buyer-originated outgoing message, response, webhook or log. A number the counterparty sent first, and the buyer side merely echoes, is not a leak. INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEFT Once every payment has resolved, no budget reservation remains. INV-NO-SIGNED-RECEIPT-IN-WEBHOOK No webhook body contains a signed receipt. INV-CONTRACT Every recorded response validates against its documented schema, and no undocumented status is returned.

docs.title: How conformance is tested
docs.text:
1. Select levels. The participant names the levels it claims.
  2. Run the cases. The runner loads the manifest for those levels (and the levels they require) and drives the system under test with signed requests from a test agent, against mock counterparties: a registry, a BPP, a Mandate Manager and Trusted Surface driver, and a PSP and rail with fault injection (timeouts, debit-then-silence, rejections).
  3. Check outcomes and invariants. For each case the runner compares the responses, states, messages, rail counts, log entries and webhooks with the case's expectations, then evaluates every global invariant.
  4. Report. The runner produces a report that anyone can reproduce. If every required case passed, a conformance authority on the public list may sign a conformance attestation listing the levels, with the digest of the report.

Informative: suggested manifest layout. The layout is levels.yaml (the level table as data), cases/<level>/*.yaml (one file per case), invariants.yaml and codes.yaml (generated from the error registry). A case looks like this:

case_id: CORE-ATOM-001
title: Concurrent completes on one open mandate never exceed the budget
level: bacp.core.1
fixture:
  mandate: {purpose: P-GRO-01, rail: in.upi.reservepay, budgets: [{period: P1M, max: {value: 100000, currency: INR}}]}
  rail: {block_amount: 10000000, debit_latency_ms: 20}
  sessions: {count: 20, amount: 100000, state: ready_for_complete}
steps:
  - parallel: 20
    request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, idempotency_key: fresh}
expect:
  responses:
    - {status: 200, body.status: completed, count: 1}
    - {status: 403, code: mandate_exhausted, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 19}
  invariants: [INV-ONE-DEBIT-PER-CHECKOUT, INV-NO-WRONG-AMOUNT, INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEFT]
  rail:
    settled_debits: 1
    settled_amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}
  state:
    session: completed

The expect vocabulary is closed: status, code, resolution, reasons, state, message codes, rail counts, log entries, webhooks, invariants, exactly_one_of, agent_requests, beckn, mcp and verdict. Anything else fails the case. In detail:

  • webhooks lists every webhook the case expects, in order, as objects with type and, for mandate.status_changed, status, reason and pause_reasons; a webhook not listed fails the case, so webhooks: [] means none is sent.
  • A responses entry MAY carry path (for example accept or complete) to say which of several parallel requests it answers.
  • exactly_one_of lists alternative expectation sets; the case passes when exactly one of them holds.
  • agent_requests counts the requests that an agent under test sends, by method and path or to the Trusted Surface.
  • beckn lists what the network trace MUST show, for example the tags of the bacp tag group as the seller receives them.
  • mcp gives the signal the MCP server sent for a step-up (url_elicitation or insufficient_scope).
  • verdict is the result of a system under test that returns no HTTP response: a verifier's or validator's code (evidence_unverifiable, schema_invalid, pass), a Trusted Surface check (ts_conformance_fail with the rule, for example TS-1), or properties of a rendered output.
  • state records the state of each state machine the case touches, keyed by machine. A case that changes the state of a machine MUST record the state it starts in as fixture.<machine>.state and the state it ends in as expect.state.<machine>, so that a checker can match the case to one transition. A case that is a refusal records the same state in both and shows that nothing changed. <machine> is the name of the machine in the specification: session, mandate, mandate_request, negotiation and the other machines that appear in state keys of the cases on this page. For the session machine the fixture key is the existing sessions.state (with count). A case that touches no state machine records no state. The rule applies to every case added from the release that introduces it; earlier cases are not rewritten.

A POST /mandates body in a case is an abbreviated fixture: a field that the schema REQUIRES but that the case does not exercise, such as operator_compensation, is present in the request under test with a valid value and is left out of the listing.

Fixture and step keys used by the cases on this page:

  • across_replicas: true sends the parallel requests of a step to different gateway replicas (gateway: {replicas: n}).
  • library_level: true means the case drives the gateway's verifier as a library, because the behaviour has no wire binding in this version.
  • create_session is a step that opens a new checkout session under the fixture mandate.
  • registry_release.published is the release time relative to the runner's clock (for example -25h).
  • registry_source is the state of the mock registry source from which the gateway refreshes its descriptor copy: reachable, or {unreachable_since: <time relative to the runner's clock>}.
  • registry_update is a step that publishes a newer registry version to the registry source; sweep is a step that lets the gateway (or named replicas) apply the registry it holds.
  • registry_by_replica gives each gateway replica its own registry version and serial, to test replicas that lag within the 24-hour window.
  • trusted_surface_event is a step in which the mock Mandate Manager sends a signed Trusted Surface event (for example mandate.paused) to the gateway.
  • system_under_test may also be verifier (the runner hands over a bundle), schema (the runner validates a published vector), trusted_surface (the runner plays the gateway and inspects what a Mandate Manager or PSP surface renders and records) or beckn_adapter (the runner plays a seller behind a validator that strips context.bacp).
  • The attestation cases use these fixture keys. conformance_authorities is the dated list that the Mandate Manager loads (entries with ca_id, operator, scope and, optionally, kind); the runner signs an attestation with the key of the entry named in iss. operators gives the declared operator of each subscriber and registry id, or unknown. mandate_manager gives its id, its mode (harness, which loads the fixture list and accepts the fixture typ bacp-conformance-test+jwt, or production) and its excluded_attesters and private_accepted_attesters. gateway_attestation gives the payload fields the case is about, the JOSE typ, and the status (ok, revoked, unreachable or {last_good_fetch: <time relative to the runner's clock>}); iat_to_exp replaces exp with a validity length. attestation_status gives the status of a jti as the gateway sees it, and as a step it changes that status. A step that names a fixture key (operators, conformance_authorities, gateway_attestation) replaces it. clock: {advance_past: …} moves the runner's clock past a time, and psp_receipt_arrives delivers a PSP-signed receipt to the gateway.
  • requirement: SHOULD marks a case for a SHOULD-level rule: it is reported, and does not fail the level.
  • applies_from is the date from which a case is required (for example 2027-05-13); before it the case is reported only.
  • relies_on names another rule or case set that the case depends on.
  • The human-participant cases also use the steps verify_bundle, validate, render, render_summary, requote, tool_call, elicitation_response, submit_each and wait_for, each named for what the runner does, and the fixture keys clock, transport, mcp_client, ts_render, bundle and acts.
  • A fixture key that names a BACP or Beckn object describes that object as the mock counterparties hold it, using the object's own field names: mandate, checkout_mandate, child_mandate, order, orders, issue, termsheet, negotiation, bpp_quote, consent_receipts, agent_credential, payment_mandates, trusted_surface_events, ts_renders and vector (a published example file). In payment_mandates, of says what a Payment Mandate belongs to: session (an open one under the session's mandate) or an order id (a closed one that paid that order). The other fixture keys are: step_up_link (the Trusted Surface link the agent receives), llm_processor (where the agent's model runs), network_validator (a validator between the gateway and the seller), notice_template (a Trusted Surface notice template) and mandate_manager (the state of the Mandate Manager under test).
  • A request body lists the fields a case is about. The runner completes any other field that the operation's schema requires from the fixture (for example reason_code and mandate_ref on a return) and never adds presence or hp_proof. A value in braces is taken from the fixture or an earlier step: {mandate_ref} (the mandate the order was placed under), {step_up_id} (the step-up the previous refusal or fixture names), {event_hash} (the hash of its signed step_up.approved event) and {event_hash_<step_up_id>} (the hash of the event for that step-up).
  • parallel sends the requests of a step at the same time: parallel: n sends n copies of the step's request, and parallel: [ … ] sends each listed request once.
  • step_up_limit sets the per-agent creation limit for post_order step-ups for the case; the value in a case is only a test setting, and the spec does not fix the gateway's own limit.
  • on_issue is a step in which the mock seller sends an unsolicited IGM on_issue with the given respondent action and resolution.
  • signer on a request or a trusted_surface_event step names the key that signs it (for example agent_key, support_operator_key_1 or a registry subscriber id such as psp-b.example.in); without it the step is signed with the key the endpoint expects.
  • system_under_test: agent means the runner plays the gateway and the Trusted Surface and observes the agent. Its steps webhook and request_from_gateway deliver a webhook to the agent and answer the agent's next request with the given response; principal_instruction: none_after_pause means the runner gives the agent no new instruction from the principal after the pause.

Schema conformance is tested with published test vectors: every example whose file name ends in .invalid.json MUST fail validation against its schema, and every other example MUST pass. The vectors are listed on Reference.

  • The example map is normative. examples/index.json lists, for each example file, whether it is valid and the schema or schemas that it is checked against (a path below source/ with an optional JSON Pointer fragment, or an absolute URL, and an instance pointer where a schema applies to one member). A runner takes the mapping from that file and does not infer it from file names. scripts/validate.py derives the map and fails when the file is stale (--write-index regenerates it). Where an invalid example is accepted by every listed schema, the entry names the repository check that rejects it in fails_by (protocol_terms_digest or alias_binding).
  • format is asserted. A validator MUST assert the JSON Schema format keyword (date-time, date, uri, uuid and the others that the schemas use), because some negative vectors fail on format alone (catalog-item.prior-price-bad-date.invalid.json and catalog-offer.bad-until.invalid.json). A validator also applies each pattern as an ECMA-262 regular expression.
  • No cryptographic vectors yet. The signature values in the examples are placeholders and the hashes that are not stated as computed do not digest anything. The suite will carry cryptographic test vectors (JCS, JWS, RFC 9421, the chains and a golden evidence bundle) that implementations of the specification produce and offer back to it after release.

docs.title: Handler-binding and budget cases
docs.text:
The cases below cover the handler binding of open mandates (including the registry source, 24-hour freshness and the set of pause reasons), the conformance attestation and the atomic reservation keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate. They are written in the manifest form above. A mandate fixture marked preinstalled: true is installed in the gateway as already signed and ACTIVE, so that the case can test complete without going through issuance. A step may carry its own expect, checked before the next step runs. system_under_test: mandate_manager means the runner drives a mock gateway that forwards the request, and checks the Mandate Manager. Amounts are integer paise.

- case_id: T0-RT-01
  title: A pilot handler that the gateway's attestation does not list backs no open mandate
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    registry: {in.erupi: {status: pilot}}
    gateway_attestation: {pilots: []}
    mandate: {rail: in.erupi, primitive: voucher, preinstalled: true}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.erupi}}
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 2}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: T0-RT-02
  title: An expired attestation does not cover a pilot handler
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    registry: {in.erupi: {status: pilot}}
    gateway_attestation: {pilots: [in.erupi], exp: past}
    mandate: {rail: in.erupi, primitive: voucher, preinstalled: true}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 1}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: T0-RT-03
  title: A wallet balance never backs an open mandate
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    psp_attestation: {type: in.ppi.wallet, primitive: balance_cap}
    mandate: {rail: in.ppi.wallet, primitive: balance_cap, preinstalled: true}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.ppi.wallet}}
      trusted_surface: approve
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 202, body.status: PENDING, count: 1}
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 1}
    state: {mandate_request: REJECTED}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: T0-RT-04
  title: Store credit is not open-eligible in this version
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    mandate: {rail: in.store_credit, primitive: balance_cap, preinstalled: true}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.store_credit}}
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 2}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}
    invariants: [INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEFT]

- case_id: T0-RT-05
  title: The credit ledger is not open-eligible in this version
  level: bacp.b2b.1
  fixture:
    mandate_request: {rail: bacp.credit_ledger, budgets: [{period: P1M, max: {value: 300000, currency: INR}}]}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: bacp.credit_ledger}}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 1}

- case_id: T0-RT-06
  title: A status downgrade reaches a mandate issued before it
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    registry: {in.erupi: {status: live}}
    mandate: {rail: in.erupi, primitive: voucher, preinstalled: true}
    gateway_attestation: {pilots: []}
    sessions: {count: 1, state: ready_for_complete}
  steps:
    - registry_update: {in.erupi: {status: pilot}}
      expect:
        webhooks: [{type: mandate.status_changed, status: PAUSED, reason: binding_ineligible, pause_reasons: [binding_ineligible]}]
        state: {mandate: PAUSED, session: cancelled}
        messages: [rail_binding_not_open_eligible]
    - create_session: {state: ready_for_complete, may_refuse: true}
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{new_session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP, only_if_session_exists: true}
  expect:
    exactly_one_of:
      - responses: [{path: create_session, status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, reasons: [binding_ineligible]}]
      - responses: [{path: complete, status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, reasons: [binding_ineligible]}]
    state: {mandate: PAUSED}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: T0-RT-07
  title: Concurrent completes on sibling payment mandates never exceed the checkout mandate's budget
  level: bacp.core.1
  fixture:
    checkout_mandate: {budgets: [{period: P1M, max: {value: 300000, currency: INR}}], settled: {value: 100000, currency: INR}}
    payment_mandates:
      - {name: A, rail: in.upi.reservepay, primitive: sbmd_block, payee: seller-a, block_amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}, matched_debits: {value: 0, currency: INR}}
      - {name: G1, rail: in.ppi.gift, primitive: balance_cap}
      - {name: G2, rail: in.ppi.gift, primitive: balance_cap}
    sessions: {count: 2, amount: 100000, payment_mandates: [G1, G2], state: ready_for_complete}
    gateway: {replicas: 2}
  steps:
    - parallel: 2
      across_replicas: true
      request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, idempotency_key: fresh}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 200, body.status: completed, count: 1}
      - {status: 403, code: mandate_exhausted, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 1}
    state: {exposure: {value: 300000, currency: INR}}
    invariants: [INV-ONE-DEBIT-PER-CHECKOUT, INV-NO-WRONG-AMOUNT, INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEFT]
    rail:
      settled_debits: 1
      settled_amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}

- case_id: T0-RT-08
  title: Loyalty points are not open-eligible in this version
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    registry: {in.loyalty: {limits: []}}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.loyalty}}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 1}

- case_id: T0-RT-10
  title: A Mandate Manager does not take the registry from a gateway endpoint
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  system_under_test: mandate_manager
  fixture:
    registry_release: {in.erupi: {status: pilot}}
    gateway_payment_handlers: {in.erupi: {status: live}}
    gateway_attestation: {pilots: []}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.erupi}}
      gateway: forwards
      trusted_surface: approve
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 202, body.status: PENDING, count: 1}
    state: {mandate_request: REJECTED}
    webhooks: []
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: T0-RT-10b
  title: Positive control for T0-RT-10, a Mandate Manager issues on a live handler that the gateway shows as reserved
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  system_under_test: mandate_manager
  fixture:
    registry_release: {in.upi.reservepay: {status: live}}
    gateway_payment_handlers: {in.upi.reservepay: {status: reserved}}
    bpp_payment_terms: {bpp.dairy.example.in: {vpa: dairy@examplebank, collected_by: BPP}}
    psp_attestation: {type: in.upi.reservepay, primitive: sbmd_block, payee: dairy@examplebank, block_amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}, funding: deposit}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.upi.reservepay, payee: {vpa: dairy@examplebank, bpp_id: bpp.dairy.example.in}, rail_limits: {block_amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}}}}
      gateway: forwards
      trusted_surface: approve
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 202, body.status: PENDING, count: 1}
    state: {mandate_request: ACTIVE}
    webhooks: [{type: mandate.status_changed, status: ACTIVE}]

- case_id: T0-RT-11
  title: A gateway cannot attest itself for a pilot handler
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  system_under_test: mandate_manager
  fixture:
    registry: {in.upi.circle: {status: pilot}}
    gateway_attestation: {iss: gateway, sub: gateway, pilots: [in.upi.circle]}
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: /mandates, tag: bacp-browse, body: {rail: in.upi.circle}}
      gateway: forwards
      trusted_surface: approve
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 202, body.status: PENDING, count: 1}
    state: {mandate_request: REJECTED}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}
