docs.title: Discovery and Profiles
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page defines how an agent learns what a BACP gateway supports, how the two sides agree on a protocol version, capabilities, negotiation features and payment handlers, how the gateway uses the network registry, and how network discovery (POST /discover) maps onto Beckn.

There are two kinds of discovery in BACP:

  • Gateway discovery. The agent reads the gateway's profile at /.well-known/bacp to learn versions, transports, capabilities, payment handlers and keys. This is the UCP /.well-known pattern.
  • Network discovery. The agent asks the gateway to search the ONDC/Beckn network for sellers and products. The gateway uses the network registry to find and verify sellers.

docs.title: Profile document
docs.text:
A BACP gateway MUST publish a profile document at the path /.well-known/bacp under its base URL, for example https://gw.bap.example.in/bacp/.well-known/bacp.

  • The profile is fetched with an unsigned GET. It carries no Idempotency-Key and needs no AgentCredential.
  • The response is application/json and MUST validate against the Profile schema of the REST binding.
  • Agents SHOULD cache the profile and SHOULD follow standard HTTP caching semantics, revalidating once the cached copy's max-age expires.
  • An agent MUST NOT rely on a profile's keys until it has checked that they match the registry record of the bap_id the profile names (see Registry lookup).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Required Meaning bacp.version REQUIRED The protocol version this profile describes. See Version negotiation. bacp.supported_versions OPTIONAL Every protocol version the gateway accepts. When it lists more than one, a request names its version in the signed BACP-Version header (Version negotiation). mcp_endpoints OPTIONAL {version: uri}: the MCP endpoint of each listed version. REQUIRED when the gateway lists more than one version and offers mcp. capability_declarations OPTIONAL {capability id: {version, extends, ...}}: machine-readable declarations of capabilities, a sibling of capabilities (Capability declarations). bap_id REQUIRED The Beckn/ONDC subscriber id of the BAP that hosts the gateway. Every AgentCredential the gateway accepts names this BAP. transports REQUIRED Bindings offered: rest, mcp, a2a. See Transports. capabilities REQUIRED Capability ids the gateway supports (see Capabilities). payment_handlers REQUIRED Payment handlers the gateway can process, as handler references. See Payment handlers in the profile. reserved_handlers OPTIONAL Handler ids or globs the gateway knows are reserved and will refuse, for example in.upi.uap. keys REQUIRED A JWK Set ({"keys": [...]}) with the gateway's public keys. The gateway signs webhooks with these keys. message_id_namespace REQUIRED The UUID namespace the gateway uses to derive Beckn message_ids (see Beckn / ONDC Binding). Agents need it to compute the nonce of a key-binding JWT for a seller. negotiation OPTIONAL The gateway's negotiation capability advert (see Negotiation capability). REQUIRED when the gateway supports negotiation. step_up_limits OPTIONAL The limits that the gateway applies to step-ups, each a {count, window} or, for the decline cool-off, a {window}: post_order_per_principal, post_order_per_order, session_per_principal, reprompt_per_issue, decline_cooloff, render_fetch_per_key and render_fetch_per_step_up. BACP sets no number. They are the gateway's own design values, never presented as external limits, and a gateway that declares none is tested against the conformance fixture's limit (Limits on step-ups). payment_handlers_registry OPTIONAL URI of the gateway's GET /payment-handlers endpoint. profiles OPTIONAL Trade profiles the gateway supports. limits.max_body_bytes RECOMMENDED The largest request body the gateway accepts. It MUST NOT exceed 256 KiB. conformance RECOMMENDED {levels, attestation, excluded_attesters[]}: the conformance levels the participant claims, its signed conformance attestation (REQUIRED to offer a pilot handler) and, on a Mandate Manager's profile, excluded_attesters[]: the ca_ids of the public conformance-authority list that it does not accept. A Mandate Manager only narrows the list and publishes the narrowing here, so that a refusal (attester_not_accepted) is testable.

Receivers MUST ignore profile fields they do not understand.

Proposed

The field name limits.max_body_bytes is proposed and is not yet in the Profile schema.

docs.text:

docs.title: Version negotiation
docs.text:
BACP versions are dates in YYYY-MM-DD form. The first dated release is 2026-10-18; the unreleased working version on main is draft (see Versioning).

  1. The agent fetches /.well-known/bacp.
  2. The agent selects a version that appears in bacp.version or bacp.supported_versions. It SHOULD prefer the most recent version it implements.
  3. If there is no common version, the agent MUST NOT call the gateway's other operations.
  4. On the network leg, the gateway states the BACP version it is speaking in context.bacp.version.

A participant that implements draft MUST expect breaking changes at any time. A dated release such as 2026-10-18 changes only as the Versioning policy allows. Version strings are a release date (YYYY-MM-DD) or draft, as defined by ProtocolVersion.

docs.title: The version of a request
docs.text:
An agent names the version of each request in the BACP-Version request header, whose value is a ProtocolVersion. A single header is enough because a profile that lists one version needs no choice.

  1. When it is required. BACP-Version is REQUIRED on every agent request when the gateway's profile lists more than one version in bacp.version and bacp.supported_versions. A request without it gets 400 invalid_request at $.headers.BACP-Version, on the pattern of idempotency_key_required. A gateway that lists one version accepts a request with no header as that version, and a request that names another version gets 400 version_unsupported. A Trusted Surface request (bacp-ts) carries the version of the session it acts on and needs no header.
  2. It is signed. bacp-version is a covered component of the request signature whenever the header is present (Covered components). A header that is present and not covered gets 401 signature_invalid, so that a party on the path cannot change the version of a signed request.
  3. An unlisted version gets 400 version_unsupported at $.headers.BACP-Version, with supported_versions[] listing the versions that the gateway lists.
  4. A session is pinned. A session is pinned to the version that it was created under, on every transport. A later request for the session that names another version gets 409 version_mismatch, and nothing changes. A new version needs a new session.
  5. The fingerprint. The version is part of the idempotency fingerprint of a request, not of the key's scope: the same key with the same body and another version is refused as 422 idempotency_conflict (Idempotency).
  6. MCP. A gateway that lists more than one version and offers mcp serves one MCP server for each version and publishes them in mcp_endpoints{version: uri}, because an MCP host may be unable to set a header. The version of a session on MCP is the version of the endpoint that created it.
  7. A2A. The A2A extension URI carries the version, https://bacp.dev/<version>/a2a, and the Agent Card declares it with required: true (Agent card).
  8. The protective floor. A request that is bacp-pay, bacp-post-order or bacp-negotiate runs the protective checks of the newest version that the gateway lists, whichever version the request names, so that naming an older version cannot switch a protective check off. A protective check is any rule of that version that refuses, escalates or raises a step-up. A version that lacks a check never lowers the floor.
  9. Never from a fetched document. A gateway and an agent MUST NOT take a version from a document that was fetched from a URL, such as a UCP profile or a seller's page. The version of a request is the signed header or the endpoint, and nothing else.

A gateway that lists one version is unaffected: the header is optional for it and the rules above change nothing.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
A capability is a named group of operations. A gateway MUST list every capability it supports in capabilities, and an agent SHOULD NOT call an operation whose capability the gateway does not list.

Capability Operations Defined in in.bacp.discover POST /discover, GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest} this page in.bacp.checkout /sessions, /sessions/{id}, /sessions/{id}/complete, /sessions/{id}/cancel Sessions and Checkout in.bacp.discounts The discounts field of POST /sessions and PUT /sessions/{id}; extends in.bacp.checkout Discounts in.bacp.payment_plan payment.plan_options[] on a session, complete.payment_plan, and session_id on POST /payment-handlers/intersect; extends in.bacp.checkout Wire binding of plans in.bacp.ledger GET /ledgers/{id}, GET /ledgers/{id}/entries, POST /ledgers/{id}/entries (agent: type: payment only), and ledger_ref and ledger_range acts on POST /trade-acts The khata credit ledger in.bacp.trade_document POST /trade-acts (GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection), GET /orders/{id}/documents Seller-side and trade acts in.bacp.ucp_checkout /checkout-sessions, /checkout-sessions/{id}, /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete, /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel: the checkout in the shape of UCP checkout, pinned to UCP release v2026-08-25; listed only if every entry criterion passes UCP checkout projection in.bacp.mandate /mandates, /mandates/{id}, /mandates/{id}/relinquish Mandates and Consent in.bacp.order /orders/{id}, /orders/{id}/cancel, /orders/{id}/returns Orders and Post-order in.bacp.issue /issues, /issues/{id}, /issues/{id}/actions, /evidence/{transaction_id} Evidence and Instruction Log

A gateway MUST support every operation of a capability it lists. in.bacp.payment_plan and in.bacp.ucp_checkout require in.bacp.checkout in the same list.

Refuse, do not ignore. A request member that a capability owns, where the gateway's version defines the capability but the gateway does not list it, MUST be refused with 400 capability_unsupported at the member's JSON path, with capability set to the capability id, and nothing is created or changed. The gateway MUST NOT ignore the member. This covers:

  • discounts on POST /sessions and PUT /sessions/{session_id} (in.bacp.discounts), at $.discounts;
  • payment_plan on complete and session_id on POST /payment-handlers/intersect (in.bacp.payment_plan), at $.payment_plan and $.session_id;
  • the members that a future capability owns.

A gateway that lists none of in.bacp.payment_plan, in.bacp.ledger and in.bacp.trade_document also exposes no tool or DataPart for them on MCP or A2A. A field that the gateway's version does not define is not capability-owned and keeps the rule of Extensibility (it is ignored on REST). The refusal is not the discount_code_unsupported warning, which a gateway that lists in.bacp.discounts returns when the seller declines codes. In the OpenAPI document, x-bacp-capability names the capability that owns an operation or a property, so that scripts/validate.py can test the rule: a value is a capability id from the table above, or a list of ids when any one of them suffices.

docs.title: Capability declarations
docs.text:
The optional profile member capability_declarations is a map beside capabilities, which stays a list of ids. Every key MUST also appear in capabilities, and a gateway that lists a key in capabilities MAY omit its declaration.

  • An in.bacp.* entry is {version, extends}: the capability's own date and the capability or capabilities that it extends (in.bacp.discounts extends in.bacp.checkout, as the table above says). The key MUST be a capability id of the table above; an id such as in.bacp.emi that BACP does not define is invalid.
  • A third-party entry, for a capability that a bank or a distributor defines, is {version, extends, registry_ref, schema_digest}. registry_ref names the entry of the extension registry, and schema_digest is the digest of the schema that the registry pins for it. The entry has no schema URL: a gateway never fetches an extension's schema at run time, because a fetched schema is a way into the money path for whoever controls the URL. A third-party key is a reverse-DNS id under a domain that its operator controls, never an in.* id.
  • Gated. A third-party entry activates only once a review process for the extension registry exists (Q-94). Until then only in.bacp.* entries are valid, a third-party entry is not activated, and any ext member of a request is refused with capability_unsupported.
  • A third-party payload travels in the ext member of a session, under the capability's key. It is closed by the schema that the declaration pins, and it is present in an MCP inputSchema only while the capability is active. An ext member that touches an amount, the payee, presence, a mandate or a disclosure is critical: the gateway refuses it unless its capability is listed and the amount also appears as a line of the base totals, and it is never a mandate constraint (Extensibility).

Negotiation, RFQs and auctions are advertised through the negotiation field rather than a capability id. Handler listing and intersection are advertised through payment_handlers_registry.

Conformance levels (see Conformance) are the testable counterpart of capabilities: a gateway that claims a level MUST support every capability that level exercises.

docs.title: Negotiation capability
docs.text:
Negotiation features are agreed by intersecting two adverts, each shaped as negotiation-session.json#/$defs/Capability:

  • the gateway (BAP side) declares its advert in the profile's negotiation field;
  • each seller (BPP) advertises bacp.negotiation as a provider tag in its Beckn on_search response.
Advert field Meaning negotiable_issues[] JSON Pointers into the term sheet that may be negotiated, for example /lines/*/unit_price or /payment/credit_days. modes[] Negotiation modes supported, for example fixed, alternating, rfq_sealed, reverse_l1. max_rounds Maximum number of rounds. round_timeout Maximum time for one round. min_offer_validity Shortest validity an offer may have. sig_algs Signature algorithms accepted for negotiation messages. firm_quote_supported Whether the participant issues firm (binding) quotes. accepted_handlers[] Payment handlers the seller accepts; feeds the handler intersection. pricing_ai_vendor Who supplies the participant's automated pricing, if anyone.

Rules:

  1. A negotiation session MUST use the intersection of the two adverts.
  2. Any term-sheet issue that is not in the intersected negotiable_issues is fixed. A counter-offer that changes a fixed issue is refused with NEG_ISSUE_NOT_NEGOTIABLE.
  3. If no max_rounds is agreed, the default is 10 for consumer sessions and 30 for business sessions.
  4. min_offer_validity is at least PT5M in every profile. A counterparty's advert cannot lower this floor.
  5. If the mode intersection is empty, POST /negotiations returns 201 with the message capabilities_incompatible (requires_buyer_input), and the agent falls back to mode fixed, an ordinary catalogue checkout.

See Negotiation.

docs.title: Payment handlers in the profile
docs.text:
payment_handlers lists the handlers the gateway can process. Each entry is a handler reference: a canonical id such as in.upi.reservepay, or an alias accepted during its deprecation window, such as upi.reservepay.block.

  • A gateway MUST emit canonical ids in new profiles. Consumers MUST accept any handler reference and MUST compare handlers only after resolving them in the handler registry.
  • A reference that does not resolve MUST be treated as not supported.
  • Listing a handler does not make it usable for every payment. Which handlers can pay for a given deal is decided by the handler intersection: the registry (live handlers, and pilot handlers only if the gateway's conformance attestation lists them), ∩ the gateway profile's payment_handlers, ∩ the seller's accepted handlers, ∩ the term sheet's payment options, ∩ the handlers the mandates allow, ∩ the handlers eligible at the session's presence, ∩ the amount limits, ∩ the instruments the Trusted Surface reports as available. The result is ordered by the principal's own preference, then the lowest all-in total, then the least authentication friction. It is never ordered by platform incentives.
  • An empty intersection gives 200 with handlers_incompatible (requires_buyer_input).

GET /payment-handlers (public, unsigned, cacheable with ETag) returns the registry as handler descriptors. The response MUST carry a Cache-Control header with a max-age of at most 86400 (for example Cache-Control: max-age=86400), so that no cache holds a copy for more than 24 hours. Because the response is unsigned, a Mandate Manager or gateway MUST NOT use it as its registry source for open-mandate eligibility (Handler binding). POST /payment-handlers/intersect computes an intersection. The intersect request carries a negotiation_id or, on a gateway that lists in.bacp.payment_plan, a session_id alone (Q-45, settled); any other gateway requires the negotiation_id. Details are on Handler Registry.

docs.title: Registry lookup
docs.text:
The gateway relies on the network registry (the ONDC registry, or another accredited registry) for every key and status it trusts. It uses the registry to:

Lookup Used for AgentCredential issuer keys and status list Verifying each agent's credential and that it is not revoked (Identity and Request Signing) BPP subscriber keys Verifying the network signatures on on_* callbacks, quotes and negotiation messages BPP subscriber keys (agent) An agent verifying the on_search sources of presented discovery results (Verifying discovery results) Mandate Manager and PSP keys Verifying mandates, rail-binding attestations, receipts and Trusted Surface events Trusted Surface origins, notify endpoint and languages of a Mandate Manager or PSP Minting trusted_surface_url only on an origin of the step-up's signer, sending the content-free app_push, and refusing to offer a language the signer does not claim (Origins and delivery) support_operator keys Accepting a handoff only from a key whose record names its agent operator and one person (Human handoff) Regulatory status (regulatory_status) Checking, before money moves, that the party in collected_by has a verified rbi_pa or bank entry, so that it is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank Operator (operator) Checking that two participants are not the same operator, for the separation rules of conformance attestations and of discovery lookups Conformance attestations Checking which conformance levels a counterparty has passed

Rules:

  1. The gateway MUST resolve keys by key id from the registry. Key ids are registry-resolvable, for example bap.example.in|ukid-7|ed25519 (subscriber id, unique key id, algorithm) or a did:web URL with a fragment.
  2. The gateway MAY cache a registry record until the record's own validity ends, and MUST NOT use it after that.
  3. A key that the registry does not know, or a credential that its status list marks revoked, MUST be rejected (agent_unregistered, agent_credential_revoked).
  4. A BACP-aware BPP resolves the BAP's keys, and the keys of the buyer's credential provider, through the same registry.
  5. An agent that verifies a discovery source MUST resolve the BPP's key from the network registry's own endpoint, or through a lookup service whose operator is neither the gateway's operator nor shares an operator with the gateway's BAP. An agent operator that also operates, or shares an operator with, the gateway's BAP MUST use the network registry's own endpoint. Operators are compared as in Conformance attestation: by the operator of the registry record with assertion: registry, never by a profile or a response that the gateway supplies, and an operator that is not asserted by the registry is unknown, which means the agent uses the network registry's own endpoint. The agent MUST NOT use a key, a registry record or a lookup response that the gateway supplies. The agent records the lookup source in the discover InstructionLog entry.

Registry record. The part of a registry record that BACP reads is the schema registry-record.json: subscriber_id, bacp_role (the Signature.role value), keys[], valid_from, valid_until and status; for a Mandate Manager or a PSP, ts_origins[], ts_notify_url, ts_call_numbers[], ts_languages[] and ts_modalities[]; and for a support_operator, operator_id and person_ref, with exactly one key. Any record may also carry the legal operator (legal_name, entity_ids[], assertion and an optional group_id), regulatory_status[] (each entry a dated, sourced statement with regime, verified_on and status of verified or declared) and a data_residency statement. assertion: registry means that the network registry's own lookup response carries the operator, which is the only form a separation check relies on; a declared or absent operator is unknown, and an unknown operator fails closed. A declared regulatory status is never treated as verified. A record whose regulatory_status has an rbi_pa or rbi_ppi entry has a company: its entity_ids[] contain a 21-character CIN. A registry may carry more fields, and a reader ignores any it does not know. Whether the ONDC network registry can carry bacp_role, operator_id, person_ref and the Trusted Surface fields is not settled (a question for ONDC). Where it cannot, BACP needs a side registry, which is a second trust root that this version does not define.

Which body anchors agent identity and issues AgentCredentials (an NPCI agent registry, the ONDC registry, or decentralised identifiers) is open (Q-02). BACP is issuer-agnostic: any accredited issuer whose keys the registry publishes can issue AgentCredentials.

docs.title: Network discovery
docs.text:
POST /discover searches the network on the agent's behalf. Capability in.bacp.discover; signature tag bacp-browse; Idempotency-Key REQUIRED.

Request fields:

Field Meaning query What to find, as a multilingual map, for example {"hi-IN": "एक लीटर दूध"}. REQUIRED. category An ONDC domain or category code, for example ONDC:RET10. delivery Delivery pincode or gps. mandate_ref An open Checkout Mandate. When present, each result is flagged within_mandate. max_wait_ms How long to collect on_search callbacks.

What the gateway does on the network:

  1. It verifies the agent's signature and credential.
  2. It sends a Beckn search through the Beckn gateway with context.bacp (agent, presence, idempotency key, and the mandate reference when given). Network participants that do not speak BACP ignore context.bacp.
  3. It collects on_search callbacks until max_wait_ms, verifies each seller's network signature against the registry, and drops callbacks it cannot verify. It keeps every callback it accepts, with its Authorization header, exactly as received (Retention of the signed callbacks).
  4. It returns the aggregated results: one entry per on_search callback, each with bpp_id, provider, items and a source_digest (the sha-256 of the raw BPP-signed on_search body that every item of the entry came from; a gateway that merges items from several callbacks of one provider returns one entry per callback), plus within_mandate when a mandate was given. Every item carries its own sponsorship, and mrp, tax_inclusive and prior_price where the seller sent them (Catalogue disclosures). A result also carries the seller's published offers[], where it sent any (Discounts). complete: false means some sellers had not answered in time.
  5. It returns ranking: the main parameters used to order results, in descending order of importance (for example distance, price and seller rating), an optional description_url, and sponsored, which is true if and only if at least one item is sponsored.

Catalogue text, including product names and descriptions, is untrusted input. Agents MUST treat it as data and never as instructions.

docs.title: Ranking by payment rungs
docs.text:
The gateway's default discovery ranking MUST NOT use any of these as a parameter:

  • the handler rungs a seller offers, or whether it offers a human-not-present (HNP) rung;
  • the seller's merchant discount rate, or its small-merchant (P2PM) category;
  • Verified Merchant status;
  • the level or acceptance of a finder fee.

The one exception is a finder fee that is paid to the operator for an item's prominence or selection: the agent then renders that item as sponsored with by: agent under Declaring the status, rule 7.

  • A seller without an HNP rung is never dropped. Its result carries needs_principal_factor: true, which tells the agent that the principal must pay that seller herself, and keeps its rank.
  • A principal's own filter ("only shops I can pay without a PIN") is allowed. The gateway logs it, and it never becomes a default for a later session.
  • This is BACP policy. BACP does not cite the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 r.5(3)(f) as the source of a prohibition. The rule extends the handler-order rule. It also reflects NPCI OC 228, which enables Reserve Pay at first "only for online verified merchants with low ticket and high frequency transactions": a seller without that rung has done nothing wrong, and ranking would otherwise penalise the small shop first.

docs.title: Seller confirmation profile
docs.text:
A seller MAY declare requires_principal_confirmation on its discover result: {reason, above_amount?}, where reason is made_to_order, age_restricted or high_value_cod. above_amount (an Amount) is REQUIRED for high_value_cod and absent for the other reasons. On Beckn the declaration travels in the bacp.confirmation tag group of the signed on_search (mapping).

  • For an order the declaration covers, the gateway raises a confirm step-up with reason constraint_unresolved (Step-up) before any money moves. It counts as a step-up like any other for any limit the specification sets on step-ups.
  • The declaration MUST NOT change a price or a handler. It is a prompt to the human, not a pricing lever.
  • A confirmation that the seller asks for at on_init without having declared it is treated like drip pricing: the same confirm step-up, reason constraint_unresolved. A seller that asks through the BPP-signed tag seller_confirmation in on_select or on_init gets a confirm step-up with reason seller_confirmation and a template sentence for the value (Seller refusals and substitution).
  • The gateway logs, for each seller, how often a declared or an undeclared confirmation is raised.

The response's transaction_id is the Beckn transaction id; the agent passes it to POST /sessions. The gateway MUST sign the response (Response signature). See Sessions and Checkout and Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: Verifying discovery results
docs.text:
A discover response is the gateway's own message. The seller's values in it (unit_price, mrp, tax_inclusive, prior_price and the seller's sponsorship) reach the agent through the gateway, so an agent that shows or relies on one of them checks it against the seller's signed callback, which the gateway serves by source_digest.

Fetching a source. GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest} (capability in.bacp.discover; RFC 9421 request signature under tag bacp-browse; no Idempotency-Key, because it is a read) returns 200 with a BecknSignedMessage: the on_search body exactly as the gateway received it, and its Beckn Authorization header.

  • The gateway serves a source only to the agent whose POST /discover produced the transaction_id. Every other caller, and an unknown digest, gets 404 not_found.
  • The gateway counts the rate limit per caller key before it looks up the transaction_id or the source_digest, so that a 429 quota_exceeded never depends on whether the source exists.
  • The gateway MUST serve a source for as long as it must keep it (Retention).
  • source_digest is sha-256 only, in the form sha-256:<base64url>, computed over the exact bytes of body as UTF-8 text. Every item of a results[] entry MUST come from the one callback that its source_digest names.

What the agent MUST verify. For each result whose items the agent presents (shows or reads to a principal) or relies on (selects, sorts or compares by prior_price, mrp or an offer figure), the agent MUST run the steps below. It runs them once for each distinct source_digest, and MAY cache the outcome by digest.

  1. Fetch the source, or reuse a cached copy. The sha-256 of body MUST equal source_digest.
  2. Parse body as JSON. A body with a duplicate member name, or one that exceeds the agent's size or nesting limits (measured on the decoded body), is unverified. RFC 8259 §4 says member names SHOULD be unique, and a duplicate lets two parsers read different values. BACP states no numeric limit.
  3. Check the binding to this search:
    • context.action is on_search;
    • context.bpp_id equals the result's bpp_id and the subscriber id in the keyId of the Authorization header;
    • context.bap_id equals the bap_id of the gateway's profile;
    • context.transaction_id equals the response's transaction_id;
    • context.message_id equals UUIDv5(message_id_namespace, agent_id | Idempotency-Key | "search"), with the namespace from the gateway's profile (Message ids);
    • created in the Authorization header is not earlier than 300 seconds before the agent sent the POST /discover;
    • the agent SHOULD also compare context.city (or context.location), where the network carries it, with the delivery area it requested; a difference is a mismatch.

Because the agent chooses the Idempotency-Key of the search and never reuses it (Idempotency), this binding stops a gateway from replaying a genuine signed callback from an earlier search. BACP adds no weaker freshness binding: a gateway that answers from a cached catalogue cannot meet it, and every claim in its results is unverified. A gateway that wants verified claims sends a targeted live search to the shortlisted sellers with the agent's message_id. 4. Resolve the BPP's key as the registry lookup rule 5 requires, never from the gateway. The key MUST be listed with registry role BPP and MUST be valid both at the created time of the signature and at the time of verification. An unknown, revoked, expired or wrong-role key leaves the source unverified. 5. Verify the Beckn signature over the body: Ed25519 over (created), (expires) and the BLAKE2b-512 digest (Signing). The agent does not compare expires with the current time, because the callback is a stored artefact; freshness comes from step 3. 6. Locate the provider and item in message.catalog and derive the values by the normative mapping. Compare them with the result.

Each item ends in one of three outcomes: verified; mismatch (steps 1 to 5 pass but a value differs); or unverified (any step fails, or the item is not in the body). A claim that the body carries and the result leaves out (for example a prior_price the gateway dropped and flagged prior_price_invalid) is not a mismatch: the agent makes no claim.

Outcome prior_price, mrp, offer figures Sponsorship unit_price Record verified Rendered per Disclosure phrases As returned As returned unverified MUST NOT be rendered or relied on: no claim sponsored (with the result's by) if the result says sponsored; otherwise rendered as undeclared, never as not_sponsored MAY be shown as the price, never as half of a reduction pair InstructionLog stage discover, reason discovery_source_unverified mismatch MUST NOT render the result's value; MAY render the value derived from the verified body The higher of the result's and the body's, by the precedence sponsored, undeclared, not_sponsored The body's value Reason discovery_source_mismatch; the agent SHOULD report it to its operator's grievance contact

The values that can make a principal pay are the reduction claim and the MRP anchor, so these fail closed. Sponsorship fails towards more disclosure, so a gateway gains nothing by breaking verification. An agent that presents nothing and relies on no claim, such as an agent in a human-not-present flow that buys by unit_price alone, has no duty to fetch a source. An agent that chooses between results by comparing unit_price MUST either verify those results by the steps above or, before complete, compare the chosen item's BPP-signed quote unit price with the discovered one. If the quote is higher, the choice no longer stands, and the agent re-ranks on quoted prices or escalates to the principal.

At checkout. When a session returns Disclosures.catalogue[], an agent that verified or presented the items MUST check each entry against the values it presented for that item at discovery. The agent MUST also check that every line item it chose from a discover response has exactly one catalogue[] entry with that item_id. A missing entry is a mismatch. The entry's source_digest MUST be one the agent checked for that item, its sponsorship.status MUST NOT be weaker than the presented value (by the precedence sponsored, undeclared, not_sponsored) and its sponsorship.by[] MUST contain every party of the sponsorship.by[] the agent presented, and its prior_price, mrp and discovered_unit_price MUST equal the presented values. Otherwise the agent records discovery_source_mismatch and treats the session as requires_buyer_review. This closes the gap in which a gateway swaps in a different genuine callback at checkout.

The agent records, in the InstructionLog entry at stage discover, the digest of every source it checked, the outcome of each, the Idempotency-Key of the search and the host of the registry lookup it used (Instruction log).

Cost to agents (informative). The work per distinct callback is one sha-256, one BLAKE2b-512 and one Ed25519 verification, which is small (analysis, not measured). An agent fetches one source for each distinct callback among the results it presents, in parallel. The size of an on_search body is not measured (not verified as of 18-10-2026), so an agent MAY cap the decoded size it accepts and treat a larger body as unverified. The real cost is registry access: ONDC's recommended lookup takes an Authorization header signed by a subscriber key, and the unsigned lookups are marked deprecated (reported by ONDC's developer documentation, not verified as of 18-10-2026), so an agent operator that is not an ONDC subscriber needs its own subscription or a lookup service it trusts that the gateway does not run (Q-70). If that is impractical, every presented item degrades to undeclared with no claim, which is safe.

docs.title: Response signature
docs.text: The gateway MUST sign the POST /discover response with RFC 9421, covering @status and content-digest (Content-Digest), under a key published in its profile's keys, the key it uses for webhooks. The response MUST carry Content-Digest, Signature-Input and Signature headers. This makes the values that only the gateway asserts (by: gateway, not_sponsored for its own ranking, and ranking) non-repudiable, also for an item that was shown but not bought. An agent MAY verify the signature, and SHOULD keep the signed response with the InstructionLog entry of the search.

docs.title: Catalogue disclosures
docs.text:
Every item in a discover response carries the data that an e-commerce entity needs to tell a buyer whether a result is a sponsored listing, what the seller's lowest recent price was, and what the printed maximum retail price is. BACP carries that data. Whether an agent operator or a gateway is itself an "e-commerce entity" under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, as amended by the Amendment Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027), is a question for counsel, and it is open (Q-66). The rules below bind BACP participants whichever way it is answered.

Item field Required Meaning sponsorship REQUIRED {status, by[]}. status is sponsored, not_sponsored or undeclared. by[] lists who sold the placement and is REQUIRED when status is sponsored and absent otherwise. mrp OPTIONAL The Legal Metrology retail sale price, inclusive of all taxes, as an Amount in integer paise. It maps from Beckn price.maximum_value. tax_inclusive REQUIRED whenever mrp or prior_price is present Whether unit_price and prior_price include all taxes. prior_price OPTIONAL {amount, basis, announced_on}: the lowest price of the item in the 30 days before announced_on, asserted by the seller (BPP). basis has one value, lowest_30d. Its presence is the claim that the seller announced a price reduction on announced_on. measure RECOMMENDED The item's sale measure, a QuantityUnit (Units). policies[] OPTIONAL Typed policies {type, allowed, window, applies_to[], description, url}, with type one of in.bacp.policy.return, in.bacp.policy.cancel and in.bacp.policy.cod (Typed policies). min_order RECOMMENDED {value, item_qty} on the item or its provider: the smallest basket total or item quantity that the seller accepts.

Sponsored. An item is sponsored when its position or selection was affected by payment, including through a ranking parameter that a party can buy. This is BACP policy. It is not a statutory definition.

Declaring the status.

  1. A gateway MUST return sponsorship on every item. An agent that receives an item with no sponsorship (from an older or non-conforming gateway) MUST treat it as undeclared.
  2. The party that orders the results MUST declare sponsored or not_sponsored for its own ranking. undeclared arises only when that order relays an upstream promotion or ordering signal whose paid status the ranking party does not know and did not price.
  3. by[] is the party that sold the placement and asserts it: bpp (the seller app), gateway (the buyer app's gateway) or agent (the agent operator). It is an array because several parties can sell placement for one item. A reader MUST render an unknown by value as "sponsored, party unknown".
  4. When a placement is sold for a provider (a "featured store"), every item of that provider in the response is sponsored, and by[] names the party that sold the placement.
  5. Monotone OR. The precedence is sponsored, then undeclared, then not_sponsored. No party lowers a value that an upstream party set, and by[] is the union of the parties that sold placement. A seller that sends bacp.disclosure with sponsored set to "true" makes the item sponsored with bpp in by[].
  6. ranking.sponsored is true if and only if some item is sponsored. The schema enforces both directions.
  7. An agent whose operator is paid for an item's prominence or selection MUST render that item as sponsored with by: agent, whatever the gateway returned.

Prior price, MRP and the price figures.

  1. Only the BPP asserts prior_price. The gateway MUST relay prior_price, mrp, tax_inclusive and the BPP's sponsorship unaltered. It MUST NOT synthesise a prior_price, and MUST NOT derive one from Beckn listed_value, offered_value or maximum_value.
  2. The gateway drops a prior_price whose amount is not above the item's unit_price, or is above mrp while tax_inclusive is true, and reports prior_price_invalid (warning, recoverable) at $.results[n].items[m].prior_price.
  3. When tax_inclusive is true and unit_price is above mrp, the gateway reports NEG_MRP_EXCEEDED at $.results[n].items[m].unit_price. A comparison with mrp runs only when tax_inclusive is true.
  4. A gateway MAY check a prior_price against prices it has itself seen for the same key: bpp_id, provider, item and the area_code of the search. If it saw a lower price in the 30 days before announced_on, it reports prior_price_contradicted (warning, advisory, recoverable) at $.results[n].items[m].prior_price and relays the value unaltered. The flag is advisory.
  5. The gateway's default ranking MUST NOT use the size of a discount. When the principal asks to sort by discount, the gateway MAY use it, computed from prior_price only, and MUST list it in ranking.main_parameters.
  6. A B2B profile is not exempt from these fields. An agent MUST NOT block a quote that carries a PTR-plus-scheme price for want of a prior_price. Schemes stay in TermSheet scheme mode (Negotiation).

What an agent that presents results MUST do. An agent presents a result when it shows or reads it to a principal.

  1. It renders each item's sponsorship with the fixed phrases of Disclosure phrases: the sponsored sentence with the party for sponsored, and the undeclared sentence for undeclared. It never renders undeclared as "not sponsored". For not_sponsored it says nothing. On audio, the label is spoken before the item. A paraphrase is non-conformant.
  2. It shows or voices a reduction only as the amount pair of prior_price ("Now ₹549. The seller's lowest price in the 30 days before this offer: ₹599"), before any percentage, and never measured from mrp.
  3. It MUST NOT show or voice a reduced price, a strike-through, a "was" or "off" claim or a percentage for an item that has no prior_price, whatever produced the reduction. It never shows mrp as a "was" price or strikes it through.
  4. It MUST NOT show or voice a price figure, percentage, "was" or "off" claim taken from catalogue free text, such as an item name or description.
  5. It SHOULD NOT voice the reduction claim of an item whose prior_price the gateway flagged prior_price_contradicted. This is a SHOULD because the rate of false flags has not been measured.
  6. For a principal that is not present (HNP), it SHOULD NOT weight sponsored items in selection unless the principal asked for that. This is guidance, and not a mandate constraint, because an unknown constraint fails closed.

After a session is created for items from a discover response, the gateway copies each such item's discovered values into Disclosures.catalogue[] (Sessions and Checkout).

docs.title: Typed policies and minimum order
docs.text:
The typed policies are a projection of tags that ONDC sellers already send, so that an agent can read a return window without parsing prose. The binding text is still the disclosure.

  1. Projection. The gateway projects returnable and return_window to in.bacp.policy.return (allowed, window), cancellable to in.bacp.policy.cancel and available_on_cod to in.bacp.policy.cod. It projects time_to_ship to the tat of the session's fulfilment option (Fulfilment options), not to a policy. description and url are counterparty text.
  2. Hashed. The session's typed policies are hashed into disclosures.hash with the rest of the disclosures, so that an approval covers them.
  3. Checked against the text. The gateway compares each typed value with the binding return_terms and cancellation_terms. A typed value that contradicts the binding text raises the warning policy_text_mismatch (requires_buyer_review) and the session moves to requires_escalation with a confirm step-up, so that the session never reaches ready_for_complete on a typed value that the text denies.
  4. What the agent says. The agent speaks the binding text, or a typed value only where the gateway has checked it against that text. A policy that the seller does not state is spoken as "not stated" (policy_not_stated, Disclosure phrases), never as "no returns".
  5. Minimum order. A session whose basket is below the min_order of its provider or of one of its items is refused with 400 invalid_request at $.items, never silently dropped or padded. min_order is a SHOULD for a seller that sets one.

docs.title: Retention of the signed callbacks
docs.text: The gateway MUST keep every on_search callback behind a source_digest it returned, as received, for as long as it keeps the session's evidence (Retention). The evidence bundle carries the callbacks for every item in the session's Disclosures.catalogue[] (Bundle contents).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
BACP reports problems on two channels, following the ACP error model. A request that the gateway could not accept fails with an HTTP error status and a flat Error object. A request that the gateway accepted, but whose business outcome the agent must act on, succeeds (200 or 201, or 202 where the operation is accepted asynchronously) with the full authoritative state and a messages[] array. This page defines both shapes, the resolution vocabulary that tells an agent what it may do next, and the registry of every code a conforming participant may emit.

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. Codes are stable identifiers. A participant MUST NOT emit a code that is not registered on this page.

docs.title: Two channels
docs.text:
Channel When HTTP status Body Protocol failure The request was malformed, unauthenticated, unauthorised, refused by the deterministic mandate verifier, or could not reach the seller. 4xx or 5xx One flat Error object Business outcome The request was processed and the resource has a new authoritative state, but the agent must take note, ask the principal, or wait. 200 or 201; 202 for asynchronous operations (POST /mandates, return requests, Trusted Surface events) The full resource (session, order, negotiation, …) with messages[]

Rules:

  1. A gateway MUST return protocol failures as 4xx or 5xx with a flat Error. It MUST NOT wrap them in a 200.
  2. A gateway MUST return business outcomes as 200, 201 or (for asynchronous operations) 202 with the full resource state and messages[]. The agent MUST treat the returned state as authoritative and MUST NOT reconstruct state from earlier responses.
  3. Step-up is never only an error. When a human must approve, the resource moves to status: requires_escalation, carries a step_up object, and carries the message step_up_required with resolution: requires_buyer_review. See Mandates and Consent and Sessions and Checkout.
  4. param is an RFC 9535 JSONPath into the request (for an Error) or into the returned resource (for a message), for example $.mandate_ref or $.payment.scheduled_debit_at. Header problems use $.headers.<Name>.

docs.title: Dual-channel codes
docs.text:
Some validator and guard codes can appear on either channel. The rule is:

  • the code is a 200 message when it describes an incoming counterparty object or a computed outcome (a handler intersection, a seller's offer);
  • the code is a 403 error when it blocks the caller's own outgoing commitment (a firm COUNTER, an ACCEPT, a bid, an award, a session update or complete).

For example, handlers_incompatible is a 200 message on POST /payment-handlers/intersect and a 403 error on an ACCEPT whose agreed payment option has no eligible handler. Registry rows marked "200 msg / 403" follow this rule.

A code that also appears as a 200 error message on a session cancelled by a mandate event (mandate_expired, mandate_revoked, mandate_paused, rail_binding_not_open_eligible) mirrors that code's error status: the message reports the same condition that complete would return as an error.

docs.title: The Error object
docs.text:
Field Type Required Meaning type enum yes Error class: invalid_request, authentication_error, authorization_error, mandate_error, payment_error, upstream_error, service_unavailable code string yes A code from the registry message string yes Human-readable explanation for logs and developers. Agents MUST NOT present it to the principal as a legal notice. param string no RFC 9535 JSONPath to the offending field resolution enum no How the agent should proceed; one of the resolution values. Gateways SHOULD send it. reasons array of string conditional Every local and rail reason that applied. REQUIRED on rail-cap and step-up errors. step_up_kind enum conditional confirm or rail_auth. REQUIRED on step-up errors. supported_versions array of string conditional The versions that the gateway lists. REQUIRED on version_unsupported and absent on every other code. capability string conditional The capability id that owns the refused member. REQUIRED on capability_unsupported and absent on every other code. reason enum conditional no_conforming_origin, language_unavailable or channel_not_allowed. REQUIRED on trusted_surface_unavailable and absent on every other code. Not to be confused with reasons. seller_reason object conditional On bpp_nack only: {code, beckn_code}, the reason the seller refused. code is item_unavailable, quantity_reduced, price_changed, not_serviceable, store_closed, agent_orders_not_accepted, terms_mismatch or other. The gateway sets it only from the BPP-signed NACK, and an unmapped Beckn code gives other. Which ONDC code maps to which value is for ONDC to answer. handoff_routes array of HandoffRoute conditional On trusted_surface_unavailable with reason language_unavailable or channel_not_allowed: the session's ai_disclosure.handoff_routes, so that the agent can offer the principal a human. Absent when the session lists none. step_up object conditional On 403 presence_not_proven for a post-order write without hp_proof: a StepUp of kind post_order (reason presence_proof) that the principal confirms on the Trusted Surface to obtain the proof (Presence proof).

Rail-cap and step-up errors MUST also carry reasons[] (every local and rail reason that applied) and step_up_kind. idempotency_in_flight and quota_exceeded MUST be sent with a Retry-After header.

{
  "type": "mandate_error",
  "code": "mandate_revoked",
  "message": "Mandate mdt_PAY7Q2W9X4K1M3 is REVOKED",
  "param": "$.mandate_ref"
}

docs.title: The Message object
Resolution
docs.text:
Every Error code and every message has exactly one resolution. On a seller-side gateway a code whose registry resolution is requires_buyer_review is emitted with requires_seller_review, because the principal who reviews is the seller's. The one exception is rail_binding_not_open_eligible, whose registry row gives a resolution per cause; the Error.resolution field then carries the one that applies:

Value Meaning for the agent recoverable The agent may fix the request itself (re-select, wait, GET and retry with the same key) without involving the principal. requires_buyer_input The agent must ask the principal for something new: set up or renew a mandate, choose another payment method, supply missing data. requires_buyer_review A human must review and approve on the Trusted Surface (step-up, disclosure review, out-of-scope action). The agent MUST NOT approve on the principal's behalf. requires_seller_review The same, for the seller principal: a message that a seller-side gateway emits and that its principal reviews, in the seller application or on the seller's Trusted Surface. The agent MUST NOT approve on the seller principal's behalf. A buyer-side gateway never emits it. unrecoverable The request cannot succeed as sent. The agent must not retry it; an operator may need to act.

"Informational" is not a resolution value. Purely informational messages use type: info with resolution: recoverable.

docs.title: Client behaviour
docs.text:
• An agent that meets a code it does not know MUST act on the HTTP status class (and, for messages, on resolution). It MUST NOT retry a 4xx with a new Idempotency-Key: a new key is a new purchase intent and is evaluated against the mandate afresh.
  • After a 5xx, a timeout or a lost response, the agent MUST first GET the resource and MAY then retry only with the same Idempotency-Key (see REST binding).
  • On payment_in_doubt the agent MUST NOT re-key. The gateway reconciles with the PSP and reports the outcome.
  • A new code MUST be registered here, with its HTTP status and resolution, before any participant emits it.
  • A conformance run fails on any unregistered code (see Conformance).

docs.title: Registry
docs.text: "200 msg" means the code arrives in messages[] on a 200 or 201 response. "200 + step_up" means the resource moves to requires_escalation with a step_up object. A dash in the Typical param column means no single field applies.

docs.title: Transport, identity and idempotency
docs.text: Code HTTP type Meaning Typical param Resolution invalid_request 400 invalid_request Generic schema or parse failure. Also returned when an order-scoped request is ambiguous because the agent holds the same order id from two sellers and did not name the seller, and when a session's basket_id is already used by sessions of another principal, presence or root open Checkout Mandate. Also returned when BACP-Version is missing and the profile lists more than one version (at $.headers.BACP-Version), when a quantity is not a multiple of the item's increment (at $.items[n].quantity), when fulfilment.option_id names an option that the session did not offer (at $.fulfilment.option_id), and when a basket is below a min_order (at $.items). the offending field; $.bpp_id for an ambiguous order; $.basket_id recoverable version_unsupported 400 invalid_request The request names, in BACP-Version, a version that the gateway's profile does not list. The error carries supported_versions[]. A request that omits a header that is REQUIRED because the profile lists more than one version is not this code: it is invalid_request at $.headers.BACP-Version. $.headers.BACP-Version; supported_versions carries the listed versions recoverable (choose a listed version) version_mismatch 409 invalid_request A request for a session names a version other than the one the session was created under. Nothing changes. $.headers.BACP-Version recoverable (name the session's version, or create a new session) capability_unsupported 400 invalid_request A request carries a member that a capability owns, and the gateway's version defines that capability but the gateway does not list it (for example discounts without in.bacp.discounts, payment_plan or a session_id on POST /payment-handlers/intersect without in.bacp.payment_plan, or a UCP buyer.consent, loyalty or cart_id member on the UCP projection). Nothing is created or changed. The content of an MCP result is the fixed capability_absent sentence (Disclosure phrases). It is not the discount_code_unsupported warning, which is a listed capability whose seller declines. the member path, for example $.discounts; capability carries the capability id unrecoverable idempotency_key_required 400 invalid_request Idempotency-Key is missing on a POST or PUT, or is not 22–64 printable ASCII characters. $.headers.Idempotency-Key recoverable idempotency_conflict 422 invalid_request The same key was reused with a different request body. A retry that adds hp_proof to a refused 403 presence_not_proven write is such a case; its message names a new key. $.headers.Idempotency-Key unrecoverable (a new key only for a new intent), or recoverable when the only change is hp_proof (retry with a new key) idempotency_in_flight 409 + Retry-After invalid_request A request with the same key is still being processed. — recoverable (retry with the same key) idempotency_store_unavailable 503 service_unavailable The idempotency store is unreachable; writes fail closed. — recoverable request_too_large 413 invalid_request The request body exceeds the gateway's limit (at most 256 KiB). Checked on raw bytes before signature verification. — unrecoverable quota_exceeded 429 + Retry-After invalid_request The agent has too many live idempotency keys or too many requests in flight, or the caller exceeded a rate limit: render fetches per Mandate Manager or PSP key, counted before the lookup, and per key and step-up after the standing check, or post_order step-ups created per (agent, principal) and per order. Retry-After is REQUIRED. The figures are the gateway's own, published in its profile (Limits on step-ups). — recoverable signature_invalid 401 authentication_error The RFC 9421 signature does not verify, lacks a required covered component, is outside its time window, or uses a tag that the endpoint or the credential's purposes does not allow. Also a handoff accept or release signed by a key whose registry role is not support_operator. $.headers.Signature-Input unrecoverable replay_detected 401 authentication_error The (keyid, nonce) pair was already seen within the signature window. $.headers.Signature-Input unrecoverable agent_unregistered 401 authentication_error The signing key or the AgentCredential does not resolve in the registry. — unrecoverable agent_credential_revoked 401 authentication_error The AgentCredential is revoked on its status list. — unrecoverable trusted_surface_only 403 authorization_error The caller is an agent, not a registered Mandate Manager or payer PSP, so it may not post Trusted Surface events or fetch a step-up's ts_render. A Mandate Manager or PSP that is not the step-up's (Step-up signers) gets 404 not_found instead. Also returned for a MandateRequest that an agent or a gateway submits with supersedes: only the principal, on the Trusted Surface, ports a mandate (Porting a mandate). — unrecoverable trusted_surface_unavailable 503 service_unavailable No Trusted Surface can take the step-up, and the gateway sent nothing that carries it to the principal. reason is no_conforming_origin (the signer has no registered origin the gateway may use and no ts_notify_url), language_unavailable (no Trusted Surface of the signer renders the step-up's language) or channel_not_allowed (the only channels that the mandate's confirmation floor allows are unavailable). With the last two the error carries handoff_routes[]. It is never recoverable: a bare 503 reads as "retry", and a retry cannot succeed until the signer registers an origin or a notify endpoint, or the principal chooses a route (Origins and delivery). — requires_buyer_input ts_render_mismatch 403 authorization_error A Trusted Surface approval's presentation.content_hash is not the sha-256 of the step-up's gateway-signed ts_render; or, for a negotiation step-up, presentation.offer_hash, the ts_render's offer_hash and the offer the step-up names differ, or the ts_render's acceptance_revocation differs from the signed offer's value. The event is refused and the session does not change. Returned to the Mandate Manager or PSP that posted it. $.presentation.content_hash, $.presentation.offer_hash unrecoverable not_found 404 invalid_request The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller, including a step-up or session that belongs to another Mandate Manager's or PSP's mandate, and a handoff accept or release signed by a support_operator key of another agent operator than the session's. the path parameter unrecoverable session_state_conflict 409 invalid_request The operation is not allowed in the resource's current state, including an agent PUT or complete on a session in human_handoff, and a handoff accept after the handoff ended (handoff.ended_at set). Also, at $.handoff.accepted_by: a handoff accept while accepted_by is set, a release by a key of the same agent operator that is not accepted_by, and an agent release after acceptance. Also a new step-up inside the decline cool-off that follows an explicit step_up.declined, and a replacement past the seller re-prompt cap of an issue, both with no new step-up (Limits on step-ups); the cool-off answer carries Retry-After set to the time left. $.status, $.handoff.accepted_by recoverable (GET, then act on the current state) bpp_timeout 504 upstream_error No on_* callback arrived within the gateway's wait window. The resource remains retrievable. — recoverable (GET, then retry with the same key) bpp_nack 502 upstream_error The seller app NACKed the Beckn request. seller_reason carries the seller's own stated reason, when its BPP-signed NACK has one. recoverable covers only a retry of the same item at a total no higher than the one the principal was shown. A substitute item or seller at a higher total needs the principal's confirmation (Seller refusals and substitution). — recoverable

docs.title: Mandate and verification
docs.text:
Code HTTP type Meaning Typical param Resolution mandate_required 403 mandate_error No mandate is referenced, or the referenced mandate is not yet ACTIVE (PENDING or REJECTED). $.mandate_ref requires_buyer_input mandate_invalid_signature 403 mandate_error A Mandate Manager, principal or agent signature over a mandate (or the closing key-binding JWT) does not verify, for example because the mandate was edited. $.mandates, $.kb_jwt unrecoverable mandate_invalid 403 mandate_error The mandate is malformed in a way the verifier cannot evaluate; the verifier fails closed. $.mandates unrecoverable mandate_schema_invalid 400 invalid_request The mandate fails its schema, for example an open payment mandate without rail_binding. $.mandates unrecoverable rail_binding_not_open_eligible 400 (also a 200 error message on a checkout session cancelled by a binding pause) invalid_request The open payment mandate's rail_binding (or the rail of a mandate request) resolves to a handler that cannot back standing authority: a reserved or deprecated descriptor, a pilot that the gateway's conformance attestation does not list in an unexpired pilots[], a handler that is not open-eligible, or a rail_binding.primitive that is not in the descriptor's binding.open_primitives. Also returned for an open payment mandate issued without rail_binding.primitive or rail_binding.registry_version, for an HNP complete when the gateway's descriptor copy is more than 24 hours old, for an HNP complete on a pilot handler when the mandate's rail_binding.conformance is absent, names another gateway, or names an attestation that is revoked or expired (binding_ineligible) or whose status list is more than 24 hours old or unreachable (attestation_status_stale), at issuance for a conformance attestation that the Mandate Manager does not accept (Conformance attestation), and at issuance for a Reserve Pay block whose payee is the buyer app, whose seller's BPP-signed payment terms the gateway does not hold and does not obtain first, or whose payee VPA is not the VPA in those terms. Evaluated against the current registry at issuance and at every complete. On complete the error carries reasons[] with the cause: binding_ineligible, reissue_required, registry_copy_stale or attestation_status_stale; at issuance it may carry attester_not_accepted (the signer is in the Mandate Manager's published exclusion list) or attester_not_independent (the authority or a funder is the same operator as the gateway, the payer PSP or the Mandate Manager, or an operator is unknown). When several reasons apply, reasons[] is ordered reissue_required, binding_ineligible, registry_copy_stale, attestation_status_stale, and resolution is that of the first. An agent that can disprove reissue_required or binding_ineligible from the mandate it holds treats the claim as a gateway fault and opens no re-issue (Handler binding). The 400 status is deliberate (see the note below this table). $.mandates, $.rail requires_buyer_input at POST /mandates, for reissue_required (have the mandate re-issued on an eligible binding) and for binding_ineligible (offer another payment method; the agent opens no resume or re-issue request without a new principal instruction); recoverable for registry_copy_stale and attestation_status_stale (a gateway or attestation-status condition: retry later, the principal is not asked) constraint_unknown 403 mandate_error The mandate carries a constraint key the verifier does not know. Unknown constraints fail closed. $.proposed_constraints unrecoverable mandate_expired 403 (also a 200 error message on a checkout session cancelled by the expiry) mandate_error The mandate is past valid_until or its rail authority has expired. A post-order write with presence: HP is not refused for this status (Post-order gate); without HP it gets 403 presence_not_allowed. $.mandate_ref requires_buyer_input mandate_revoked 403 (also a 200 message: error on a checkout session cancelled by the revocation, warning on negotiation sessions) mandate_error The mandate was revoked by the principal, by a rail safety switch or by agent relinquishment. A post-order write with presence: HP is not refused for this status (Post-order gate); without HP it gets 403 presence_not_allowed. $.mandate_ref requires_buyer_input mandate_paused 403 (also a 200 error message on a checkout session cancelled by the pause) mandate_error The principal paused the mandate, or the gateway paused it for a debit on its Reserve Pay block that matches no BACP payment (unmatched_rail_debit, removed only by the principal), and only these reasons are in force. While a gateway pause reason (binding_ineligible, reissue_required) is also in force, rail_binding_not_open_eligible is returned instead. A post-order write with presence: HP is not refused for this status (Post-order gate); without HP it gets 403 presence_not_allowed. $.mandate_ref requires_buyer_input mandate_exhausted 403 mandate_error A budget, the rail block or max_executions is used up, counting in-flight reservations and every Reserve Pay block at its full amount. A post-order write with presence: HP is not refused for this status (Post-order gate); without HP it gets 403 presence_not_allowed. At mandate request (and on the activation event of a sibling block) also: a requested Reserve Pay block that, at its full amount, does not fit the remaining headroom of every budget window of its root. $.mandate_ref, $.checkout_mandate_ref requires_buyer_input mandate_scope_mismatch 403 mandate_error The request falls outside the mandate: amount, category, merchant, PIN code, line items, checkout_hash, data shared outside data_scopes, reuse of a closed payment mandate, purpose bounds at mandate request, or a handler that does not resolve. At mandate request also: a Reserve Pay request without payee or without rail_limits.block_amount, a checkout_mandate_ref that names no ACTIVE root open Checkout Mandate of the principal, block amounts under one root (the requested one included) that would exceed its smallest budget max, or a new root open Checkout Mandate for a principal who already holds an ACTIVE root at the same Mandate Manager whose notice does not state every other root's budgets and the combined total. At complete also: a human-not-present debit to a seller with an unresolved reversal under the root (reasons: [seller_reversal_unresolved]; a human-present payment is allowed), an open mandate presented at a gateway that is not its BAP (agent.bap_id; for a mandate without one, a credential whose hash is not agent.credential_hash), and a second debit for a checkout_hash that already has a reservation or settled debit under the root. $.checkout_hash, $.mandate_ref, $.payee, $.rail_limits.block_amount, $.checkout_mandate_ref, $.agent.bap_id, $.agent.credential_hash requires_buyer_review amount_not_positive 403 mandate_error A payable amount, a tender or a ledger posting is zero, negative or not an integer number of paise. $.amount unrecoverable presence_not_allowed 403 mandate_error The request's presence (HP or HNP) is not in the mandate's presence_allowed, or a trade act (POST /trade-acts) carries presence: HNP. $.presence requires_buyer_review presence_not_proven 403 mandate_error A post-order write with presence: HP has no valid hp_proof: none (the error then carries step_up, a post_order step-up whose ts_render names the write, the same pending one on a repeat), one for another action, order or issue, one for RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED or RESOLUTION_REJECTED on an issue whose resolution has changed since it was shown (subject_hash), or one already used, or, for a trade act, a proof whose step-up shows a different subject than the one submitted (subject_hash: the exact document body, the ledger entry's entry_hash or the statement's head_hash; the proof is not consumed). Or, on an assisted session, a Trusted Surface approval was not made with the principal's own factor or names no assisted operator of the session. Or an ACCEPT_REVOKE of an acceptance that the principal approved on the Trusted Surface carries no valid hp_proof. Or a Trusted Surface approval of a rail_auth step-up, or of a confirm step-up whose approval releases a debit, carries user_action: voice_confirm_plus_device (Voice confirmation). Or an approval is below the mandate's confirmation_floor, or on a channel outside it (Confirmation floor), or its device_signature does not verify against the mandate's principal.device_jkt[]. Nothing is sent to the network. $.hp_proof, $.presentation.user_action requires_buyer_review rail_limit_exceeded 403 + reasons[], step_up_kind: rail_auth mandate_error A rail cap other than an AFA threshold would be exceeded: per-transaction, period, first-24-hour, remaining block or channel cap. $.amount requires_buyer_review log_chain_invalid 403 mandate_error The InstructionLog chain is broken or its head does not match the log_head sent on the network. $.log_head unrecoverable constraint_unresolved 200 + step_up — A constraint cannot be evaluated deterministically for this request, so the gateway falls back to a human confirmation. $.step_up requires_buyer_review collector_not_authorised 403 payment_error The party in collected_by is not an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank according to the registry. No money moves. $.payment.collected_by unrecoverable receipt_invalid 400 invalid_request A receipt is malformed or is not signed by a registered PSP key. $.receipt unrecoverable evidence_forbidden 403 authorization_error The caller is not a party of record for the evidence bundle. — unrecoverable evidence_unverifiable 422 invalid_request The evidence bundle fails verification: signatures, the chain (including a negotiation receipt whose received_at is earlier than that of an entry before it in the chain without clock_step_observed; two receipts at one log_seq for different entries; a CounterSignature payload without log_seq, log_entry_hash or prev_entry_hash; under the sunset text for allowed_until_receipt, also a receipt of an ACCEPT or ACCEPT_REVOKE without log_entry_hash, or a CounterSignature that names a transcript position holding another message), or step 6 (a step-up entry without its signed Trusted Surface event, an approval without a Presentation or with a content_hash that does not match its ts_render, a step-up event whose ts_render is missing from ts_renders[] or whose total, payee or checkout_hash differs from the BPP-signed quote or whose price_breakup_hash differs from the disclosures hash, a ts_render whose catalogue_disclosure[] differs from the bundle's Disclosures.catalogue[] or omits a qualifying entry, a Disclosures.catalogue[] entry whose source_digest the agent's discover log entry does not list or whose signed source does not match, a negotiation step-up whose ts_render carries an offer_hash or acceptance_revocation that differs from the signed offer, or a first agent entry that is not ai_disclosure). A verifier reports the same code. — unrecoverable cancel_not_allowed 403 authorization_error The seller refuses the cancellation under its cancellation terms (@ondc/org/cancellable, cancellation_terms). A mandate or scope failure is mandate_scope_mismatch, and a presence failure is presence_not_allowed. $.order_id requires_buyer_review return_not_allowed 403 authorization_error The return is outside the return window, the item is not returnable, or the quantity exceeds what was ordered and not yet returned. $.items[n] requires_buyer_review

Why rail_binding_not_open_eligible is 400. On complete, this code can be a refusal by the deterministic verifier of a well-formed, signed mandate (for example after a registry downgrade), which would normally be a 403 mandate_error. BACP keeps it on 400 invalid_request deliberately, so that one code keeps one status at POST /mandates and at complete and the registry entry stays unchanged. Moving the code to 403 was considered and not adopted. Both statuses are on the protocol-failure channel and carry the same resolution, so a client handles them the same way.

docs.title: Session and payment messages
docs.text:
These are always 200 or 201 messages. prior_price_contradicted and prior_price_invalid arrive in messages[] of a discover response; the others arrive on a session.

Code Message type Meaning Typical param Resolution ai_disclosure disclosure First message of every session: the AI notice, pointing at the session's ai_disclosure with its typed routes to a human. $.ai_disclosure recoverable step_up_required error A human approval is needed; see the step_up object. $.step_up requires_buyer_review step_up_approved info The principal approved the step-up on the Trusted Surface. $.step_up recoverable step_up_declined warning The principal declined the step-up on the Trusted Surface; the session is cancelled and no money moves. — requires_buyer_input step_up_expired warning The step-up link expired without approval, or the approval was acted on (presentation.acted_at) after expires_at. No money moves. $.step_up requires_buyer_input quote_expired warning The seller's quote expired before complete; the session returns to incomplete. $.quote.expires_at recoverable (re-select) quote_mismatch warning The seller's quote differs from what the agent requested (items or quantities). $.line_items recoverable or requires_buyer_review preticked_addon_removed warning The gateway removed an add-on the seller had pre-selected. $.line_items[n] recoverable drip_pricing_detected warning The total rose between quote and checkout, or a mandatory charge appeared late. $.totals requires_buyer_review payment_mode_fee_inconsistent warning A convenience fee applies to some debit payment modes the seller accepts and not others, or differs between them (NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5, which binds the Payee PSP). A SHOULD, never a refusal; in HNP it also raises a confirm step-up (constraint_unresolved). $.totals requires_buyer_review charge_recipient_invalid warning A stated bacp.charge recipient breached the type-to-recipient rule (Fees on the payer's screen); the gateway ignored it and applied the recipient mapping. $.totals[n] recoverable operator_compensation_mismatch warning A session carries a seller-paid entry in intermediary_compensation[] while the mandate's notice says from_sellers: none (Operator compensation). $.intermediary_compensation[n] requires_buyer_review charge_recipient_unmapped warning A charge line arrived with a type that the recipient mapping does not cover; the line is kept with recipient: other. $.totals[n] recoverable discovery_price_changed warning A unit price at on_select is higher than the price shown at discovery. requires_buyer_review when the item was shown with a prior_price, and the session then has a confirm step-up. Otherwise recoverable, and the agent tells a present principal the new price. A lower price never raises it. $.line_items[n].unit_price recoverable, or requires_buyer_review when the item was shown with a prior_price prior_price_contradicted warning Advisory. The gateway has itself seen a lower price for the item in the 30 days before the announced_on of its prior_price. The value is relayed unaltered. The agent SHOULD NOT voice the reduction claim. $.results[n].items[m].prior_price recoverable prior_price_invalid warning The gateway dropped a prior_price that was not above the item's unit_price, or was above mrp while tax_inclusive was true, or whose seller-sent decimal could not be converted to integer paise. $.results[n].items[m].prior_price recoverable sponsored_listing disclosure The item at $.disclosures.catalogue[n] was shown as sponsored. The agent presents the sponsored phrase with the party from by[]. $.disclosures.catalogue[n] recoverable sponsorship_undeclared disclosure Nobody in the chain stated whether the item at $.disclosures.catalogue[n] was sponsored. The agent presents the undeclared phrase, never "not sponsored". $.disclosures.catalogue[n] recoverable prior_price_claim disclosure The item at $.disclosures.catalogue[n] was shown with a seller-asserted prior price. The agent presents the prior_price phrase and never a bare percentage. $.disclosures.catalogue[n] recoverable discount_code_expired warning A submitted discount code is past its validity. The code is absent from discounts.applied[]. $.discounts.codes[n] recoverable discount_code_invalid warning A submitted code is unknown to the seller, or the gateway reports every rejection with this code. $.discounts.codes[n] recoverable discount_code_already_applied warning A submitted code is already applied to the session. $.discounts.codes[n] recoverable discount_code_combination_disallowed warning A submitted code cannot be combined with a discount that is already applied. $.discounts.codes[n] recoverable discount_code_user_ineligible warning A submitted code is not available to this buyer. $.discounts.codes[n] recoverable discount_code_unsupported warning The seller or network takes no discount codes. $.discounts.codes[n] recoverable policy_text_mismatch warning A typed policy of the session or catalogue (in.bacp.policy.return, .cancel or .cod) contradicts the binding return_terms or cancellation_terms. The session moves to requires_escalation with a confirm step-up (reason constraint_unresolved) and cannot reach ready_for_complete until the principal has reviewed. $.policies[n] requires_buyer_review disclosures_missing error A mandatory pre-contract disclosure (seller name, total price, return terms, cancellation terms, country of origin, expected delivery or price breakup) is missing; the session cannot reach ready_for_complete. $.disclosures requires_buyer_review split_order_suspected warning Orders to the same seller within a short window look like a split to stay under a step-up threshold. $.totals requires_buyer_review payment_in_doubt warning The PSP did not confirm the debit; the gateway is reconciling. $.payment.status recoverable (do NOT re-key) payment_failed error The debit failed; no money moved and the budget reservation is released. $.payment requires_buyer_input debited_not_confirmed warning The principal was debited but the seller never confirmed; a refund to source has started (refund_route: gateway_collector) or has been requested from the seller's collector (seller_collector). With reversal_basis: rbi_tat the message states the rail turnaround time and the ₹100 a day compensation; with bacp_policy it never states an RBI compensation entitlement; with unknown it names the refund, UDIR and the Ombudsman routes and says that RBI's rules apply if the bank shows the payment as failed or pending. $.payment.reversal_deadline recoverable return_refused warning The seller rejected a return (RETURN_REJECTED). Never terminal: the message carries the operator's grievance_contact in args[], and a seller's refusal to take back goods that the principal reports as defective is not the end of the matter (Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, r.6(3)). $.return.status requires_buyer_review seller_cancelled warning The seller cancelled an order that the principal had not asked to cancel (an unsolicited on_cancel).
