Never terminal: the message carries the grievance_contact in args[], and the refund follows the refund rules (r.4(8) of the same Rules requires cancellation charges to be symmetric). $.state requires_buyer_review budget_after info The remaining mandate budget after a PSP-signed receipt was applied (computed by the gateway, unsigned). $.payment.budget_after recoverable pre_debit_notice info A pre-debit notice has been issued; no money moves until it matures. $.payment.scheduled_debit_at recoverable pre_debit_opt_out warning The principal opted out of the notified debit; the session is cancelled with no rail traffic. $.payment requires_buyer_input session_cancelled info The session was cancelled (by the agent, by TTL or because the mandate ended). $.mandate_ref recoverable mandate_revoked error (checkout session) / warning (negotiation) The mandate was revoked while the session or negotiation was live. $.mandate_ref requires_buyer_input

docs.title: Negotiation, RFQ and auction codes
docs.text:
See Negotiation and RFQ and Auctions.

Code HTTP Meaning Typical param Resolution NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID 400 The negotiation message or TermSheet fails its schema, or carries an extension issue the guard cannot evaluate. the offending field recoverable NEG_ISSUE_NOT_NEGOTIABLE 200 msg / 403 A counter changes an issue that is not in the agreed negotiable_issues. $.term_sheet recoverable NEG_STALE_OFFER 409 The message cites an offer that is not the live offer. $.in_reply_to recoverable (GET, then respond to the live offer) NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED 200 msg / 403 (own, local) The cited offer is past expires_at on the offeror's receipt, or the acceptor's gateway refused locally to dispatch an accept within 5 s of expires_at on its own clock. An accept refused as expired whose dispatched_at is not after expires_at and which passed freshness is crossing_contested, not this code. $.offer_hash recoverable (fresh offer or REQUEST_EXTENSION) NEG_ACCEPT_NONCONFORMING 422 (own) / 200 msg (counterparty text) The acceptance does not use the prescribed manner (a signed bacp.neg.accept); chat, voice or an unsigned accept does not bind. $.untrusted_counterparty_text recoverable NEG_TERMS_DRIFT 200 msg, state BREACH_FLAGGED The seller's on_init or confirm terms differ from the accepted offer. $.bound_term_sheet_hash requires_buyer_review NEG_MRP_EXCEEDED 200 msg (counterparty) / 403 (own) A unit price including tax exceeds the MRP of a retail package. Also in a discover response: an item with tax_inclusive: true whose unit_price is above its mrp (a 200 message on POST /discover). $.term_sheet.lines[n].unit_price, $.results[n].items[m].unit_price recoverable NEG_MSMED_CREDIT_CAP 200 msg (incoming) / 403 (own firm) Credit days to a micro or small enterprise exceed the statutory cap. $.term_sheet.payment.credit_days recoverable NEG_DRIP_PRICING 200 msg A charge appeared after the first round, or the all-in total rose beyond the mandate's tripwire. $.live_offer.all_in_total requires_buyer_review NEG_FALSE_URGENCY 200 msg / 403 The offer's validity window is shorter than the minimum (PT5M for B2C). $.expires_at requires_buyer_review (msg) / recoverable (403) NEG_BASKET_SNEAK 200 msg / 403 A counter adds lines or add-ons the principal did not assert. $.term_sheet.lines requires_buyer_review / recoverable NEG_PERSONALISED_PRICING 200 msg / 403 The pricing basis is undeclared or uses prohibited attributes. $.term_sheet.pricing_basis requires_buyer_review / recoverable NEG_EXPOSURE_EXCEEDED 200 + step_up Outstanding firm commitments across this principal's negotiations would exceed total_max or a remaining budget. $.term_sheet requires_buyer_review NEG_INJECTION_SUSPECTED 200 msg Counterparty free text looks like an instruction to the agent; it is quarantined as data. $.untrusted_counterparty_text recoverable NEG_CASH_LIMIT 403 A cash tranche of ₹2 lakh or more. $.term_sheet.payment.schedule recoverable NEG_RERA_TOKEN_CAP 403 A property token above 10% without a linked registered agreement. $.term_sheet.deposit recoverable NEG_CREDIT_DISCLOSURE_MISSING 403 An EMI, BNPL or credit-funded option lacks lender, APR or KFS. $.term_sheet.payment recoverable NEG_EMI_NO_COST_FALSE 403 An interest-bearing EMI is labelled no-cost. $.term_sheet.payment.emi recoverable NEG_EINVOICE_IRN_MISSING 403 (dispatch gate) A B2B invoice that needs an IRN has none. — recoverable NEG_EWB_MISSING 403 (dispatch gate) An e-way bill is required before dispatch and is missing. — recoverable NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN 200 msg (screen flag) A collusion heuristic flagged the bids, or an RFQ or auction was cancelled because its award was revoked. It never blocks. — requires_buyer_review NEG_EARLY_AWARD 403 Award attempted before response_by while invitees are still to respond. $.response_by unrecoverable for that action NEG_EARLY_REVEAL 403 A sealed bid was revealed before the commit phase closed. — unrecoverable for that action NEG_SHILL_BID 403 A bid from the seller or a declared affiliate. — unrecoverable for that action NEG_DUTCH_PRICE_INCREASE 403 A Dutch tick higher than the previous tick. — unrecoverable for that action NEG_RETRACTION_REFUSED 403 A retraction that the auction's retraction_rule does not allow, or one inside the anti-sniping window. — unrecoverable for that action NEG_AWARD_RULE 403 The award does not follow the published award rule, or the RFQ or auction was cancelled after a revoked award and cannot be awarded again. The principal's gateway also refuses with it an award that cites a standing accept that it did not lodge for that auction and lot, that has expired, or that has been used or released. $.bid_hash, $.standing_accept_id unrecoverable for that action NEG_DEPOSIT_REQUIRED 400 A sealed auction or sealed RFQ has no bid deposit. $.bid_deposit recoverable NEG_DEPOSIT_INVALID 403 The bid deposit reference does not verify or does not cover the bid. $.bid_deposit_ref recoverable NEG_CLOCK_SKEW 422 A message's dispatched_at is more than 5 s from the receiver's clock at receipt. The bound is a freshness check, a BACP choice, and never decides order. The agent MUST NOT re-sign and retry. $.dispatched_at recoverable NEG_ATTESTATION_REFUSED 403 The buyer's credential provider refused the within_bounds attestation. — requires_buyer_review bid_not_improving 409 The bid does not improve on the bidder's own previous bid (reverse auction) or the current highest (English auction) by the increment. $.amount recoverable auction_not_open 409 The auction has not opened or has closed. — recoverable auction_closed_no_award terminate reason / 200 msg The auction closed without awarding this bidder. — unrecoverable rfq_not_awarded terminate reason The RFQ was awarded to another seller. — unrecoverable capabilities_incompatible 200 msg / 403 The buyer's and seller's negotiation capabilities do not intersect (for example no common mode), and the agent falls back to fixed. Also: an offer's or a draft's acceptance_revocation value is not permitted (allowed_until_receipt on every leg in this version; waived with waiver_basis in a consumer session off Beckn), or a session message declares a profile other than the one fixed when the session opened; the offer never becomes LIVE. Also: either party refuses the declared profile (reason profile_not_supported or profile_misdescribed, $.context.bacp.profile), or a firm message's protocol_terms.hash is not the receiver's. $.mode, $.acceptance_revocation, $.context.bacp.profile, $.protocol_terms requires_buyer_input handlers_incompatible 200 msg (intersect) / 403 (ACCEPT) No payment handler is eligible for the agreed payment option at this presence. — requires_buyer_input untrusted_counterparty_text 200 msg (info) Counterparty free text, returned only as data, with origin: counterparty. The agent framework MUST NOT execute it. A counterparty value inside a gateway message travels in its args[] instead (slot rule). $.untrusted_counterparty_text recoverable withdraw_lost_crossing 200 msg Our WITHDRAW crossed the counterparty's ACCEPT and lost; the offer stands accepted. $.offers recoverable accept_revoke_honoured 200 msg Sunset only; not returned in this version. Under allowed_until_receipt, the proposer received the ACCEPT_REVOKE before the acceptance it names, and the pair matched: the offer is ACCEPT_REVOKED and there is no agreement. Returned with the proposer's CounterSignature on the revoke. $.offers recoverable accept_revoke_after_receipt 200 msg Sunset only; not returned in this version. The proposer received the acceptance before the ACCEPT_REVOKE; the acceptance stands. $.offers requires_buyer_review accept_revoke_not_allowed 200 msg The offer sets acceptance_revocation: waived, as every live firm offer does in this version; the ACCEPT_REVOKE is countersigned, logged and refused, and the acceptance stands. $.offers requires_buyer_review accept_void_withdrawn 200 msg Our ACCEPT crossed the counterparty's WITHDRAW and lost; there is no agreement. $.offers recoverable seller_accept_void 200 msg The seller's ACCEPT lost a crossing with our withdrawal. $.offers recoverable agreed_by_counterparty 200 msg The counterparty accepted our live firm offer; the negotiation is AGREED. $.state requires_buyer_review crossing_contested 200 msg (warning) A withdraw and an accept crossed and the transcript positions do not decide the outcome, or a needed receipt is missing, late or unverifiable. BACP evidence does not settle formation; neither gateway proceeds; the protocol records no breach event. The session is ESCALATED on both sides and both principals are asked. The agent MUST stop and MUST NOT resend. $.state, $.offers requires_buyer_review crossing_unconfirmed 200 msg (info) A contested crossing closed CANCELLED because neither principal confirmed it before the earlier of the offer's expires_at and the end of the step-up link. No breach event and no protocol-computed charge; the exposure reservation is released once. $.state recoverable formation_disputed 200 msg (info) A contested crossing closed CANCELLED because one principal confirmed and the other declined or was silent. No breach event and no protocol-computed charge; the message carries the grievance_contact of both sides. Whether a contract formed is for ODR or the courts. $.state recoverable principal_declined 200 msg (info) The principal declined an AGREED or BOUND deal under the term sheet's cancellation.terms by the Trusted Surface event negotiation.agreed.declined. Performance of a term, not a breach, where the terms permit cancellation at that stage; with the flag no_stage_term when the terms are silent on the stage (no fee is computed); with a breach claim flag, never a finding, when the terms make the stage non-cancellable or the charge goes unpaid. $.state recoverable agreed_by_agent 200 msg (info) The agent accepted a firm offer on the principal's behalf without a step-up (accept_confirmation: autonomous). Built from gateway templates in the principal's language and delivered by the mandate's notice_route, never through the agent's own output. $.state recoverable purchase_offered_by_agent 200 msg (info) In a consumer session the agent's accept of a non-firm offer is a purchase offer. Same content and delivery as agreed_by_agent; the stop control shows only where a carrier exists to honour it. $.state recoverable autonomous_unavailable_no_notice_route 200 msg (info) The mandate says autonomous but notice_route is absent or not usable, so the gateway treated it as ask and raised a confirm step-up. $.mandate_ref recoverable offer_expired_during_approval 200 msg / ts_render.language template The offer ran out while the principal was approving, or the acceptor's gateway refused to dispatch within 5 s of expires_at. The Trusted Surface says "the offer ran out while you were approving", never "you declined". $.offer_hash requires_buyer_review seller_counter_at_init 200 msg The seller's on_init differs from our non-firm offer, which makes it a counter-offer. $.live_offer requires_buyer_input negotiation_terminated 200 msg The negotiation ended (rounds, deadline, revocation or TERMINATE). $.state requires_buyer_input cancelled_no_penalty 200 msg After a firm-offer breach the principal cancelled without penalty. $.state recoverable bid_not_revealed 200 msg A committed sealed bid was never revealed; it is excluded and its deposit forfeited. — unrecoverable NEG_CLOSED 400 A sealed-bid commit arrived after the commit phase closed. — unrecoverable for that action NEG_REVEAL_MISMATCH 400 A revealed bid and salt do not hash to the bidder's commitment, or the bidder made no commitment. — unrecoverable for that action requires_escalation 200 msg (error) The agent's firm counter or acceptance was not sent because it falls outside the negotiation mandate, or the seller accepted a non-firm offer that binds only after principal approval. The negotiation carries a step_up. Not to be confused with the session status of the same name. $.term_sheet, $.step_up requires_buyer_review seller_purchase_offer 200 msg (info) The seller accepted the agent's non-firm offer. That acceptance is a purchase offer to the buyer, which binds only after the principal approves it within the mandate. $.step_up requires_buyer_review bpp_no_on_init 200 msg (warning) After the agent's ACCEPT, the seller returned no on_init order (no callback, or a Beckn error). $.state recoverable auction_awarded 200 msg (info) The neutral auctioneer awarded the auction to this bidder. — recoverable

docs.title: Payment-handler and rail codes
docs.text:
These are raised by the handler and rail layer. When a gateway surfaces one over HTTP it MUST use the status given here. "200 msg" codes come back on POST /payment-handlers/intersect as excluded[].reason or as messages. See Payments and Handler Registry.

Code HTTP when surfaced Meaning Typical param Resolution presence_handler_mismatch 403 The handler needs a human-completed authentication but the request is human-not-present (or the handler needs an assisted session). $.presence requires_buyer_review reservepay_block_wrong_payee 403 A Reserve Pay debit for a seller other than the block's payee. $.payment.handler requires_buyer_input (pay this seller with another eligible handler under the per-leg rule, usually one human-present payment; a new block for this seller is offered only beside a one-time human-present payment, never after a failed payment) payee_mismatch rail failure receipt Rail-level twin of the above: the rail refused a debit to a payee its authority does not cover. — requires_buyer_input cod_not_allowed 403 Cash on delivery is not allowed by the governing mandate. — requires_buyer_input cod_open_orders_cap 403 / 200 msg (intersect) The mandate's cap on open COD orders is reached. — requires_buyer_input credit_funding_not_allowed 403 / 200 msg (intersect) A credit-funded handler without credit_funding_allowed: true on the governing mandate. — requires_buyer_input card_not_enabled_for_cnp 200 msg The issuer declined because card-not-present use is disabled. The agent MUST NOT silently try another card. — requires_buyer_input split_tender_afa_on_total 200 + step_up The AFA threshold applies to the total across tenders; splitting does not avoid it. $.step_up requires_buyer_review refund_to_ppi_forbidden 403 A refund of a card, UPI or net-banking payment into a wallet. — unrecoverable refund_not_to_source 403 A refund to anything other than the original instrument without an explicit payer instruction. — requires_buyer_input (explicit payer instruction) refund_short_of_terms warning (200 msg) A refund below the amount paid does not match the lines in charges_retained[], or a reversal is below the full debit. The refund is never blocked or held; the message names the IGM route. $.refund requires_buyer_review credit_acceptance_requires_hp 403 An agent attempted to accept a loan offer; acceptance is human-present only. — requires_buyer_review repayment_payee_not_lender 403 A loan repayment or refund directed to anyone other than the lender. — unrecoverable nach_mandate_above_cap 403 A NACH mandate above the cap for its authentication mode. — requires_buyer_input mandate_cancelled rail failure receipt The rail-level standing instruction (for example a NACH UMRN) was cancelled. — requires_buyer_input pre_debit_notice_too_late 403 The pre-debit notice does not precede the debit by at least 24 hours. $.payment.scheduled_debit_at recoverable pending_approval 200 (state) A maker-checker approval is pending. — requires_buyer_review plan_sum_mismatch 400 The tenders of a payment plan do not add up to the total. $.payment_plan recoverable plan_order_invalid 400 The capture order of a payment plan is invalid, including a plan with more than one tender that has no hold primitive or with such a tender before the last. $.payment_plan recoverable bacp_mandate_required 400 On the UCP checkout projection (in.bacp.ucp_checkout), a complete_checkout carries no instrument whose credential is a BACP closed payment mandate. No rail call is made. It is also the code of the unrecoverable UCP message that explains the refusal. $.payment.instruments unrecoverable plan_not_offered 400 On a gateway that lists in.bacp.payment_plan, the tenders of payment_plan hash to neither the plan_hash of an entry of payment.plan_options[] nor that of a plan the principal confirmed on the Trusted Surface. Nothing is debited. $.payment_plan recoverable (choose an offered plan) plan_conflict 409 A different plan is already live for this checkout_hash (P1). Nothing is debited and no mandate usage changes. $.payment_plan recoverable (GET the session, then act on the live plan) refund_exceeds_capture 400 A refund larger than the amount captured. — unrecoverable refund_exceeds_debit 400 A refund larger than the rail debit. — unrecoverable duplicate_debit rail refusal A second debit for the same closed payment mandate or checkout_hash. — unrecoverable basket_not_allowed rail refusal Basket data was sent on the payment leg, which is basket-blind. — unrecoverable credit_limit_exceeded 403 A credit-ledger sale above the ledger's credit limit. — requires_buyer_input entry_disputed 409 The credit-ledger entry is disputed and cannot be settled or acknowledged. — requires_buyer_review schema_invalid 400 A credit-ledger posting fails its schema, for example a payment with only a screenshot as evidence. — unrecoverable evidence_invalid 400 A credit-ledger payment cites a receipt whose signature or amount does not match. — unrecoverable

docs.title: Rail and ledger refusals
docs.text:
These codes are returned by a rail or by the khata credit ledger to the participant that called it. They follow the "rail refusal" rows of the table above: no money moves. A gateway that reports one to an agent MUST use the code unchanged and, over HTTP, the status given here.

Code Raised by HTTP when surfaced Meaning Typical param Resolution afa_required rail refusal 403 The debit needs an additional factor of authentication (for example a human-present wallet debit without 2FA). On a standing mandate the same condition is a rail_auth step-up instead (see step-up reasons). — requires_buyer_review insufficient_balance rail refusal 403 A wallet, UPI Lite, store-credit or loyalty balance is too low for the debit. — requires_buyer_input ppi_not_reloadable rail refusal 403 A load into a gift PPI, which cannot be reloaded. — unrecoverable pre_debit_notice_missing rail refusal 403 No matured 24-hour pre-debit notice covers this card e-mandate or NACH debit. $.payment.scheduled_debit_at recoverable (send a notice and wait) consent_window_closed rail refusal 409 Cardholder consent for a refund was given after the refund left pending_cardholder_consent or after its 7-day window. — unrecoverable voucher_expired rail refusal 403 An e-RUPI voucher is past its validity; unredeemed value returns to the sponsor. — unrecoverable voucher_purpose_mismatch rail refusal 403 An e-RUPI voucher redeemed at a merchant outside its purpose. — unrecoverable bill_already_paid rail refusal 409 A BBPS bill that is already paid. — unrecoverable amount_mismatch rail refusal 422 A BBPS payment that differs from the fetched bill amount when partial payment is not allowed. $.amount recoverable payee_name_mismatch rail refusal 422 The bank's beneficiary name look-up does not match the expected payee name for an account-to-account transfer. — requires_buyer_review maker_checker_required rail refusal 403 An account-to-account payment was approved by its maker, or without 2FA; a different human checker must approve. — requires_buyer_review invalid_state rail refusal 409 An account-to-account payment is not in the state the operation needs (approve when not pending_approval, credit when not sent). — unrecoverable illegal_cod_transition rail refusal 409 A cash-on-delivery order state change that the COD state machine does not allow. — unrecoverable loan_offer_not_lender_signed rail refusal 422 The loan offer presented for acceptance does not match the lender-signed KFS offer. — unrecoverable disbursal_not_to_end_beneficiary rail refusal 403 A loan disbursal to an account other than the end beneficiary's. — unrecoverable cooling_off_over rail refusal 409 A penalty-free exit from a loan after its cooling-off period ended. — unrecoverable refund_not_allowed rail refusal 400 A refund that cites no successful debit with that RRN. — unrecoverable poster_not_party ledger refusal 403 The poster of a ledger entry is not the ledger's creditor or debtor, or its signature does not verify under that party's registry key. — unrecoverable ack_signature_required ledger refusal 400 An acknowledgement without the counterparty's signature. — requires_buyer_input ack_not_by_counterparty ledger refusal 403 An acknowledgement by anyone other than the counterparty of the poster. — unrecoverable ack_signature_invalid ledger refusal 400 The acknowledgement signature does not verify under the counterparty's registry key. — unrecoverable grn_attestation_required ledger refusal 400 An acceptance-dated credit sale without a buyer-signed GRN attestation. — requires_buyer_input grn_attestation_invalid ledger refusal 400 The GRN attestation is not signed by the ledger's debtor, or the GRN was already used. — unrecoverable grn_date_invalid ledger refusal 400 The GRN date precedes the invoice or delivery date, is in the future, or differs from the sale's reference date. — recoverable receipt_required ledger refusal 400 A payment entry without a PSP-signed rail receipt. — requires_buyer_input receipt_reused ledger refusal 409 The rail receipt has already settled ledger entries, on this ledger or on any other ledger that the creditor's custodian holds (uniqueness is keyed on the rail and the RRN or UTR). — unrecoverable ledger_head_mismatch ledger refusal 409 A posting or acknowledgement whose prev_hash or head_hash is not the ledger's current chain head (compare-and-swap). Nothing is appended. $.prev_hash recoverable (GET the ledger, then act on the current head) settlement_payee_unmatched ledger message 201 msg A payment entry cites a receipt whose payee matches none of the creditor's settlement_accounts[] (or the new_payee after TReDS discounting), or whose issued_at is before the settled sale. The entry is accepted as pending_ack for the creditor and settles nothing until the creditor acknowledges it. $.settlement_evidence requires_buyer_review nothing_to_settle ledger refusal 409 A payment entry when the ledger has no acknowledged open sale entries. — unrecoverable credit_note_exceeds_open ledger refusal 400 A credit note larger than the sale's open amount. — recoverable

docs.title: Internal and nested reasons
docs.text:
These values are not registry codes. A participant MUST NOT put them in Error.code or messages[].code. Some reach the agent only inside a registered code, as shown.

Value Where it arises How it reaches the agent local:per_txn, local:block_remaining, local:per_month, local:first_24h, local:binding_expired The verifier's local rail-cap checks In reasons[] of rail_limit_exceeded rail:<reason>: block_expired, delegation_inactive, pin_auth_used, pin_auth_expired, unknown_rail_ref, unsupported_rail, payee_mismatch, amount_mismatch, pre_debit_notice_missing, pre_debit_opt_out, rail_limit_exceeded The payer PSP's pre-check of the bound rail In reasons[] of rail_limit_exceeded. A pre-debit notice that has not matured is not a breach: the session gets the pre_debit_notice message instead, and rail:pre_debit_opt_out cancels the session with pre_debit_opt_out. The same reason is the error of a signed failure receipt, reported with payment_failed. unsupported_rail, block_exists, device_limit Rail set-up by the payer PSP on the Trusted Surface: attesting a rail type the PSP does not support, a second active Reserve Pay block for the same payee, too many Circle delegate devices Never to the agent; the mandate request is not activated handler_mismatch, unsupported_handler The gateway's payment-handler lookup The gateway first checks the handler against the mandate's rail binding (mandate_scope_mismatch, $.payment.handler); the handler intersection excludes an unknown handler with not_in_registry. A debit refused this way is reported as payment_failed. refund_not_allowed, refund_exceeds_debit on a post-order refund The rail refund call As status: FAILED:<code> on the order's refund adjustments[] entry auction_exists, not_sealed, no_award The neutral auctioneer (create, commit, Dutch award without an accepted tick) invalid_request (400); the auctioneer's text is in message auctioneer_not_neutral, not_eligible The neutral auctioneer (seller-run auction, bidder outside the allowlist) mandate_scope_mismatch (403) discovery_source_unverified, discovery_source_mismatch An agent's check of a discovery source (Verifying discovery results): unverified when any step fails, mismatch when the signed body differs from the result Never on the wire. The agent records it in the InstructionLog at stage discover and renders the item without the claim, as the table there says discount_source_unknown An agent finds an applied[] entry with a code that it did not submit (Discounts) Never on the wire. The agent records it in the InstructionLog and tells a present principal NEG_ATTESTATION_INVALID A seller's Beckn error on on_init when the buyer's within_bounds attestation does not verify bpp_no_on_init NEG_BREACH sub_category of the IGM issue the gateway raises for a breach other than terms drift The IGM issue on the negotiation, not a code capture_failed A payment-plan tender capture that returned no success and no rail code error of a failed payment-plan result, with failed_tender handler_non_paying, mandate_exceeds_rail_limit The handler binding check (class N handler; a mandate limit above the rail's limit) Not surfaced; binding checks that reach the agent use presence_handler_mismatch, cod_not_allowed, cod_open_orders_cap, credit_funding_not_allowed or reservepay_block_wrong_payee

docs.title: Step-up reasons
docs.text:
step_up.reason (with step_up.kind) is one of:

Reason Kind When above_step_up_threshold confirm The amount is above the mandate's step_up.above_amount. new_merchant confirm First order with this seller under the mandate. outside_categories confirm The category is outside the mandate's step-up-free categories. first_order confirm First order under the mandate. above_afa_limit rail_auth The debit is above the rail's AFA threshold (₹15,000; ₹1 lakh for listed categories). afa_threshold_card_emandate rail_auth A card e-mandate debit above the AFA threshold. afa_crossborder_cnp rail_auth A non-recurring, cross-border, card-not-present payment whose acquirer requests AFA. split_tender_afa_on_total rail_auth The total across tenders is above an AFA threshold. credit_acceptance confirm (HP) Acceptance of a loan offer. negotiation_out_of_mandate confirm A negotiated term is outside the negotiation mandate. negotiation_between_reservation_and_max confirm The price is between the reservation price and total_max. accept_confirmation confirm The guard returned acceptable, the mandate's accept_confirmation is ask or absent, and the agent called accept. The ts_render carries offer_hash. Nothing seller-visible is sent before negotiation.step_up.approved. rfq_prescribes_waiver confirm An agent-created RFQ sets acceptance_revocation_required: waived, which waives the principal's own ICA s.5 right. seller_confirmation confirm A BPP-signed on_select or on_init carries the bacp tag seller_confirmation: the seller asks for the buyer's own confirmation (a first cash-on-delivery order, an amount above the seller's threshold, a new credit line, a credit limit exceeded, or another reason). At most one per checkout_hash. refund_received confirm The gateway holds a refund receipt of the order's collector's PSP and not of the payer PSP, and asks the principal to confirm on the Trusted Surface that the credit arrived ("I have received ₹X"). Only that approval releases the spend of a debited_not_confirmed debit (Usage ledger). constraint_unresolved confirm Fallback when a constraint cannot be evaluated deterministically, and the reason for discovery_price_changed on an item shown with a prior_price and for policy_text_mismatch.

docs.title: Refund states
docs.text: Receipt.refund_state is one of pending_cardholder_consent, reversed_to_bank_account, released_block, credit_note_issued, refunded_to_source (the default for a completed refund to source) and adjusted_against_dues. A card refund before the bill is paid MUST be adjusted_against_dues and MUST NOT pass through pending_cardholder_consent. See Rail Bindings.

docs.title: Evidence and Instruction Log
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

When an agent buys something on a principal's behalf, every party may later need to show what was authorised, what was instructed, what was offered and what was paid. BACP produces that evidence as a by-product of every transaction, using three artefacts:

Artefact Schema Produced by Proves InstructionLog entries instruction-log-entry.json The agent operator's gateway The ordered chain prompt → intent → cart → mandate → payment → order, tamper-evident Receipt receipt.json The verifier that acted: PSP, BPP or Mandate Manager That a payment, refund, checkout or mandate step happened, anchored to the rail Evidence bundle EvidenceBundle in the REST binding The gateway, on request Everything above for one transaction, verified and signed, for a dispute

docs.title: InstructionLog
docs.text: The InstructionLog is a signed, append-only, hash-chained record kept per checkout session. It lets a reviewer reconstruct what the principal authorised and what they instructed, without the operator being able to rewrite history afterwards.

docs.title: Entry contents
docs.text:
Field Meaning seq 0 for the first entry of the session, then +1 per entry, with no gaps. session_id, transaction_id The session and the Beckn transaction, end to end. stage What kind of step this is (see Stages). actor Who performed the step: user, agent, gateway, trusted_surface, bpp, psp, or a session participant: assisted_operator, seller_operator, sub_agent (Human participants). actor_ref The participant's participant_id (REQUIRED for assisted_operator, seller_operator and sub_agent), or on a handoff entry the key id of the support operator who accepted or released it. at When it happened. channel, language For example voice and hi-IN. content_hash sha-256 of the raw content (a transcript, audio, a structured intent, a quote, a receipt). content_ref Where the operator keeps the encrypted raw content. summary A short multilingual summary. model The model id, version and, for voice or translated turns, translation_model. refs Cross-references: mandate_ref, checkout_hash, message_id, order_id, rrn, receipt_id, issue_id; at stage discover, also idempotency_key, source_digests[], source_checks[] and registry_lookup; at stage cart, discount_codes[] ({code_mac, source}). prev_hash, entry_hash The chain links (Hash chain). signature The operator's signature.

Only hashes and references leave the operator. Raw content stays encrypted at the agent operator, and is released only inside an evidence bundle to a party entitled to it (Access).

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
stage Recorded when Typical actor ai_disclosure The agent presents the AI disclosure and the routes to a human. It is the first entry whose actor is agent, before intent (Human participants) agent prompt The principal instructs the agent (text or voice; voice records channel, language and translation model) user intent The agent turns the instruction into a structured intent or mandate request agent discover A search is sent and results arrive. The agent records the Idempotency-Key of the search, the source_digest of every discovery source it checked, the outcome of each (verified, mismatch or unverified, with the reason discovery_source_mismatch or discovery_source_unverified) and the host of the registry lookup it used (Verifying discovery results). content_hash covers the discover response as returned agent, gateway cart Items are selected; the handler comparison is logged here agent, gateway disclosure The BPP's signed quote and disclosures arrive; records checkout_hash and the disclosures hash bpp mandate A mandate is activated, used or changes status, including each gateway pause reason (binding_ineligible, reissue_required) added or removed, with the registry_version (Handler binding); records mandate hashes gateway, trusted_surface step_up A step-up is requested, approved, declined or expires gateway, trusted_surface payment A debit is initiated (basket-blind instruction), a receipt arrives, an in-doubt debit is reconciled, a refund is issued gateway, psp order on_confirm creates the order bpp post_order Cancels, returns, status changes and post-order refunds agent, assisted_operator, bpp, psp grievance An IGM issue is raised and every action on it agent, bpp negotiation Every negotiation message and counter-signature agent, bpp guard Every negotiation guard verdict (constraint ids only) gateway ledger Credit-ledger postings and acknowledgements gateway, seller_operator handoff A handoff to a human is requested, accepted by a registered support operator, or released (Human handoff) agent, gateway

The stage disclosure is the seller's quote; the AI disclosure is always ai_disclosure. The negotiation, guard and ledger stages are described in Negotiation and Credit and Split Tender.

docs.title: Signer roles
docs.text:
• Every entry is signed by the agent operator (the gateway's BAP registry key) with signature.role: operator, whatever its actor. The actor field records who acted; the signature records who attests to the record.
  • The signature is asymmetric (ES256 or EdDSA), as a detached JWS over the JCS form of the entry minus signature. A shared-secret MAC MUST NOT be used, because it cannot give non-repudiation.
  • The acts of other parties are proved by their own signatures on the artefacts the entry hashes and references: the BPP's signature on the quote, the PSP's on the Receipt, the principal's and MM's on the mandate, the Trusted Surface's on a step-up event. A human act is never proved by the operator's signature alone: the bundle carries the signed Trusted Surface events themselves (Bundle contents).

docs.title: Hash chain
docs.text:
entry_hash = sha-256( JCS( entry minus {entry_hash, signature} ) )
prev_hash  = entry_hash of entry seq - 1
prev_hash of seq 0 (genesis) = sha-256( session_id as UTF-8 bytes )

Hashes are written sha-256:<base64url>. The log head is the entry_hash of the last entry, or the genesis hash when the log is empty.

Anchoring. The gateway MUST put the current log_head in context.bacp.log_head on every committing Beckn message it sends (init, confirm, update, cancel, issue). Those messages are signed on the network, so the BPP and the network hold independent copies of the head at each commitment. An operator that deletes or rewrites an entry produces a chain that no longer matches the heads recorded in the network trace.

  "session_id": "ses_01HZXB",

  },

docs.title: Chain verification
docs.text:
A verifier MUST check a log as follows, and MUST reject it at the first failure:

  1. The log is not empty.
  2. Every entry validates against instruction-log-entry.json.
  3. For entry i (counting from 0): seq = i, and session_id equals the first entry's.
  4. prev_hash equals the genesis hash for i = 0, and the previous entry's entry_hash otherwise.
  5. Recomputing entry_hash gives the stored value.
  6. signature verifies against the registry key named by its kid.
  7. If an expected head is known (for example from context.bacp.log_head in a network message, or from the gateway's current state), the last entry_hash equals it.

The gateway MUST run this check on the session's log before complete. A broken chain returns 403 log_chain_invalid (unrecoverable) and no money moves (Deterministic evaluation).

docs.title: Receipts
docs.text:
A Receipt is the signed statement of the party that acted: the payer PSP for a payment or refund, the BPP for a checkout, the Mandate Manager for a mandate. It follows AP2's mandate, checkout and payment receipts and adds the Indian rail references.

Field Rule receipt_type mandate, checkout, payment or refund. iss The verifier that acted. A payment or refund receipt MUST be signed with a registry key of role PSP; a checkout receipt with a key of role BPP. result success, failure or in_doubt. reference The hash of the closed mandate that was presented: sha-256 over the JCS form of the mandate minus status, usage and signatures. mandate_ref, open_mandate_ref The closed mandate id and its open parent. transaction_id, order_id The Beckn transaction, end to end, and the order. checkout_hash, amount, payee Required on a successful payment or refund receipt. amount MUST be greater than zero. rail The rail evidence (below). refund_state Refund receipts only (below). fx Optional foreign-currency view; settlement stays in INR. signature The issuer's signature.

docs.title: Rail evidence
docs.text:
• rail.type is a handler reference; producers SHOULD emit the canonical id. rail.type, rail.rail_ref and rail.status are always present.
  • UPI family (upi.*, in.upi.*, in.cod.upi, in.pos.tap, in.pos.dynamic_qr): a successful payment or refund receipt MUST carry the 12-digit rrn, and MUST carry utr whenever the handler descriptor's settlement.evidence_refs lists it.
  • Other handlers: the receipt MUST carry at least one of rrn, utr or rail.evidence. rail.evidence is a string map whose keys come from the descriptor's settlement.evidence_refs (for example arn and auth_code for cards, umrn for NACH, voucher_id for e-RUPI, ledger_entry_id for store credit and bacp.credit_ledger, awb for a COD record).
  • rail.evidence MUST NOT contain anything the descriptor lists under data_minimisation.never_collect (PIN, OTP, card number, CVV, expiry, Aadhaar number).
  • Cash on delivery moves no money through a rail and has no payment Receipt; the order records the collection against the shipment awb.

Rail references let receipts be joined with the rail's own dispute channel (UDIR for UPI). See Handler Registry.

docs.title: Refund receipts
docs.text: A refund receipt MUST be signed by a registered PSP, and the gateway applies it only to a payment of the same checkout_hash and payee. A payment success or failure receipt is applied only when it is signed by the PSP of the closed Payment Mandate's auth_binding.psp_id (HNP: the open Payment Mandate's rail_binding.psp_id), and each receipt_id and rail reference is applied once; otherwise the gateway answers 400 receipt_invalid and the reservation stays (Usage ledger). A refund receipt MUST identify the original payment (original_rrn, original_utr, or an original_* key in rail.evidence), proving the refund went back to the original method, and MUST carry refund_state: refunded_to_source (the default for a completed refund to source), released_block, pending_cardholder_consent, reversed_to_bank_account, credit_note_issued or adjusted_against_dues. A card refund before the bill is paid MUST be adjusted_against_dues and MUST NOT pass through pending_cardholder_consent.

docs.title: budget_after is never signed
docs.text: The PSP holds no mandate budgets. A Receipt MUST NOT contain budget_after, and the schema rejects one that does. The gateway computes the remaining budget from its own ledger after applying the receipt and returns it unsigned in session.payment.budget_after (Mandates). A verifier MUST ignore any budget figure that claims to come from a receipt.

docs.title: How receipts are used
docs.text:
• The gateway applies a payment receipt to the mandate ledger only after verifying its signature against a registry key of role PSP and checking that it belongs to the mandate. A forged or mismatched receipt is refused with 400 receipt_invalid.
  • A webhook MUST NOT embed a signed Receipt. It carries a ReceiptRef: receipt_id, receipt_hash (sha-256 over the JCS form of the full signed receipt), receipt_type, result, and where present amount, refund_state and rail {type, rrn, status, original_rrn}.
  • The full signed receipt is available to the party of record by authenticated GET on its owning resource (/sessions/{id}, /orders/{id}, /orders/{id}/returns/{rid}). An agent that relies on it MUST check that its hash equals the receipt_hash it was sent.

docs.title: Evidence bundle
docs.text: GET /evidence/{transaction_id} returns the evidence bundle for a transaction: everything a grievance officer, an ODR body, a regulator or the principal needs to verify the purchase, without trusting the agent or its operator.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Field Contents transaction_id The Beckn transaction. agent_credential_hash Hash of the AgentCredential the agent used. mandates[] The open Checkout and Payment Mandates, each wrapped in a JWS by the operator (the payload keeps the principal and MM signatures), and the closed mandates exactly as presented (agent-signed or principal-signed attached JWS). checkout The BPP-signed quote (bpp_signed_quote), checkout_hash, disclosures_hash and the disclosures they hash (including catalogue[]), and bpp_signed_payment_terms: the seller's payment terms from on_init (Beckn payments[], with collected_by and the payee VPA in params.virtual_payment_address) as the gateway received them, kept as {body, authorization}: the raw on_init body and its Beckn Authorization header, which verifies against the BPP's registry key (Beckn signing). REQUIRED for every Reserve Pay leg (Sibling Payment Mandates). receipts[] The full signed receipts: the BPP's checkout receipt, the PSP's payment receipt, and any refund receipts. consent_receipts[] The ConsentReceipts under which data was shared. instruction_log[] The session's full InstructionLog. discovery_response The signed POST /discover response as {status, body, content_digest, signature_input, signature}, where body is the response content exactly as sent, with no content coding, and its sha-256 is the content_hash of the session's agent-written discover InstructionLog entry. REQUIRED when Disclosures.catalogue[] is present and that entry exists. The verifier rebuilds the signature base from status (@status) and the stored content_digest. discovery_sources[] For a session whose items came from POST /discover: the BPP-signed on_search callback behind every source_digest in checkout.disclosures.catalogue[], each as {body, authorization} exactly as the gateway received it (Retention of the signed callbacks). A verifier checks that the sha-256 of each body equals the source_digest and that the authorization verifies against the BPP's registry key, and compares the item values in the body with checkout.disclosures.catalogue[]. trusted_surface_events[] Every signed Trusted Surface event of the transaction, verbatim as received at /trusted-surface/events (step-up results, mandate activation, credit acceptance, AFA completion), each with its Presentation. ts_renders[] The gateway-signed ts_render (compact JWS) of every step-up that a step_up.approved, step_up.declined, negotiation.step_up.approved or negotiation.step_up.declined event in trusted_surface_events[] names, byte-identical to what the Trusted Surface fetched. The content_ref of such an event's presentation is the fragment #/ts_renders/<index>, an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the render's position in this array; an index outside the array, or a content_hash that differs from the sha-256 of the render found there, is evidence_unverifiable. In a bundle released to a seller or a payer PSP, a summary step-up's render is left out and ts_render_digests[] carries it instead. notice_renders[] For every autonomous negotiation act of the transaction: the gateway-signed notice (agreed_by_agent or purchase_offered_by_agent) and the receipt of its delivery to the principal by the mandate's notice_route, as {code, render, content_hash, delivery}. A notice is not a step-up and has no event. A reviewer answers "I never agreed" from its content_hash. ts_render_digests[] Only in a bundle released to a seller or a payer PSP: for each summary step-up over a multi-seller basket, {step_up_id, render_hash, cover}, where render_hash is the sha-256 of its ts_render and cover is the covers[] entry of this transaction's leg. The other sellers' lines stay out of the bundle. verification The gateway's own result: steps_passed (0 to 6), chain_valid, and for step 6 catalogue_result and catalogue_unchecked[]. bundle_signature The operator's signature over the whole bundle minus bundle_signature.

A human-readable rendering of a bundle, the informative summary profile in.bacp.evidence.summary.1, is described in Human participants. It is built only from the signed artefacts in the bundle and is never itself evidence.

For a negotiated purchase the bundle also carries the negotiation transcript, the accepted offer, the within_bounds attestation and the bound on_init, so that a reviewer can check what was offered and agreed without seeing the principal's reservation price (Negotiation).

docs.title: AP2 five-step verification
docs.text:
A bundle verifies only if all six steps pass (the five AP2 steps and step 6), the InstructionLog chain is valid, and the bundle signature verifies:

  1. Closed Checkout Mandate. It is signed by the open Checkout Mandate's cnf key (HNP) or by the principal who signed the parent (HP); its parent_mandate_id is the open mandate; and the open mandate's principal and MM signatures verify.
  2. Checkout hash. The BPP signature on the quote verifies against a registry key of role BPP; sha-256(JCS(quote)) equals checkout_hash; and the closed Checkout Mandate carries that checkout_hash and the quote total.
  3. Checkout receipt. The BPP-signed checkout receipt is a success and its reference equals the hash of the closed Checkout Mandate.
  4. Closed Payment Mandate. It is signed by the open Payment Mandate's cnf key (or the principal); its parent is the open Payment Mandate, whose signatures verify; its checkout_hash and amount match; and its checkout_mandate_ref is the closed Checkout Mandate.
  5. Payment receipt. The PSP-signed payment receipt is a success; its reference equals the hash of the closed Payment Mandate; its checkout_hash and amount match; and it carries the rail evidence required for its handler (Rail evidence).
  6. Trusted Surface events. Every trusted_surface_events[] entry verifies against a registry key of role Mandate Manager or PSP. The signer of every step_up.* and negotiation.step_up.* event MUST also be one of the keys that Step-up signers derives from the mandates in the bundle: the issuer of the mandate that the render's mandate_id names, or the PSP that the table names for that step-up from the bundle's Payment Mandates. A registry Mandate Manager or PSP key that is not one of them is evidence_unverifiable. Every InstructionLog entry at stage step_up that records an approval or a decline has a matching event, whose hash the entry's content_hash carries. Every step_up.approved, mandate.activated, loan.accepted and payment.afa_completed event carries a Presentation, and for a step-up its content_hash is the hash of the step-up's ts_render and its checkout_hash is the bundle's checkout_hash. A contested crossing records late_receipt_party in its transcript entry; two receipts at one log_seq that name different entries, or a decrease of received_at along a chain without clock_step_observed, is evidence_unverifiable. A negotiation.step_up.approved event carries a Presentation with offer_hash instead of checkout_hash: the verifier MUST check that it equals the offer_hash of the step-up's ts_render and of the signed offer in the bundle's negotiation transcript, and that the ts_render's acceptance_revocation, where present, equals that offer's value; the quote comparisons below do not apply to such an event. negotiation.step_up.approved and negotiation.step_up.declined are step-up events for the next rule: their ts_render MUST be in ts_renders[], with its hash and signature checked, and a missing one is evidence_unverifiable; the quote comparisons below never apply to them. A negotiation.agreed.declined or negotiation.purchase_offer.withdrawn event carries a Presentation with offer_hash, which the verifier checks against the offer in the negotiation transcript. For every other step-up event, ts_renders[] MUST hold a ts_render whose sha-256 is that content_hash (where the event carries one) and whose signature verifies against the gateway's registry key, and the verifier MUST compare its total, its payee (seller_name) and its checkout_hash with the BPP-signed quote in checkout, and its price_breakup_hash with checkout.disclosures_hash; a missing render or any mismatch fails the step. Where the step-up's ts_render carries covers[] (a summary step-up over a basket), the verifier instead finds the covers[] entry whose session_id is the bundle's session and compares its checkout_hash and amount with the BPP-signed quote and its payee.vpa with the payee VPA of the PSP payment receipt; the summary's total, seller_name and checkout_hash, and the Presentation.checkout_hash equality above, are not checked against this leg's quote. In a bundle that carries the summary only as a ts_render_digests[] entry, the event's content_hash MUST equal its render_hash and the same comparison is made with its cover; that the cover is an entry of the render is checked by a reviewer that holds the full render (the principal, the grievance officer or the ODR body). The InstructionLog's first entry whose actor is agent is at stage ai_disclosure. Where the bundle carries checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms, its authorization MUST verify over its body against the registry key of the BPP that the body's context.bpp_id names, as of the signature's created time, and the payee VPA of the PSP payment receipt MUST equal the payee VPA in those terms; for a Reserve Pay payment the terms MUST be present and the open Payment Mandate's payee.vpa and payee.bpp_id MUST equal the VPA and the bpp_id in them (Sibling Payment Mandates). For a session step-up of kind confirm or rail_auth the verifier also checks the catalogue disclosure: every Disclosures.catalogue[] entry of checkout.disclosures that is sponsored or undeclared, or has a prior_price, MUST have an entry in the ts_render's catalogue_disclosure[], so that an omission fails; where the session's agent-written discover InstructionLog entry exists for the bundle's transaction_id, checkout.disclosures.catalogue[] MUST hold exactly one entry for each line item of the BPP-signed quote whose item appears in a source named in that entry's refs.source_digests; each entry's sponsorship, prior_price and unit_price MUST equal (JCS) those of the Disclosures.catalogue[] entry that its index names (unit_price against discovered_unit_price; on a summary step-up, of the leg that covers[cover_index] names, which only a verifier that holds that leg's bundle can check); and counterparty_text[name_ref].text MUST equal a language value of the item's name in the BPP-signed quote for that item. For each Disclosures.catalogue[] entry whose source_digest appears in refs.source_digests of the session's discover InstructionLog entry written by the agent, the signed source in discovery_sources[] whose sha-256 is that digest MUST verify against the BPP's registry key as of the signature's created time; its context.message_id MUST equal the derivation from the idempotency_key in that log entry; and its item values MUST match those of the Disclosures.catalogue[] entry, derived by the normative mapping. An entry whose digest is not there was not checked by the agent; the verifier records it as unchecked, and it does not fail the step. Where the session's agent-written discover InstructionLog entry exists, discovery_response MUST be present, its signature MUST verify against the gateway's profile key, and the sha-256 of its body MUST equal that entry's content_hash; each entry's sponsorship.status MUST then be no weaker than, and its sponsorship.by[] a superset of, those of the same item in discovery_response. Where there is no such entry, the sponsorship comparison is recorded as unchecked and does not fail the step. This makes the verifier, not the gateway, the judge of whether the sponsorship and prior price shown at checkout are those the seller sent. Any other failure of step 6 is evidence_unverifiable; a catalogue check that fails or is unchecked is recorded in verification.catalogue_result and catalogue_unchecked[] and does not stop the issue (see Attaching evidence to an IGM issue). Step 6 proves what the principal was shown and, through EvidenceBundle.checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms, whom the seller asked to be paid; neither the quote nor ts_render carries the payee's VPA or settlement account.

The gateway runs this verification when it builds the bundle and records the result in verification. A reviewer SHOULD re-run it independently rather than trust verification.

docs.title: Attaching evidence to an IGM issue
docs.text:
• Before raising an issue the gateway MUST assemble the bundle and verify it fully. If it does not pass all six verification steps with a valid chain, POST /issues returns 422 evidence_unverifiable and nothing is sent (Orders and Post-order). The one exception is the catalogue checks of step 6: a catalogue entry that fails or is unchecked does not stop the issue; the gateway records it in verification (catalogue_result, catalogue_unchecked[]) and sends the issue. A gateway MUST NOT refuse to raise an issue because of a catalogue check.
  • The Beckn issue carries the bundle by reference: evidence_bundle_ref (the /evidence/{transaction_id} URI) and evidence_bundle_hash (sha-256 over the JCS form of the bundle). The bundle itself is also returned on the Issue to the agent.
  • When the issue is escalated to GRIEVANCE, the same bundle, identified by the same hash, goes to the GRO. ODR bodies receive it the same way, out of protocol.
  • For a payment issue, the RRN or UTR in the bundle and on the issue is the join key with the rail's dispute channel.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
The bundle contains personal data and the principal's instructions. The gateway MUST release it only to:

  • the principal, or the agent acting under the principal's mandate for that transaction;
  • the counterparties of record (the seller and the payer PSP of that transaction);
  • the grievance redressal officer or ODR body handling an issue on it;
  • a regulator, on lawful request.

Anyone else gets 403 evidence_forbidden. Selective disclosure keeps the basket away from the PSP and the instrument away from the seller where the format allows it. A summary step-up's full ts_render, which lists every seller of a basket, goes only to the principal (or the agent acting for the principal), the grievance officer, the ODR body and a regulator; a seller or a payer PSP gets its ts_render_digests[] entry instead.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
Record Kept by Retention Mandates, notices, consent and sharing records Mandate Manager At least 7 years, exportable in machine-readable form Personal data received by a seller Each recipient Data Fiduciary dpdp.data_retention of the mandate and retention.recipient_max of the ConsentReceipt, never below the one-year minimum of DPDP Rule 8(3), and erased afterwards Idempotency keys and stored responses Gateway At least 24 hours (48 hours recommended) Replay-cache nonces Gateway Until the signature's expires (at most 300 seconds) InstructionLog, receipts and evidence bundles Agent operator (gateway) and PSP Long enough to serve grievances, disputes and regulatory review; see below BPP-signed on_search callbacks behind a returned source_digest Gateway As long as the evidence bundle of any session that used an item from them, and in any case as long as the InstructionLog Negotiation transcripts Agent operator Proposed: 2 years for B2C, longer for B2B and public procurement (Q-56)

Where these records contain payment data, RBI's directive on Storage of Payment System Data (RBI/2017-18/153, 06-04-2018) already requires RBI-authorised payment system providers to store that data only in India (the foreign leg of a cross-border transaction may also be stored abroad).

Until Q-15 is settled, a gateway, Mandate Manager or PSP adapter MUST store InstructionLogs, receipts and evidence bundles that contain payment data only in India, and MUST NOT send that payment data to any processor outside India (see Data localisation).

Proposed

A single retention table for InstructionLogs, receipts and evidence bundles, with downstream erasure on a deadline, is open (Q-17).

See Security and Privacy for encryption and access control of operator records.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page walks through one complete BACP transaction, from mandate setup to a refund. It is a guided tour of the normative pages, not a replacement for them: each step links to the page that defines the rules.

docs.title: The scenario
docs.text:
• Who. Meera lives in Bengaluru (PIN code 560034). She uses Sakhi, a Hindi voice agent run by Vaani Voice Commerce Pvt Ltd. Sakhi's BACP gateway runs at Vaani's Buyer App, bap.vaani.example.in.
  • What. Sakhi orders chakki atta 2 kg (₹110), milk 1 L (₹68) and toor dal 500 g (₹89) from Meera's regular ONDC kirana, bpp.kirana.example.in.
  • How Meera pays. Through an open mandate bound to a UPI Reserve Pay block of ₹3,000 for 30 days, payable to the kirana. The mandate caps each order at ₹1,500 and asks Meera to confirm anything above ₹1,200. A UPI Circle binding works the same way and is described at the end.
  • Then. One milk packet arrives damaged, and Sakhi returns it. The ₹68 goes back to Meera's UPI account.

All amounts on the wire are integer paise: ₹302 is {"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"}.

Example values

Identifiers such as mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3, ses_… and ORD-KIR-88231, and the RRN shown below, are illustrative. They match the examples in the OpenAPI document.

docs.title: What every call carries
docs.text:
Every agent call in this walkthrough is an HTTPS request to the gateway with:

  • an RFC 9421 Signature-Input and Signature made with Sakhi's cnf key, with a tag parameter that limits what the request may do;
  • a Content-Digest header (RFC 9530) over the raw body;
  • the AgentCredential in the BACP-Agent header;
  • on every POST and PUT, an Idempotency-Key of 22–64 characters.

The rules are in Identity and Request Signing. The gateway verifies the signature on the raw bytes before it parses the body, and rejects a tag that the endpoint does not accept or that Sakhi's credential does not list in purposes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Meera
    participant A as Sakhi (agent)
    participant G as BACP gateway (BAP)
    participant TS as UPI app (Trusted Surface) and Mandate Manager
    participant P as Payer PSP and NPCI
    participant S as Kirana (BPP)
    A->>G: GET /.well-known/bacp
    A->>G: POST /mandates (bacp-browse)
    G-->>A: 202 PENDING with Trusted Surface link
    U->>TS: Approve with UPI PIN
    TS->>P: Create Reserve Pay block payable to the kirana
    TS->>G: Signed mandate.activated (bacp-ts)
    G-->>A: Webhook mandate.status_changed ACTIVE
    A->>G: POST /discover (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: Beckn search and on_search
    A->>G: POST /sessions (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: Beckn select and on_select
    A->>G: PUT /sessions/id (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: Beckn init and on_init
    A->>G: POST /sessions/id/complete (bacp-pay)
    G->>P: Basket-blind debit of ₹302
    P-->>G: Signed receipt with RRN
    G->>S: Beckn confirm and on_confirm
    G-->>A: completed with order
    A->>G: POST /orders/id/returns (bacp-post-order)
    G->>S: Beckn update and on_update
    G->>P: Refund ₹68 to source
    G-->>A: Webhook return.updated

docs.title: Step 0: Read the gateway profile
docs.text:
GET /.well-known/bacp — unsigned, no tag.

Sakhi fetches the gateway's profile and checks that the gateway supports a protocol version Sakhi speaks, the REST transport, the capabilities in.bacp.mandate, in.bacp.discover, in.bacp.checkout and in.bacp.order, and the handler in.upi.reservepay. It also reads message_id_namespace, which it needs in step 7.

On Beckn: nothing.

docs.title: Step 1: Disclose and capture the instruction
docs.text:
Sakhi's first message in every session discloses that Meera is talking to an AI and offers a human: "Aap ek AI sahayak se baat kar rahe hain…" ("You are talking to an AI assistant…"). The text and the routes to a human come from Sakhi's AgentCredential (disclosure.ai_notice, disclosure.handoff_routes). Because Sakhi is a voice agent, one route is a phone number with "press 0", not only a web link. The operator logs the disclosure at stage ai_disclosure, the first entry whose actor is the agent. See Human Participants and the Trusted Surface.

Meera says: "Har mahine ka kirana tum mangwa dena, teen hazaar tak." ("Order the groceries every month, up to three thousand.") Sakhi's operator records the turn as the first instruction log entry (stage prompt, channel voice, spoken language hi-IN, with the Roman-script transcript tagged hi-Latn-IN), with hashes of the audio and transcript and the translation model used. Sakhi turns it into structured constraints and logs that as stage intent.

On Beckn: nothing.

docs.title: Step 2: Request the mandate
docs.text:
POST /mandates — tag bacp-browse.

{
  "purpose_code": "P-GRO-01",
  "rail": "in.upi.reservepay",
  "presence_allowed": ["HNP", "HP"],
  "proposed_constraints": {
    "amount_per_txn": {"value": 150000, "currency": "INR"},
    "budgets": [{"period": "P1M", "max": {"value": 300000, "currency": "INR"}}],
    "categories_allow": ["ONDC:RET10"],
    "delivery_pincodes": ["560034"],
    "step_up": {
      "above_amount": {"value": 120000, "currency": "INR"},
      "outside_categories": true
    },
    "reject_preticked_addons": true
  },
  "data_scopes": ["NAME", "PHONE", "DELIVERY_ADDRESS"],
  "action_scope": ["DISCOVER", "QUOTE", "ORDER", "PAY", "CANCEL", "RETURN", "RAISE_ISSUE", "SHARE_DATA"],
  "validity": "P30D",
  "language": "hi-IN",
  "webhook_url": "https://agents.vaani.example.in/bacp/hooks"
}

rail carries the canonical handler id in.upi.reservepay. The legacy alias upi.reservepay.block still resolves to it during its deprecation window, but new artefacts emit the canonical id (Handler Registry). action_scope lists the actions used later in this walkthrough, including RETURN and RAISE_ISSUE. webhook_url is where the gateway sends mandate.status_changed, which arrives before any session exists.

What the gateway does. It verifies the signature and credential, then checks the request against the bounds of purpose P-GRO-01 (grocery replenishment): the per-transaction cap, a periodic budget, categories inside ONDC:RET10, and a validity of no more than 90 days. A request outside the purpose bounds is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch before anything reaches Meera's phone. It then forwards the request, with Sakhi's cnf key, to the Mandate Manager.

Response. 202 with status: PENDING and a trusted_surface_url that expires after at most 15 minutes. Sakhi never signs or activates the mandate.

On Beckn: nothing. Mandates are off-network. See Mandates and Consent.

docs.title: Step 3: Meera approves on her UPI app
docs.text:
Sakhi says "Kripya apne UPI app mein manzoori dein" ("Please give your approval in your UPI app") and Meera opens the link in her UPI app, which is the Trusted Surface.

  1. The app shows, in Hindi, the limits, the category, the data items that will be shared (name, phone, delivery address), the recipient, and how to withdraw.
  2. Meera taps approve and enters her UPI PIN.
  3. The payer PSP creates a Reserve Pay (SBMD) block of ₹3,000 for 30 days. The block is payable to the kirana's collection VPA: a Reserve Pay block serves one seller. The PSP signs an attestation of the block reference, limits, expiry and payee.
  4. The Mandate Manager checks that the constraints are within the rail limits, then builds an open Checkout Mandate and an open Payment Mandate. Meera's principal signature covers both, and the Mandate Manager countersigns both. The Payment Mandate carries rail_binding.type: in.upi.reservepay and the PSP attestation. Both carry Sakhi's cnf key, audit_uri, data_scopes and a data-retention period. It also issues a DPDP consent receipt.
  5. The Mandate Manager posts a signed mandate.activated event to POST /trusted-surface/events on the gateway. That endpoint accepts only registry keys of a Mandate Manager or PSP, under tag bacp-ts. An agent that calls it gets 403 trusted_surface_only.
  6. The gateway logs the mandate hashes and sends Sakhi the webhook mandate.status_changed with status ACTIVE.

Sakhi confirms: "Ho gaya. ₹3,000 tak, sirf kirana, ₹1,200 se upar poochungi." ("Done. Up to ₹3,000, groceries only, and I will ask you about anything above ₹1,200.")

On Beckn: nothing.

docs.title: Step 4: Discover
docs.text:
Ten days later Sakhi runs a scheduled reorder. Meera is not present (HNP).

POST /discover — tag bacp-browse.

{
  "query": {"hi-IN": "दो किलो चक्की आटा, एक लीटर दूध, आधा किलो तूर दाल"},
  "category": "ONDC:RET10",
  "delivery": {"pincode": "560034"},
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3"
}

On Beckn. The gateway looks up Sakhi's credential status and the sellers' keys in the registry, then sends a Beckn search through the Beckn gateway with context.bacp (presence: HNP, the agent, the idempotency key). It collects on_search callbacks, verifies each seller's network signature and returns results flagged within_mandate, with the ranking parameters it used (distance, price, rating), and each item marked not_sponsored, sponsored or undeclared, with the seller's MRP where it sent one. See Discovery and Profiles.

docs.title: Step 5: Create the checkout session
docs.text:
POST /sessions — tag bacp-browse.

{
  "transaction_id": "6f1c2a8e-0c7b-4f7e-9d0e-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "bpp_id": "bpp.kirana.example.in",
  "provider_id": "P-112",
  "items": [
    {"id": "I-ATTA-2KG", "quantity": 1},
    {"id": "I-MILK-1L", "quantity": 1},
    {"id": "I-TOOR-500G", "quantity": 1}
  ],
  "presence": "HNP",
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "channel": "voice",
  "language": "hi-IN",
  "webhook_url": "https://agents.vaani.example.in/bacp/hooks"
}

On Beckn. The gateway sends select and waits for on_select, which carries the seller's quote (₹267) and its time to live.

Response. 201 with the full session in status incomplete and the quote. See Sessions and Checkout.

docs.title: Step 6: Add delivery, data sharing and the payment handler
docs.text:
PUT /sessions/{session_id} — tag bacp-browse. The body is a full replace of the session's mutable fields: the same items, plus fulfilment (delivery to Meera's saved address), data_share (name, phone and address, with the consent receipt reference) and payment.handler: in.upi.reservepay.

What the gateway does.

  • It checks that every shared field is inside the mandate's data_scopes and covered by a consent receipt. Sharing an email address here would fail with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.
  • On Beckn it sends init with minimal billing data and payment terms, and waits for on_init. The seller returns a signed quote of ₹302 (₹267 plus ₹35 delivery), its disclosures, and a pre-ticked ₹15 "delivery insurance" add-on.
  • It removes the pre-ticked add-on, re-runs init without it, and tells Sakhi with the message preticked_addon_removed. It compares unit prices and fee lines with on_select to detect drip pricing. The ₹35 delivery line is not a drip fee; a new packing, convenience or COD fee line would be.
  • It checks the seller's disclosures, including country of origin, expected delivery and price breakup. A missing disclosure would send the session to requires_escalation with disclosures_missing.
  • It runs the mandate verifier as an advisory pre-check. The pre-check never reserves budget.

Response. 200 with status ready_for_complete and the checkout_hash, the hash of the BPP-signed quote.

Consent receipt

A per-seller consent receipt is minted at init, before any personal data reaches the seller; no data is released on a class receipt alone (Q-12).

docs.title: Step 7: Close the mandates
docs.text:
Sakhi now turns the open mandates into closed ones for exactly this checkout. Both are attached compact JWS objects signed with Sakhi's cnf key:

  • a closed Checkout Mandate with amount ₹302 (30200 paise), the checkout_hash and parent_mandate_id pointing at the open checkout mandate;
  • a closed Payment Mandate with the same amount and checkout_hash, parent_mandate_id pointing at the open Payment Mandate, checkout_mandate_ref naming the closed Checkout Mandate, payee set to the kirana's collection VPA, and auth_binding.type: parent_rail_binding, which means the debit runs under the Reserve Pay block.

Sakhi also prepares a key-binding JWT (kb_jwt) for the seller with aud = bpp.kirana.example.in and nonce = the Beckn confirm message id. This is optional. The message id is a UUIDv5 under the gateway's published message_id_namespace, so Sakhi can compute it (Closing an open mandate).

On Beckn: nothing.

docs.title: Step 8: Complete and pay
docs.text:
POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete — tag bacp-pay. A browse-tagged complete fails with 401 signature_invalid.

{
  "presence": "HNP",
  "checkout_mandate": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUuY2hlY2tvdXQuMSJ9.c2ln",
  "payment_mandate": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln",
  "checkout_hash": "sha-256:vRBpqmLq4AipYw1ZNnIL3trdLVrcHQAQ0g5RurJB4CQ",
  "accepted_disclosures_hash": "sha-256:vq4x2opsK4KIM-scKiTGRWd4Fzxs-GBx7lO8Glgm_U4",
  "kb_jwt": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJub25jZSI6Im4ifQ.c2ln"
}

checkout_mandate and payment_mandate are the closed mandates from step 7, each an attached compact JWS (the values above are shortened placeholders).

What the gateway does. The transport layer has already checked the signature, the bacp-pay tag, the AgentCredential, the nonce and the idempotency key. The gateway then runs the deterministic verifier, which fails closed and stops at the first failure (Deterministic evaluation):

  1. The amount is a positive number of paise.
  2. The open mandates are correctly signed, ACTIVE, not revoked and within their validity, and PAY is in action_scope. HNP is in presence_allowed.
  3. The closed mandates are signed by the cnf key, bind to the open mandates, carry the checkout_hash of the BPP-signed quote and an amount equal to the quote total, name the right payee, and have not been used.
  4. Constraints: category ONDC:RET10 and PIN code 560034 are allowed, ₹302 is below the ₹1,500 per-order cap, and the ₹3,000 monthly budget has ₹0 spent or reserved.
  5. Split-order detection: no other order to the kirana under this mandate in the last 10 minutes pushes the total above ₹1,200.
  6. Rail caps: the Reserve Pay block (₹3,000, payable to the kirana) has enough balance and has not expired. Reserve Pay needs no per-debit additional factor: Meera entered her UPI PIN when the block was created.
  7. Step-up rules: ₹302 is below the ₹1,200 threshold, so Meera is not asked.
  8. Disclosures, add-ons, data sharing and the instruction-log chain are in order.
  9. The party collecting the money is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank, according to the registry. Otherwise the gateway returns 403 collector_not_authorised and no money moves.

Finally it consumes the closed Payment Mandate (a closed Payment Mandate can pay at most once), reserves ₹302 against the monthly budget, and moves the session to complete_in_progress. The constraint, split-order, rail-cap and step-up checks and this commit run under a per-mandate lock, so concurrent calls cannot together exceed the budget.

On the rail. Outside the lock, the gateway asks the payer PSP to debit ₹302 from the Reserve Pay block. The request carries only payee, amount, rail reference, mandate reference and checkout hash: no basket. NPCI returns RRN 629318004417, and the PSP signs a payment receipt with the RRN.

This is the first debit on the block, so it is covered by the authorisation Meera gave when the block was created. A second or later unattended debit on a Reserve Pay block follows the notice-gated pattern: the gateway issues a pre-debit notice and debits only after it matures (Q-03; see Rail Bindings).

On Beckn. The gateway sends confirm with payment.status: PAID, the RRN, collected_by, and context.bacp carrying mandate_ref (with Sakhi's kb_jwt) and the current instruction-log head. The kirana answers on_confirm with order ORD-KIR-88231.

Response. 200 with status completed, the order and the payment state. The gateway turns the reservation into a settled spend from the signed receipt and returns the remaining budget, ₹2,698, as payment.budget_after and as the message budget_after. It also sends Sakhi the webhook payment.receipt, which carries a receipt reference, not the signed receipt.

If the PSP times out, the payment becomes in_doubt. Sakhi then calls GET /sessions/{session_id} and, if needed, retries complete with the same Idempotency-Key. A new key would be a new purchase intent and could never debit twice for the same closed mandate. See Payments.

docs.title: Step 9: Fulfilment
docs.text:
The kirana sends unsolicited on_status updates until the order is delivered. The gateway forwards each as a signed webhook order.updated to Sakhi's webhook_url. Webhooks never embed signed receipts: they carry a receipt reference with its hash, and Sakhi fetches the full receipt with GET /orders/ORD-KIR-88231 (tag bacp-browse) when it needs it.

If Sakhi held the same order id from two sellers, it would call GET /orders/ORD-KIR-88231?bpp_id=bpp.kirana.example.in, and its signature would cover the query string through @query.

On Beckn: unsolicited on_status from the seller, and status when Sakhi reads the order. Tracking through track is proposed and has no REST operation yet (Beckn / ONDC Binding).

docs.title: Step 10: Return the damaged milk
docs.text:
Meera says "Doodh ka packet phata hua aaya, wapas karo." ("The milk packet arrived torn, send it back.") Sakhi reads back the return (1 L milk, ₹68 back to the same UPI account) and Meera says "Haan" ("Yes"). Both transcripts are tagged hi-Latn-IN. Returns are always human-present (presence: HP), and a voice "Haan" is not proof of presence. Sakhi's first attempt, without hp_proof, gets 403 presence_not_proven with a post_order step-up whose signed render names this return on this order. Meera confirms the return on her UPI app (the Trusted Surface), and Sakhi retries with hp_proof: that step-up's id and the hash of the signed approval event. The proof works for this return only, and only once (Presence proof).

POST /orders/ORD-KIR-88231/returns — tag bacp-post-order.

{
  "items": [{"id": "I-MILK-1L", "quantity": 1}],
  "reason_code": "002",
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "presence": "HP",
  "hp_proof": {"ts_event_hash": "sha-256:M4pQ8rT2vX6zB1dF5hJ9kL3nP7sW0yA4cE8gI2mO6qU", "step_up_id": "stp_01HZPORET01q8W3nK5vRt7YcLm2"},
  "evidence": [
    {
      "type": "image",
      "hash": "sha-256:KArKH3tsITnbzaQ_h7yf91N2zdrnaEcfKy5IDFOJd7A",
      "uri": "https://agents.vaani.example.in/e/1.jpg"
    }
  ],
  "refund_to": "original_method"
}

What the gateway does. It checks that RETURN is in the mandate's action_scope, that the order is inside the seller's return window and that the item is returnable. Returns stay allowed even if Meera has since revoked the mandate: they are protective actions.

On Beckn. It uses the seller's return reason codes (get_return_reasons) and sends update with update_target: item. The seller answers on_update with Return_Initiated.

Response. 202 with status: RETURN_INITIATED and a pending ₹68 refund.

Later the seller sends on_update with Return_Approved, then Liquidated: perishables are not picked up. The gateway issues the refund exactly once, on the first of Liquidated or Return_Delivered:

  • On the rail. It asks the PSP to refund ₹68 to the original source, quoting the original RRN. The PSP signs a refund receipt with the refund RRN, original_rrn and refund_state: refunded_to_source.
  • It appends the return and refund adjustments to the order, logs the post-order stage, and sends the webhook return.updated. Sakhi can read the full state at GET /orders/ORD-KIR-88231/returns/{return_id}.

Sakhi tells Meera: "₹68 wapas aa gaye, reference number available hai." ("The ₹68 has come back; the reference number is available.") See Orders and Post-order.

docs.title: Step 11 (optional): Raise a grievance
docs.text: If the refund had not arrived, Sakhi would call POST /issues (tag bacp-post-order) with category PAYMENT, the mandate reference, the RRN and an evidence bundle reference. The gateway assembles and signs the evidence bundle (mandates, the BPP-signed quote, receipts and the instruction-log chain) and raises an ONDC IGM 2.0 issue on Meera's behalf, with the agent as the complainant in actors[] (type AI_AGENT, Proposed: Q-11). Accepting a proposed resolution is an issue action (POST /issues/{issue_id}/actions) with presence: HP and hp_proof. Payment-side disputes are cross-referenced to the RRN for the UPI dispute channel. See Evidence and Instruction Log.

docs.title: What would have changed
docs.text: Situation What happens The order total is ₹1,350 Above the ₹1,200 step-up threshold. The PUT in step 6 (or complete) moves the session to requires_escalation with a step_up of kind confirm and a Trusted Surface link valid for at most 15 minutes. If Meera confirms, the session returns to ready_for_complete and Sakhi calls complete again with the step_up_id, still under the block. Meera can instead pay with her UPI PIN as a one-off human-present payment (in.upi.intent, auth_binding.type: upi.pin), which does not draw on the block. The order total is ₹1,600 Above the ₹1,500 per-order cap. The verifier rejects it with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch; the agent cannot override it. Meera revokes the mandate The gateway learns within 60 seconds, cancels open sessions and blocks new complete calls with 403 mandate_revoked. The rail rejects any debit that races the revocation.
