"यह एक अनुमान है, आपसे लिया जाने वाला दाम नहीं।" loyalty_provisional "A loyalty benefit may apply later. It is not in this total." "लॉयल्टी का लाभ बाद में लागू हो सकता है। वह इस कुल राशि में शामिल नहीं है।" policy_not_stated "The {policy} policy is not stated." "{policy} नीति नहीं बताई गई है।" capability_absent "This shopping service does not offer that feature, so your request was not applied." "यह शॉपिंग सेवा यह सुविधा नहीं देती, इसलिए आपका अनुरोध लागू नहीं हुआ।" party bpp "the seller's app" "विक्रेता का ऐप" party gateway "the shopping service" "शॉपिंग सेवा" party agent "your assistant's provider" "आपके सहायक की कंपनी" party assisted_operator "the assistant helping you" "आपकी मदद कर रहा सहायक" party unknown "a party in the chain" "बीच का कोई पक्ष"

The hi-IN sentences say, in English: "Sponsored: {party} has been paid to show this"; "Whether this is sponsored has not been stated"; "Now ₹{price}. Seller's lowest price in the 30 days before this discount: ₹{prior}"; and "MRP (maximum retail price) ₹{mrp}". The party phrases say, in English: "the seller's app", "the shopping service", "your assistant's company" and "some party in the chain". The discount phrases say, in English: "Discount (code {code}): ₹{amount} less"; "Code {code} was not accepted"; "If this code is used, your assistant's company earns"; and "This shopping service does not offer that feature, so your request was not applied" (capability_absent, which has no slot). The new keys say, in English: "This item was not added by you: it was added by {party}" (added_not_by_you; the party is the one that the line's added_by names: seller is spoken as the seller's app); "This is an estimate, not a price you will pay" (cart_estimate, used only if a cart capability is ever added, Q-95); "A loyalty benefit may apply later; it is not in this total" (loyalty_provisional); and "The {policy} policy is not stated" (policy_not_stated, where {policy} is one of three fixed words: return (वापसी की), cancellation (रद्द करने की) or cash on delivery (कैश ऑन डिलीवरी की)). The part in braces and brackets of discount_applied is left out for an automatic discount, which has no code.

Rules:

  1. The agent says the sentence for each item whose sponsorship.status is sponsored or undeclared, with {party} taken from by[] (several parties are joined with a fixed "and" or "और"; an unknown value uses the unknown-party phrase). There is no sentence for not_sponsored: the agent says nothing.
  2. On audio the sentence is spoken before the item it labels, in the principal's session language.
  3. Amounts are rendered with Indian digit grouping. The prior_price sentence is the only way to voice a prior price. The mrp sentence is the only way to voice an MRP, and it is never voiced as a "was" price.
  4. A principal whose language is not en-IN or hi-IN hears the operator's own fixed and reviewed translation of the same sentence, as for the acceptance-revocation sentences: a Trusted Surface or an agent in another language uses a fixed translation of the same sentence from its own templates, and never a free translation made at run time. Whether a reviewed translation route exists for fixed legal labels in the Eighth Schedule languages is open (Q-68).
  5. {party}, {price}, {prior}, {mrp}, {code}, {amount} and {policy} are the only slots. {code} is filled from the code the agent itself submitted, never from applied[].code, which a seller could fill with text. The title of a discount is seller text, shown only as labelled counterparty text. An item name, if it is spoken, is a separate, labelled seller value and never part of a sentence.
  6. On a step-up, the Trusted Surface repeats the sentences in its own fixed wording (Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface).

docs.title: AI disclosure
docs.text:
The agent's first message in every session is the AI disclosure, with typed routes to a human (Sessions and Checkout):

  • Every session carries ai_disclosure{notice, handoff_routes[]}, taken from the AgentCredential's disclosure.ai_notice and disclosure.handoff_routes. ai_disclosure is always present; handoff_routes is absent when the credential lists none. The disclosure message points at it with param: $.ai_disclosure.
  • An AgentCredential whose agent.channels includes voice, ivr or upi123pay MUST list a tel: route (RFC 3966), optionally with DTMF digits (for example "press 0"), because a feature-phone caller cannot open a web link. A route with DTMF digits is always a tel: route. The schema rejects a credential that lists only https: routes, and a route that pairs DTMF digits with an https: URI.
  • An agent SHOULD NOT split one intended order into several payments to change the fee that a seller bears. The gateway's suspected-split-order check enforces it (Split-order detection); BACP adds no new trigger for it.
  • The gateway writes an InstructionLog entry at stage ai_disclosure, actor: agent. It is the first entry whose actor is agent, before intent. The stage disclosure is the seller's quote, not the AI disclosure.
  • On the network, context.bacp.ai_disclosure: true is REQUIRED, and the gateway MUST mirror it into the bacp tag group, so that a seller learns that an AI agent is ordering even when a validator strips context.bacp (Beckn / ONDC Binding). The gateway MAY also send acting_for, operator_name and operator_grievance_contact. It sends acting_for.gstin and acting_for.display_name only when the mandate's data_scopes include ACTING_FOR, and otherwise omits them.

Example disclosure in Hindi ("You are talking to an AI assistant. Press 0 to talk to a human."): "hi-IN": "आप एक AI सहायक से बात कर रहे हैं। किसी इंसान से बात करने के लिए 0 दबाएँ।"

docs.title: Human handoff
docs.text:
A principal can ask for a human at any time, including after the mandate is revoked.

  1. The agent calls POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff (tag bacp-browse) with action: request and one of the session's ai_disclosure.handoff_routes (no route when the session lists none). The agent picks a route whose languages include the session's language, where one exists, and otherwise says so to the principal. The gateway MUST accept it in every session state and whatever the mandate's status, and returns 201.
  2. An open session moves to status human_handoff. While it is there, the gateway refuses PUT and complete from the agent with 409 session_state_conflict at $.status, and holds any step_up.approved event without applying it (Presentation record). A session in any other state keeps its status and records handoff.
  3. A human support operator accepts with action: accept, signed with a registry key of role support_operator under tag bacp-handoff. Only then does the gateway set handoff.accepted_by (that key's id) and handoff.accepted_at. The gateway reads the key's registry record, which names the agent operator (operator_id) and the one person who holds the key, and answers an acceptance as follows, each time without changing the handoff:
    • a key whose registry role is not support_operator, or a signature under any other tag: 401 signature_invalid;
    • a support_operator key of another agent operator than the session's: 404 not_found, so that the key has no standing and the answer is no oracle for which sessions exist;
    • an accept while accepted_by is already set: 409 session_state_conflict at $.handoff.accepted_by.
  4. The handoff ends with action: release. The gateway accepts a release signed under bacp-handoff by the accepted_by key, or signed by the agent under bacp-browse only while accepted_by is absent (withdrawing an unanswered request). A release leaves the session in human_handoff, changes nothing and is answered as follows: a key whose role is not support_operator: 401 signature_invalid; another agent operator's support_operator key: 404 not_found; a key of the same agent operator that is not accepted_by, or an agent's release after acceptance: 409 session_state_conflict at $.handoff.accepted_by. On release a session in human_handoff returns to incomplete, the gateway sets handoff.ended_at, and then applies a held approval only if its step-up has not expired and its checkout_hash still equals the session's.
  5. The operator binding in steps 3 and 4 and this restart ship together, because each restart is a fresh chance for a competitor's key to accept first. accept and release are each one compare-and-set on handoff.accepted_by and handoff.ended_at, so that they are linearisable on any instances. An accept sets accepted_by only while both are absent. An agent's release sets ended_at only while accepted_by is still absent; if an accept won, the release changes nothing. An accept after ended_at is set gets 409 session_state_conflict at $.status and changes nothing. A request that arrives while ended_at is set starts a new handoff in one compare-and-set that applies only while ended_at is still set, in which the gateway clears accepted_by, accepted_at and ended_at, sets requested_at and route from the request, returns 201, and the earlier handoff stays in the InstructionLog at stage handoff. An accept is therefore refused only for the handoff that has ended, never for one requested afterwards. A session therefore never ends incomplete with accepted_by set.
  6. The gateway writes every act to the InstructionLog at stage handoff, an acceptance or a release by a support operator with actor: gateway and the operator's key id in actor_ref.

Session.handoff is {route, requested_at, accepted_by, accepted_at, ended_at}. A handoff is requested while accepted_by is absent, connected once it is set, and ended once ended_at is set. A new request after a handoff has ended starts the next handoff of the session (Human handoff, step 5). A session in human_handoff leaves it by a release (to incomplete) or by cancel, TTL or a stopped mandate (to cancelled). On the network a handoff maps to Beckn support → on_support, and the MCP tool is bacp_human_handoff (MCP and A2A).

docs.title: Presence proof
docs.text:
presence: HP on a post-order write (cancel, return, raise issue, issue action) or on a trade act (GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection, ledger acknowledgement) is not only a declaration. The principal proves it on the Trusted Surface, through a step-up of kind post_order (Presence, Post-order gate):

  1. A post-order write with presence: HP and no hp_proof gets 403 presence_not_proven. The error carries step_up, a StepUp with kind: post_order and reason: presence_proof, whose ts_render names the write: action, order_id and, for an issue action, issue_id and, for RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED or RESOLUTION_REJECTED, subject_hash; for a trade act, subject_ref and subject_hash; for a RETURN, items and reason_code, and for a CANCEL, reason_code. Nothing is sent to the network. The gateway keeps at most one pending post_order step-up per (subject_ref, action) (for an order write, per (order_id, action, issue_id)): a step-up is pending until it expires, is declined, or its proof is consumed. A repeat of the refused write returns the same step_up_id and ts_render, except that for RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED or RESOLUTION_REJECTED on an issue whose resolution no longer hashes to the pending step-up's subject_hash the gateway voids that step-up and creates a new one. A voided step-up is no longer pending: the gateway refuses every event for it with 404 not_found and nothing changes, and serves its ts_render to no one. The creation of post_order step-ups is limited per (agent, principal) and per order_id, a replacement for a step-up voided because the counterparty revised the resolution is limited per (principal, issue_id) instead, and a principal who declined is not asked again at once (Limits on step-ups). A step-up reaches its final state through the status read described in step 3.
  2. The principal confirms on the Trusted Surface, which posts the usual step_up.approved event with its Presentation. The gateway checks it as for any step-up approval.
  3. The agent retries the write with hp_proof{ts_event_hash, step_up_id}: the post_order step-up's id and the sha-256 over the JCS form of its signed step_up.approved event. Both fields are REQUIRED. The retry uses a new Idempotency-Key: the refused request and the retry differ in body, so the same key gets 422 idempotency_conflict, whose resolution is recoverable and whose message names a new key (Idempotency). The agent learns the ts_event_hash from the step-up status, never from the Trusted Surface: GET /step-ups/{step_up_id} (tag bacp-browse, a different path from the render fetch of the Mandate Manager and PSP) returns StepUpStatus {step_up_id, kind, status, ts_event_hash?}, where status is pending, approved, declined, expired, voided or superseded, and ts_event_hash is present exactly when status is approved. The step_up.updated webhook carries the same object. Only the agent credential whose request created the step-up may read it: any other caller gets 404 not_found, including another credential of the same agent operator. A step-up the gateway voided after a counterparty's revision reads voided, and a write that cites it gets 403 presence_not_proven with a new Error.step_up.
  4. The gateway accepts the proof only for the action, order_id and issue_id named in that step-up's ts_render. A proof issued for another order, action or issue gets 403 presence_not_proven. For a RETURN it also matches the write field by field against the ts_render: the items, as a multiset of {id, quantity}, and the reason_code (a CANCEL matches its reason_code, and its items where the render carries them). A write that differs gets 403 presence_not_proven and sends nothing to the network. No new hash travels on the wire: the render is signed, so content_hash already covers both fields. The gateway's pending key for a RETURN adds a digest of {items sorted by id, reason_code}, so that separate returns of milk and of atta do not collide; the digest is not a wire field. The gateway consumes a RETURN proof only if no other approved RETURN proof of the same order overlaps it in items; a second, overlapping proof gets 403 presence_not_proven. While a RETURN step-up of an order is pending, the gateway creates no second RETURN step-up of that order whose items overlap it: the repeat returns the existing one. For RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED and RESOLUTION_REJECTED the gateway also hashes the issue's current resolution when the write arrives and refuses the proof with 403 presence_not_proven if that hash is not the ts_render's subject_hash (or if a resolution exists where none was shown): a remedy the seller revised after the principal confirmed needs a new confirmation. Any other issue action, in particular ESCALATED, is not bound to the resolution and is accepted on a valid proof for its own action. For a trade act the gateway hashes the submitted subject (the exact document body, the entry's entry_hash, or the head_hash at through_seq) and refuses the proof with 403 presence_not_proven, without consuming it, if that hash is not the ts_render's subject_hash: an act that differs from what the principal saw, for example a GRN with an objection added, needs a new confirmation. A statement acknowledgement whose head_hash is no longer the ledger's head is refused with 409 ledger_head_mismatch.
  5. An hp_proof is single-use. The gateway consumes it inside the atomic section keyed on the order's root Checkout Mandate (Usage ledger), or, for a trade act that has no order, keyed on the ledger_id, so that of two writes citing one proof, on any instances, exactly one succeeds and the other gets 403 presence_not_proven.

A human-present complete is proven by the principal's signatures on the closed mandates and needs no hp_proof.

docs.title: Limits on step-ups
docs.text:
The gateway publishes every figure below in its profile (step_up_limits in /.well-known/bacp), as a count over a window in the style of negotiation.step_up_cap. BACP sets no number: they are the gateway's own design values and are never presented as external limits. A gateway that declares none is tested against the limit that the conformance fixture sets.

  • Creation. The creation of post_order step-ups is counted per (agent, principal) and per order_id, and the creation of session step-ups is counted per (agent, principal) like post_order step-ups (session_per_principal). A replacement that the gateway creates after a counterparty's revision is not counted here. An excess gets 429 with Retry-After. One principal's exhausted quota never blocks another principal of the same agent, whose write still gets 403 presence_not_proven with a step_up.
  • Render fetch. The ts_render fetch is counted per caller key before the step-up is looked up, as before, and also per (caller key, step_up_id) after the standing check. An excess gets 429 with Retry-After.
  • Decline cool-off. Only an explicit step_up.declined starts it. Expiry does not, so a principal who was away has a way back (for the step-up itself, expiry still means decline, TS-2). For a post_order step-up the key is (order_id, action, issue_id), and for a session step-up it is (root open Checkout Mandate or, without one, principal, bpp_id, kind), so that opening a new session does not escape it. Inside the published window, a new step-up for that key is refused with 409 session_state_conflict and Retry-After set to the time left, with no new step-up and no prompt. There is no escape when the subject changes: a changed reason_code or quantity does not reopen the key, because an agent could then flip a field to dodge the cool-off. A principal who declined by mistake waits out the window or uses the grievance route. The Trusted Surface never asks the principal to confirm a decline, and the decline label is neutral (TS-2). The basis is the dark-pattern guideline on "nagging" (Annexure 1, item 10) and, from 01-01-2027, Rule 4(15) of the E-Commerce Rules.
  • Seller re-prompt cap. A revision of an issue's resolution voids the pending step-up and would create a replacement. Replacements are counted per (principal, issue_id) under the published limit. Past it, the gateway creates no new step-up, answers the agent 409 session_state_conflict, shows the principal no prompt, and the issue goes to the grievance route. Each render of a replacement carries the template sentence "the seller has changed this offer N times" (hi-IN: "विक्रेता ने यह ऑफ़र N बार बदला है।"; draft wording), never seller text. Without the cap a seller could revise again and again until a tired principal accepts a worse remedy. Past the cap a principal can no longer accept a later, better offer in the flow and uses the grievance route.

Retry-After is REQUIRED on each of these 429 and 409 responses. The hi-IN sentence says, in English: "The seller has changed this offer N times."

docs.title: Seller-side and trade acts
docs.text:
Where a money clock starts, the record says whether a human or an agent acted. A credit-ledger acknowledgement, a GRN, a CRAC and an MSMED written objection carry a typed actor{kind, role, participant_ref, mandate_ref} (common.json $defs/Actor; Trade Profiles). A human acts as principal, assisted_operator or seller_operator; an agent acts as agent or sub_agent.

An agent records such an act only when the principal is present: the act MUST carry hp_proof of a post_order step-up whose ts_render names it (action GRN, CRAC, MSMED_OBJECTION or LEDGER_ACK, with subject_ref and subject_hash). No mandate scope authorises an agent's trade act, and mandate_ref on the actor only records the mandate the agent acted under (for an order-less ledger act it also names the Mandate Manager that issues the step-up).

A gateway that lists in.bacp.trade_document (GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection) or in.bacp.ledger (ledger acknowledgement) offers one operation, POST /trade-acts (tag bacp-post-order), and, for documents, GET /orders/{order_id}/documents:

  1. The agent posts the act with presence: HP and no hp_proof. presence: HNP is refused with 403 presence_not_allowed.
  2. The gateway answers 403 presence_not_proven with a post_order step-up whose ts_render carries action, subject_ref and subject_hash. Nothing is sent to the seller and nothing is appended to a ledger.
  3. The principal approves on the Trusted Surface, which shows exactly the subject, and the agent retries with hp_proof and a new Idempotency-Key (Presence proof).
  4. The response carries, for a GRN, a CRAC or an MSMED objection, delivery: recorded or delivery: sent.

Recorded, not sent. Until the carriage of a buyer-issued GRN or CRAC on Beckn is settled (Q-33), delivery is recorded: the gateway MUST NOT emit a Beckn GRN or CRAC for a recorded act, a recorded act MUST NOT set or move the MSMED due date in the BACP ledger, and support staff see it as "not sent to seller". A principal who files an objection is told on the Trusted Surface that it is recorded but not yet sent to the seller, and that it does not stop the 15-day clock of the MSMED Act until it is sent in writing (whether an objection sent by an agent is in writing, and whether a recorded objection starts or stops the clock, is open: Q-21, Q-83). A ledger acknowledgement is BACP-native, takes effect at once and carries no delivery.

The documents' bodies carry counterparty text (a reason, an objection). The Trusted Surface labels it as counterparty text, and an agent MUST NOT load a counterparty DocumentRef.uri into model context.

docs.title: Legal time bands
docs.text:
The rules on this page rest partly on law in force and partly on law with a later start date. As of 18-10-2026:

From Instrument What it requires Where BACP answers it In force Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, r.4(9) Consent to a purchase by an explicit and affirmative action; no pre-ticked boxes TS-2; ts_render content rule 3 In force CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 Apply to platforms, advertisers and sellers; interface interference among the listed patterns TS-1, TS-2, TS-4 In force RBI AFA Directions 2025 (authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Authentication validates the credentials of the customer who originates the payment instruction Principal's own factor; the assisted rule goes further as BACP policy In force Information Technology Act, 2000, s.11(c) (India Code) A record sent "by an information system programmed by or on behalf of the originator to operate automatically" is attributed to the originator Presentation and signed Trusted Surface events in the bundle In force Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, s.46 and s.89 "The service providers whether Government or private shall provide services in accordance with the rules on accessibility formulated by the Central Government under section 40 within a period of two years from the date of notification of such rules" (s.46). A contravention is punishable with a fine up to ₹10,000 for the first and ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh for a later one (s.89) TS-3 (modality); Trusted Surface accessibility beyond modality stays a SHOULD, with a conformance case In force Rajive Raturi v Union of India, 2024 INSC 858, 08-11-2024 Rule 15(1) of the RPwD Rules was held ultra vires; the Union was directed to delineate mandatory rules, as s.40 requires, within three months of the judgment. Whether such rules have since been notified is not verified as of 18-10-2026 The mandatory accessibility standard for Trusted Surfaces is unsettled; TS-3 stays the BACP floor In force G.S.R. 359(E), 10-05-2023 Inserted a requirement that websites, apps and ICT-based public facilities and services comply with IS 17802 (Part 1) 2021 and (Part 2) 2022, into the sub-rule that Raturi later held ultra vires. A draft S.O. 3962(E) of 16-07-2026 that is reported to propose IS 17802 is not verified as of 18-10-2026 Informative only 13-11-2026 DPDP Act s.6(9) and DPDP Rules r.4 Consent Managers registered with the Board; records of consents given, denied or withdrawn captured_via.presentation; Q-16 01-01-2027 Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 789(E) Complainant gets a copy of the complaint as recorded; compliance with the dark-pattern guidelines and a yearly self-audit Evidence summary; TS-2, TS-4 13-05-2027 DPDP Act s.9(1) Verifiable consent of the lawful guardian of "a person with disability who has a lawful guardian" A Proposed participant role lawful_guardian with no disability data in the participant record and no ACTING_FOR or assisted-operator stand-in for the guardian's consent; no schema in this version 13-05-2027 DPDP Act ss.5(3), 6(3), 6(4), 6(10); DPDP Rules, 2025, r.3(c) and r.9 Notice and consent request with the option of English or an Eighth Schedule language; the consent request gives the contact of the Data Protection Officer or an authorised person; the notice describes how to exercise rights and complain; that person's business contact information is published; withdrawal as easy as consent; the Data Fiduciary proves that notice was given and consent obtained TS-3, TS-5; ts_render content rule 2; Trusted Surface events in the bundle

The mapping to requirement ids is on Regulatory Mapping.

docs.title: Fail-safe defaults
docs.text:
Every open question marked "Open, fail-safe default" on Open Questions has a default that refuses, escalates to the principal on the Trusted Surface, or keeps a feature off. Such a default is relaxed only in a dated release of BACP:

  • A gateway, Mandate Manager or PSP MUST NOT apply a relaxed form of a fail-safe default by configuration, profile field or bilateral agreement while it claims a conformance level of a release that states the default. No profile field signals a relaxed default; the profile is fetched unsigned and could not prove one.
  • An escalation to the Trusted Surface under a fail-safe default (Q-12, Q-52) leaves a signed Trusted Surface event with a Presentation in the evidence bundle.
  • Conformance cases T1-27 to T1-32 test the six fail-safe defaults of 2026-10-18 (Human-participant cases).

docs.title: Evidence summary profile (informative)
docs.text:
Dispute staff, a grievance officer, PSP support or the National Consumer Helpline need to read a bundle, often in the complainant's language. The profile in.bacp.evidence.summary.1 is an informative, human-readable rendering of an evidence bundle:

  • It is built only from the signed artefacts in the bundle (mandates, the BPP-signed quote, receipts, Trusted Surface events), never from operator-written summaries.
  • It is deterministic and template-built: the same bundle, language and template version give identical bytes. Amounts are in ₹ with Indian digit grouping, times in IST, and each item carries a flag saying whether its signature verified.
  • It carries the bundle_hash (sha-256 over the JCS form of the bundle) that it summarises.
  • For a negotiation it states the outcome of a crossing in one sentence, in English and hi-IN, built from signed artefacts alone (four integers: the two sender_log_seq and the two log_seq):
    • withdraw won: "The seller's withdrawal reached the buyer's system before the buyer sent the acceptance, so there is no agreement." / "ख़रीदार के मंज़ूरी भेजने से पहले ही, विक्रेता का ऑफ़र वापस लेने का संदेश ख़रीदार के सिस्टम तक पहुँच गया, इसलिए कोई सौदा नहीं हुआ।"
    • accept won: "The buyer's acceptance reached the seller's system before the seller sent the withdrawal, so the agreement stands." / "विक्रेता के ऑफ़र वापस लेने का संदेश भेजने से पहले ही, ख़रीदार की मंज़ूरी विक्रेता के सिस्टम तक पहुँच गई, इसलिए सौदा पक्का है।"
    • contested: "The order and the withdrawal crossed: confirm or cancel. No breach is recorded either way." / "ऑर्डर और ऑफ़र वापस लेने का संदेश, दोनों एक-दूसरे के पहुँचने से पहले ही भेजे गए: पुष्टि करें या रद्द करें। आप जो भी चुनें, किसी पर सौदा तोड़ने का मामला दर्ज नहीं होता।"
    • impossible: "Both systems show they received the other's message first, so the record cannot be relied on and is treated as contested." / "दोनों सिस्टम दिखाते हैं कि दूसरे का संदेश उन्हें पहले मिला, इसलिए इस रिकॉर्ड पर भरोसा नहीं किया जा सकता और इसे विवादित माना जाता है।"
  • It is never evidence. A reviewer verifies the bundle, not the summary.

Requesting a summary. GET /evidence/{transaction_id}/summary?language= (tag bacp-browse; MCP tool bacp_evidence_summary_get with the arguments transaction_id and language) returns EvidenceSummary: {profile, bundle_hash, language, template_id, text, items[]}, each item {ref, verified}. The callers are the callers of the bundle (Access), each served only the summary of the bundle built for it, so that a seller or a payer PSP gets no other seller's lines. The grievance officer named in the operator's grievance_contact may also fetch it, acting for the principal: the complainant's copy of the complaint, which G.S.R. 789(E) r.4(5) requires from 01-01-2027, then reaches a principal who has no API client. Anyone else gets 403 evidence_forbidden. A gateway MAY offer the endpoint; the summary is never evidence.

docs.text:
• Q-11: IGM actor types for an AI agent and for seller staff.
  • Q-13: validity of voice, tap or operator-relayed confirmation.
  • Q-21: MSMED deemed acceptance and objections sent by an agent.
  • Q-62: who certifies assisted operators.
  • Q-63: whether a PSP may render a third-party ts_render, and IVR callbacks.

docs.title: Identity and Request Signing
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page defines who an agent is on the wire and how every request proves it: the AgentCredential, the operator behind it, RFC 9421 request signatures with signature tags, replay protection, Content-Digest, idempotency, signing on the Beckn network leg, and key rotation and revocation.

The design goal is that an agent can never do more than its credential and its principal's mandates allow, even if the agent is fully compromised. The agent is untrusted; its key is scoped by purpose, its requests are bound to their exact bytes, and every check happens in the gateway before the request body is parsed.

docs.title: AgentCredential
docs.text:
An AgentCredential identifies one agent, the legal entity that operates it, and the BAP whose gateway it uses. It is an SD-JWT verifiable credential with vct: in.bacp.agent.1. Its claims are defined by agent-credential.json.

Claim Meaning vct Always in.bacp.agent.1. iss The issuer: the network registry or an issuer it accredits (Q-02). sub The agent id, for example did:web:agents.example.in:krishi-voice. iat, exp Issue and expiry times. exp MUST be no later than iat + 180 days. operator The operator's legal_name, entity_id (CIN, LLPIN, GSTIN or PAN) and grievance_officer; optionally an incident_contact and an ai_inventory_ref. bap The BAP subscriber_id and ukid (unique key id) the agent is bound to. agent The agent class (shopping, voice_shopping, assisted, sub_agent), model_family, build, and optionally channels, languages and uap_agent_id. cnf.jwk The agent's public key (RFC 7800). The matching private key signs the agent's requests and closes its open mandates. purposes The signature tags this key may use: any of bacp-browse, bacp-pay, bacp-post-order, bacp-negotiate. disclosure ai_notice (a multilingual AI-disclosure text), human_handoff_url and handoff_routes[] (typed routes to a human: channel, a tel: or https: uri, optional dtmf, only on a tel: route, languages, hours). When agent.channels includes voice, ivr or upi123pay, handoff_routes MUST contain a tel: route. The agent's first message in every session MUST present the notice and offer the handoff (Human participants). conformance The conformance levels the agent's stack has passed, with a signed attestation (see below). status.status_list The status-list uri and index idx used to check revocation.

uap_agent_id is reserved for an agent id issued under a future NPCI agent registry. It MUST be null or absent until such a registry is published.

conformance MUST carry levels[], the ids of the conformance levels passed (bacp.core.1, bacp.pay.upi.1, bacp.pay.all.1, bacp.neg.1, bacp.b2b.1, bacp.auction.1, bacp.ts.1), plus the signed attestation.

RBI's directive on Storage of Payment System Data (RBI/2017-18/153, 06-04-2018) already requires RBI-authorised payment system providers to store payment data only in India. Where an agent operator's own model may process payment data is open (Q-15). Until it is settled:

  • The credential and the registry record MAY carry a data_residency statement (payment_data, llm_region, log_region, transfer_basis). It is OPTIONAL in this version.
  • A gateway MUST NOT treat a missing or incomplete data_residency statement as permission to send payment data outside India. The gateway's own storage and processing of payment data stays in India (Data localisation).

docs.title: Presenting the credential
docs.text:
• An agent MUST send its AgentCredential, as a compact SD-JWT with only the disclosures the gateway needs, in the BACP-Agent request header on every request except the unsigned GET /.well-known/bacp and GET /payment-handlers calls.
  • The legacy header name BACP-Agent-Credential is removed in 2026-10-18. An agent MUST NOT send it, and a gateway MUST NOT accept it in place of BACP-Agent.
  • The credential header is a covered component of the request signature, so it cannot be swapped.

docs.title: Verifying the credential
docs.text:
Before acting on any request, the gateway MUST check, and reject with 401 on failure:

  1. The credential's signature verifies against the issuer's key in the registry (agent_unregistered otherwise).
  2. The status list does not mark it revoked (agent_credential_revoked).
  3. It has not expired.
  4. bap.subscriber_id is the gateway's own BAP.
  5. The request signature's keyid resolves to cnf.jwk.
  6. The signature's tag is listed in purposes (signature_invalid).

docs.title: Agent operators and the registry
docs.text:
Every agent is run by an agent operator, a legal entity that is onboarded and identified through the network registry. The operator:

  • holds the AgentCredential and answers for it through the named grievance officer;
  • keeps its own operator signing key separate from the agent's cnf key and out of the agent's reach. The operator key signs instruction-log entries and evidence bundles; the agent key signs requests and closes mandates. A verifier MUST NOT accept one in place of the other;
  • signs instruction-log entries asymmetrically. HMAC MUST NOT be used, because it cannot give non-repudiation;
  • keeps an AI inventory, red-teams the agent, reports incidents, and runs a kill switch that revokes its agents' credentials.

The registry is the root of trust for every key BACP uses: AgentCredential issuers, BAPs, BPPs, Mandate Managers and PSPs. A gateway MUST resolve every key by its registry key id, for example bap.example.in|ukid-7|ed25519, and MUST NOT trust a key presented only in a request. See Registry lookup, which names the registry-record.json fields that BACP reads, among them the operator_id of a support_operator key (the agent operator that the key serves), the Trusted Surface origins of a Mandate Manager or PSP, and the legal operator, regulatory_status[] and data_residency of any subscriber. An AgentCredential's operator.entity_id and a registry record's operator.entity_ids[] use the same EntityId shape (type of CIN, LLPIN, GSTIN or PAN, and value).

docs.title: Conformance-authority keys
docs.text:
A key of the registry role conformance_authority (Signature.role) signs conformance attestations and nothing else. Such a key qualifies only if it belongs to an entry of the public conformance-authority list; a key that the registry record or a profile presents without a list entry does not qualify. The role grants no right to sign a mandate, a receipt, a request or a rail attestation.

  • An attestation's exp is at most 180 days after its iat.
  • A verifier of an attestation reads its status list and refuses to rely on the attestation when the list marks it revoked, when the copy it holds is more than 24 hours old, or when the list cannot be reached; a stale or unreachable list does not pause a mandate, while a revocation, an expiry or a lapse of the entry or key (next bullet) does (Handler binding). This rule is fail-closed for issuing a mandate and for a new complete on a pilot handler; it never blocks a status check, a reversal, a refund or a post-order write.
  • An entry that is removed from the latest dated release of the list, whose validity has ended or whose status is revoked, and a key that is removed from its entry, no longer qualify: an attestation that rests on them is a lapsed attestation for every mandate bound to it (Rules).

docs.title: Request signatures
docs.text: Every agent request to a gateway, other than the two unsigned discovery GETs above, MUST carry an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature made with the private key matching the credential's cnf.jwk, in the Signature-Input and Signature headers.

docs.title: Covered components
docs.text:
The signature MUST cover:

Component When @method Always @authority Always @path Always @query Whenever the target URI has a query component, for example GET /orders/ORD-KIR-88231?bpp_id=bpp.kirana.example.in content-digest Always (see Content-Digest) bacp-agent Always: the AgentCredential header. Exception: a request under tag bacp-ts, bacp-handoff or bacp-mm-event is signed with a registry key, carries no BACP-Agent header and does not cover bacp-agent idempotency-key On every request other than GET and HEAD bacp-version Whenever the request carries a BACP-Version header. The header is REQUIRED when the gateway's profile lists more than one version (Version negotiation). A header that is present and not covered is refused with 401 signature_invalid content-type SHOULD be covered whenever the request has a body

A signature that does not cover a required component MUST be rejected with 401 signature_invalid. A signer MAY cover additional components.

docs.title: Signature parameters
docs.text:
The Signature-Input MUST carry these parameters:

Parameter Rule created Signing time, integer seconds since the Unix epoch. expires Expiry time. expires − created MUST be greater than 0 and at most 300 seconds. nonce A fresh random value for every request (see Replay protection). keyid The id of the agent's cnf key. tag One of the signature tags.

Example, for POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete:

Signature-Input: sig1=("@method" "@authority" "@path" "content-digest" "content-type" "idempotency-key" "bacp-agent");created=1792501322;expires=1792501622;nonce="q8Fz1V2w";keyid="sakhi-2026-10";tag="bacp-pay"
Signature: sig1=:MEUCIQDexampleSignatureBase64Value=:

docs.title: Signature algorithms
docs.text:
BACP signatures use exactly two algorithms: ES256 (ECDSA with P-256 and SHA-256) and EdDSA with Ed25519.

  • Every verifier of a BACP signature (RFC 9421 requests and webhooks, JWS mandates, receipts, ConsentReceipts, attestations and InstructionLog entries) MUST support both.
  • Every signer MUST use one of the two. A signature with any other algorithm MUST be rejected (401 signature_invalid on a request).
  • The conformance suite will carry test vectors for both. The signature values in the published examples are placeholders: they are well-formed and do not verify. Real vectors come from implementations of the specification and are offered back to it after release.

This settles Q-42. The Beckn network leg keeps the network's own Ed25519 signing (see Network leg signing).

docs.title: Verification order
docs.text:
The gateway MUST verify on the raw request bytes, before any JSON parsing, in this order. The first failure ends processing:

  1. Body size. A body larger than the gateway's limit (at most 256 KiB) gets 413 request_too_large.
  2. Signature-Input and Signature are present and well formed.
  3. Every required component is covered.
  4. tag is the tag the endpoint requires and is in the credential's purposes.
  5. The validity window holds (see Replay protection).
  6. Content-Digest matches the raw body.
  7. keyid resolves through the registry and the credential (401 agent_unregistered if unknown).
  8. The signature verifies.
  9. The (keyid, nonce) pair has not been seen (401 replay_detected).

Failures at steps 2–6 and 8 return 401 signature_invalid. Only then does the gateway parse the body and apply idempotency.

docs.title: Signature tags
docs.text:
A tag states what kind of action a request performs. An AgentCredential lists the tags its key may use in purposes, so an operator can, for example, issue a browse-only credential. Each endpoint accepts exactly one agent tag, or one of two for negotiation messages; any other tag MUST be rejected with 401 signature_invalid, even if the credential lists it. An agent endpoint that is not listed in the table below gets 401 signature_invalid as well: there is no default tag (REST).

Tag Meaning Endpoints bacp-browse Reads, discovery, cart building and other non-committing calls POST /discover; POST /sessions, GET and PUT /sessions/{id}, POST /sessions/{id}/cancel, POST /sessions/{id}/handoff (action: request, and action: release before acceptance); POST /mandates, GET /mandates/{id}, POST /mandates/{id}/relinquish; GET /orders/{id}, GET /orders/{id}/returns/{rid}; GET /issues/{id}; GET /evidence/{transaction_id}; GET /evidence/{transaction_id}/summary; GET /step-ups/{step_up_id}; POST /negotiations, GET /negotiations/{id}, GET /negotiations/{id}/offers, and non-firm messages other than withdraw and accept_revoke on POST /negotiations/{id}/offers; POST /rfqs, GET /rfqs/{id}; GET /auctions/{id}; POST /payment-handlers/intersect; GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}; GET /ledgers/{id}, GET /ledgers/{id}/entries; GET /orders/{id}/documents; POST /checkout-sessions, GET and PUT /checkout-sessions/{id}, POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel bacp-pay Commits money POST /sessions/{id}/complete; POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete bacp-post-order Mandate-scoped writes on an existing order, trade acts and ledger postings POST /orders/{id}/cancel; POST /orders/{id}/returns; POST /issues; POST /issues/{id}/actions; POST /trade-acts; POST /ledgers/{id}/entries bacp-negotiate Binds the principal in a negotiation Firm offers and counter-offers, withdraw and accept_revoke on POST /negotiations/{id}/offers; POST /negotiations/{id}/accept; POST /rfqs/{id}/award; POST /auctions; bids on POST /auctions/{id}/bids; POST /auctions/{id}/award bacp-ts Trusted Surface events and render fetches. Never an agent tag. POST /trusted-surface/events and GET /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id}, signed with the registry key of the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP bacp-handoff A human support operator accepts or releases a handoff. Never an agent tag. POST /sessions/{id}/handoff (action: accept or release), signed with a registry key whose role is support operator bacp-mm-event A gateway reports a mandate event (use, relinquished, pause_changed) to the Mandate Manager. Never an agent tag. The webhook mandate.event, delivered to the mandate's audit_uri and signed with the registry key of the gateway's BAP (Mandate events)

POST /trusted-surface/events and GET /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id} MUST accept only signatures under tag bacp-ts by the registry key of the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP. For a session step-up these are the issuer of the session's mandate and the PSP named in rail_binding.psp_id of the leg's planned open Payment Mandate under the session's root; for a summary step-up over a multi-seller basket (one whose ts_render carries covers[]), only the issuer of the shared root, and no payer PSP; for a post_order step-up, the issuer of the mandate the order was placed under and the PSP named in auth_binding.psp_id of the order's closed Payment Mandate (any of them under split tender) (Step-up signers). A request under bacp-ts carries no BACP-Agent header, and its signature does not cover bacp-agent. A request that carries an AgentCredential, or is signed by an agent key, MUST be refused with 403 trusted_surface_only, whatever its tag. A request signed by any other Mandate Manager or PSP key MUST be answered 404 not_found, never 403, so that the endpoints do not reveal which sessions and step-ups exist.

A handoff acceptance (action: accept on POST /sessions/{id}/handoff) MUST be signed under tag bacp-handoff by a registry key whose role is support operator: a key the registry issues to one human support operator of the agent operator, never to an agent and never as a shared desk key. bacp-handoff is not a value of an AgentCredential's purposes. An acceptance under any other tag, or signed by a key whose role is not support operator, is refused with 401 signature_invalid; one signed by a support operator key of another agent operator is answered 404 not_found; and one that arrives while accepted_by is set is answered 409 session_state_conflict. The same split applies to a release. Revocation of the key takes effect at the next registry refresh, as for other keys. The gateway records the key id as handoff.accepted_by (Human handoff). Only that key, under bacp-handoff, may later release the handoff (action: release). A request under bacp-handoff carries no BACP-Agent header, and its signature does not cover bacp-agent.

The gateway signs its webhooks to the agent with a key published in its profile's keys, so that the agent can verify them. It signs the content-free app_push that it sends to a Mandate Manager's or payer PSP's ts_notify_url the same way, and a receiver that cannot verify the signature ignores the push (Origins and delivery). It signs the response of POST /discover with the same key, under RFC 9421, covering @status and content-digest (Response signature).

Proposed

A dedicated tag for gateway-signed webhooks, bacp-webhook, is proposed (Q-58). Until it is settled, an agent MUST verify every webhook against a key in the gateway profile's keys, MUST NOT act on a webhook that fails verification, and MUST NOT reject a webhook only because its signature has no tag or an unknown one.

docs.title: Replay protection
docs.text:
Rule Requirement Window expires − created MUST be in (0, 300] seconds. Clock skew A receiver MUST allow, and MUST NOT allow more than, 5 seconds of clock skew: reject when now + 5 < created or now − 5 > expires. Nonce cache The receiver MUST keep every (keyid, nonce) pair it has accepted until that signature's expires, and MUST reject a repeat with 401 replay_detected. Record after verify A nonce MUST be recorded only after the signature verifies, so that forged requests cannot fill the cache. Bounded cache The cache is bounded by the 300-second window; entries MAY be evicted once expired. Shared state A gateway that runs as several instances MUST share the nonce cache in an atomic store.

The same 5-second skew applies to every inbound signed message, including negotiation messages and the counterparty's receipts for messages BACP sent. For negotiation it is a freshness bound only: the order of two negotiation messages comes from transcript positions, never from these times (Signed seller acceptance and clock skew).

docs.title: Content-Digest
docs.text:
Every signed request MUST carry a Content-Digest header as defined by RFC 9530, computed with sha-256 over the exact bytes of the request body, for example:

Content-Digest: sha-256=:X48E9qOokqqrvdts8nOJRJN3OWDUoyWxBf7kbu9DBPE=:

A request without a body carries the digest of the empty body. The receiver MUST recompute the digest over the raw bytes it received and MUST reject a mismatch with 401 signature_invalid. Because content-digest is a covered component, changing one byte of the body invalidates the signature.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Every POST and PUT MUST carry an Idempotency-Key. GET requests do not.

docs.title: The key
docs.text:
• The key MUST be 22–64 printable ASCII characters and SHOULD carry at least 122 random bits (for example a UUIDv4).
  • For POST /discover the key MUST be generated afresh for each search from at least 122 random bits (for example a UUIDv4), MUST NOT be predictable from earlier keys, and MUST NOT be reused, even after the gateway's idempotency record has expired. The key binds the sellers' on_search callbacks to this search (Verifying discovery results).
  • Keys are scoped to (agent, canonical operation, path parameters). The same key on a different operation, or on the same operation with other path parameters, is a different key. The BACP-Version of a request is part of its fingerprint, which the gateway compares with the stored request's, and not part of the key's scope: the same key with the same body and another version is not a different key but a conflict (422 idempotency_conflict), and the gateway executes nothing a second time.
  • The gateway carries the key end to end: in context.bacp.idempotency_key and in the derivation of the Beckn message_id (see Network leg signing).
  • One key is one intent. A new key means a new intent and goes through mandate evaluation afresh. A closed payment mandate can still pay only once, so a new key never causes a second debit for the same checkout.

docs.title: Outcomes
docs.text:
Situation Status Code or header Key missing or malformed on a POST or PUT 400 idempotency_key_required First request with this key As the operation defines The response is stored Same key, same body, after the first response The stored status Stored body, plus Idempotent-Replayed: true Same key, different body, or the same body under another BACP-Version 422 idempotency_conflict (unrecoverable: use a new key only for a new intent) Same key while the first request is still being processed 409 idempotency_in_flight, with Retry-After Per-agent limit of live keys or in-flight requests exceeded 429 quota_exceeded, with Retry-After The idempotency store is unavailable 503 idempotency_store_unavailable (writes fail closed) Body larger than the gateway's limit 413 request_too_large

Rules:

  1. Body equality is semantic. Bodies are compared in JCS form, so member order and whitespace do not matter, but null and an absent member differ.
  2. What is stored. 2xx and 4xx responses are stored and replayed. 5xx responses MUST NOT be stored: a retry after a 5xx executes again.
  3. Retention. Keys MUST be kept for at least 24 hours; 48 hours is RECOMMENDED.
  4. Quotas. The store MUST bound, per agent, the number of live keys (default 10,000) and in-flight requests (default 64). It MUST NOT evict a live key early to make room.
  5. Lost responses. If an agent does not receive a response, it MUST first read the resource (for example GET /sessions/{id}) and then retry, if still needed, with the same key. It MUST NOT retry a complete with a new key to recover a lost response.
  6. Unregistered codes. A client that receives a 4xx with a code it does not know MUST NOT retry with a new key.

docs.title: Artefact signatures
docs.text:
A BACP artefact that carries a Signature object (kid, alg, value) is signed over a payload that this section fixes, in the form that this section fixes. The two statements below are the interoperable rule: two independent implementations that follow them verify each other's artefacts.

Form: a detached JWS. Signature.value is a detached JWS in the sense of RFC 7515 Appendix F, in its compact serialisation with the payload segment omitted: BASE64URL(protected header) || ".." || BASE64URL(signature). The b64 header parameter (RFC 7797) is not used, so the signing input is BASE64URL(protected header) || "." || BASE64URL(payload) with the payload below.

  • Protected header. {alg, kid}, and also typ where the specification requires one for the artefact. alg is ES256 or EdDSA and equals Signature.alg. The header kid MUST equal Signature.kid. A value whose header alg or kid differs from the Signature object that carries it does not verify.
  • No embedded payload. A signer omits the payload segment. A verifier recomputes the payload as below, never trusts a payload that the value carries, and refuses a value whose payload segment is not empty.
  • Which artefacts. This form applies to a Signature object. An artefact that is defined as a compact JWS that carries its payload keeps that form: the attached JWS that closes a mandate (whose payload still holds the mandate's own signatures[]), the operator's wrapper of a mandate in an evidence bundle, a CounterSignature, a ts_render (whose header carries typ: bacp-ts-render+jws, Typed JWS) and a gateway-signed notice.

Payload: the JCS form of the artefact minus the members it excludes from its hash. The signed bytes are the RFC 8785 (JCS) form of the artefact without the members listed here, which are the members that the artefact's own hash also leaves out, so one canonical form serves both.

Artefact Signature member Members left out of the signed bytes Mandate, open or closed signatures[] status, usage, signatures, and in a closed Payment Mandate record that the gateway stores, auth_binding.afa_ref (the bytes whose sha-256 is the mandate hash) InstructionLog entry signature signature (the entry_hash is signed) Receipt signature signature (the receipt_hash is over the signed receipt, signature included) ConsentReceipt signature signature Negotiation message signatures[] signatures, counter_signature, received_at (the bytes whose sha-256 is the msg_hash) Trusted Surface event (TrustedSurfaceEvent) signature signature Evidence bundle bundle_signature bundle_signature

Where an artefact carries several signatures (a mandate has the principal's and the Mandate Manager's, a negotiation message the network participant's and the agent's), each signature covers the same payload independently. The Mandate Manager's countersignature does not cover the principal's signature, the signatures can be verified in any order, and removing one leaves the others valid. A StandingAccept and the signed objects of an auction are signed over their JCS form without signature, as their own descriptions say.

Signature.role is outside the signed bytes, so a label proves nothing. A verifier takes a signature's role from the resolution of its kid (a registry key's role, or for principal the device key that the Mandate Manager attested), never from Signature.role. A signature whose role differs from that resolution does not count, and two entries with the same kid are invalid. A verifier that finds an artefact with two entries of the same kid counts the role that the label claims as missing and refuses the artefact with evidence_unverifiable (or mandate_invalid for a mandate).

docs.title: Network leg signing
docs.text:
The gateway, acting as the BAP, signs its Beckn/ONDC messages with the BAP's registry key, as the network requires. On Beckn/ONDC this is an Ed25519 signature over a BLAKE2b-512 digest of the request body, sent in the Authorization header and verified against the sender's registry record. BACP does not replace this signing; the agent's RFC 9421 signature ends at the gateway.

The network's own signing is normative on the Beckn leg. BACP does not require Beckn 2.0 signed acknowledgements; the gateway SHOULD use them, and the request-signature binding of callbacks, where the counterparty supports them. The CounterSignature that negotiation timing relies on is a BACP artefact carried in the negotiation message, not a Beckn acknowledgement (settled in Q-43; see Negotiation).

Rules for the network leg:

  1. Deterministic message ids. The gateway MUST derive each Beckn message_id as a UUIDv5 under its published message_id_namespace over agent_id | idempotency_key | action (the exact name is in Message ids), so a retried call re-sends an identical message.
  2. Duplicate rejection. A BACP-aware receiver MUST reject a duplicate message_id within the message's ttl with a NACK. The gateway treats that NACK as "already received".
  3. Callback binding. Where the counterparty does not support signed acknowledgements, the gateway MUST bind each on_* callback to its request by (transaction_id, message_id), accept only the first, and log duplicates. An unsolicited callback with an unknown message_id is ignored and logged.
  4. Mandate binding. On init, confirm, update, cancel and IGM issue, context.bacp.mandate_ref is REQUIRED. It MAY carry a kb_jwt signed with the agent's cnf key, with aud = the bpp_id and nonce = the confirm message_id, so that a BACP-aware seller can check that the agent holds the mandate's key.

Durable artefacts (credentials, mandates, receipts, log entries, negotiation messages) are signed separately as compact or detached JWS over their JCS form, with a key id that the registry resolves. See Mandates and Consent and Evidence and Instruction Log.

docs.title: Key rotation and revocation
docs.text:
Key or credential Rotation Revocation AgentCredential and its cnf key exp at most 180 days after iat; the operator re-issues with a new cnf key The issuer marks the credential revoked in its status list. The gateway rejects it with 401 agent_credential_revoked. Registry keys (BAP, BPP, Mandate Manager, PSP, credential issuer) At least every 180 days Removed or marked invalid in the registry record; verifiers stop accepting signatures under it once they refresh the record Operator signing key Per the operator's registry record As for registry keys Conformance attestation exp at most 180 days after iat The authority marks the attestation revoked in its status list, or the entry is removed from the latest release of the public list (Conformance-authority keys)

Rules:

  1. A gateway MUST re-check a credential's status no later than the end of the cached registry record's validity, and MUST NOT accept a credential after its status list shows it revoked.
  2. An operator's kill switch revokes its agents' credentials through the status list. Once a credential is revoked, the gateway sends no further network traffic for that agent.
  3. An open mandate's cnf key is part of the signed, immutable mandate. A closed mandate made with any other key fails verification. So when an agent rotates its cnf key, open mandates bound to the old key can no longer be closed, and the principal needs to approve new mandates for the new key.
  4. Mandate Manager and PSP keys sign mandates, attestations and receipts that are used later as evidence. A verifier resolves the signing key by its key id in the registry.

docs.title: Mandates and Consent
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

A mandate is the signed, immutable statement of what a principal (the person or business on whose behalf an agent acts) has authorised the agent to do. Every BACP commitment that moves money, shares personal data or binds the principal is evaluated against a mandate by deterministic, non-LLM code at the gateway. A ConsentReceipt is the DPDP record of the notice the principal saw and the personal data they agreed to release to a named recipient.

Artefact Schema Signed by Mandate (bacp.AgentMandate) mandate.json Principal and Mandate Manager (open); agent cnf key or principal (closed) ConsentReceipt (DPDP) consent-receipt.json Mandate Manager

Negotiation bounds (reservation price, walk-away terms) are not carried by this mandate. They live in a separate negotiation mandate, described in Negotiation, so that verifiers that only understand checkout and payment mandates never meet a constraint they do not know.

docs.title: Mandate kinds and forms
docs.text:
One schema covers four mandate types: the AP2 matrix of open/closed × Checkout/Payment. The vct and the wire-compatible ap2_vct name the type.

Checkout (kind: checkout) Payment (kind: payment) Open (form: open) in.bacp.mandate.checkout.open.1: what the agent may buy, where, how much, with what data in.bacp.mandate.payment.open.1: the standing payment authority, bound to a rail primitive through rail_binding Closed (form: closed) in.bacp.mandate.checkout.1: one exact basket (checkout_hash) and amount in.bacp.mandate.payment.1: one exact payment, authorised through auth_binding
  • An open mandate is long-lived. It carries constraints and the agent key (cnf) that is allowed to close it. It is created only through the Mandate Manager and the Trusted Surface (Issuance).
  • A closed mandate narrows one open mandate to a single transaction. It names its parent in parent_mandate_id and carries checkout_hash and amount; the schema requires all three for form: closed.
  • The closed Checkout Mandate goes to the seller (BPP). The closed Payment Mandate goes to the payer PSP. The PSP never sees the basket and the seller never sees the instrument: the payment leg carries only payee, amount, mandate reference and checkout_hash.
  • Every Payment Mandate, open or closed, MUST carry checkout_mandate_ref, the Checkout Mandate it pays for.
  • An open Payment Mandate MUST carry rail_binding. A closed Payment Mandate MUST carry auth_binding and MUST NOT carry rail_binding.

docs.title: Required content of an open mandate
docs.text:
Besides the fields the schema requires of every mandate (vct, mandate_id, kind, form, iss, iat, valid_from, valid_until, principal, agent, purpose, action_scope, presence_allowed, constraints, revocation, signatures), an open mandate MUST carry:

  • cnf, the agent key that may close it;
  • data_scopes (it MAY be empty);
  • audit_uri, where every use is reported;
  • dpdp.data_retention, the ISO 8601 retention period imposed on recipients;
  • at least one frequency bound: constraints.budgets or constraints.max_executions.

A closed mandate inherits these from its parent and need not repeat them.

docs.title: Immutability and delegation
docs.text:
Everything in a mandate except status, usage and signatures is signed and immutable. The mandate hash, used as Receipt.reference (see Evidence), is sha-256 over the JCS (RFC 8785) form of the mandate minus those three fields. An edit to any signed field, such as a raised cap, makes every signature fail, and the gateway returns 403 mandate_invalid_signature.

parent_mandate_id chains (a closed mandate, or a sub-agent delegation requested with parent_mandate_id on POST /mandates) MUST only narrow: the child's scope, constraints and validity are each a subset of the parent's. A closed mandate's valid_until MUST NOT be later than its parent's.

docs.title: Example: open Payment Mandate
docs.text:
{
  "vct": "in.bacp.mandate.payment.open.1",
  "ap2_vct": "mandate.payment.open.1",
  "mandate_id": "mdt_PAY7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "parent_mandate_id": null,
  "checkout_mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "kind": "payment",
  "form": "open",
  "iss": "mm.psp.example.in",

docs.title: Issuance
docs.text:
An agent never signs or activates an open mandate. It requests one. The principal approves it on a Trusted Surface (the payer PSP's app, or a Mandate Manager app), and the Mandate Manager (MM) issues it.

  1. The agent calls POST /mandates (tag bacp-browse) with a MandateRequest: purpose_code, rail, presence_allowed, proposed_constraints, data_scopes, action_scope, validity (an ISO 8601 duration), language, channel (the channel on which the principal will approve) and webhook_url, and REQUIRED operator_compensation (Operator compensation). The gateway MUST accept webhook_url, so that mandate.status_changed can reach the agent before any session exists. To add a seller to an existing root open Checkout Mandate, the request also carries checkout_mandate_ref (pattern ^mdt_[A-Za-z0-9]{12,40}$). A request for a payee-bound primitive carries payee{vpa, bpp_id}, and a request for a Reserve Pay block also carries the block amount it asks for in rail_limits.block_amount (Sibling Payment Mandates). A request that the principal originates on the Trusted Surface to move a mandate to another gateway carries supersedes{mandate_id} (Porting a mandate); an agent never sends it. Proposed: when action_scope is omitted, all eight actions (DISCOVER, QUOTE, ORDER, PAY, CANCEL, RETURN, RAISE_ISSUE, SHARE_DATA) are requested, and the Trusted Surface shows that full scope to the principal before approval.
  2. Before anything reaches the Trusted Surface, the gateway or the MM MUST reject the request:
    • with 400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible if rail resolves to a handler that cannot back an open mandate at this gateway: one that is not open-eligible or has no binding.open_primitives, a reserved or deprecated descriptor, or a pilot descriptor that the gateway's conformance attestation does not list (Handler binding);
    • with 403 constraint_unknown if proposed_constraints has a key this page does not define (see Fail-closed handling);
    • with 400 invalid_request at $.operator_compensation if the request has no operator_compensation, or one that is not consistent with the disclosure.compensation_model of the signing AgentCredential (Operator compensation);
    • with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch if it has no amount_per_txn; has no periodic budget; has no categories_allow, or one outside the purpose's categories; asks for a longer validity than the purpose allows; exceeds any per-transaction or per-period bound of the purpose (Purpose bounds); asks for a data scope the purpose does not allow; names a purpose_code that is not in the purpose-code registry; or exceeds the static limits of the requested rail, including a rail_limits.block_amount above the handler's per-block limit in the handler registry (at $.rail_limits.block_amount);
    • if rail resolves to in.upi.reservepay (primitive sbmd_block): with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.payee if the request has no payee, and at $.rail_limits.block_amount if it has no rail_limits.block_amount; with 400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible if the gateway holds no BPP-signed payment terms of the seller payee.bpp_id and does not obtain them first (a Beckn init to that seller, never followed by confirm), if that payee is the buyer app (a block collected by the BAP) and presence_allowed includes HNP, or if payee.vpa is not the VPA in those terms; and, for every Reserve Pay request, with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch if the requested rail_limits.block_amount breaks the sum-of-blocks rule, or 403 mandate_exhausted if it does not fit the root's headroom, at $.checkout_mandate_ref for a request with checkout_mandate_ref and at $.rail_limits.block_amount for a request without it, whose root is the one it proposes. These checks run before anything reaches the rail, so the principal's PSP is never asked to create a block that the MM would then refuse.
  3. Otherwise the gateway returns 202 with a MandateHandle in PENDING, carrying a trusted_surface_url deep link, which is an https URL on an origin of the issuing Mandate Manager or a rail deep link that opens the payer PSP's own app (Origins and delivery). The link expires after at most 15 minutes.
  4. The principal opens the link. The Trusted Surface shows the notice in the principal's language (English or a language of the Eighth Schedule): limits, categories, data items, recipient class, withdrawal route and grievance route, and the operator compensation: what the principal pays the operator, and what sellers pay the operator or the buyer app. The notice, with the compensation, is hashed into the ConsentReceipt notice. For a payee-bound primitive the notice also shows the payee name the bank returns for payee.vpa and the seller's bpp_id. For a Reserve Pay block it shows the requested block amount and, unless the payer PSP attests a block-debit feed, the unseen-draw statement (Usage ledger). For a block whose attested funding is credit, the notice says "credit" in the principal's language and, for an interest-bearing credit line, that interest may run from each debit (NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 26.1.2). For a sibling Payment Mandate it shows the other Payment Mandates under the same root, their combined total, and the amount each budget of the root has left (its max less the root's exposure). The principal approves with an explicit action and the rail's own authentication (for UPI, the UPI PIN).
  5. The payer PSP creates or links the rail primitive (for example a Reserve Pay block, a UPI Circle delegation or an AutoPay mandate). It MUST use a primitive listed in the handler descriptor's binding.open_primitives, and signs a rail attestation: a JWS over {rail_ref, type, primitive, limits, expiry, payee, funding} (and, for a gift PPI, custody). It MUST NOT create a Reserve Pay block larger than the requested rail_limits.block_amount.
  6. The MM checks handler eligibility against the current registry, taken from the dated BACP release and never from a gateway endpoint, records that registry's version in rail_binding.registry_version (and, where it reads the release manifest, the registry_serial and the digest of the registry file in rail_binding.registry_serial and rail_binding.registry_digest), and MUST refuse issuance (rail_binding_not_open_eligible) if the attested primitive is not in the descriptor's binding.open_primitives, the descriptor is not open-eligible, or its status is neither live nor an attested pilot. For a pilot handler the MM MUST first verify the gateway's conformance attestation, forwarded in the request's gateway_attestation, find the handler in its pilots[], and write rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti} into the mandate. The MM then copies agent.bap_id from the verified AgentCredential's bap.subscriber_id into the mandate, never from the request, and checks that every BACP constraint is at or below the attested rail limits, and, for a Reserve Pay block, that the attested block_amount is at most the requested one and that the attested expiry is no later than the root open Checkout Mandate's valid_until. It refuses an attested funding of credit (or a missing one, or an overdraft account without a deposit attestation) when the root lacks credit_funding_allowed: true, with 403 credit_funding_not_allowed (Handler binding), and refuses a gift PPI whose attestation does not state custody: principal_side. It builds the open Checkout and open Payment Mandates, or, for a request with checkout_mandate_ref, only the open Payment Mandate (Sibling Payment Mandates). If the MM refuses issuance at this step after the rail primitive exists, it MUST revoke the primitive at the rail and report the outcome in rail_revocation{status} on the mandate.rejected event it sends to the gateway. A refused block whose revocation is unconfirmed is exposure at its attested block_amount until the revocation is confirmed or the block expires, although it never became ACTIVE (Usage ledger). The principal signs both (signatures[].role: principal) and the MM countersigns both (role: mandate_manager). The MM allocates a status-list entry per mandate and issues the ConsentReceipt.
  7. The MM sends a signed mandate.activated event to the gateway's /trusted-surface/events (tag bacp-ts, registry key of role MM or PSP). The event MUST carry the Presentation of the approval: surface, channel, language, modality, the hash of the notice shown and the principal's action. The gateway records an InstructionLog entry at stage mandate and sends the webhook mandate.status_changed (ACTIVE) to the agent. For a sibling Reserve Pay block the gateway applies the activation inside the atomic section keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate (Usage ledger), so that an activation and a complete never both take the same headroom: if the block at its full attested amount no longer fits every budget window that contains the activation, the gateway refuses the event with 403 mandate_exhausted and never treats the mandate as ACTIVE; the MM then revokes the mandate and its block at the rail and sends mandate.revoked with rail_revocation{status}. If that status is unconfirmed, the block is exposure at its attested block_amount until the revocation is confirmed or the block expires.

A verifier MUST accept an open mandate only if a principal signature and an MM signature both verify against registry-resolvable keys of those roles, and the rail attestation verifies against a key of role PSP and matches rail_binding.rail_ref, rail_binding.type and rail_binding.primitive.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Principal
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP Gateway
    participant MM as Mandate Manager
    participant TS as Trusted Surface (payer PSP app)
    participant N as NPCI and issuer
    U->>A: Order my groceries every month, up to ₹3,000
    A->>G: POST /mandates with purpose, rail, constraints, data scopes, webhook_url
    G->>G: Check unknown constraints, schema, purpose bounds, rail static caps
    G->>MM: Mandate request with the agent cnf key
    MM-->>G: PENDING request id and Trusted Surface link (15 min)
    G-->>A: 202 PENDING with trusted_surface_url
    A->>U: Please approve in your UPI app
    U->>TS: Open link, read notice, approve with UPI PIN
    TS->>N: Create rail primitive (block, delegation or mandate)
    N-->>TS: rail_ref
    TS->>MM: Approval with device signature and PSP rail attestation
    MM->>MM: Check constraints are within rail limits
    MM->>MM: Principal and MM sign open Checkout and Payment Mandates
    MM->>MM: Issue ConsentReceipt and status-list entries
    MM->>G: Signed event mandate.activated
    G->>G: InstructionLog entry at stage mandate
    G-->>A: Webhook mandate.status_changed ACTIVE

docs.title: Operator compensation
docs.text:
A principal who knows how the operator behind her agent is paid can discount its advice. The mandate request therefore carries operator_compensation, and the Trusted Surface shows it in the notice before the principal approves.

{
  "from_principal": [{"basis": "per_order", "amount": {"value": 2000, "currency": "INR"}}],
  "from_sellers": "finder_fee"
}
Field Content from_principal[] What the principal pays: one or more {basis, amount?}. basis is per_order (a fee on each order), period (a fee for a period named in the operator's terms) or none. amount is REQUIRED for per_order and period, and absent for none. A none entry stands alone. from_sellers What sellers pay the operator or the buyer app for orders it brings: finder_fee (an ONDC buyer finder fee), channel_margin, none or other.
  • The Mandate Manager MUST NOT activate a mandate whose request has no operator_compensation (400 invalid_request at $.operator_compensation; the mandate never becomes ACTIVE), and MUST show the value in the notice and hash it into the ConsentReceipt notice (notice.operator_compensation is REQUIRED).
  • The source of the declaration is the operator. When the AgentCredential carries disclosure.compensation_model, the request MUST be consistent with it: none means every from_principal basis is none and from_sellers is none; seller_paid means from_principal is none and from_sellers is not none; principal_paid means a from_principal entry is not none and from_sellers is none; mixed means both. Otherwise the request is refused with 400 invalid_request at $.operator_compensation.
  • This is BACP policy, not a statutory duty. No Indian rule found requires an agent operator to disclose a seller-paid commission (not verified as of 18-10-2026), and BACP cites no law for it (Q-79).
  • When a session's intermediary_compensation[] has an entry with source: seller while the mandate's notice says from_sellers: none, the gateway adds the warning operator_compensation_mismatch (requires_buyer_review) and logs it at stage disclosure. It tells the principal once per mandate on the Trusted Surface and reports the mismatch to the Mandate Manager. The Mandate Manager then asks the operator for a corrected notice, which takes effect only on the principal's re-approval.
  • When the AgentCredential has no compensation_model, the notice says that the operator has not declared its compensation model to its credential issuer.
  • Per-order amounts are shown again at the time of the order as an operator charge. What sellers pay is carried per order in intermediary_compensation[] and is never read out per order.

docs.title: Sibling Payment Mandates
docs.text:
A Reserve Pay block pays one seller, so a principal who shops hands-free across several sellers holds one open Payment Mandate per payee-bound instrument, all under one root open Checkout Mandate whose budgets cap the total (Multi-seller basket).

  • Requesting a sibling. A MandateRequest with checkout_mandate_ref asks for one more open Payment Mandate under an existing root. checkout_mandate_ref MUST name an ACTIVE root open Checkout Mandate of the same principal; otherwise the MM refuses it with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.checkout_mandate_ref. The MM builds only an open Payment Mandate, whose checkout_mandate_ref is that root and whose constraints narrow the root's (Immutability and delegation). It never builds a second Checkout Mandate or a second budget for the same basket. parent_mandate_id stays reserved for sub-agent delegation.
  • Payee. An open Payment Mandate whose rail_binding.primitive is sbmd_block MUST carry payee{vpa, bpp_id} and, when the seller's BPP-signed terms name a provider, payee.provider_id, which MUST equal message.order.provider.id of those terms at every leg. A leg whose provider differs is refused with 403 reservepay_block_wrong_payee and nothing is debited (a BACP rule whose basis is RBI Master Direction on Payment Aggregators 2025 para 13(f), under which a PA ensures that a marketplace takes no payment for a seller not onboarded on it, and para 13(e), a merchant ID per merchant; the block-payee match itself is BACP policy); one seller app can serve several shops from one collection VPA, which is why the VPA alone is not enough (whether ONDC seller apps share one VPA is not verified as of 18-10-2026). A request without it is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.payee. payee.vpa MUST equal the VPA in the seller's BPP-signed payment terms (Beckn payments[].params.virtual_payment_address of on_init), and the attested payee MUST equal payee.vpa; otherwise issuance is refused with 400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible and nothing is sent to the rail (Handler binding).
  • The payee is bound to BPP-signed terms, always. The gateway MUST hold the BPP-signed payment terms of the seller payee.bpp_id before a Reserve Pay request goes to the Trusted Surface, including for a set-up outside any checkout. If it holds none, it obtains them first by a Beckn init to that seller that it never follows with confirm, or refuses the request with 400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible. The terms are the raw on_init body as received together with its Beckn Authorization header, verified against the registry key of the BPP named in context.bpp_id, which MUST be payee.bpp_id. No per-object JWS is needed (Q-43; Beckn signing). The gateway keeps them as bpp_signed_payment_terms for every Reserve Pay leg (Evidence bundle).
  • Requested block amount. A Reserve Pay request carries rail_limits.block_amount, the block the principal is asked to set up. The gateway and the MM check it at step 2 of Issuance, the notice shows it, and the payer PSP creates no larger block. It MUST NOT exceed the handler's per-block limit in the handler registry; otherwise the request is refused at step 2 with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.rail_limits.block_amount. If the attested block_amount is larger than the requested one, the MM refuses issuance at step 6 and revokes the block at the rail.
  • Every Reserve Pay request is checked against a root. The per-block limit, the sum-of-blocks rule and the headroom check below apply to every Reserve Pay request, with or without checkout_mandate_ref.
