The gateway escalates with resolution requires_buyer_review and releases nothing before the confirmation.

Example: a class receipt issued at mandate setup.

docs.title: Marketing consent
docs.text:
Marketing is not part of a purchase, a mandate or a spend, so it has its own consent event. It is never a purpose.code of a mandate, and a ConsentReceipt for personal data (the receipt above) never covers it.

Fail-safe (normative). With no active marketing ConsentReceipt for a seller, the gateway and the Mandate Manager report every marketing purpose of that seller as granted: false. A seller's own default, a UCP buyer.consent member (source: "business" is a default, not consent), a class receipt (recipient.bpp_id: "*") and a receipt for personal data never grant one. The principal is never asked for marketing consent inside a payment step-up: a Presentation of a bacp-pay step-up that carries a marketing grant is refused, because consent is its own event on the Trusted Surface, one purpose and one channel at a time, with "no" as the first or an equal option.

Proposed

The receipt below is Proposed: it can change shape in a later dated release without a !, because a Proposed rule is not yet part of what a conforming implementation must do. Whether it satisfies DPDP s.6(1) and the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 together is a question for counsel (Q-101); the fail-safe above does not depend on the answer.

A marketing ConsentReceipt has consent_kind: "marketing" (consent-receipt.json). The Mandate Manager issues it, and the principal gives it on the Trusted Surface (captured_via, never the agent). It has no mandate_ref, no data_items and no purpose. Instead it carries purposes[] (each {code, text, granted}, none preselected) and channels[] (sms, whatsapp, voice_call, email, push), and it reuses notice, captured_via, withdrawal (as easy as giving consent), grievance and retention. recipient.bpp_id MUST NOT be "*": a marketing receipt names one seller. A purpose that the principal was not asked about does not appear and is not granted.

docs.title: Consent Manager registration
docs.text:
DPDP Rule 4 and Act s.6(9) apply from 13-11-2026. How the MM relates to a registered Consent Manager is open (Q-16). Until it is settled, these fail-safe rules apply:

  • An MM MUST NOT act, or describe itself, as a Consent Manager unless it is registered with the Data Protection Board.
  • On receipts issued on or after 13-11-2026, cm_registration_no MUST be the Board registration number when the MM acts as a Consent Manager, and MUST be null otherwise. A null value means the receipt records consent given to the recipient Data Fiduciary, not through a Consent Manager.
  • An MM that acts as a registered Consent Manager MUST NOT also act as credential provider (re-verifying closed mandates, issuing within_bounds attestations); that role runs as a logically separate component with its own registry key.

docs.title: Data minimisation
docs.text:
• principal.ref is a pairwise pseudonymous id at the MM. It is never an Aadhaar number, and no BACP artefact carries one.
  • principal.device_jkt[] is optional: the RFC 7638 thumbprints of the device keys that the principal enrolled on the Trusted Surface at issuance. It is not a constraint, so a gateway that does not know it ignores it. Where it is present, a Presentation's device_signature MUST verify against one of the keys (Presentation record); its absence never weakens an approval, so a feature-phone principal keeps an equal path.
  • data_scopes lists the only personal data fields the agent may release: NAME, PHONE, DELIVERY_ADDRESS, EMAIL, AGE_OVER_18, GSTIN, ACTING_FOR. ACTING_FOR allows the gateway to tell the seller the GSTIN and display name of whom the agent acts for (context.bacp.acting_for.gstin and display_name, and their mirror tags); without it they are omitted. The purpose limits which scopes may be requested. The gateway sends acting_for to a seller only under a per-seller ConsentReceipt whose data_items[] lists ACTING_FOR, so that the principal's consent to this disclosure is on record for that seller. For a sole proprietor, whose GSTIN or name is personal data, this serves the DPDP Act, 2023, s.6(1) and s.6(10) from 13-05-2027. A request carries no buyer GSTIN of its own: the only GSTIN that reaches a seller is acting_for.gstin, which the mandate's data_scopes fix, and a request that names a GSTIN other than that one, or any GSTIN under a mandate without ACTING_FOR, is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch before anything is sent to the seller. On an ONDC B2B order the gateway projects acting_for.gstin into the order's buyer_id.
  • When a session update shares data (data_share), the gateway MUST check that SHARE_DATA is in action_scope, that every field is in data_scopes, and that consent_receipt_ref names an active, not withdrawn, ConsentReceipt of this mandate (the class receipt, or a per-seller receipt for the session's seller). Before any personal data is sent to the seller at init, the gateway MUST hold an active per-seller ConsentReceipt from the MM whose recipient.bpp_id is that seller. Otherwise it returns 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.data_share.fields or $.data_share.consent_receipt_ref, before anything is sent to the seller.
  • No personal data travels through the Beckn gateway in search. Delivery data goes only to the chosen seller, at init.
  • The payment leg is basket-blind: the PSP receives payee, amount, mandate reference and checkout_hash only.
  • Webhooks MUST NOT carry personal data outside the receiving agent's data_scopes.
  • The MM is data-blind: it holds mandates, notices, consent records and usage, never order or payment payloads.
  • When the principal withdraws consent on the Trusted Surface (consent.withdrawn), the receipt becomes WITHDRAWN and further data release under it is refused.

The MM keeps mandate, notice, consent and sharing records for at least 7 years in machine-readable form, and MUST give them to the principal on request, on the Trusted Surface, in machine-readable form. A REST export interface is not part of this version (Q-16), and the full retention schedule is open (Q-17). See also Evidence: retention and Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page lists every question that BACP version 2026-10-18 cannot answer on its own, and the questions it has settled. Each open question names the body whose answer BACP needs and the working position this version takes until then. Other pages link here with anchors such as open-questions.md#q-16.

No question blocks 2026-10-18

No open question blocks version 2026-10-18. One, Q-77, is marked Blocking for settlement only: its fail-safe default applies, and the mark means that settling it needs the approvals that GOVERNANCE.md requires for a Blocking question. No other question is marked Blocking. A question is Blocking when, without its answer, a dated release cannot make a normative, testable statement, or would publish a design that conflicts with a rule already in force. Ten questions were Blocking before this release. Five are now settled with a concrete rule (Q-41, Q-42, Q-43, Q-44 and Q-47, plus Q-28 and Q-53, which were not Blocking). The other five (Q-12, Q-15, Q-16, Q-20 and Q-52) stay open but are non-blocking: each has a fail-safe default that the normative text states and that applies until the question is settled. A fail-safe default refuses, escalates to the principal on the Trusted Surface, or keeps a feature disabled; it never assumes the favourable answer.

How open questions are handled. Every open question has a working position. Where a wrong guess could move money, release personal data or bind a party, the working position is a fail-safe default and is stated as a rule on the page that links here. An answer from the owner is applied in a later dated release under the versioning policy: a change that relaxes a fail-safe default is backwards-compatible; one that tightens it is a breaking change and gets the notice period. A newly found question that would block a normative, testable statement is marked Blocking here and must be resolved, or given a fail-safe default, before the next dated release.

Owners. NPCI, RBI, ONDC, Legal counsel, MeitY/DPDP, or the BACP Working Group (BACP WG). Where several bodies are involved, the owner is the one that must give the answer.

docs.title: Q-01 Liability for agent error
docs.text:
Question. Who bears the loss when an agent mis-buys within a valid mandate: the agent operator, the buyer app, the PSP or the user? Owner. RBI, with NPCI and ONDC.

Working position. BACP makes evidence complete by default (InstructionLog, receipts, evidence bundle) and makes no claim about the legal allocation. Proposed network policy: the operator remediates out-of-mandate actions without the user having to prove fault. See Evidence and Instruction Log.

docs.title: Q-02 Agent identity anchor
docs.text:
Question. Which body anchors agent identity and issues the AgentCredential: an NPCI UAP registry, the ONDC registry or DeDi, or DIDs and VCs? Owner. ONDC, with NPCI.

Working position. An issuer-agnostic SD-JWT VC, with the ONDC registry or DeDi as the default issuer, and a uap_agent_id slot reserved for NPCI. See Identity and Request Signing.

docs.title: Q-03 Pre-debit notice for Reserve Pay and OTM
docs.text:
Question. Does the RBI E-mandate Framework 2026 pre-debit notice of at least 24 hours apply to Reserve Pay (single-block multi-debit) repeat debits, and to OTM? NPCI's Reserve Pay product page says the payer is "notified each time money is deducted" and mentions no pre-debit notice. Owner. NPCI.

Working position. Fail-safe: an unknown pre-debit-notice status is treated as "required 24 h" from the second unattended debit on the block. See Rail Bindings. Findings of 18-10-2026: the UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 section 15 (OTM) has no pre-debit notice (it requires post-debit notices, para 15.7), section 16 (Reserve Pay) has no authentication-factor clause, and the scope of the E-mandate Framework 2026 para 2 (recurring payments) for OTM is not confirmed.

docs.title: Q-04 Reserve Pay issuers and account types
docs.text:
Question. Which issuers support Reserve Pay, and do any issuers apply a practice stricter than NPCI's rule of one block at a time per merchant per mobile number? Owner. NPCI.

Working position. The account types are answered by NPCI UPI OC 228 (08-10-2025) and the UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 16.1: all UPI-permitted sources of funds, including savings, current and overdraft accounts, RuPay credit cards and pre-sanctioned credit lines. OC 228 enables Reserve Pay, to begin with, only for "online verified merchants with low ticket and high frequency transactions". No public NPCI list of the issuers that support Reserve Pay was found as of 17-10-2026 (an absence finding, not a quotation), so the issuer list stays open, and a vendor page that reports issuers allowing only one block per user is not supported by any NPCI text found. BACP supports every account type, reads the source of funds (deposit or credit) from the PSP's attestation, and treats a credit-funded block as a credit leg. See Rail Bindings.

docs.title: Q-05 UPI 123PAY limit
docs.text:
Question. RBI raised the UPI 123PAY per-transaction limit from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 on 09-10-2024 and said NPCI would issue instructions. Has NPCI implemented ₹10,000 for every 123PAY channel? Owner. NPCI.

Working position. Default ₹10,000, configurable in the handler descriptor.

docs.title: Q-06 IGM version
docs.text:
Question. IGM 2.0 comments out the DISPUTE level, while escalation to ODR is current practice. Which version does BACP target? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. Target IGM 2.0 and treat ODR as an out-of-protocol reference. See Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: Q-07 Member-only NPCI circulars
docs.text:
Question. What do NPCI circulars OC 237, OC 238 and OC 141E, and the UPI Procedural Guidelines, say? They are available only to members. Owner. NPCI.

Working position. Obtain them through a member bank. The upi.uap.* handler slot stays reserved.

docs.title: Q-08 UPI Circle details
docs.text:
Question. What are the cooling period and the per-transaction cap for human secondary users of UPI Circle? NPCI's full-delegation release says only "a short cooling period". Owner. NPCI.

Working position. Both are configurable in the handler descriptor.

docs.title: Q-09 context.bacp on ONDC
docs.text:
Question. Will ONDC accept the context.bacp extension, or must it always be mirrored into message.order.tags[]? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. Mirror it into a bacp TagGroup. See Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: Q-10 PSP verification of closed mandates
docs.text:
Question. Will payer PSPs verify closed Payment Mandates and sign rail_binding attestations? Owner. NPCI, with PSPs.

Working position. A PSP adapter inside the gateway's trust zone signs attestations. Start with a pilot with one PSP. Whether a payer PSP can report every debit on a Reserve Pay block to the gateway (a block-debit feed), and in what form, is part of this question; until it is answered, the pause reason unmatched_rail_debit applies only where a PSP attests such a feed (Usage ledger). The scope includes a modification of a block that the principal makes on the seller's platform (Consolidated Circular para 16.9): the optional rail.block_modified event is defined, and is used only where a feed is attested.

docs.title: Q-11 AI_AGENT in IGM
docs.text:
Question. Will ONDC register AI_AGENT as an IGM 2.0 actor type (the type of an actors[] entry), given that the IGM 2.0 enum has only AGENT, which means a fulfilment agent? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. A namespaced extension value, mirrored in tags.

docs.title: Q-12 Class consent receipts for unknown sellers
docs.text:
Non-blocking: fail-safe default

Was Blocking. The protocol rule is settled in 2026-10-18; the legal question stays open with the fail-safe default below. The default is relaxed only in a dated release (Fail-safe defaults); it is testable by conformance case T1-27 (cases T1-27 to T1-32 cover the six fail-safe defaults).

Question. Does a class ConsentReceipt (recipient *) meet DPDP Rule 3 for human-not-present orders to sellers who are unknown when the mandate is set up? Must the per-seller receipt at init be normative before any data is released? Owner. MeitY/DPDP, with legal counsel.

Settled in 2026-10-18. A per-seller ConsentReceipt, naming that seller's bpp_id, MUST be minted by the Mandate Manager at init before any personal data reaches the seller. A class receipt (recipient.bpp_id: "*") only pre-authorises: if the gateway does not hold an active per-seller receipt for the seller, it sends nothing and returns 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.

Still open. Whether the class pre-authorisation, given when the seller is unknown, is valid consent under DPDP Act ss.5–6 and Rule 3, which apply from 13-05-2027.

Fail-safe default. Until Q-12 is settled, and from 13-05-2027, the first release of personal data to a seller not named in any receipt the principal approved MUST be confirmed by the principal on the Trusted Surface, which shows that seller's Rule 3 notice; the gateway escalates with requires_buyer_review and releases nothing before the confirmation. See Mandates and Consent and Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Q-13 Voice consent
docs.text:
Question. Is voice consent valid for mandate setup or for human-present confirmations? Owner. Legal counsel.

Settled for money

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T6) for money. The gateway refuses voice_confirm_plus_device on a rail_auth step-up and on any confirm step-up whose approval releases a debit (403 presence_not_proven), on the strength of RBI/2025-26/79 paras 5(a) and 6(b) and UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 para 19.2.2. In human-not-present the debit rests on the mandate's authentication model, so there the refusal is BACP policy implementing this question, not an RBI requirement. A PIN entered over a UPI 123PAY IVR stays upi_pin. See Voice confirmation. Whether a voice or operator-relayed "yes" is valid consent for a non-money confirmation stays with counsel.

Working position. Voice is used only for human-present confirmations that move no money. Money always needs a PIN on the Trusted Surface. A voice confirmation needs a challenge that the Trusted Surface draws and the agent never sees (Voice confirmation).

docs.title: Q-14 GST TCS for agent platforms
docs.text:
Question. Is an agent platform an "e-commerce operator" for GST TCS under CGST s.52? Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position. Carry GST fields; no TCS logic.

docs.title: Q-15 Payment-data localisation
docs.text:
Non-blocking: fail-safe default

Was Blocking. Made non-blocking by the fail-safe default below. The default is relaxed only in a dated release (Fail-safe defaults); it is testable by conformance case T1-28 (cases T1-27 to T1-32 cover the six fail-safe defaults).

Question. RBI payment-data localisation is in force. Where must mandates, receipts, the InstructionLog and evidence bundles be stored, and in which region may the language model process payment data? Owner. RBI.

Findings. RBI's directive on Storage of Payment System Data (RBI/2017-18/153, 06-04-2018) requires RBI-authorised payment system providers to store payment system data only in India. RBI's FAQ on the directive (26-06-2019) allows processing abroad if the data is deleted abroad and brought back to India within one business day or 24 hours of processing, whichever is earlier. Whether an agent operator's language model is such processing, and whether an agent operator that is not a payment system provider is covered at all, needs RBI's answer.

Fail-safe default. Until Q-15 is settled, BACP is stricter than the FAQ:

  • A gateway, Mandate Manager or PSP adapter MUST store mandates, receipts, the InstructionLog and evidence bundles that contain payment data only in India.
  • These components MUST NOT send payment data to a language model, log store or other processor outside India, even transiently; the FAQ's one-business-day processing allowance is not used.
  • The data_residency statement (payment_data, llm_region, log_region, transfer_basis) is OPTIONAL in this version. A gateway MUST NOT treat a missing or incomplete statement as permission to send payment data outside India.

Still open: where an agent operator's own model may process the payment data it receives. See Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Q-16 Mandate Manager as Consent Manager
docs.text:
Non-blocking: fail-safe default

Was Blocking. Made non-blocking by the fail-safe default below. The default is relaxed only in a dated release (Fail-safe defaults); it is testable by conformance case T1-29 (cases T1-27 to T1-32 cover the six fail-safe defaults).

Question. DPDP Rule 4 applies from 13-11-2026. Should the Mandate Manager register as a Consent Manager, or integrate with one? Is co-locating the Mandate Manager with the payer PSP, and giving it the role of credential provider that re-verifies closed mandates, compatible with a data-blind Consent Manager? From what date is cm_registration_no mandatory, and how is the 7-year machine-readable export offered? Do RBI-registered Account Aggregators count as Consent Managers? Owner. MeitY/DPDP.

Findings. Rule 4 and the First Schedule (registration and obligations of Consent Managers), and Act s.6(9), apply from 13-11-2026 (G.S.R. 846(E) rule 1 and G.S.R. 843(E); see Q-53). Under the Act a Data Principal may give consent through a Consent Manager; nothing found requires every consent record to pass through one.

Fail-safe default. Until Q-16 is settled:

  • A Mandate Manager MUST NOT act, or describe itself, as a Consent Manager unless it is registered with the Data Protection Board. On ConsentReceipts issued on or after 13-11-2026, cm_registration_no MUST be the Board registration number when the MM acts as a Consent Manager, and MUST be null otherwise. A null value means the receipt records consent given to the recipient Data Fiduciary, not through a Consent Manager.
  • An MM that acts as a registered Consent Manager MUST NOT also perform the credential-provider role (re-verifying closed mandates, issuing within_bounds attestations). That role MUST run as a logically separate component with its own registry key.
  • The MM keeps mandate, notice, consent and sharing records for at least 7 years and MUST give them to the principal, on request on the Trusted Surface, in machine-readable form. A REST export endpoint (GET /mm/records?principal=) is not part of this version.

Still open: whether an MM co-located with the payer PSP may register as a Consent Manager, and whether RBI-registered Account Aggregators count as Consent Managers. See Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Q-17 DPDP forward compliance
docs.text:
Question. How does BACP meet the DPDP duties that start in May 2027: breach signalling, children's data (verifiable parental consent, no profiling), correction propagation (s.8(3)), consent for model training, downstream erasure with an SLA, and a retention table for the InstructionLog, receipts and evidence? Owner. MeitY/DPDP.

Working position. Proposed messages bacp.erasure_request, bacp.correction, bacp.breach_signal and principal.minor_status. Needed before 13-05-2027. See Security and Privacy.

Minor mode, once principal.minor_status exists, drops every discovery item whose sponsorship.status is sponsored or undeclared, and turns off personalised ranking. This is BACP policy. DPDP s.9(3) bars targeted advertising directed at children and applies from 13-05-2027; whether a sponsored slot that is not targeted is "targeted advertising" is a question for counsel (Q-66). The list does not empty for want of a status, because the ranking party declares sponsored or not_sponsored for its own ranking and undeclared arises only for a relayed upstream signal (Catalogue disclosures). Until minor_status exists, a minor gets no minor mode.

docs.title: Q-18 List of authorised payment aggregators
docs.text:
Question. Is there a machine-readable list of RBI-authorised payment aggregators to check collected_by against, or must the buyer app attest? Owner. RBI.

Working position. The gateway checks a verified rbi_pa or bank entry in the regulatory_status of the collector's registry record, attested at onboarding. A declared entry is never treated as verified.

docs.title: Q-19 Waiver of acceptance revocation
docs.text:
Question. Can an offer waive the acceptor's right under Indian Contract Act s.5 to revoke an acceptance? Owner. Legal counsel.

Findings. Section 5 reads: "An acceptance may be revoked at any time before the communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards." Under s.4 that communication is complete as against the acceptor "when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer". Neither section says "unless otherwise agreed", and no statute or other source found permits a waiver of that right. The Information Technology Act, 2000, s.10A covers "the revocation of proposals and acceptances" in electronic form; s.13 fixes, "save as otherwise agreed", only when an electronic record is despatched and received. The Uttar Pradesh amendment to s.5 (U.P. Act 57 of 1976) concerns proposals that must be kept open for a specified time, not acceptances.

Working position (settled as design choice (c) by owner decision of 17-10-2026). A firm offer MUST state acceptance_revocation; there is no default. In this version every receiver refuses allowed_until_receipt with capabilities_incompatible, on every binding: a review of the matched-pair rule found that the proposer could still choose the receipt order after seeing both the acceptance and the revoke. The rules that would honour it are kept as sunset text, with the conditions under which a later version may lift the refusal. waived is permitted only with a signed waiver_basis (a contract or the buyer's own RFQ) and only outside consumer sessions; on Beckn, a waived offer with no basis, and in a consumer session any waived offer, may be accepted only by a human shown the consequence sentence. In a consumer session on REST, MCP or A2A no value is permitted, so only non-firm offers are possible there. The waiver may still not hold. See Acceptance revocation.

Asked of counsel.

  1. Can a proposal, a protocol default or a prior framework agreement exclude the right under s.5, second paragraph?
  2. Is the time of receipt under the Information Technology Act, 2000, s.13(2) the "knowledge" of the proposer under s.4?
  3. Is a countersigned HTTP exchange an instantaneous communication in the sense of Bhagwandas Goverdhandas Kedia v. Girdharilal (1966 AIR 543)?
  4. Does the Uttar Pradesh Explanation to s.5 bind a quotation made in response to an RFQ?
  5. Does a waiver set by the offeror bind a human acceptor who joined only through a seller app's terms and conditions?
  6. Is a right that is advertised but not enforced worse, for the acceptor, than a waiver that is shown?
  7. Does a "delete for everyone" in a messaging app, or a call asking the other party to stop before the message is read, count as a revocation under ss.4–5?

Protocol terms (18-10-2026). Every firm message now names protocol_terms{version, hash}, which state, among other things, the stipulation of IT Act s.12(2). Two further points for counsel: whether IT Act s.11 attribution makes a hash that an agent sends the principal's agreement for s.13, and whether a consumer's approval on the Trusted Surface that cites the terms is "otherwise agreed" under s.13. Section 11 was not re-read for this change (not verified as of 18-10-2026). Whether a buyer may revoke an agent's purchase offer until the seller's on_init is dispatched is also for counsel (Withdrawal of a purchase offer).

docs.title: Q-20 Fees and the MRP ceiling
docs.text:
Non-blocking: fail-safe default

Was Blocking. Made non-blocking by the fail-safe default below. The default is relaxed only in a dated release (Fail-safe defaults); it is testable by conformance case T1-30 (cases T1-27 to T1-32 cover the six fail-safe defaults).

Question. Do delivery, packing or convenience fees count toward the MRP? What exactly is the Legal Metrology exemptions: Rule 3 (application of Chapter II: packs above 25 kg or 25 L, cement, fertiliser and farm produce in bags above 50 kg, packs for industrial or institutional consumers) and Rule 26 (exemption from the Rules as a whole, for example packs of 10 g or 10 ml or less, and loose commodities ordered through e-commerce channels)? Owner. Legal counsel.

Findings. Rule 18(2) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 bars selling a packaged commodity above its MRP (Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 4362, answered 26-03-2025). Rule 3, as substituted by G.S.R. 629(E) (23-06-2017), takes three classes out of Chapter II only: packages above 25 kg or 25 L; cement, fertiliser and agricultural farm produce in bags above 50 kg; and packages for industrial or institutional consumers. Rule 26 exempts certain packages from the Rules as a whole. Both were read in the official PDFs and, per the Department of Consumer Affairs list of amendments, Rule 3 is unchanged since 2017 (checked 18-10-2026; the Gazette portal itself was not searched). No official source was found on whether delivery, packing or convenience fees count toward the MRP.

Fail-safe default. Until Q-20 is settled, the MRP ceiling (validator V-01) is applied in its stricter reading:

  • In a B2C negotiation, every line that carries an mrp is checked against it, whatever its retail_package_mrp_required value. The Rule 3 and Rule 26 exemptions, signalled by retail_package_mrp_required: false, are honoured only in B2B.
  • Mandatory packing and convenience charges count toward the MRP: for the lines checked against MRP, the sum of unit price including tax times quantity, plus every mandatory packing and convenience charge of the term sheet, MUST NOT exceed the sum of mrp times quantity.
  • delivery and the other charge codes stay separate disclosed charges outside the MRP comparison.

An answer that fees sit outside the MRP relaxes this default (backwards-compatible). See Negotiation.

docs.title: Q-21 MSMED traders and deemed acceptance
docs.text:
Question. Are Udyam-registered traders excluded from MSMED Act s.15 (Office Memorandum of 02-07-2021)? Is deemed acceptance machine-checkable? Owner. Legal counsel.

Findings. MSMED Act s.2(b) Explanation: the day of acceptance is the day of actual delivery, or, if the buyer objects in writing within fifteen days of delivery, the day the supplier removes the objection; with no objection in that time, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery. The fifteen days enter s.15 only through the "appointed day" (the day after fifteen days from acceptance or deemed acceptance), which applies when there is no written agreement (Gazette of India, 16-06-2006). The MSME Office Memorandum 5/2(2)/2021-E/P&G/Policy of 02-07-2021 restricts benefits to retail and wholesale trade MSMEs to priority-sector lending; its legal effect on s.15 is open. Also open: how a buyer's written objection travels on the network.

Working position. Traders get a warning only. Acceptance is the GRN or the on_acceptance event, which records the delivery date and any written objection.

docs.title: Q-22 Firm-offer breach penalty
docs.text:
Question. Should a breach of a firm offer carry a network-defined penalty, or only the bilateral cancellation_terms? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. An IGM issue plus a reputation event; the buyer may cancel without penalty.

Also asked of ONDC. Whether the RET cancellation terms govern a BACP firm contract after CONTRACTED; and a Beckn carrier for accept_revoke (an init with a bacp.neg.accept_revoke TagGroup in the same transaction_id) that network validators accept. In this version an offer with acceptance_revocation: allowed_until_receipt is refused on every leg; on a Beckn leg the refusal stays until such a carrier exists (sunset condition (e)).

Beckn carriers for negotiation receipts and withdrawals (18-10-2026). Two carriers are not defined for Beckn legs and go to ONDC: a bacp.receipt TagGroup in Ack.tags (RET 1.2.5 Ack has tags; ONDC core v0 has status only; whether validators and live participants accept it is not verified as of 18-10-2026), and a buyer's withdrawal of a purchase offer (an init withdrawn before on_init) with a buyer terminate. Until then every Beckn crossing that depends on an unreceipted message is contested, and the stop control is absent on a Beckn consumer purchase-offer notice. ONDC is also asked whether cancellation terms apply before on_confirm.

docs.title: Q-23 Transcript escrow key
docs.text:
Question. Who governs the regulator escrow key for negotiation transcripts? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. Transcripts are encrypted to the parties plus an escrow key.

docs.title: Q-24 within_bounds proof
docs.text:
Question. Should within_bounds be a trusted attestation or a zero-knowledge range proof? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. An attestation from the buyer's credential provider.

docs.title: Q-25 Neutral auctioneer
docs.text:
Question. Who operates the neutral auctioneer on ONDC? Owner. ONDC. This gates only the Auctions conformance level.

Working position. A network-designated service; GeM and eNAM for their own markets. See RFQ and Auctions.

Dutch award audit (18-10-2026). Dutch awards follow the auctioneer's chain order, and tick_close makes a later reordering provable. It does not prevent a rogue auctioneer from choosing the processing order of near-simultaneous arrivals in the first place, so a neutral auctioneer is still needed.

docs.title: Q-26 Unsolicited on_select
docs.text:
Question. Do ONDC 1.x validators accept an unsolicited on_select for seller-paced rounds and auction ticks? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. Unsolicited on_select mirrored in tags, with buyer polling as the fallback.

docs.title: Q-27 Interest-free seller credit
docs.text:
Question. Is interest-free seller credit (khata, net-N) outside the RBI Digital Lending Directions? Owner. RBI.

Working position. Treated as trade credit; a financier makes it an in.fin.* or in.credit.* handler.

docs.title: Q-29 eNACH cap
docs.text:
Question. What are the eNACH ₹1 crore net-banking and debit-card cap (NPCI FY2023-24/003) and any NACH pre-debit rule? NPCI Circular 010 (2020) is confirmed: ₹10 lakh for net-banking and debit-card e-mandates, ₹1 lakh for Aadhaar eSign, and ₹50 lakh for security mandates (loan category). Circular 003 of FY2023-24 exists by title; its ₹1 crore figure is reported only by vendors. No RBI pre-debit rule for NACH was found: the E-mandate Framework 2026 covers cards, PPIs and UPI only. Owner. NPCI.

Working position. A configurable cap with a default of ₹10 lakh; BACP's own 24-hour notice applies.

docs.title: Q-30 Gift PPI redemption
docs.text:
Question. May a PSP adapter redeem gift PPI codes on the user's behalf? Owner. RBI, with PPI issuers.

Working position. Codes are vaulted at the Trusted Surface or the PSP adapter; the agent never sees them.

docs.title: Q-31 OTM validity
docs.text:
Question. What is the OTM validity (60 days or a 14-day execution window), and may an agent trigger capture? Owner. NPCI.

Working position. Configurable; the shortest window wins.

docs.title: Q-32 Checkout BNPL
docs.text:
Question. Can checkout BNPL fit the Digital Lending para 9(i) specific-end-use exception when the merchant is the beneficiary? Owner. RBI.

Working position. Only when the lender documents the end use and pays the end beneficiary directly.

docs.title: Q-33 GRN and CRAC on Beckn
docs.text:
Question. How does a buyer-issued GRN or CRAC travel on Beckn? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. An update with a bacp.docs tag.

docs.title: Q-34 REQUEST_EXTENSION within ttl
docs.text:
Question. Can a seller answer REQUEST_EXTENSION within ONDC's PT30S ttl? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. An extension is a new signed offer carried on the seller's next message.

docs.title: Q-35 Bid retraction
docs.text:
Question. Does the bidder's right to retract under Sale of Goods Act s.64 apply to e-auctions and override a no_retraction rule? Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position. before_close_outside_window is the default for English auctions. accept_revoke never governs bid_retract: a bid's retraction follows the auction's retraction_rule, whatever its acceptance_revocation value (Acceptance revocation). Also asked of counsel: does the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, s.62 reach a bidder's retraction before the sale is complete?

docs.title: Q-37 RTO fee
docs.text:
Question. Can a return-to-origin fee be charged to a consumer for a refused COD order? Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position. Only if disclosed in the first round and allowed by the mandate.

docs.title: Q-38 e-RUPI
docs.text:
Question. How do agent redemption of e-RUPI and refunds after redemption work? Owner. NPCI.

Working position. Open-eligible only where redemption without the beneficiary present is supported. Until this is answered, in.erupi has registry status pilot, so it backs an open mandate only at a gateway whose conformance attestation lists it.

docs.title: Q-39 Agentic card tokens
docs.text:
Question. When will agentic card tokens be generally available in India, and how do CoFT and AFA apply to them? Owner. RBI, with card networks.

Working position. Pilot-gated: a pilot handler backs a mandate only when the gateway's conformance attestation lists it.

docs.title: Q-40 LIFO split-tender refunds
docs.text:
Question. Is last-in-first-out refund allocation across split tenders acceptable under PA Master Direction para 10(f)? Owner. RBI.

Working position. LIFO by default; tender_specific where lines were bound to a tender.

docs.title: Q-48 Agent signature on negotiation messages
docs.text:
Question. Should an agent also sign the negotiation message body with its cnf key, so that signed messages stay verifiable over A2A without a network participant? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. A negotiation message carries the sending network participant's registry signature; the agent's act is evidenced by its RFC 9421 request signature. See MCP and A2A.

docs.title: Q-49 Refund settlement signal
docs.text:
Question. What signal confirms that a refund credit has settled, so that reversal_pending can move to reversed (and the saga extend to IMPS and PPI)? Owner. NPCI.

Working position. The reversed state is normative; its trigger is not yet defined. The evidence that releases a budget once a refund has settled is defined: a refund receipt signed by the payer PSP of the debit that cites original_rrn for the full amount, or a collector-PSP receipt plus the principal's confirmation on the Trusted Surface (Usage ledger). Whether a payer PSP can sign such evidence is Q-90.

docs.title: Q-51 PA marketplace limits
docs.text:
Question. How are the payment aggregator marketplace limits (PA Master Direction paras 10(b), 13(f)) represented, and what is the "only onboarded sellers" check? Owner. RBI.

Working position (18-10-2026). BACP has no settlement_eta. The seller's settlement terms are ONDC's settlement_basis, settlement_window and withholding_amount, carried unchanged (Who pays). The question stays open with RBI only for the marketplace limits.

docs.title: Q-52 Contract Act timing
docs.text:
Non-blocking: fail-safe default

Was Blocking. Made non-blocking by the fail-safe default below. The default is relaxed only in a dated release (Fail-safe defaults); it is testable by conformance case T1-32 (cases T1-27 to T1-32 cover the six fail-safe defaults).

Question. The dispatch and receipt timing of negotiation messages, the WITHDRAW/ACCEPT crossing rule and the dispatch-time assumption rest on Indian Contract Act ss.4–7. Do they hold for electronic negotiation messages? Owner. Legal counsel.

Findings. The text of Contract Act ss.2 and 4–7 has been checked against India Code. Still open: whether mapping dispatch and receipt to CounterSignature timestamps, and the crossing tie-break, hold for electronic messages. The Information Technology Act, 2000, s.13 sets "despatch" and receipt rules for electronic records "save as otherwise agreed to between the originator and the addressee", so the parties may agree their own.

Fail-safe default. The timing rules in Negotiation are normative as protocol terms that participants agree to, in the sense of the Information Technology Act, 2000, s.13. Until Q-52 is settled:

  • When a withdraw and an accept cross and the outcome is decided by the BACP crossing rule, neither gateway proceeds to init, complete or confirm on that deal automatically. The buyer gateway MUST escalate to the buyer principal on the Trusted Surface (requires_buyer_review), the seller gateway MUST raise the case to the seller principal (requires_seller_review) and MUST NOT auto-confirm, and each proceeds only on its principal's confirmation. The fail-safe is two-sided.
  • The crossing outcome (withdraw_lost_crossing, accept_void_withdrawn, seller_accept_void, crossing_contested) is still recorded in the transcript as evidence.

The rule since 18-10-2026. A crossing is decided by transcript positions inside the loser's own chain, never by timestamps (Contested crossings). Where the positions do not decide it, the outcome is crossing_contested: BACP evidence does not settle formation, neither gateway proceeds and the protocol records no breach event. BACP does not say "no contract", because a protocol term cannot declare that no contract exists.

Still open, for counsel:

  1. Whether an agreed protocol term (IT Act s.13 "save as otherwise agreed"; s.12(2); ICA s.7(2)) can fix the dispatch and knowledge moments of ICA s.4 as countersigned transcript positions, with an unprovable order treated as "BACP evidence does not settle formation".
  2. Whether a time tie-break survives anywhere against the Illustration to s.5 (moot under the committed-order rule unless one is added).
  3. Whether a principal who declines a deal formed by a crossing and held under the fail-safe is in breach, and whether a principal_declined under permitting terms is ever a breach.
  4. Whether an acceptance dispatched before expires_at but received after it is in time unless the offer prescribes receipt, and whether the hashed protocol_terms statement that expires_at is a receipt deadline displaces that.
  5. Whether Rule 4(8) of the E-Commerce Rules (parity) limits a principal_declined charge before CONTRACTED in consumer sessions.

docs.title: Q-54 Token requestor duties
docs.text:
Question. Is a BACP operator a CoFT "token requestor"? If so, the merchant-listing, de-registration and re-consent-on-reissue duties apply. Owner. RBI.

Working position. None yet.

docs.title: Q-55 Aadhaar offline verification
docs.text:
Question. What is the Aadhaar offline VC verification profile, and how is OVSE registration of verifiers recorded? Owner. MeitY/DPDP.

Working position. Relevant only if VCs are used. An Aadhaar number is never collected.

docs.title: Q-56 Transcript retention
docs.text:
Question. How long must negotiation transcripts be kept? Two years (the Consumer Protection Act limitation period) is proposed but unverified. Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position. Two years for B2C; longer for B2B and public procurement.

docs.title: Q-57 IGM SLA timelines
docs.text:
Question. What are the IGM SLA timelines (48-hour acknowledgement, one-month resolution, Level I/II)? The ONDC policy text could not be verified as of 17-10-2026. Should BACP auto-escalate on missed clocks? Owner. ONDC.

Partly answered. The 48-hour acknowledgement and one-month resolution are maximums under Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(5), restated by ONDC on its complaint page. IGM 2.0 carries them as per-issue durations (expected_response_time, expected_resolution_time) with no network default. Still open: auto-escalation on a missed clock, and the ONDC Network Policy IGM chapter, which was not verified as of 17-10-2026.

Working position. Proposed: normative ack_by and resolve_by timers. See Beckn / ONDC Binding and Orders and Post-order.

docs.title: Q-58 Webhook signature tag
docs.text:
Question. Should gateway-signed webhooks carry a dedicated RFC 9421 signature tag, bacp-webhook, listed in the gateway's profile, so that a webhook signature can never be confused with any other signed message? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. Proposed: the tag is bacp-webhook. Fail-safe default until it is settled: an agent MUST verify every webhook against a key in the gateway profile's keys and MUST NOT act on a webhook that fails verification; it MUST NOT reject a webhook only because its signature has no tag or an unknown one. See Identity and Request Signing and REST.

Upstream issue UCP #659 (as of 18-10-2026). BACP's webhook signature already covers webhook-id and webhook-timestamp (REST), so the header-coverage point of that issue (closed upstream on 31-07-2026) is met. Only the dedicated tag stays open.

docs.title: Q-62 Certification of assisted operators
docs.text:
Question. Who certifies the human assisted operators (village-level entrepreneurs at Common Service Centres, bank business correspondents, buyer-app agents) who complete sessions for principals on channel: assisted, and what identifier does that body issue, so that Participant.ref of an assisted_operator can be checked? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. An assisted_operator entry is REQUIRED on every assisted session and every Trusted Surface approval names it (Presentation.assisted_by), but its ref is asserted by the agent operator and not verified against a registry. The principal approves with the principal's own factor, never the operator's tap (BACP policy). Since 18-10-2026 the ref is namespaced scheme:id (csc_vle, bank_bc, ondc_np_agent or other) and the gateway sets Participant.ref_verification, which is asserted until a registry exists that the gateway can name and which an agent can never set to verified. assisted_by and Participant.ref are attribution, never authentication, and the Trusted Surface announces the operator before the factor without reading "unverified" aloud. See Human participants.

docs.title: Q-63 Third-party render input on PSP surfaces
docs.text:
Question. Do NPCI's rules for PSP apps allow a payer PSP's app or IVR to render a step-up from a third-party, gateway-signed ts_render? Can an IVR or UPI 123PAY flow carry a confirm-only callback, and in which languages? Owner. NPCI, through a member bank.

Working position. The Trusted Surface renders only from ts_render and its own templates (TS-1). StepUp.delivery: ivr_callback is Proposed until this question is answered; a gateway offers it only where its PSP confirms the flow. The question also asks whether a UPI 123PAY or IVR flow can read and capture a challenge that the Trusted Surface draws (the voice challenge), whether a PSP may publish the numbers it calls from (ts_call_numbers[]), and whether PSP apps already refuse to render or debit a link whose payer is not the logged-in VPA (which would make payer_ref a restatement). If the challenge cannot be captured, voice approvals are unavailable and feature-phone principals lose voice for non-money confirmations, while money is unaffected because voice never releases it. See Human participants.

docs.title: Q-65 Agent-initiated draw on a Reserve Pay block
docs.text:
Question. NPCI UPI OC 228 describes a Reserve Pay debit as one "initiated by the customer action on merchant's platform", and the UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 16.6, as one "initiated by the User action on Merchant's platform". Does a debit that an AI agent triggers for the principal, under a mandate, count as such a customer action? Owner. NPCI, with Legal counsel.

Working position. None of the rules depend on the answer. BACP counts every block as reserved spend at its full amount and binds it to one payee seller (Usage ledger, Per-leg rule) whichever way it is answered. A gateway uses an existing block for an HNP leg only under these rules. See Rail Bindings.

docs.title: Q-66 E-commerce entity status for sponsored listings and prior prices
docs.text:
Question. The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) require sponsored listings to be "distinctly identified" (r.4(12)) and define a prior price as "the lowest price of a good or service thirty days prior to the announcement of price reduction" (r.4(13)). Rule 4(12) binds "every e-commerce entity", and r.4(13) binds "an e-commerce entity or the seller" that announces a reduction. Open points for counsel:

  • Is an agent operator, or a BACP gateway, an "e-commerce entity" (2020 Rules r.3(1)(b): a person who "owns, operates or manages digital or electronic facility or platform")?
  • Does r.4(12) attach in a human-not-present flow, where no human sees the list?
  • Is a price shown beside a maximum retail price, an MRP strike-through, or a coupon, bank offer or cart-level minimum-value offer, an "announcement of price reduction"?
  • Whose lowest price counts under r.4(13): this platform's, all platforms' or offline prices too?
  • Do r.4(12) and r.4(13) bind for-resale (B2B) purchases (section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 excludes a person who buys for resale or for any commercial purpose from "consumer"; whether that exclusion applies to r.4(12) and r.4(13) is a question for counsel, as of 18-10-2026)?
  • Does a gateway that alters or computes a prior price become the party that announces the reduction?
  • Is brand-funded placement of an item a "sponsored listing" when the seller did not pay?
  • Is a sponsored slot that is not targeted, shown to a minor, "targeted advertising" under DPDP s.9(3)?

Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position. BACP carries the data and applies the stricter reading wherever counsel's answer would otherwise matter. Every item carries a per-item sponsorship; a prior price is only ever the seller's lowest_30d figure with its announcement date; an MRP is never a "was" price; and no reduction, strike-through or percentage is shown for an item without a prior_price, whatever produced the reduction. B2B profiles are not exempt. BACP states that its fields carry the data an e-commerce entity needs, and does not state that they satisfy a duty. See Catalogue disclosures.

docs.title: Q-67 Ranking parameters that a party can buy
docs.text:
Question. Should each entry of ranking.main_parameters become an object that carries its relative importance and a flag for whether a party can raise it by payment (a purchasable attribute), so that a buyer can see which ranking parameters are paid for? Owner. BACP WG, with Legal counsel (r.5(3)(f) as substituted requires main parameters "in descending order" with an "easily and publicly available description").

Working position. main_parameters stays a list of strings in descending order of importance, with an optional description_url. A parameter that a party can buy is covered by the definition of "sponsored": an item whose position was affected by it is sponsored. A self-declared purchasable flag would be set by the party it is meant to constrain, and changing the type breaks every producer and consumer, so it is not in this version.

docs.title: Q-68 Reviewed translations of fixed legal labels
docs.text:
Question. Is there a reviewed translation route for fixed legal labels (the disclosure phrases) in the Eighth Schedule languages other than Hindi? Owner. MeitY/DPDP, through Bhashini.

Working position. en-IN and hi-IN are defined, and are draft wording until the human-experience review seat and the owner sign them off. For any other language, an operator uses its own fixed, reviewed translation of the same sentence, never a translation made at run time. The same route is needed for the Trusted Surface's fixed sentences that Human participants adds: the TS-6 refusal, the assisted announcement, "a matching code does not make a link safe", "your bank never asks for your PIN on a call it makes", the no-PIN-basis notice and the seller_confirmation and re-prompt sentences. The disclosure phrases capability_absent, added_not_by_you, cart_estimate, loyalty_provisional and policy_not_stated, and the marketing-consent sentences of the Trusted Surface, are drafts and need the same review.

docs.title: Q-69 ONDC catalogue tags for sponsored listings and prior price
docs.text:
Question. Will ONDC publish catalogue tags for a sponsored listing and for a prior price (and any vocabulary for its basis), so that BACP can map to them instead of its own bacp.disclosure tags? Owner. ONDC.

Working position. BACP maps its fields to its own bacp.disclosure TagGroup (Catalogue disclosure mapping). When ONDC publishes tags, only that mapping changes; the BACP field names stay.

docs.title: Q-70 Registry access and cached catalogues for verifying discovery sources
docs.text:
Question. An agent that verifies a discovery source needs the seller's key from the network registry (Verifying discovery results). Can an agent operator that is not itself an ONDC subscriber query the registry, or must it subscribe or use a lookup service? And what should a gateway do when it answers from a cached catalogue, which cannot meet the search binding, or from a Beckn 2.0 signed catalogue index, which this version does not cover? Owner. ONDC.

Working position (fail-safe default). An agent that cannot verify a source renders every item of it with no reduction claim and no MRP anchor, and renders its sponsorship as undeclared (or sponsored, if the result says so). A cached answer is unverified for the same reason. BACP adds no weaker freshness binding. A gateway that wants verified claims sends a targeted live search to the shortlisted sellers with the agent's message_id.

docs.title: Q-71 Agent-side verification of the on_init quote
docs.text:
Question. An agent can verify a discovery source with the seller's signature. It cannot yet verify, at run time, the on_init quote that the gateway relays, for example that a seller's automatic discount was not removed by the gateway when the buyer app collects the payment. Should the agent be able to fetch the seller-signed on_init body, using the same pattern as the discovery source? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. The evidence bundle's bpp_signed_quote catches such a change on dispute, after the fact. The mandate bounds the amount in a human-not-present flow. No run-time check exists in this version. A residual remains: applied[].automatic is derived by the gateway from the breakup tag offer/auto, so a gateway that submits an affiliate offer and labels it automatic: true escapes the discount rule 2 check at run time. It is caught only from bpp_signed_quote on dispute.

docs.title: Q-73 Trusted Surface repeat of catalogue disclosures
docs.text:
Question. The Trusted Surface repeats sponsorship and prior-price sentences before the total (Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface). Three points are open:

  • Should the item names in the repeat reach a payer PSP on a rail_auth render, which then learns what was bought?
  • Should a long basket aggregate sponsored sentences the way it aggregates undeclared ones? Aggregation is acceptable on audio only if the visual render keeps a line for each item, and a prior_price sentence is never aggregated.
  • Should a Mandate Manager or payer PSP fetch and verify the seller-signed sources itself, instead of trusting the gateway's signature on the render?

Owner. BACP WG, with the human-experience review.

Working position. Names are included. Only undeclared sentences aggregate, and only above three entries. The Trusted Surface trusts the gateway's signature on the render, and the agent checks the repeat at run time; a rogue gateway that shares an operator with the agent is caught only on dispute. A long basket puts many sentences before the PIN, which the human-experience review is asked to weigh.

docs.title: Q-74 Provisional and instrument-linked discounts on plain sessions
docs.text:
Question. The UCP Discount extension has provisional discounts (those that depend on eligibility, such as a bank or card offer, a loyalty tier or a buyer assertion) and an eligibility claim on each. Should a plain checkout session carry them, so that a UCP or ACP producer maps without loss? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. No. A discount that depends on the payment instrument or on a buyer assertion stays in TermSheet scheme mode, which carries an eligibility proof. The schema rejects provisional and eligibility on a plain session, so a producer that sends them fails loudly instead of being half-mapped. See Discounts.

docs.title: Q-75 Zero-payable orders
docs.text:
Question. A discount of 100% of the order makes the payable amount zero. Should BACP carry a zero-payable order, with no debit, through a mandate? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. No. Mandate evaluation step 0 refuses a payable amount that is not greater than zero (amount_not_positive), so a fully discounted order is refused.

docs.title: Q-76 Gateway-funded and buyer-app-funded discounts
docs.text:
Question. Should a discount that the gateway or the buyer app funds, and that is not in the seller's signed quote, be carried? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. No. Such a discount would break the rule that the closed mandates carry the amount of the seller-signed quote total, and it would make the payable depend on the gateway. The gateway never adds or keeps a discount the seller did not sign.

docs.title: Q-77 Explicit user action on UPI Circle
docs.text:
Question. NPCI OC 201B (NPCI/UPI/OC-201B/2025-26, 08-10-2025) extends UPI Circle to IoT devices and software and states that "debit transactions using IoT shall be only initiated by explicit user action." May a UPI Circle delegation back a human-not-present debit under a standing open mandate that an agent executes without the principal present? Is that "explicit user action", and does "IoT" there cover software profiles such as an AI agent? Owner. NPCI, Legal counsel. Linked from Q-60.

Working position (fail-safe default). in.upi.circle backs no open mandate, even when a conformance authority whose scope includes it is listed and the gateway's attestation lists it, until an NPCI member bank and counsel answer. A Mandate Manager refuses an open mandate request on in.upi.circle with rail_binding_not_open_eligible, and a gateway refuses every human-not-present complete under an open mandate on it. The registry marks the handler open_eligible: false for this reason. A human-present payment through Circle is unaffected. See UPI Circle.

Blocking for settlement. This question is marked Blocking so that settling it, or any other change that lets in.upi.circle back an open mandate, needs the approvals that GOVERNANCE.md requires for the resolution of a Blocking question (two maintainers and steering group sign-off), and for the interim period the further approval that GOVERNANCE.md (c) requires. The fail-safe default above means that it does not block the release.

docs.title: Q-78 Where a convenience fee is disclosed when an agent selects the payment mode
docs.text:
Question. NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 asks the Payee PSP to disclose a convenience fee "upfront to the User on the merchant payment page(s) prior to the selection of the payment mode", and to keep it consistent across the available debit payment modes (net banking, debit card, UPI and credit card). When an agent selects the mode, is a Trusted Surface reading, or the mandate notice with a convenience_fees constraint, disclosure "to the User" before that selection? Does "credit card" sit inside "debit payment modes", are PPI wallets debit payment modes, and does para 7.5 reach in.cod.upi? Owner. NPCI, Legal counsel.

Working position (fail-safe default). The gateway warns with payment_mode_fee_inconsistent and never refuses. In human-present checkouts the Trusted Surface shows the fee before the factor. In HNP the warning raises a confirm step-up, and a convenience fee that the mandate's convenience_fees does not cover raises one too. A warning that proves a false positive is narrowed by data, and no money moves on it. See Fees on the payer's screen.

docs.title: Q-79 Operator fees and commissions
docs.text:
Question. Must an agent acting for a buyer disclose a commission that a seller pays it? Does NPCI FAQ Q17 ("UPI App providers shall NOT charge Platform Fee or any other charge") reach an agent operator that is a UPI application provider? Is a per-order operator fee a "bundled fee" under rule 5(7) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (from 01-01-2027), and is a BACP gateway or agent operator an "e-commerce entity" or "marketplace e-commerce entity" (rule 3(1)(b), (g))? What is the GST treatment of an operator fee line, and which BACP party is the "operator" for CGST s.52 TCS and Income-tax Act s.194-O TDS? Does the operator refund an operator charge when an order is cancelled for the seller's fault? Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position. No Indian rule was found that requires an operator to disclose a seller-paid commission (not verified as of 18-10-2026). BACP requires the declaration in the mandate notice as its own policy (Operator compensation), and the operator_charges[] line discloses a fee without licensing one.

docs.title: Q-80 ONDC recipient on the breakup
docs.text:
Question. Does the ONDC breakup carry a recipient for a charge line? Is misc the carrier for convenience fees, and is the np_fees channel margin payer-borne? Who bears the collector's P2M MDR when the buyer app collects (collected_by: BAP), and does RSF carry it as a deduction line? Does a P2PM seller keep zero MDR on orders that a network participant collects? Owner. ONDC.

Working position (fail-safe default). BACP publishes its own title_type to recipient mapping (Charge recipient mapping). An unmapped type is kept with recipient: other and a warning, never a refusal. The mapping changes when ONDC answers; the field names stay.

docs.title: Q-81 Retained payment charges, MDR on refunds and on UPI mandates
docs.text:
Question. May a disclosed non-refundable payment charge (convenience, payment_handling, platform) be kept, including on a return for a defective, deficient, spurious or late item, and how does the symmetry of rule 4(8) of the Rules apply? Does netting MDR off a refund breach rule 6(3) or 7(4)? Is MDR reversed on refunds and on TAT reversals? Do Reserve Pay and OTM count as "UPI Mandates" under NPCI FAQ Q22 (no prescribed MDR)? Is splitting a payment below ₹2,000 permitted, and is the pricing circular behind FAQ Q17 and Q34 binding? Owner. Legal counsel, NPCI.

Working position (fail-safe default). A refund below the amount paid must match the lines in charges_retained[], or the gateway returns refund_short_of_terms without blocking the refund. No conformance case passes a retained payment-related charge, or a retention on a return for a defect, until this is answered. A refund is never reduced by MDR or aggregator fees. See Refunds.

docs.title: Q-83 Counsel flags from the plan, ledger and trade-act bindings
docs.text:
Question. Five points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the bindings:

  1. Whether silence after a delivered notice of a ledger entry is acceptance or dispute (the ack_window default).
  2. Whether attested seller delivery evidence fixes the MSMED acceptance date, and whether BACP may drop the requirement of a buyer-signed GRN for an acceptance-dated sale (with Q-21).
  3. Whether a TCS line (CGST Act s.52) may appear in a buyer-facing total.
  4. Who bears the ₹100-per-day compensation of the RBI turnaround-time circular when a split-tender plan is unwound.
  5. Whether the 90th-percentile limit on statement acknowledgements, a BACP design value, is enough to protect a principal.

Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position (fail-safe default). (1) An entry is disputed at ack_window only where a notice was delivered. (2) Seller-only evidence is recorded with acceptance_basis: unattested and no due date is derived from it. (3) A TCS line never enters a buyer-facing total or a projected UCP total. (4) The question is recorded and no allocation is made by BACP. (5) Statement acknowledgements are limited as above and a per-entry dispute stays possible.

docs.title: Q-84 Whether the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules reach machine timestamps
docs.text:
Question. The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 761(E)), Rule 7, say that "No entity shall use, display or record any time reference other than Indian Standard Time (IST) for all purposes". The Rules are notified and not in force as of 18-10-2026; they commence 180 days after publication, about 24-02-2027 (the exact day is not verified). From commencement, does Rule 7 prohibit (a) storing or transmitting RFC 3339 timestamps with Z or +00:00 that denote the same instant as an IST time, (b) RFC 9421 created Unix-epoch integers, or (c) the Z timestamps that ONDC's validator requires on Beckn messages? Is the "standard format" of Rule 5 a mandatory format for machine records or only for display? Does Rule 7 reach entities outside the critical sectors of Rule 8(4)? Do Rules 5(2) and 6(1) bind times shown on a Trusted Surface render? Owner. Legal counsel, ONDC (for the Z on context.timestamp).

Working position. Every comparison is on instants. BACP-owned timestamps SHOULD carry +05:30; Beckn context.timestamp follows ONDC and keeps Z; every time shown or told to a person on a Trusted Surface is in IST; participants keep clocks traceable to NIC or NPL time. Under the committed-order rule the values that decide formation are integers, not time references. A schema pattern that required +05:30 is not adopted now, because it would be breaking and cannot be met on Beckn. The SHOULD becomes a MUST, if counsel says Rule 7 reaches machine timestamps, in a release dated before 24-02-2027.

docs.title: Q-85 Counsel flags from the negotiation timing rules
docs.text:
Question. Points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the rules:

  1. Whether a principal-signed standing_accept is the principal's own acceptance under ICA s.7.
  2. Whether an agent may accept a bid for a farmer under eNAM or APMC rules.
  3. Whether one Trusted-Surface-signed negotiation mandate is "explicit and affirmative action" under Rule 4(9) of the E-Commerce Rules for each later purchase.
  4. Whether a gateway or agent operator is the principal's agent under ICA Chapter X (s.214).
  5. Whether a buyer's signed declaration of commercial purpose can displace consumer status under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.2(7) for a sole proprietor's livelihood purchase.
  6. Whether a Dutch tick acceptance is a bid under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, s.64(2), whether an instant award is the announcement, and whether s.62 can exclude retraction (Q-35).

Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position (fail-safe default). (1) A standing accept exists only where the auctioneer enables it, and absent it only the base rule applies. (2) An agri seller gateway treats accept_confirmation as ask, so a farmer always taps their own acceptance. (3) accept_confirmation is never preselected and an absent key is ask. (4) The operator's role is recorded and no allocation is made by BACP. (5) A consumer marker always wins. (6) The text says that the bidder's tick message is legally a bid and that the award completes the sale.

docs.title: Q-86 Counsel flags from the Trusted Surface and human-participant rules
docs.text:
Question. Points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the rules:

  1. Whether a voice or operator-relayed "yes" satisfies Rule 4(9) of the E-Commerce Rules for a non-money confirmation.
  2. Whether an assisted operator's act can be attributed to the principal under IT Act s.11(b), and what proves "authority".
  3. Whether a gateway or agent operator is a "platform" under para 3 of the Dark Patterns Guidelines.
  4. Whether device_signature is an electronic authentication technique under IT Act s.3A.
  5. Whether a UPI debit that the account holder authenticates with her own PIN, but that a third party's BACP step-up link induced, is an unauthorised electronic transaction for issuer liability under RBI/2025-26/79 para 9(b).
  6. Whether a gateway that reads support_operator registry records is a fiduciary or a processor of the employees' personal data.

Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position (fail-safe default). (1) Voice confirms only what moves no money, and the question stays open for that. (2) Participant.ref is attribution, never authentication, and the principal's own factor is always required. (3) The Trusted Surface rules apply to the gateway and the operator whichever way it is answered. (4) device_signature is never called an electronic signature, and no verifier relies on it unless the mandate lists principal.device_jkt[]. (5) TS-6 is a MUST, so that the induced debit does not arise. (6) The record holds only a pairwise person_ref and the key, never Aadhaar.

docs.title: Q-87 Registry carriage of the Trusted Surface and support-operator fields, and the ONDC refusal codes
docs.text:
Question. Can the ONDC network registry carry bacp_role, operator_id, person_ref, ts_origins, ts_notify_url, and the legal operator (entity_ids[], assertion), regulatory_status[] and data_residency (registry-record.json)? Which ONDC error code maps to each seller_reason.code (the code 40002 is unlabelled in the ONDC build file)? Is there a seller code for "agent orders not accepted"? Who is the certifier of assisted operators (Q-62)? Owner. ONDC.

Working position (fail-safe default). Beckn's Subscriber.type is BAP, BPP or BG only. Until ONDC answers, a gateway that cannot read a signer's ts_origins from the registry mints no trusted_surface_url for it and answers 503 trusted_surface_unavailable, and a side registry would be a second trust root that this version does not define. An unmapped refusal code gives seller_reason.code: other. Principals of an unregistered signer lose link-based step-ups until it registers. An operator that the registry does not assert is unknown and fails every separation check closed, so pilot handlers that need a conformance attestation stay unavailable for open mandates, as today, and a collector with no verified regulatory_status entry gets 403 collector_not_authorised.

docs.title: Q-88 RBI treatment of a Reserve Pay block debit and an OTM execution
docs.text:
Question. Does RBI treat a debit under a single-block-multiple-debits (Reserve Pay) block, or an execution of a UPI one-time mandate, as exempt from two-factor authentication under the AFA Directions (RBI/2025-26/79), or as already authenticated when the block or mandate was created? Owner. RBI.

Working position. Neither appears in Annexure-1 of RBI/2025-26/79, so the registry sets no afa.rbi_annex1_item for in.upi.reservepay, in.upi.otm or in.upi.circle, and the schema forbids it for a handler that relies on authentication at block creation or registration. The basis of such a debit is cited to NPCI OC 200 item 3, para (d) (Reserve Pay) and to UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 paras 15.2 and 15.4 (OTM). The answer decides whether a future rbi_annex1_item is ever set on these handlers. The registry grades only the NPCI layer of the basis (afa.verification), and notes that no RBI exemption basis for the later debits was found.

docs.title: Q-94 Review process for third-party extensions
docs.text:
Question. Who reviews and admits a third-party extension (a capability under a reverse-DNS id, declared with a registry_ref and a schema_digest) to the extension registry, on what criteria, and how is an entry published and revoked? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). No third-party declaration is active. A gateway ignores no third-party entry silently: it does not activate it, and every ext member of a request is refused with 400 capability_unsupported. Only in.bacp.* declarations are valid. A third-party entry will be published in a dated release together with the registry release manifest (source/handlers/release.json), so that its digest is checked like a handler's. Principals lose nothing today except an option that a bank or a distributor would add: it waits for a BACP release. See Capability declarations.

docs.title: Q-95 A gateway-held cart
docs.text:
Question. Should BACP add a cart that the gateway holds between discovery and a session (UCP's dev.ucp.shopping.cart)? No ONDC primary source shows a server-held cart: the buyer builds the cart in the buyer application and sends select. Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). The capability is parked: a gateway does not list it, the UCP projection answers 404 for the cart operations, and a request that carries cart_id is refused with 400 capability_unsupported at $.cart_id (UCPF-06). A cart lives with the agent operator, and a principal on a feature phone has no gateway-held list. Any future cart MUST meet these controls: each cart line carries transaction_id and source_digest and a gateway-assigned added_by, so that conversion still runs the discovery_price_changed check and the sponsorship copy; a cart total is an estimate (estimate: true, spoken with the cart_estimate sentence), is never a Presentation and is never approved by a step-up; a cart belongs to one (agent, principal) pair and anyone else gets 404; a conversion re-quotes every line (a new select, a new checkout_hash) and never takes prices from the cart; and a replayed conversion with another presence, root mandate or basket_id gets 409. The projection's alternative, to validate and re-quote, is open.

docs.title: Q-96 Linking a buyer's account at a seller
docs.text:
Question. Should an agent be able to link the principal's account at a seller (UCP's identity linking, which uses the OAuth authorization-code flow), so that the seller fills the buyer, address and instruments from its stored state? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). Parked: no tool, DataPart or REST operation links an account. The negatives are normative now: no seller one-time password or password is requested or relayed by an agent, no seller-account token appears in a tool argument, a tool result, the InstructionLog, an evidence bundle or model context, and a link token is never a mandate (MCP authentication). Any future capability MUST meet these controls: the authorisation endpoint comes only from the seller's registry record; linking is a Trusted Surface consent event in every case and the seller's own origin is a second route only when the principal's modality is visual, never on voice or feature-phone channels; the token is bound to the agent key, the principal and the seller as audience; its scope is no wider than data_scopes and a ConsentReceipt covers it; and an address or instrument that the seller fills in never feeds fulfilment or complete, and any difference gives requires_buyer_review. Whether an account that a seller creates from a chained grant is consent is a question for counsel (Q-101).

docs.title: Q-97 Ask: natural-language questions to a seller
docs.text:
Question. Should BACP carry UCP's Ask capability, a natural-language question to a business and its answer? Ask is in no UCP release as of 18-10-2026 (it is on UCP's main branch after v2026-08-25, Q-82). Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). Parked. If it is added, an answer is untrusted_counterparty_text: it is never an input of a human-not-present decision, never a binding disclosure and never evidence, and the agent MUST NOT execute anything it says.

docs.title: Q-98 Loyalty memberships and benefits
docs.text:
Question. Should BACP carry UCP's loyalty extension (memberships, tiers, benefits and earning forecasts on a checkout)? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). Parked, and the controls that apply today are normative: a provisional loyalty benefit never enters total or charge_lines[], a plain session carries no loyalty discount (Discounts), and a paid membership that a seller adds is a line with added_by, read to the principal as a line she did not add. A loyalty claim on a plain session is refused (UCPF-06 on the projection). Points as a tender stay with Q-59, which is closed.

docs.title: Q-99 Catalogue lookup by id and product variants
docs.text:
Question. Should BACP add lookup of catalogue items by id and a variant model (options, selected options, product and variant ids) beyond today's POST /discover results? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position. Not added: no panel evidence for either yet. An agent re-discovers an item by search, and an item is one CatalogItem with its own id.

docs.title: Q-100 Purchasable ranking parameters
docs.text:
Question. Should an agent be able to ask the gateway to rank by a purchasable parameter (a promoted placement, a sponsored rank) in the request? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). Not added. If it is, the request field takes a value from a gateway-listed enum, is never a mandate constraint (an unknown constraint fails closed and this would be a new family), and the result is sponsored under Catalogue disclosures and shown as such.

docs.title: Q-101 Counsel flags from the UCP capability parity rules
docs.text:
Question. Five points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the rules:

  1. Whether a seller's business default (source: "business", granted: true) can ever be consent under DPDP Act s.6(1).
  2. Whether an account that a seller creates from a chained grant is consent.
  3. How a BACP marketing receipt relates to the preferences under the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (TCCCPR), and whether it satisfies DPDP s.6(1) with them.
  4. Whether an upward weight adjustment after a human-not-present payment is a new supply that needs fresh consent, and whether the GST invoice must show the final weighed quantity.
  5. What DPDP retention duty attaches to a list or cart that an agent holds.

Owner. Legal counsel.

Working position (fail-safe default). (1) and (3) A seller default is never consent, and with no marketing receipt every marketing purpose is granted: false; the receipt is Proposed (Marketing consent). (2) No linking capability exists. (4) An adjustment can only reduce the amount unless the principal agreed an adjustment_band and a hold exists (Weighed goods). (5) The agent operator's own retention rules apply, and BACP holds no cart.

docs.title: Q-102 ONDC and NPCI points of the UCP capability parity rules
docs.text:
Question. Four points for ONDC and one for a UPI member bank:

  1. What ONDC buyer-app feature codes 011 and 013 mean.
  2. Whether the ONDC B2B buyer_id is a GSTIN only.
  3. Which Beckn paths carry a selectable fulfilment, a unitized.measure outside RET11 and a seller-view added_by, and whether any domain can carry a fractional ordered measure.
  4. Whether a one-time UPI block can be captured in part, with the rest released, which an upward adjustment_band needs.

Owner. ONDC, NPCI (through a member bank).

Working position (fail-safe default). The gateway sends quantity.count only where the seller's pack measure equals the increment, and refuses otherwise (Quantity and units). The gateway projects acting_for.gstin into buyer_id and sends nothing else as a buyer identity. A band is accepted only where the rail holds the amount and the hold can be captured in part; otherwise adjustments are down only.

docs.title: Q-103 Annexure-1 treatment of a FASTag top-up and an NCMC top-up
docs.text:
Question. Does Annexure-1 of the RBI authentication directions (RBI/2025-26/79) exempt from two-factor authentication (1) a top-up of a FASTag, as an "NETC transaction" under row 4, and (2) a top-up of an NCMC card, which no row names? Owner. RBI, NPCI.

Working position (fail-safe default). Row 4 reads "NETC transactions" and the source circular (RBI/2019-20/126, 30-12-2019, para 4) exempts transactions in the NETC system; neither names a top-up. The registry keeps rbi_annex1_item: 4 for in.ppi.netc_topup as a reading (as of 18-10-2026). No row names an NCMC top-up, so in.ppi.ncmc_topup carries no exemption and no rbi_annex1_item, and authentication applies under para 6(a) (afa.model: per_txn_2fa). The pre-debit notice exemption for both handlers is a separate rule from the e-mandate framework.

docs.title: Q-104 Wire form of the carried-exposure increment after a port
docs.text:
Question. When a use of a superseded root reaches the Mandate Manager after it has signed the successor, the Mandate Manager sends the successor's gateway a signed carried-exposure increment (Porting). Which event, endpoint or TrustedSurfaceEvent value carries it, and what does it contain (period, window_start, amount and the seq of the use it comes from)? Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). BACP defines no wire form in this version. The rule is stated: the increment counts against the successor, and the gateway applies it inside the root's atomic section. Until a form is defined, the Mandate Manager does not sign the successor before it holds a closed event and every event up to its last_seq, or 60 seconds have passed without one. In that second case every window is incomplete and is pre-filled at max, so the carried exposure is treated as at the old max.
