The successor's gateway never receives the superseded root's events, so the rule binds the Mandate Manager and not that gateway. A use that arrives after signing makes the Mandate Manager revoke the successor and ask the principal to port again.

docs.title: Q-105 Payload schema of the notice render
docs.text:
Question. What is the payload of the gateway-signed notice render of an agreed_by_agent or purchase_offered_by_agent act (Human participants)? No schema defines it, so the bytes that go into notice_renders[] cannot be tested with a valid and an invalid example. The members that the text names are code, offer_hash, language, total, revoke_route, grievance_contact and expires_at. Owner. BACP WG.

Working position (fail-safe default). BACP defines no notice payload schema in this version. A notice is a gateway-signed compact JWS that is not a TsRender and not a step-up, and the specification names its content in prose. A verifier checks that each entry of notice_renders[] is a compact JWS signed by the gateway's registry key and does not parse its payload.

docs.title: Proposed design choices awaiting owner decision
docs.text: No design choice is awaiting an owner decision. Design choices (a), (c) and (d) are settled.

docs.title: Q-89 TAT row 4(b) and a payment that the rail completed
docs.text:
Question. Does row 4(b) of the Annex of RBI/2019-20/67 ("Account debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location", auto-reversal within T+5, ₹100 a day beyond it) apply to a UPI P2M payment whose payee credit the rail confirmed, where only the seller's application-level order confirmation (the Beckn on_confirm) never arrives? Owner. Legal counsel, RBI.

Working position (fail-safe default). The message states the T+5 turnaround and the ₹100 a day only where the payer PSP reports the debit as pending or deemed (reversal_basis: rbi_tat). Where the PSP reports the credit as completed (bacp_policy) it states no RBI compensation, and where the response does not say (unknown) it names the refund, UDIR and Ombudsman routes and adds that RBI's rules apply if the bank shows the payment as failed or pending. If row 4(b) does apply, the bank pays on its own and the message adds nothing; if it does not, BACP promises no remedy that may not exist. Principals lose nothing they hold today except a promise that may be false. See Debited but not confirmed.

docs.title: Q-90 What a payer PSP can sign about a refund credit and about a deemed or pending debit
docs.text:
Question. Can a payer PSP sign refund-credit evidence that cites original_rrn for a refund that the acquirer initiated through URCS (NPCI OC 165)? Do PSP response codes tell a deemed or pending debit from a completed one at the moment on_confirm goes missing? Does NPCI de-duplicate a debit on the gateway's PSP idempotency key? Owner. NPCI, through a member bank.

Working position (fail-safe default). The budget is released on evidence (a) from the bound payer PSP, or on evidence (b), a collector-PSP receipt plus the principal's confirmation on the Trusted Surface, so that a seller with an insider at its payment aggregator cannot restore the budget. If no payer PSP can sign the evidence, path (b) needs one confirmation for each refunded order, and without it the spend stays, as before. If the codes do not tell, every case reads reversal_basis: unknown. BACP asserts no de-duplication by the rail: the gateway allows at most one debit per checkout_hash.

docs.title: Q-91 Re-attestation of a Reserve Pay block under a successor root
docs.text:
Question. Will payer PSPs sign a fresh attestation for an existing Reserve Pay block, so that a successor root can re-bind it without revoking it? Owner. NPCI.

Working position (fail-safe default). A successor root MAY re-bind a block that its predecessor held when the payer PSP re-attests it. Where no PSP does, the old blocks are revoked and created again, the principal enters the UPI PIN once for each seller, and both blocks count as exposure while a revocation is unconfirmed (Porting a mandate).

docs.title: Q-92 Deemed-debit scope after OC 228, and overdraft funding
docs.text:
Question. What is the scope of a deemed debit for UPI Reserve Pay after NPCI OC 228 (08-10-2025), given that OC 88/2020-21 and OC 128/2021-22, which OC 200 recites, are member-only? Should a payer PSP attest an overdraft account as deposit or as credit? Owner. NPCI.

Working position (fail-safe default). A credit-side timeout after a successful debit is read as deemed (OC 200 para (d); Consolidated Circular para 32.3), and a timeout on the debit side is a decline (OC 228). An overdraft account is credit unless the PSP attests deposit, and a missing funding is credit, so that a block on such an account needs credit_funding_allowed: true.

docs.title: Q-93 Gift PPI refund after expiry or closure, and to a non-reloadable instrument
docs.text:
Question. Where does a refund go when a gift PPI has expired or been closed? Does PPI Master Direction para 14.3(a) let a refund be credited to a non-reloadable gift PPI above the limits of para 10.1? Owner. RBI, Legal counsel.

Working position. The registry records refund to the same PPI immediately (para 14.3(a)), a transfer back to the source with the holder's consent (10.1(c)), and, for a balance left after expiry, a payment to the holder in a bank account on request for a non-bank issuer (13.3). The gap is not verified as of 18-10-2026.

docs.title: Settled
docs.text: These questions are settled in BACP 2026-10-18. Each answer is normative in this version; the linked pages state the rule. A settled answer changes only in a later dated release, under the versioning policy.

docs.title: Q-28 Handler naming
docs.text:
Settled

Settled in 2026-10-18.

Question. Who governs handler names (in.* or bacp.*), and how long is the alias deprecation window? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Handler ids under in.* (rails and instruments) and bacp.* (BACP constructs) are canonical; earlier names such as upi.circle.delegate are aliases. Registry changes, including new ids, aliases and status changes, are normative changes under GOVERNANCE.md: a 14-day review and two maintainers' approval, one of them the payments editor, after the proposal process. The deprecation window is set by the versioning policy: a deprecated alias stays supported for at least two dated releases after the release that deprecates it and at least 180 days after that release, whichever is later. Removing an alias is a breaking change and gets at least 90 days' notice. This also settles what was proposed design choice (b), canonical in.* handler ids.

docs.title: Q-41 Closing open mandates
docs.text:
Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in 2026-10-18.

Question. What is the interoperable SD-JWT / KB-JWT encoding for closing open mandates, in place of the detached-JWS cnf closing? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. BACP 2026-10-18 has one interoperable encoding for a closed mandate: an attached compact JWS whose payload is the Mandate JSON, including an inner signature with role: agent made by the open mandate's cnf key, and whose header kid is the cnf key id. The optional kb_jwt on complete keeps its current rules. An SD-JWT / KB-JWT selective-disclosure encoding is not part of this version; a later release may add it as a new mandate vct without changing this one. The conformance suite will carry test vectors for the attached-JWS form. See Mandates and Consent.

docs.title: Q-42 Mandatory signature algorithm
docs.text:
Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in 2026-10-18.

Question. ES256 is mandatory and EdDSA allowed, but no ES256 test vectors exist and the implementation exercised so far signs only with EdDSA. Should ES256 stay mandatory, should EdDSA become mandatory, or should both be required? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Both are mandatory to verify. Every verifier of a BACP signature (RFC 9421 requests and webhooks, JWS mandates, receipts, ConsentReceipts, attestations and InstructionLog entries) MUST support ES256 (ECDSA P-256) and EdDSA with Ed25519. Every signer MUST use one of the two; no other algorithm is allowed. The conformance suite will carry test vectors for both. See Identity and Request Signing.

docs.title: Q-43 Network-leg signing
docs.text:
Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in 2026-10-18.

Question. Should Beckn messages be signed with a detached JWS over JCS, or with Beckn's Ed25519 + BLAKE2b Authorization header? Does BACP require Beckn 2.0 signed ACKs and the CounterSignature on which negotiation timing depends? Owner. ONDC.

Answer.

  • On the Beckn leg the network's own signing profile is normative: on Beckn 1.x and ONDC, the Ed25519 + BLAKE2b-512 Authorization header. BACP adds no transport signature of its own.
  • BACP does not require Beckn 2.0 signed ACKs. A gateway SHOULD use them, and the request-signature binding of callbacks, where the counterparty supports them.
  • The CounterSignature that negotiation timing relies on is a BACP artefact, not a Beckn ACK: a JWS by the receiving participant's registry key over the request digest and message id, returned in the negotiation message's counter_signature (on Beckn, inside the bacp TagGroups), so it does not depend on the Beckn version.
  • A counterparty that does not return valid CounterSignatures is treated as not supporting firm negotiation: the gateway MUST send it only non-firm offers (firm: false), so that formation follows the purchase-offer flow.
  • Evidence of what a seller sent rests on the same header signature: the gateway keeps the raw on_init body and its Authorization header (EvidenceBundle.checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms), which a verifier checks against the BPP's registry key. A per-object JWS over payments[] would be a convenience, not a requirement (Sibling Payment Mandates).

Whether ONDC validators accept the bacp TagGroups at all is Q-09. See Beckn / ONDC Binding and Negotiation.

Receipts in Ack.tags (18-10-2026). Transport Ack signing is still not required. A bacp.receipt TagGroup in the Ack carries a CounterSignature that verifies on its own by the counterparty's registry key, so it does not borrow trust from the transport. See Q-22 for the ONDC dependency.

docs.title: Q-47 Purpose-code governance
docs.text:
Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in 2026-10-18.

Question. Who governs the purpose-code registry and its bounds? The Sahamati Fair Use page that inspired it is marked "no longer relevant". Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. The BACP WG governs the purpose-code registry. The purpose-bounds table in Mandates and Consent is the normative registry for 2026-10-18. A change to a code or a bound is a normative change under GOVERNANCE.md and ships only in a dated release; lowering a bound or removing a code is a breaking change. A purpose_code that is not in the table is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.

docs.title: Q-53 DPDP commencement dates
docs.text:
Settled

The dates are fixed in the Gazette. Re-check only if an amending notification is published.

Question. What are the final DPDP commencement dates, given a reported MeitY consultation to shorten 18 months to 12 and a reported corrigendum G.S.R. 113(E)? Owner. MeitY/DPDP.

Answer. The DPDP Rules 2025 are G.S.R. 846(E) and the Act's commencement notification is G.S.R. 843(E), both dated 13-11-2025. Together they set three dates:

From Rules (G.S.R. 846(E), rule 1) Act (G.S.R. 843(E)) 13-11-2025 (in force) Rules 1, 2 and 17–21 ss.1(2), 2, 18–26, 35, 38–43, 44(1) and 44(3) 13-11-2026 Rule 4 (Consent Managers) s.6(9) and s.27(1)(d) 13-05-2027 Rules 3, 5–16, 22 and 23 ss.3–5, 6(1)–(8) and 6(10), 7–17, 27 (except 27(1)(d)), the penalty provisions ss.28–34, 36, 37 and 44(2)

The corrigendum G.S.R. 892(E) (10-12-2025) and the DPDP (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 (S.O. 5458(E), Order dated 05-10-2026, Gazette issue 06-10-2026) change wording only and move no date. The reported consultation to shorten the eighteen-month period and the reported corrigendum G.S.R. 113(E) appear only in secondary sources; no amending notification had been found as of 17-10-2026. See Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Q-60 Conformance attestation
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026, for the next dated release.

Question. Which registry role signs a conformance attestation, who may hold that role, and is the proposed payload (iss, sub, levels[], pilots[], exp, status) final, and which explicit JOSE typ does the attestation carry? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. The role is conformance_authority (Signature.role). Only a key of an entry in a public, dated, per-handler conformance-authority list qualifies; an entry is an independent lab or a rail-sponsor bank, scoped to named handlers, and the list ships empty. A Mandate Manager may narrow the list by publishing an exclusion list and never add to it. The payload is conformance-attestation.json, with the JOSE typ bacp-conformance+jwt, subject_role, scope, jti, registry_version, manifest_digest and report_digest. The Mandate Manager verifies it at issuance and writes rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti} into every pilot mandate; the gateway re-checks the bound jti at every complete. An attestation status list that is revoked, more than 24 hours old or unreachable fails closed, for issuance and for a new complete only. See Conformance attestation. Holders at release: none, so a Mandate Manager still refuses open mandates on every pilot handler. Adding an entry needs the approval in GOVERNANCE.md. Settling this question does not open the human-not-present path on in.upi.circle, which waits for Q-77.

docs.title: Q-72 Signed discovery results
docs.text:
Settled

Settled by owner decision of 18-10-2026, for the release dated 15-12-2026.

Question. The gateway verifies each seller's on_search signature, but nothing carried that signature to the agent, so a gateway could change a seller-asserted prior_price, mrp or sponsorship value between the seller and the agent. Should an agent be able to verify seller-asserted discovery values itself? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Yes. Each results[] entry carries a source_digest, the sha-256 of the raw seller-signed on_search body that every item of the entry came from. The gateway serves that body, with its Beckn Authorization header, at GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}. An agent that presents or relies on a seller-asserted value checks the digest, the binding of the callback to its search, and the Beckn signature against a registry key that it resolves itself, never from the gateway, and derives the values by the normative mapping. An unverified value is rendered with no claim, and sponsorship is rendered as undeclared at least. The gateway signs the discover response. Values that only the gateway asserts become non-repudiable through that signature. The seller's honesty is still not proved: verification shows that the seller said it. See Verifying discovery results; the open parts are Q-70 and Q-71.

docs.title: (a) Open mandates on class-O handlers
docs.text:
Settled

Was proposed design choice (a). Settled in 2026-10-18 by owner decision of 17-10-2026, in a narrowed form.

Question. May an open (human-not-present) payment mandate bind to any class-O handler, or only to the UPI standing authorities? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer.

  • An open payment mandate may bind to any class-O handler, but only through a mandate primitive whose limits the rail or the issuer enforces (limits_enforced_by rail or issuer). Each descriptor lists these primitives in binding.open_primitives. The mandate names the primitive it uses in rail_binding.primitive, the PSP attestation covers it, and the Mandate Manager refuses issuance otherwise (rail_binding_not_open_eligible). For in.ppi.wallet only ppi_emandate is open-eligible, never the wallet balance.
  • The descriptor's status must be live, or pilot only when the gateway's conformance attestation lists the pilot in pilots[]; the Mandate Manager verifies this before issuing. The attestation payload and its signer are settled (Q-60).
  • Eligibility is re-checked against the current registry at every complete. A registry downgrade pauses the affected mandates and cancels their open sessions.
  • The atomic reservation is keyed on the root open checkout mandate, so sibling open payment mandates cannot together exceed its budgets.
  • in.store_credit, in.loyalty and bacp.credit_ledger, whose limits the merchant or BACP enforces, are not open-eligible in this version (Q-59, Q-46). in.erupi is pilot until Q-38 is answered. Agentic card tokens stay pilot-gated (Q-39).

See Mandates and Consent and Handler Registry.

docs.title: (c) Acceptance revocation
docs.text:
Settled

Was proposed design choice (c), "acceptance revocation waived by default". Settled in 2026-10-18 by owner decision of 17-10-2026, amended the same day after review: allowed_until_receipt is refused everywhere, and the rules that would honour it are kept as sunset text.

Question. Should every firm offer waive, by default, the acceptor's right under Indian Contract Act s.5 to revoke an acceptance before it reaches the proposer, or should the waiver be opt-in per offer? Owner. BACP WG; the validity of any waiver stays with Legal counsel (Q-19).

Answer.

  • acceptance_revocation is REQUIRED on every firm offer, and there is no default. A gateway never inserts or normalises the value before hashing.
  • In this version every receiver refuses allowed_until_receipt with capabilities_incompatible, on every binding. The value stays in the schemas. A matched-pair rule that would honour it on the REST, MCP and A2A bindings is kept as sunset text: the revoke names the acceptance and the offer and is dispatched no earlier than the acceptance; the proposer appends a revoke it receives first to its transcript and holds it until 5 seconds after the revoke's dispatch; and the receiver returns its CounterSignature, with log_entry_hash, in the synchronous response to each message, so that it commits to receipt order before it sees the next message. A later version lifts the refusal only when the sunset conditions hold.
  • accept_revoke and withdraw are sent under bacp-negotiate. Every accept_revoke is countersigned, logged and refused (accept_revoke_not_allowed). Exposure release is idempotent, keyed on offer_hash.
  • waived needs a signed waiver_basis (a contract, or the buyer's own RFQ) that the acceptor's gateway obtained from its own principal before the offer arrived, that names the counterparty (np_id or GSTIN) and that the principal marked as a waiver basis, and is refused in consumer sessions: sessions whose profile is a consumer profile, that declare none, or whose buyer side acts for an individual or sends no acting_for. The profile is fixed when the session opens.
  • On Beckn legs, a waived offer with no basis, and in a consumer session any waived offer, may be accepted only by a human shown the consequence sentence; the only schema error excused is the missing basis. In a consumer session on REST, MCP or A2A no value is permitted, so only non-firm offers are possible there.
  • A negotiation approval is posted as negotiation.step_up.approved with Presentation.offer_hash, never with checkout_hash.
  • The Trusted Surface shows the value only as a fixed consequence sentence followed by the cancellation terms, never as "cannot cancel". BACP does not yet say which value an offer SHOULD use.
  • RFQ awards have no fixed value. The comparison set is frozen at close (for rfq_iterated, the close of the final shortlist round); a revoked award, possible only under the sunset text, cancels the RFQ or auction (NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN), and it cannot be awarded again (NEG_AWARD_RULE). accept_revoke never governs bid_retract.

See Acceptance revocation, Award and Trade Profiles.

docs.title: (d) Multi-seller hands-free shopping
docs.text:
Settled

Was proposed design choice (d). Settled in 2026-10-18 by owner decision of 17-10-2026.

Question. Given that a Reserve Pay block pays one seller, in what order does an agent fall back when it buys from several sellers with no human present, and what does each fallback mean for the principal? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer.

  • A multi-seller purchase is a basket of sessions, one per seller, grouped by a gateway-local basket_id. No payment spans sellers, and there is no atomicity across sellers.
  • Per leg, the gateway plans the payment in this order: the principal's designated preference; then the seller's existing payee-bound instrument, such as a block already held for that seller (3a); then a gift PPI the principal designated; then one planned human-present step, raised for the whole basket before any debit. UPI Circle and agentic card tokens back no open mandate while they are pilot and no listed conformance authority has attested the gateway for them (Q-60); UPI Circle also waits for Q-77. No rung ranks above the principal's preference.
  • A new per-seller block (3b) is offered only beside a one-time human-present payment to the same seller, with equal weight, never after a failed payment and never on an IVR callback. A block set up outside a checkout is exempt.
  • Every sibling Payment Mandate sits under one root open Checkout Mandate; a block names its payee (payee{vpa, bpp_id}), bound to the seller's signed payment terms; the blocks under a root sum to no more than its smallest budget; each block counts as reserved spend at its full amount; revoking the root revokes each block.
  • A change of a leg's funding class (own deposit, prepaid or borrowed), fee-bearer, payee or collector raises a rail_fallback step-up; an in_doubt leg is never re-routed.

See Mandates and Consent and Sessions and Checkout. Whether an agent draw on a block counts as a customer action is open (Q-65).

docs.title: Q-44 Binding for plans, ledgers and documents
docs.text:
Settled

Was Blocking. Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T4).

Question. What are the REST, MCP and A2A bindings for split-tender payment plans, credit ledgers and trade documents (GRN, CRAC, invoices)? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. All three are bound, each behind a capability id that a gateway lists in its profile, so that a gateway that lists none keeps the earlier behaviour:

  • in.bacp.payment_plan: payment.plan_options[] on a session and complete.payment_plan. Plans are offered by the gateway or confirmed on the Trusted Surface, never composed by the agent. See Wire binding of plans.
  • in.bacp.ledger: paginated reads and an agent payment posting under a payee match, a pending_ack fall-back and a head compare-and-swap. See On the wire: in.bacp.ledger.
  • in.bacp.trade_document: POST /trade-acts for GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection and ledger acknowledgement, with subject_hash on every act, and GET /orders/{order_id}/documents. See Seller-side and trade acts.

A gateway that does not list in.bacp.payment_plan still refuses a complete that carries payment_plan (conformance case T1-31). Tranches are accepted in the fail-safe form: a tranche carries no debit authority at complete. The carriage of a buyer-issued GRN or CRAC on Beckn stays with Q-33, so a trade act on a document is delivery: recorded until then. Counsel's points are in Q-83.

docs.title: Q-45 Intersection for plain sessions
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T4).

Question. Should POST /payment-handlers/intersect support plain checkout sessions that have no TermSheet? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Yes, on a gateway that lists in.bacp.payment_plan: the request may carry a session_id alone. The answer covers only the session's own sellers, uses a closed reason enum with no amounts and no counterparty text, gives a resolution per reason and a bpp_id per seller, is rate-limited per agent before the lookup, is never forwarded to a seller and is never authority (complete re-evaluates). A gateway that does not list the capability keeps the negotiation_id requirement. See Handler intersection.

docs.title: Q-64 Support-operator keys in the registry
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T6).

Question. How does a registry enrol and revoke keys of role support_operator, the keys with which a human support operator of an agent operator accepts and releases a handoff under tag bacp-handoff? What does the registry record hold (the agent operator the person works for, one key per person), who vets the person, and how fast does a revocation reach gateways? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. The registry record of a support_operator key is registry-record.json with bacp_role: support_operator, operator_id (the agent operator the person works for), person_ref (a pairwise reference to one person, never an Aadhaar number), keys (exactly one key), valid_from, valid_until and status. There is one key per person and no shared desk keys. A revocation takes effect at the next registry refresh, as for other keys. A key of another agent operator has no standing and gets 404 not_found; a key whose role is not support_operator gets 401 signature_invalid; and a key of the same agent operator that is not accepted_by gets 409 session_state_conflict (Human handoff). Support staff without a per-person key cannot accept a handoff, so a principal who asks for a human waits until the operator enrols them. Who vets the person is the agent operator's duty under its own HR process; counsel's question on whether a gateway that reads these records is a fiduciary or a processor of the employees' personal data is open with counsel (Q-86). Whether the ONDC network registry can carry operator_id and person_ref is a question for ONDC.

docs.title: Q-61 Gateway-to-MM mandate events
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

Question. Should a gateway tell the Mandate Manager that issued a mandate when it pauses that mandate because its rail binding is no longer eligible (binding_ineligible, reissue_required) or lifts such a pause, so that the Trusted Surface can show the principal why the agent cannot pay and can offer re-issue? If so, through which signed event and endpoint? POST /trusted-surface/events runs from the MM or PSP to the gateway, and every webhook runs from the gateway to the agent, so BACP 2026-10-18 has no channel in this direction. Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Yes, on the audit_uri that the mandate already carries, with no new Mandate Manager endpoint. The gateway reports a use, a relinquishment and every addition or removal of a gateway-originated pause reason as a MandateEvent (use, relinquished, pause_changed), numbered per mandate by seq and chained by prev_hash, signed under RFC 9421 by the registry key of its BAP with the tag bacp-mm-event, and delivered within 60 seconds and retried with the same event_id. The Mandate Manager accepts an event only from the BAP of the mandate's agent.bap_id, and records event_gap on a missing seq. A delivery failure never blocks a refund, a reversal or a post-order write, and no money moves on the event: every gateway still re-derives eligibility at step 1 of evaluation. The Mandate Manager derives the change of registry status and its own issuance record itself, and learns an attestation swap and unmatched_rail_debit (which needs a block-debit feed, Q-10) only from the event. A relinquishment of a root with blocks is not complete for the principal until the Mandate Manager reports rail_revocation, and the agent delivers the Trusted Surface revoke route until then. A MandateEvent carries no text for the principal, so it is not a notice: BACP still defines no gateway-to-Trusted-Surface notice event, and a process.notice_route of tel or sms remains the way to meet the condition for autonomous (Negotiation). See Mandate events and Handler binding.

docs.title: Q-36 Atomicity across gateways
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

Question. How are budgets and negotiation exposure kept atomic across gateways (a principal with two buyer apps) and across replicas of one gateway? Should the Mandate Manager hold the authoritative reservation ledger? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Budgets are atomic per root inside one gateway, and each open mandate belongs to one gateway: the mandate carries agent.bap_id, copied by the Mandate Manager from the verified AgentCredential, and any other gateway refuses it with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.agent.bap_id (a mandate without bap_id is bound by credential_hash, which the gateway compares). A mandate moves to another gateway only by a principal-initiated successor root on the Trusted Surface, which carries the spend already made and revokes the old root first. The earlier working position, that the Mandate Manager publishes outstanding exposure, is replaced: nobody proposed a Mandate-Manager-held ledger, and a synchronous one would put every complete on the Mandate Manager's availability. Replicas of one gateway keep sharing a linearisable ledger. The gateway takes the principal-keyed section before the root's section, never the reverse, and a firm commitment of the negotiation guard is written into the root's ledger as a reservation keyed by offer_hash. See Atomic reservation and Porting a mandate.

docs.title: Q-50 Cross-seller split detection
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

Question. Should split-order detection add a cross-seller velocity signal keyed on (mandate, window) instead of the seller? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. Split-order detection is keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate and the seller, within 10 minutes, and counts completed and in-flight orders. The seller is identified by the tax id in the BPP-signed terms, else by the payee VPA, else by the pair bpp_id and provider_id. The covers[] legs of a summary-approved basket are exempt, because the principal has approved each of them. A cross-seller velocity signal is not added: velocity across different sellers is bounded by the budgets. See Step-up and Atomic reservation.

docs.title: Q-46 Exposure of credit-ledger deals
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

Question. Should the cross-session exposure check count B2B credit-ledger deals against the checkout mandate's budgets or against credit_ledger.max_outstanding? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. A credit-ledger sale counts against the checkout mandate's budgets and against credit_ledger.max_outstanding only when it is booked by a gateway complete under the buyer's mandate, inside the root's atomic section. A sale that the creditor posts never touches the budgets. A disputed entry keeps its count until it is resolved or credit-noted. A payment that settles a sale counts within the sale, never on top of it, and releases max_outstanding only; a credit_note releases both. See Booking and settling.

docs.title: Q-59 Merchant- and BACP-enforced handlers
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7), as closed: not open-eligible in this release.

Question. May an open payment mandate bind to in.store_credit, in.loyalty or bacp.credit_ledger, whose limits are enforced by the merchant or by BACP rather than by a rail or an issuer? If so, who may sign their attestations and receipts when the payee is also the party that acts, and how does a credit-ledger sale, which has no payment receipt, resolve its budget reservation? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. in.store_credit, in.loyalty and bacp.credit_ledger are not open-eligible in this release, and their descriptors have presence.hnp: none, because the limits of each are enforced by the merchant or by BACP and not by a rail or an issuer. A principal who wants to pay human-not-present from store credit, loyalty or a khata ledger cannot yet; human-present payment is unaffected. The conditions for opening them are written down now, so that opening later is a registry change plus an owner decision:

Proposed

A handler whose limits a merchant or BACP enforces MAY back an open mandate only when all of these hold, each tested by a conformance case (T7-40 and the cases of the handler-binding cases):

  1. Attestations and receipts are never signed by a key of the payee's operator.
  2. A failure receipt signed by the payee keeps the reservation counted as spent until the principal confirms on the Trusted Surface.
  3. A credit-ledger acknowledgement comes from the principal's or the Mandate Manager's key, never the agent's cnf key.
  4. A store-credit debit carries the merchant-signed balance_before and balance_after.
  5. A loyalty redemption carries a programme-signed conversion_value.

Whether a gateway that funds a ledger needs RBI registration under the RBI Act, 1934, s.45-IA is a question for counsel (not verified as of 18-10-2026). See Handler binding and Booking and settling.

docs.title: Q-82 Pinned UCP release for the UCP checkout projection
docs.text:
Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T4 with the T8 apply).

Question. Should the in.bacp.ucp_checkout projection pin a tagged release of the Universal Commerce Protocol or a commit? Owner. BACP WG.

Answer. The projection pins UCP's tagged release v2026-08-25 (25-08-2026, commit cd78fb3), the latest of UCP's four releases as of 18-10-2026. The pin was commit a5e7cfe (12-10-2026) on UCP's main branch, which upstream labels draft and which is 39 commits after the tag; four of the 41 pinned files differ, so the move changes the copies of link.json, policy.json, warning_code.json and ucp.json. Three changes that UCP made on main after the tag are not in the pinned release, and BACP does not depend on them: the Ask capability, the cart rule that line_items SHOULD be [], and the registry of policy types (the tagged text lists dev.ucp.shopping.policy.return and .warranty). A gateway MUST NOT claim UCP compatibility on any other UCP version. A later re-pin to a newer tag re-runs the projection checks. The projection's handler keys are the UCP aliases dev.bacp.<handler id>, each with a schema at https://bacp.dev/schemas/ucp/<handler id>.json (decided 18-10-2026, after the owner confirmed that BACP holds bacp.dev); the old keys stay accepted for the dated release that introduces the alias. See UCP checkout projection.

docs.title: Other settled points
docs.text: Question Answer Lifetime of single-use payment tokens and step-up links At most 15 minutes. May a buyer app hold one Reserve Pay block for many sellers? No: one block per seller ((d)). How does a 24-hour AutoPay notice fit a 10-minute quote? The notice-gated checkout pattern in Rail Bindings. Which header carries the credential, and what does the signature cover? BACP-Agent; see Identity and Request Signing. Is a rail-cap breach an escalation or an error? Only AFA thresholds escalate; other caps return 403 rail_limit_exceeded (Errors). How are colliding handler aliases resolved? Exact beats glob; see Handler Registry. Naming governance is settled in Q-28. What evidence do non-UPI receipts carry? rail.evidence keyed by the descriptor's evidence references; see Rail Bindings. Does BACP carry fee allocation (MDR, aggregator commission, finder fee, settlement_eta)? No (18-10-2026). BACP makes normative what the principal pays and to whom, and keeps the seller's own costs informative (Who pays). Is a seller or agent human_confirmation_required field adopted? No (18-10-2026). Sellers already refuse unattended payment through accepted_handlers and COD refusal. The guarded alternative is the seller requires_principal_confirmation profile, which MUST NOT change a price or a handler (Discovery). Is BACP wire-compatible with UCP checkout? No (18-10-2026). Its checkout lifecycle and status names follow UCP's (BACP spells cancelled and adds human_handoff), but paths, totals and the sign of discounts, the ucp envelope, the complete payload and payment authority, and the MCP argument shape differ. The earlier claim of wire compatibility is retracted, and the differences are listed in BACP and other protocols. Is a match code (ts_match_code) shown on the Trusted Surface? A MAY, guarded (18-10-2026). It is derived from the render's content_hash, shown on app or web only, never read on IVR or UPI 123PAY, never a voice challenge, never a control and never evidence, and it is a MAY because a phishing page simply shows no code (Human participants). Is a Trusted Surface page allowed to take a UPI PIN? No (18-10-2026), as BACP policy: a PIN is taken only in the PSP's own app or on a call that the principal places to the PSP's published number, never on a web page and never on a call that the Trusted Surface places. That NPCI rules already say so is not verified as of 18-10-2026 (PIN rule). Is per-mandate evaluation atomic? Yes, within one gateway, keyed on the root open checkout mandate (Security and Privacy); across gateways see Q-36.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

An index of the normative artefacts of this BACP version: the JSON Schemas, the OpenAPI document, the payment-handler registry and the example vectors. All of them are published next to this specification; the lists on this page are generated from the source/ directory of the specification repository.

Versioned URLs

Schema $ids have the form https://bacp.dev/schemas/<name>.json. In a published release they are served at https://bacp.dev/<version>/schemas/<name>.json, where <version> is draft, latest or a date, and every $ref inside them points to the same release. Tools MUST resolve $refs by $id, not by file path. ts-render.json refers to components of bacp.openapi.yaml; a validator loads that document as a resource under its published URL (https://bacp.dev/<version>/services/bacp.openapi.yaml).

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
All schemas are JSON Schema draft 2020-12.

The human-participant types in common.json (LanguageTag, Participant, ParticipantRole, HandoffRoute, Presentation, HpProof, Actor) are described in Human Participants and the Trusted Surface.

Schema Title Description agent-credential.json AgentCredential Claims of an SD-JWT VC (vct in.bacp.agent.1) issued by a registry-accredited issuer to an agent operated by a registered legal entity and bound to a BAP subscriber. beckn-context-bacp.json Beckn context extension: context.bacp Added to Beckn/ONDC context on every BACP-originated message. Non-BACP NPs ignore it. Mirrored in message.order.tags[descriptor.code=bacp] where a network validator rejects unknown context keys. common.json BACP common types Shared definitions: Amount, PositiveAmount, Hash, Jws, Jwk, Signature, Presence, LangText, LanguageTag, RailType, Channel, Handler, Duration, IssueStatus, IssueMeta, HandlerId, HandlerRef, RailTypeV1, UdyamCategory, Party, DocumentRef, Citation, ParticipantRole, Participant, HandoffRoute, Presentation, HpProof, Actor, ConformanceLevel, EntityId, QuantityUnit, ChargeRecipient, MandatePrimitiveType, OperatorCompensation, ProtocolVersion conformance-attestation.json Conformance attestation payload The payload of a BACP conformance attestation: a compact JWS with the JOSE header typ bacp-conformance+jwt, signed by a key in the public conformance-authority list. It records that the subject passed BACP protocol tests. It is not approval, certification or onboarding by NPCI, RBI, ONDC or any public body. conformance-authority-list.json Conformance-authority list The public, dated list of conformance authorities: the only way to admit a signer of conformance attestations, published as source/registry/conformance-authorities.json. It ships empty. consent-receipt.json ConsentReceipt (DPDP) One receipt per recipient Data Fiduciary (merchant/BPP) per mandate. Issued by the data-blind Mandate Manager acting as (or for) a DPDP Consent Manager. A receipt with consent_kind marketing (Proposed) is standalone, names one seller and carries marketing purposes and channels. credit-ledger-entry.json CreditLedgerEntry One entry in a bilateral, hash-chained credit ledger (khata, B2B net-N, distributor credit) behind handler bacp.credit_ledger. Both parties sign or acknowledge. No money moves on a sale entry: settlement entries reference rail receipts (RRN/UTR) of another handler. fx.json FX disclosure Foreign-currency view of a cross-border payment. Settlement stays INR: inr_total is an INR Amount = round(foreign_amount * rate * (1 + markup_bps/10000)). handler-descriptor.json HandlerDescriptor One entry of the BACP payment-handler registry. Descriptors are data: limits and rules are configuration, not code. instruction-log-entry.json InstructionLogEntry Append-only, hash-chained evidence of prompt -> intent -> cart -> mandate -> payment. entry_hash = sha-256(JCS(entry minus entry_hash and signature)). Raw content is stored by the operator; only hashes leave it unless an evidence bundle is requested. loan-offer.json Credit-at-checkout offer list (KFS) Key Fact Statement fields, unbiased multi-lender display (every matched offer, unmatched lenders named, pre-disclosed ranking metric), cooling-off, and the lender as repayment payee. RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025 paras 6(i), 6(iii), 6(iv), 8(i), 9(ii)-(iii), 10 (08-05-2025 numbering; RBI has since withdrawn these Directions in its consolidation into entity-wise directions, see Credit and Split Tender). mandate-negotiation.json NegotiationMandate (separate BACP negotiation mandate) A separate BACP mandate that carries the bacp.neg.* constraints, so that legacy AP2/VI verifiers, which fail closed on unknown constraint types, still accept the AP2-compatible checkout and payment mandates. Same envelope conventions as mandate.json (SD-JWT over JCS, MM + principal signatures, status list). Verified only by the buyer's guard and credential provider, never by the seller. mandate.json Mandate AP2 v0.2-compatible Checkout or Payment mandate, open or closed, with AA consent-artefact semantics. Everything except status, usage and signatures is signed and immutable. negotiation-session.json NegotiationSession Authoritative full-state view of one bilateral negotiation (one buyer, one seller, one transaction_id), as returned by the gateway (ACP full-state pattern). RFQs and auctions own several sessions. offer.json Negotiation messages (Offer, CounterOffer, Accept, Reject, Withdraw, Terminate, RequestExtension, AcceptRevoke, BidCommit, BidReveal, BidRetract) Structured, signed and expiring negotiation messages. Only these are binding. Discriminated by type. payment-plan.json PaymentPlan (split and multi-tender) How one accepted all_in_total is paid: several tenders now (gift card + UPI) and/or tranches over time (token advance + loan + balance). One closed payment mandate and one Receipt per tender. Step-up and AFA are evaluated on the plan total, never per tender. receipt.json Receipt (rail-anchored) Signed by the verifier that acted (AP2 Mandate/Checkout/Payment Receipt). A successful payment or refund receipt on a UPI-family handler (upi., in.upi., in.cod.upi, in.pos.tap, in.pos.dynamic_qr) MUST carry the 12-digit RRN, and carries the UTR only when the handler descriptor's settlement.evidence_refs lists utr. Any other successful payment or refund receipt MUST carry at least one of rrn, utr or rail.evidence. registry-record.json RegistryRecord The part of a network registry record that BACP reads about one subscriber: its id, BACP role, keys and validity, the Trusted Surface origins, notify endpoint, call numbers, languages and modalities of a Mandate Manager or PSP, the operator and person of a support operator, and, for any subscriber, its legal operator, regulatory status and data residency. registry-release.json RegistryRelease The manifest of one publication of the registry files: registry_version, a strictly increasing registry_serial, published_at in IST and the JCS sha-256 digest of each file. It is published as source/handlers/release.json. ucp/<handler id>.json UCP payment handler dev.bacp.<handler id> One schema for each of the 57 handlers of the registry (for example ucp/in.upi.circle.json): the schema of the UCP alias key dev.bacp.<handler id> that the UCP checkout projection declares. An entry carries the BACP handler id as id and no config. termsheet.json TermSheet Multi-issue term sheet carried in every binding Offer. Every issue carries {value, negotiable, status}. Reservation values never appear here. Issues not listed are fixed. ts-render.json TsRender The payload of a ts_render, the compact JWS that the gateway signs once per step-up over the JCS form of this object and serves to the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP. The fields are defined on the Human participants page.

Each example is named <schema>.<case>.json and is checked against <schema>.json (rfq.* and auction.* against the Rfq and AuctionSpec definitions of negotiation-session.json, and common.<definition>-<case>.json against that definition of common.json, for example common.presentation-* against #/$defs/Presentation). A <component>.<case>.json whose <component> names no schema file is checked against the OpenAPI component schema of that name in PascalCase, for example mandate-request.* against #/components/schemas/MandateRequest and ts-render.* against TsRender in bacp.openapi.yaml. Files ending in .invalid.json are negative vectors: a conforming validator MUST reject them. The file examples/index.json is the normative map from each example to the schema or schemas it is checked against, and a validator MUST assert format (Conformance). docs.title: Regulatory Mapping
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page maps every regulatory and policy requirement that BACP tracks to the part of the specification that answers it. Each row gives the requirement, the instrument it comes from, the BACP control, and whether BACP 2026-10-18 covers it, covers it partially, or leaves a gap. Every partial or gap row names what is missing and, where one exists, links the open question that must be answered first.

This is the only page that uses requirement identifiers (REQ-…, PAY-…, NEG-…, TRADE-…). They are stable labels for traceability between this page, the open questions and conformance reports.

Not legal advice

This mapping is an engineering aid for implementers and reviewers. It is not legal advice and it does not establish that any deployment complies with any law, direction or network policy. Several sources are cited from secondary material or are unverified, and are marked as such. Laws, directions and circulars change; the citations were last checked as of 17-10-2026. Each participant remains responsible for its own compliance and should take advice from qualified counsel.

docs.title: How to read this page
docs.text:
• Status judges the specification, not a deployment. "Covered" means the specification as written satisfies the requirement. It does not mean any implementation has been certified.
  • Group is the regulator or body whose instrument is the primary source. A row is listed once, under its primary source, even when several instruments apply.
  • Forward-dated duties. DPDP duties that start in November 2026 or May 2027 are mapped now; their dates are in Security and Privacy.
  • N/A rows are operator duties outside the wire protocol (contracts, audits, data-lifecycle jobs), which belong in an operator conformance checklist, or requirements whose source has been withdrawn.
  • Source labels. A source with no qualifier was checked against the primary text (RBI, NPCI, MeitY, Gazette, ONDC or statute). "Secondary", "press", "not verified" or "not checked" marks a source that could not be seen in a primary text. "BACP policy" marks the part of a requirement that BACP adds beyond what the instrument says.

docs.title: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
docs.text:
RBI directions, master directions and circulars on authentication, e-mandates, payment aggregators, cards, PPIs, digital lending, payment-data storage and turnaround times. The FREE-AI recommendations are non-binding.

Digital Lending Directions withdrawn

RBI now lists the Digital Lending Directions 2025 (DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26, 08-05-2025) and the KFS circular (DOR.STR.REC.13/13.03.00/2024-25) among the circulars withdrawn by its Department of Regulation, in its consolidation into entity-wise directions. Rows citing "Digital Lending Directions" give the paragraph numbers of the 08-05-2025 text; they have not yet been mapped to the consolidated directions. See Credit and Split Tender.

Requirement Source BACP control Status REQ-113 Financial data only through a ReBIT AA flow via a regulated FIU, minimum scope RBI NBFC-AA Master Direction (2016, updated 2024) paras 6.3, 7; ReBIT (routing all financial data through an AA is BACP policy) — Gap: No Account Aggregator consent reference for affordability or financial-data use REQ-117 A mandate alone never moves money RBI NBFC-AA Master Direction para 5(3) (pattern); RBI AFA Directions 2025 para 6 An open payment mandate needs rail_binding, a closed one auth_binding; a mandate alone never moves money (Mandates) Covered REQ-212 Check restricted destinations for transfers; payment system data stored only in India RBI Storage of Payment System Data (RBI/2017-18/153, 06-04-2018); DPDP Act s.16, Rule 15 — (Security and Privacy) Partial: Fail-safe default: gateway, MM and PSP adapter store and process payment data only in India; agent-side model region open → Q-15 REQ-301 Every agent payment runs under an e-mandate or exemption, or gets fresh 2FA RBI AFA Directions 2025 para 6, Annex 1 Open mandates bind to a class-O standing authority, only through a primitive whose limits the rail or issuer enforces (binding.open_primitives), re-checked at every complete; closed human-present mandates bind to a per-transaction 2FA (Mandates, Handler Registry) Covered REQ-302 Agent never stores or replays PIN, OTP or biometrics RBI AFA Directions 2025 para 6(b) (dynamic factor; the no-storage rule is BACP policy) The agent never holds a PIN, OTP or biometric; descriptors list never_collect (Security and Privacy) Covered REQ-303 Recurring payments use an e-mandate; AFA above ₹15,000 (₹1 lakh for listed categories) RBI E-mandate Framework 2026 para 8 AFA thresholds produce a rail_auth step-up (Mandates, Rail Bindings) Covered REQ-304 Show the issuer's ≥24 h pre-debit notice; honour opt-out RBI E-mandate Framework 2026 para 6 Pre-debit notice relayed and opt-out honoured; notice-gated checkout; fail-safe 24 h notice for repeat Reserve Pay and OTM debits (Rail Bindings) Covered (see Q-03) REQ-305 Payments only through RBI-authorised PAs or banks; no funds held; no card storage RBI PA Directions 2025 paras 5, 10(a)–(b), 16; Annex 1 para 2.1 Collecting party checked against the registry record's regulatory_status (a verified rbi_pa or bank entry) before money moves (collector_not_authorised) (Payments) Covered (see Q-18) REQ-306 Refund to the original method unless the user instructs otherwise RBI PA Directions 2025 para 10(f); Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(10) (refunds as prescribed by RBI, within a reasonable time) Refunds to the original method, identified by the original rail reference (Rail Bindings) Covered REQ-307 "Debited but not confirmed" state; T+5 / T+1 tracking; tell the user about ₹100/day RBI TAT circular (RBI/2019-20/67, 20-09-2019) Payment saga state reversal_pending with reversal_deadline; debited_not_confirmed message follows reversal_basis: it states T+5 and ₹100 a day only for rbi_tat, never for bacp_policy, and names the refund, UDIR and Ombudsman routes for unknown (Checkout). Each tender of a payment plan carries its own reversal_deadline, rail_ref and derived psp_key (Plans on the wire) Partial: Refund-settlement trigger undefined; saga UPI-only → Q-49. Whether TAT row 4(b) reaches a payment that the rail completed and only the seller's confirmation is missing is not verified as of 18-10-2026 and is asked of counsel and RBI, so the message promises no compensation outside rbi_tat REQ-308 Machine-readable dispute and ODR channel linked to UTR/RRN RBI ODR circular (RBI/2020-21/21, 06-08-2020) Annex paras 5.1–5.4 (UTR/RRN linkage is BACP's choice) IGM issue carries the RRN or UTR; payment disputes raised through the PSP channel by RRN (Beckn binding) Covered REQ-309 AI disclosure; switch to a human at any time RBI FREE-AI report (13-08-2025) para 4.4.54 (non-binding; not verified as of 17-10-2026) AI disclosure with typed routes to a human (a tel: route, optionally with DTMF digits, on voice, IVR and UPI 123PAY) in the AgentCredential and the first session message, logged at stage ai_disclosure; POST /sessions/{id}/handoff in any state and after revocation, with status human_handoff, acceptance only by a registered human support operator, and release back to the agent (Human participants) Covered REQ-310 AI inventory, red-teaming, incident reporting, kill switch RBI FREE-AI report (13-08-2025) Recs 20–23, para 4.4.58 (non-binding; not verified as of 17-10-2026) AI inventory reference and incident contact in the AgentCredential; credential revocation as kill switch (Identity) Partial: No red-team or incident artefact in conformance REQ-401 Instrument model covers UPI variants, Lite, 123PAY, Reserve Pay/Circle, cards, e-RUPI, e₹ and BBPS, each with limits, auth mode and refund route RBI and NPCI rail rules Payment-handler registry: 57 descriptors with limits, authentication, refund route (Handler Registry) Covered REQ-402 Enforce configurable rail caps (Lite ₹1,000 / ₹5,000; 123PAY ₹10,000) RBI offline payments framework (RBI/2021-22/146, updated 04-12-2024); RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, Oct 2024 Configurable rail caps in handler descriptors; device-bound handlers not open-eligible (Handler Registry) Covered (see Q-05) REQ-403 Mandate constraints map to e₹ programmability and e-RUPI restrictions RBI CBDC Concept Note (07-10-2022) s.5.7; RBI Digital Rupee FAQ Q22 Programmability and voucher primitives in descriptors (Handler Registry) Partial: No mapping from mandate constraints to e₹ or e-RUPI rules REQ-404 Bill payments through BBPS operating units, fetch before pay, no scraping RBI BBPS Directions 2024 para 4(d) ("no scraping" is BACP policy) BBPS handlers with Bharat Connect transaction reference as evidence (Handler Registry) Covered REQ-405 Cross-border: show currency, FX rate and markup; CNP AFA; DPDP s.16 check RBI AFA Directions para 10; FEMA; DPDP Act s.16 FX disclosure view with INR settlement; cross-border card-not-present AFA step-up (Payments) Partial: No restricted-destination check under DPDP s.16 → Q-15 REQ-406 Credit at checkout only from RBI-regulated lenders, with lender, APR and KFS disclosed RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025 paras 6, 8(i) (withdrawn; 08-05-2025 numbering) Credit options carry lender, regulated-entity status, APR and KFS (Credit and Split Tender) Covered (Account Aggregator consent is tracked under REQ-113) PAY-102 No handler marked "human presence required" runs without a human auth event RBI AFA Directions para 6 Human-present-only handlers refuse human-not-present requests (presence_handler_mismatch) (Payments) Covered PAY-107 Disclose credit funding and hold prior consent RBI/2023-24/58 (prior consent; disclosure is BACP policy) credit_funding_allowed on the governing mandate; credit handlers need it (Credit and Split Tender) Partial: The PSP attestation carries funding (an overdraft account is credit unless the PSP attests deposit, and a missing value is credit) and a credit without credit_funding_allowed is refused with credit_funding_not_allowed; the consent reference itself is still not carried PAY-108 Lite and Lite X never available to remote agents; marked device-bound RBI offline payments framework; NPCI UPI Lite is class A (device-bound), never open-eligible (Handler Registry) Covered PAY-109 No storage of PAN, CVV or expiry; keep only last 4 digits and issuer RBI CoFT 2021 paras 4.1–4.2; PA Directions 2025 Annex 1 para 2.1 Descriptors forbid storing card number, CVV and expiry; retain last four digits only (Security and Privacy) Covered PAY-110 Token provisioned with consent and AFA; bound to card, requestor and merchant; never presented elsewhere RBI CoFT 2021 para 3.5; Annex conditions 1, 2, 6 Card-token handler descriptor; a token is never presented at another merchant (Rail Bindings) Partial: Merchant-binding rule stated, but no gateway check or error code → Q-54 PAY-111 Token requestor lists tokenised merchants and offers de-registration RBI CoFT Annex condition 3 — Gap: Token-requestor merchant listing and de-registration → Q-54 PAY-112 Fresh consent on card renewal before re-linking RBI CoFT Annex condition 5 — Gap: No re-consent state on card reissue → Q-54 PAY-113 A "CNP not enabled" decline becomes an actionable error; no silent fallback RBI/2019-20/142 card_not_enabled_for_cnp with no silent fallback (Errors) Covered PAY-114 Unattended card debits only under an e-mandate or an agentic token RBI E-mandate Framework 2026; AFA Directions Annex 1 (agentic tokens are card-network programmes, not an RBI rule) Open mandates may bind to card e-mandates or agentic tokens; AFA above threshold (Handler Registry) Covered (see Q-39) PAY-116 Cross-border CNP AFA step-up when the acquirer asks RBI AFA Directions para 10 Step-up reason afa_crossborder_cnp when the acquirer requests AFA (Errors) Covered PAY-117 EMI: show principal, interest and discount; never call interest-bearing EMI "no cost" RBI Credit Card Master Direction 6(b)(iii) TermSheet EMI fields; interest-bearing EMI cannot be no-cost (Negotiation) Covered PAY-118 Refunds that create a card credit balance surface the consent states RBI Credit Card Master Direction 10(h) Refund states pending_cardholder_consent, reversed_to_bank_account (Errors) Covered PAY-119 Never refund card, UPI or net-banking payments into a PPI; store credit only on instruction RBI PPI Master Direction 14.3; PA Master Direction 10(f) refund_to_ppi_forbidden; store credit only on explicit instruction (Payments) Covered PAY-120 Refunds of PPI payments go back to the same PPI; a refund of a failed, returned, rejected or cancelled PPI transaction is applied to the PPI immediately RBI PPI Master Direction para 14.3(a) (as updated 30-09-2026) PPI refunds return to the same PPI (Rail Bindings); the split-tender unwind refunds an earlier PPI tender to the same PPI at once (Split tender rules) Covered PAY-121 Enforce PPI caps; no credit-line funding of PPI loads RBI PPI Master Direction 9.1, 9.2 (caps); the credit-line load ban rests on a press-reported RBI clarification (letter not public) PPI wallet limits in the descriptor (Handler Registry) Partial: No rule blocking credit-line loads of PPIs PAY-122 Gift PPI spendable by an agent without AFA; no reload or cash-out RBI PPI Master Direction 10.1, 15.3(5) Gift PPI is class O; codes vaulted away from the agent (Credit and Split Tender) Covered (see Q-30) PAY-123 Net banking only as a redirect; no credentials handled RBI AFA Directions para 6 (redirect-only is BACP policy) Net banking is class C (redirect); credentials never collected (Handler Registry) Covered PAY-124 eNACH carries UMRN, cap, frequency and validity; stop on revocation; T+1 RBI TAT circular, row 7b eNACH debit carries UMRN, cap, frequency and validity; stops on cancellation (Rail Bindings) Covered PAY-125 Credit offer shows lender, amount, tenor, APR, EMI, penal charges and KFS RBI Digital Lending Directions paras 6(iii), 8(i) (withdrawn; 08-05-2025 numbering) Loan offers carry lender, amount, tenor, APR, EMI, interest, penal charges and KFS (Credit and Split Tender) Covered PAY-126 Multi-lender display: every matched offer, unmatched lenders named, pre-disclosed ranking metric RBI Digital Lending Directions paras 6(i) (every matched offer, unmatched lenders named), 6(iv) (pre-disclosed ranking metric) (withdrawn;
