the Reserve Pay block-payee match itself is BACP policy payee.provider_id of the block equals message.order.provider.id of the seller's BPP-signed terms at every leg; a mismatch gets 403 reservepay_block_wrong_payee (Sibling Payment Mandates) Partial: Whether ONDC seller apps share one collection VPA across providers, and whether the signed terms carry provider.id, is not verified as of 18-10-2026 (a question for ONDC) PAY-137 Charges other than the price are distinctly displayed to the payer before the transaction RBI Payment Aggregators Master Direction 2025 (RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141) para 10(c) Payer-borne charge lines with a recipient; the Trusted Surface reads each fee line before the factor (Fees on the payer's screen) Covered PAY-140 Debit-card MDR is not passed on to customers RBI/2017-18/105 (06-12-2017), para 6; in force not verified as of 18-10-2026 MDR is never a payer line and never in a receipt (Who pays) Partial: whether the circular is still in force is not verified PAY-142 A card convenience fee is indicated to the cardholder transparently before the transaction RBI Credit Card and Debit Card Directions 2025 para 77 (binds issuers; context only) Fee lines shown before the factor; the consistency warning covers fees across debit modes Partial: the duty binds issuers, not BACP participants TRADE-113 Recurring payments as mandates; AFA above ₹15,000 RBI E-mandate Framework 2026 Recurring payments as mandates; AFA above threshold (Rail Bindings) Covered TRADE-116 Low-capability channels with enforced limits RBI rules for 123PAY, Lite and AePS Low-capability channel handlers with enforced limits (Handler Registry) Covered REQ-119 Voice never releases money; authentication validates the originating customer's credentials, with one dynamic factor unique to the transaction RBI/2025-26/79 paras 5(a), 5(f), 6(b); NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 para 19.2.2; BACP policy for human-not-present The gateway refuses voice_confirm_plus_device on rail_auth and on a debit-releasing confirm; a PIN is taken only on a PSP-operated surface (Voice confirmation, PIN rule) Covered (see Q-13 for non-money confirmations) REQ-120 An authentication exemption is recorded against its RBI Annexure-1 row, never against a rail rule RBI/2025-26/79 para 6(a) and Annexure-1 (seven rows; later additions apply) Handler descriptor afa.rbi_annex1_item, REQUIRED for exempt and exempt_below_threshold and FORBIDDEN for at_block_creation and at_registration_only; the closed Payment Mandate's afa_ref (Handler registry) Covered (see Q-88) REQ-121 A debit authenticated with the account holder's own PIN, but induced through another person's step-up link, would fall outside the issuer's compensation duty RBI/2025-26/79 para 9(b) TS-6: a Trusted Surface renders a step-up only to the principal or payer that the render names (mandate_id, payer_ref) (Requirements TS-1 to TS-6) Partial: Whether the induced debit is an unauthorised transaction is for counsel → Q-86

docs.title: NPCI and card networks
docs.text:
NPCI scheme rules and circulars for UPI, NACH and Bharat Connect, and card-network programmes. Several NPCI sources are available only to members or through press reports.

Requirement Source BACP control Status PAY-103 No P2P collect; collect only to a verified merchant VPA NPCI circular of 29-07-2025 (press report) UPI collect handler marked P2M only (Handler Registry) Partial: No verified-merchant-VPA rule PAY-104 Agent carts use a dynamic QR or intent bound to the order ID; reject static QR NPCI UPI rules (static and dynamic QR); rejecting static QR for agent carts is BACP policy Dynamic QR or intent bound to the order id; static QR rejected for agent carts (Rail Bindings) Covered PAY-105 P2M caps by category (₹1 lakh / ₹5 lakh), configurable NPCI circular of 28-08-2025 (press report) Category P2M caps applied by the handler intersection amount filter (Handler Registry) Covered PAY-106 OTM: block, then single capture, then release RBI statement of 07-12-2022 (PR 2022-2023/1321; notes UPI single-block-single-debit); vendor documentation OTM block, single capture, release (released_block) (Rail Bindings) Covered (see Q-31) PAY-138 A UPI convenience fee is disclosed upfront and is consistent across debit payment modes; no surcharge on UPI NPCI/UPI/CC/01 (18-09-2026) para 7.5; the duty binds the Payee PSP payment_mode_fee_inconsistent warning (a SHOULD, never a refusal); convenience_fees mandate constraint in HNP (Fees on the payer's screen) Partial: whether disclosure through an agent is disclosure "to the User" is counsel's and NPCI's question (Q-78) PAY-139 Merchants do not pass MDR on to UPI customers; UPI apps charge no platform fee NPCI FAQ updated 15-10-2026, Q34 and Q17 (an FAQ; no circular found) MDR, PA commission and finder fee never principal-facing; an operator fee is a disclosed line that is not a licence to charge (Who pays) Covered REQ-410 Software on UPI Circle only where NPCI permits it, onboarded by the secondary PSP bank after due diligence and app security evaluation NPCI UPI OC 201B (NPCI/UPI/OC-201B/2025-26, 08-10-2025) general item 4 and secondary-app items in.upi.circle is pilot; an open mandate on it needs a conformance attestation from a listed authority, and in.upi.circle stays closed to open mandates for now (UPI Circle, Conformance) Partial: Whether software and AI profiles are within the circular's scope is not answered → Q-77 REQ-411 Debits using IoT on UPI Circle are initiated only by explicit user action NPCI UPI OC 201B p.1: "debit transactions using IoT shall be only initiated by explicit user action" No open (human-not-present) mandate on in.upi.circle; human-present Circle payments are unaffected (UPI Circle) Partial: The circular does not define "explicit user action" or mention agents → Q-77 REQ-412 UPI Circle first-24-hour limit NPCI UPI OC 201 (13-08-2024) item 9 (a daily transaction limit of ₹5,000 in the first 24 hours) and OC 201B (08-10-2025) item 8 (a cumulative limit of ₹5,000 for the first 24 hours); NPCI UPI Circle product page (₹2,000) first_24h kept at ₹2,000 and graded conflict in the registry; the stricter value is enforced (Handler Registry) Partial: The two NPCI sources conflict; which figure the rail enforces is not confirmed as of 18-10-2026 PAY-115 Agentic-token intent object kept as dispute evidence Mastercard Agent Pay launch, 29-04-2025 (Agentic Tokens; dispute support); keeping the intent object is BACP policy Agentic token intent primitive in the descriptor (Handler Registry) Partial: Intent object not kept in receipts or evidence → Q-39 PAY-202 Show only the bank-returned payee name; agent cannot edit it NPCI payee-name rule (secondary); RBI/2024-25/99 The user sees only the bank-returned payee name; the agent cannot edit it; a name mismatch is held for human confirmation (Rail Bindings) Covered PAY-206 NACH mandates registered only with human AFA; eSign ≤₹1 lakh; NB/DC cap configurable NPCI/2020-21/NACH/Circular No.010, 15-07-2020 (secondary; not verified against the NPCI text as of 17-10-2026) NACH mandate caps by authentication mode (nach_mandate_above_cap) (Rail Bindings) Covered (see Q-29) PAY-208 No NACH presentment after cancellation; T+1 refund NPCI NACH OC 008 (not verified); RBI TAT row 7b No presentment after cancellation (mandate_cancelled); T+1 refund (Rail Bindings) Covered PAY-211 UPMS registration bound to an underlying mandate, inheriting its limits NBBL circulars NPCI/2023-24/BBPS/009 (31-08-2023) and /016 (11-10-2023); RBI E-mandate Framework 2026 UPMS registration bound to an underlying mandate (Rail Bindings) Covered TRADE-134 BBPS fetch-then-pay plus auto-pay NBBL (Bharat Connect) UPMS circulars NPCI/2023-24/BBPS/009, /016 BBPS fetch-then-pay and UPMS auto-pay handlers (Handler Registry) Covered PAY-231 A Reserve Pay block and a UPI OTM are authenticated when they are created; execution is validated by digital signature NPCI UPI OC 200 item 3, para (d); UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 paras 15.2 and 15.4 afa.source of in.upi.reservepay and in.upi.otm cites these rules; neither handler carries an rbi_annex1_item (Handler registry) Covered (see Q-88)

docs.title: MeitY: IT Act, CERT-In, DPDP Act, DPDP Rules and Aadhaar
docs.text:
The CERT-In Directions of 28-04-2022 under s.70B(6) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (in force), the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules 2025, and UIDAI regulations. Rule 4 and Act s.6(9) (Consent Manager registration) apply from 13-11-2026; Rules 3, 5–16, 22 and 23 and the Act's duties and penalties (ss.3–17 except s.6(9), and the Board's proceedings and penalties in ss.28–34) from 13-05-2027 (Rules G.S.R. 846(E) and Act commencement G.S.R. 843(E), both of 13-11-2025; see Security and Privacy).

Requirement Source BACP control Status REQ-107 Revoke or pause at any time, including partially; propagate in ≤60 s DPDP Act s.6(4) (withdrawal at any time); RBI NBFC-AA Master Direction para 6.6 (pattern); pause, partial revocation and the 60 s target are BACP policy Revoke and pause on the Trusted Surface, propagated within 60 s; live firm offers withdrawn (Mandates) Partial: No partial revocation (narrowing scope or categories) REQ-111 Mandate Manager is data-blind DPDP Rules, First Schedule Part B item 2 Mandate Manager stores mandates and logs only; payment leg is basket-blind (Security and Privacy) Partial: Fail-safe default: an MM acting as a registered Consent Manager does not also act as credential provider; co-location with the PSP open → Q-16 REQ-112 MM keeps records for 7 years and exports them machine-readably DPDP Rules, First Schedule Part B items 3–4 Mandate Manager keeps records for 7 years (Security and Privacy) Partial: Machine-readable export required on the Trusted Surface; no REST export endpoint in this version → Q-16 REQ-118 Separate explicit consent for model training DPDP Act s.6(1) (specified-purpose consent; a separate training consent is BACP's reading) — Gap: No separate consent class for model training → Q-17 REQ-201 Itemised notice before sharing: fields, purpose, recipient, withdrawal and complaint routes, language DPDP Act s.5; DPDP Rule 3 ConsentReceipt records itemised fields, purpose, recipient, language, withdrawal and grievance routes (Security and Privacy) Partial: Per-seller receipt required at init before any release; validity of the class pre-authorisation open, with Trusted Surface confirmation as fail-safe from 13-05-2027 → Q-12 REQ-202 Consent only from an explicit affirmative user action DPDP Act s.6(1); Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(9) for purchases Consent captured only on the Trusted Surface by an affirmative action, with a device signature (Security and Privacy) Covered REQ-203 Data to a merchant ⊆ mandate data_scopes and what the order needs DPDP Act s.6(1) Data shared ⊆ mandate data_scopes, covered by a ConsentReceipt; otherwise mandate_scope_mismatch (Security and Privacy) Covered REQ-204 Selective disclosure through Aadhaar VC or DigiLocker; Aadhaar number never sent or stored Aadhaar Act; UIDAI Aadhaar Offline Verification Handbook (January 2026) Aadhaar number never collected; selective-disclosure data items (Security and Privacy) Partial: No VC verification profile; no Aadhaar-number scan → Q-55 REQ-205 Aadhaar VC verifiers are registered OVSEs Aadhaar (Authentication and Offline Verification) Amendment Regulations 2025 (cited via the UIDAI Handbook; Gazette text not checked) — Gap: OVSE registration of verifiers not captured → Q-55 REQ-206 Withdrawal as easy as consent; erasure at agent, processors and merchants DPDP Act s.6(4), s.6(6), s.8(7); DPDP Rule 3 ConsentReceipt withdrawal URI and erasure signal; consent-withdrawn event (Security and Privacy) Partial: No downstream erasure message, acknowledgement or SLA → Q-17 REQ-207 Keep order, payment and delivery records and logs ≥1 year, then erase DPDP Rules 8(3), 6(1)(e) ConsentReceipt retention.legal_minimum (one year); mandate dpdp.data_retention (Security and Privacy) Partial: No retention policy for InstructionLog, receipts, evidence or gateway logs → Q-17 REQ-208 Publish DPO contact; grievances within 90 days (e-commerce 48 h / 1 month) DPDP Rules 9, 14(3); Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(5) for the 48 h / 1 month e-commerce timelines Operator grievance officer in the AgentCredential; recipient DPO contact; IGM response times (Security and Privacy) Partial: DPO contact optional; no SLA metrics → Q-17 REQ-209 Breach notice to users and the Board without delay (Board report within 72 h); cross-participant breach signal DPDP Act s.8(6); DPDP Rule 7 — Gap: No breach-signal message (proposed bacp.breach_signal) → Q-17 REQ-210 Under 18: verifiable parental consent; no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising DPDP Act s.9; DPDP Rules 10 and 12 Age-over-18 data scope only (Security and Privacy) Gap: No minor mode or parental-consent artefact → Q-17 REQ-211 MM acting as Consent Manager is Board-registered from Rule 4 commencement DPDP Rule 4; First Schedule ConsentReceipt cm_registration_no (Security and Privacy) Partial: From 13-11-2026, cm_registration_no is required when the MM acts as a Consent Manager and null otherwise; whether the MM must register is open → Q-16 REQ-213 SDFs run an annual DPIA and audit and document algorithmic due diligence DPDP Act s.10; DPDP Rule 13 Operator governance; AgentCredential model family and build support the inventory (Conformance: Operator, attested, not tested) N/A: operator duty outside the protocol REQ-214 s.8(3) accuracy duty; correction-propagation message DPDP Act s.8(3) — Gap: No correction-propagation message → Q-17 REQ-215 Processor contracts (including LLM hosts) carry DPDP security and erasure clauses DPDP Act s.8(2), s.8(7)(b); DPDP Rule 6(1)(f) Contractual duty of the operator (Conformance: Operator, attested, not tested) N/A: operator duty outside the protocol REQ-216 Large e-commerce: erase after 3 years inactive, with a 48 h warning DPDP Rules 8(1)–(2), Third Schedule item 1 (e-commerce entities with at least two crore registered users in India) Operator data-lifecycle duty (Conformance: Operator, attested, not tested) N/A: operator duty outside the protocol REQ-217 Report specified cyber incidents (including data breaches and leaks) to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them CERT-In Directions under IT Act, 2000 s.70B(6) (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28-04-2022; in force) (secondary) Each participant's own report (Security and Privacy) Partial: Reporting is a participant duty outside the protocol; no cross-participant signal to start other participants' clocks (proposed bacp.breach_signal) → Q-17 REQ-218 Keep ICT system logs for a rolling 180 days within India; produce them to CERT-In on request CERT-In Directions of 28-04-2022 (secondary) Stated as a participant duty covering gateway and InstructionLog logs (Security and Privacy) Partial: No protocol retention table for InstructionLog, receipts, evidence or gateway logs → Q-17 REQ-219 Synchronise ICT system clocks to the NTP servers of NIC or NPL, or servers traceable to them CERT-In Directions of 28-04-2022 (secondary) Signature created / expires with a 5 s clock-skew bound (Security and Privacy); a clock-traceability MUST for negotiation participants, which is a duty on each clock and never an ordering input (Negotiation) N/A: operator duty outside the protocol REQ-407 Health purchases via UHI/NHCX; health data under an ABDM consent artefact, with separate consent ABDM (programme, not a statute); separate consent for health data is BACP policy, since the DPDP Act has no sensitive-data category Document reference type for an ABDM consent artefact (Trade Profiles) Gap: No health data scope or separate consent class → Q-17 REQ-408 Notices in English plus the chosen Eighth Schedule language; log model and version DPDP Act s.5(3), s.6(3); model logging is BACP policy Multilingual notices; notice language and translation model recorded in ConsentReceipt and InstructionLog (Security and Privacy) Covered NEG-194 When an electronic record is despatched and received, save as otherwise agreed; an unacknowledged record is deemed never sent where an acknowledgement is stipulated IT Act, 2000 s.12(2), s.13(1) Protocol terms named in every firm message (protocol_terms{version, hash}) (Negotiation) Partial: Whether the terms are "otherwise agreed" for a consumer, and s.11 attribution → Q-19, Q-52 REQ-413 Consent to disclose whom an agent acts for; a sole proprietor's GSTIN and name are personal data DPDP Act, 2023, s.6(1) and s.6(10) (from 13-05-2027) ACTING_FOR in the ConsentReceipt data_items[]; the gateway sends acting_for to a seller only under a per-seller receipt that lists it (Data minimisation) Covered REQ-414 Notice and consent request in English or an Eighth Schedule language DPDP Act, 2023, s.6(3) (from 13-05-2027), cited as alignment Language fail-safe: a Trusted Surface that cannot render the step-up's language renders nothing, and the gateway answers 503 trusted_surface_unavailable with handoff routes (Language fail-safe) Partial: A principal whose language no Trusted Surface serves gets a human route, not self-service REQ-415 An assisted operator's act attributed to the principal Information Technology Act, 2000, s.11(b) and s.11(c) assisted_by and Participant.ref are attribution, never authentication; ref_verification is asserted until a registry exists (Assisted channel) Partial: Whether the operator's act is attributable, and what proves authority, is for counsel → Q-86 and Q-62 REQ-416 Verifiable consent of the lawful guardian of a person with disability who has one DPDP Act, 2023, s.9(1) (from 13-05-2027) None in this version: a Proposed participant role lawful_guardian, with no disability data and no ACTING_FOR or assisted stand-in (Legal time bands) Gap: No schema before a later release REQ-417 Marketing communication needs the principal's clear affirmative action for that purpose, and withdrawal as easy as consent DPDP Act, 2023, s.6(1) and s.6(4) (from 13-05-2027); Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (not checked against the primary text as of 18-10-2026) The fail-safe (no receipt, no grant) is normative; a standalone marketing ConsentReceipt (Proposed) carries purposes[] with none preselected, channels[], a named seller and the withdrawal route (Marketing consent) Partial: The receipt is Proposed, and its relation to the TCCCPR preferences is open (Q-101)

docs.title: CCPA and Consumer Protection
docs.text:
The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 and the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns 2023. The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026) apply from 01-01-2027. They substitute r.4(2) and r.4(5)–(7), r.5(3)(a), (c) and (f), r.6(5)(d) and r.7(1)(a), and add r.4(11)(c) (no search manipulation), r.4(12)–(15) (sponsored listings, prior price, seller name on the invoice, Dark Patterns compliance and self-audit), r.5(6)–(7) and r.6(5)(j). Rows below cite the 2020 numbering and note where the amendment changes it.

Requirement Source BACP control Status REQ-311 No confirm without a covering mandate or confirmation; decline pre-ticked add-ons Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 r.4(9) No confirmation without a covering mandate; pre-ticked add-ons removed (preticked_addon_removed) (Checkout) Covered REQ-312 Agent uses none of the 13 dark patterns toward the user CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns 2023 (compliance and a yearly self-audit made mandatory by new r.4(15) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, inserted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026, G.S.R. 789(E) of 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027); the Guidelines text has been read: the pattern list is Annex 1) Widening only on the non-agentic Trusted Surface (Security and Privacy) Partial: No rule against dark patterns in agent-to-user messages REQ-313 Detect merchant dark patterns: basket sneaking, drip pricing, false urgency, subscription traps CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns 2023 (compliance and a yearly self-audit made mandatory by new r.4(15) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, inserted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026, G.S.R. 789(E) of 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027); the Guidelines text has been read: the pattern list is Annex 1) Drip pricing, pre-ticked add-on, false-urgency and basket-sneaking checks (Checkout) Partial: No subscription-trap detection REQ-314 Show mandatory disclosures before commit: total with breakup, seller, origin, return terms, delivery Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.6(5), r.5; ONDC buyer-app duty. From 01-01-2027 the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E)) substitute r.5(3)(a), (c) and r.6(5)(d) (the new clause lists country of origin, best-before date, return terms and return-shipping cost) and add r.6(5)(j) (GSTIN or MSME registration number) Disclosures require total with breakup, seller, origin, delivery, return and cancellation terms; missing → disclosures_missing (Checkout) Covered REQ-315 Expose ranking main parameters and any sponsorship Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.5(3)(f) (ranking parameters), r.5(4) (differentiated treatment); sponsored listings distinctly identified under new r.4(12), inserted by the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027); the same amendment substitutes r.5(3)(f) (ranking parameters "in descending order") from that date Every discovery item carries a per-item sponsorship (sponsored, not_sponsored or undeclared, with the party that sold the placement); ranking.main_parameters is in descending order of importance; ranking.sponsored summarises the items (Catalogue disclosures) Partial: per-item sponsorship and ranking order are carried; whether an agent operator or a gateway is the e-commerce entity, and how the duty applies where no human sees the list, are open → Q-66 REQ-323 Show the prior price with a price reduction; the prior price is the lowest price in the 30 days before the announcement Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(13), inserted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027); Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules r.2(m) and r.18(2) (retail sale price inclusive of all taxes; text checked as of 18-10-2026) prior_price{amount, basis: lowest_30d, announced_on} asserted by the seller and never created by the gateway; mrp and tax_inclusive carried separately; an agent voices a reduction only as the amount pair, and no reduction, strike-through or percentage without a prior_price (Catalogue disclosures). A discount line from a coupon is never shown as a reduced item price, a strike-through or a percentage of an item price unless the item carries a verified prior_price (Discounts); whether a coupon, a bank offer or a cart-level offer is an announced reduction is not settled Partial: whose lowest price counts, whether the rule binds an agent operator or a gateway, and whether a coupon is an announced reduction are open → Q-66 REQ-324 No manipulation of search results or search indexes against the user's query Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(11)(c), added by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) Ranking parameters and per-item sponsorship are disclosed; the default ranking does not use discount size (Catalogue disclosures). No conformance case detects manipulation of the order itself Gap: audit only; no conformance hook for the order of results REQ-325 Explain the main ranking parameters in descending order, with their relative importance, in an easily and publicly available description Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.5(3)(f), substituted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) ranking.main_parameters in descending order of importance and an optional ranking.description_url (Discovery) Covered REQ-326 Show the seller's name on the invoice in the same font size as the e-commerce entity's name Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(14), inserted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) None: BACP carries no invoice display rule Gap: no design REQ-327 A marketplace does not use collected information to sell goods under its own brand, or to promote a seller as associated with it, without express and affirmative consent Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.5(6), inserted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) None Gap: no design REQ-328 No bundled fee for an unrelated service (loyalty and membership programmes excepted) Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.5(7), inserted by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) A per-order operator fee is a disclosed operator_charges[] line, outside the BPP quote (Fees on the payer's screen); BACP does not decide whether it is a bundled fee Partial: whether a per-order operator fee is a "bundled fee" is counsel's question (Q-79) REQ-329 Show the seller's GST or MSME registration number Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.6(5)(j), added by the (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) None: the mandatory disclosures carry no registration number Gap: no design REQ-330 Do not represent that a service has sponsorship, approval or affiliation that it lacks; a conformance attestation is not approval Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.2(47)(i)(d) and (e) (unfair trade practice) The attestation says "passed BACP protocol tests", never "certified" or "approved", and is not offered in place of any rail onboarding or certification; a profile that labels it otherwise is non-conforming (Conformance; case DISP-01) Covered REQ-321 Grievance officer acknowledges in 48 h and resolves in 1 month; ticket number Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules r.4(5), r.5(3)(b); r.4(5) as substituted from 01-01-2027 (G.S.R. 789(E)) keeps 48 h / one month and adds giving the complainant a copy of the complaint as recorded Grievance officer in the AgentCredential; issue id; expected response times (Beckn binding) Partial: No SLA clocks or auto-escalation → Q-57 PAY-132 Payment-method fees shown before commit; compare totals CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; drip pricing) Per-option all-in totals from round 1; handler comparison logged (Handler Registry) Covered NEG-114 on_init term hash must equal the accepted offer hash, otherwise NEG_TERMS_DRIFT CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; bait and switch) on_init terms must equal the accepted offer, otherwise NEG_TERMS_DRIFT and BREACH_FLAGGED (Negotiation) Covered NEG-121 An accepted firm offer must be honoured; breach goes to IGM CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; bait and switch) Firm-offer breach logged to IGM; buyer cancels without penalty (Negotiation) Covered (see Q-22) NEG-122 quote.price equals all_in_total from round 1 CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; drip pricing) all_in_total required from round 1 and equal to the quote price (Negotiation) Covered NEG-123 Minimum offer validity (floor PT5M in every profile) CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; false urgency) Minimum offer validity (floor PT5M in every profile), NEG_FALSE_URGENCY (Negotiation) Covered NEG-135 Step-up when the all-in total rises CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; drip pricing) Step-up when the all-in total rises beyond the mandate tripwire (Negotiation) Covered NEG-171 Pricing basis declared; no device-based pricing CCPA notices to ride-hailing apps, Jan 2025 (press reports; no primary text) Pricing basis declared; prohibited attributes refused (NEG_PERSONALISED_PRICING) (Negotiation) Covered TRADE-121 Total payable with all fees; later fees need re-consent CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; drip pricing) Charges carry the round they were first disclosed; later fees need re-consent (Negotiation) Covered TRADE-133 Subscriptions: pause, skip, resume, change quantity, one-step cancel with proof CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (Gazette of India Part III s.4 No. 783, 30-11-2023; docs.title: Security and Privacy
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page states the BACP threat model and the controls that answer it, then how BACP handles personal data under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025. The controls are defined normatively on the pages linked from each row; this page collects them so that an implementer or auditor can check coverage in one place.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text:
BACP assumes that:

  • Every language model and every agent is a potential attacker. Prompt injection cannot be prevented, so an agent is never trusted to verify anything that matters. It never holds a UPI PIN or OTP, never signs consent, and is never an authentication factor.
  • All seller and counterparty content is untrusted input: catalogue text, offers, chat, IGM messages and webhook-relayed text may carry dark patterns or injected instructions.
  • The payment rail is authoritative for money movement, but BACP does not rely on rail limits to bound BACP budgets (see Atomic reservation).
  • The gateway is trusted to enforce policy deterministically, and is held to that by conformance tests and by evidence, not by its word.
  • The Trusted Surface (the payer PSP or Mandate Manager app) is non-agentic. It alone captures consent, PINs and step-up approvals.

The guiding rule is: the model proposes, the engine decides. Every commitment that binds the buyer passes a deterministic, non-LLM verifier inside the gateway, which fails closed.

docs.title: Prompt injection: the model proposes, the engine decides
docs.text:
1. Every money-moving or binding action (complete, a firm COUNTER, an ACCEPT, a bid, an award, a post-order write) MUST pass the gateway's deterministic mandate evaluation (and, in negotiation, the guard). This code MUST NOT call a language model and MUST fail closed on anything it cannot evaluate, including unknown mandate constraints.
  2. The verifier keys on structured identifiers (item_id, bpp_id, category codes, amounts in paise), never on display names, so homoglyph or injected titles change nothing.
  3. Injected quantities are bounded by the mandate's line_items, amount_per_txn, budgets and step-up rules. An out-of-bounds cart leads to a step-up or a refusal, never to an automatic payment.
  4. Counterparty free text is untrusted data. It MUST be returned only as a message with code untrusted_counterparty_text; it cannot call tools, change mandates or trigger an ACCEPT. Suspected instructions are flagged NEG_INJECTION_SUSPECTED.
  5. The only mandate-related signal a negotiating model sees is the guard's verdict (acceptable, not_acceptable, needs_escalation). The bounds themselves never enter the model's context.
  6. Widening anything (a larger budget, a new category, a price above the reservation) happens only on the Trusted Surface. The diff shown to the buyer is rendered there, never by the agent.

docs.title: Mandate and limit abuse
docs.text:
• Mandates are immutable, signed artefacts with an explicit purpose code, action_scope, data_scopes, budgets, allow-lists and step-up rules. Unknown constraint keys fail closed.
  • At mandate request, the gateway or Mandate Manager MUST reject a request that exceeds the purpose's bounds, or names a purpose code not in the registry, before anything reaches the Trusted Surface (mandate_scope_mismatch). The purpose-code registry is governed by the BACP working group (settled in Q-47).
  • BACP constraints MUST be at or below the bound rail's limits.
  • An AFA threshold produces a rail_auth step-up. Every other rail cap produces 403 rail_limit_exceeded with every local and rail reason in reasons[].
  • Revocation stops new commitments within 60 seconds. Protective post-order writes (cancel, return, issue) on existing orders remain allowed, with the principal present, after a revocation, a pause for any reason, expiry or exhaustion.

docs.title: Merchant spoofing
docs.text:
• Every Beckn callback MUST be verified against the seller app's registry key, and the signer MUST equal the bpp_id in the callback's context. A key of the wrong registry role MUST be refused.
  • A callback MUST be bound to the request it answers. Unsolicited callbacks that do not match a known order, return, issue or negotiation MUST be ignored and logged, never applied. See Beckn / ONDC Binding.
  • Seller identity in a quote is bound into the closed checkout mandate through checkout_hash, so a substituted seller cannot be paid under the buyer's mandate.
  • Before any money moves, the gateway MUST check from the registry that the party in collected_by is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank (collector_not_authorised otherwise).

docs.title: Replay protection
docs.text:
• The RFC 9421 signature carries created, expires, nonce, keyid and tag. expires − created MUST NOT exceed 300 s, and clock skew of up to 5 s is allowed. Participants subject to the CERT-In Directions already synchronise their system clocks to the NTP servers of NIC or NPL (or servers traceable to them), which keeps them well inside this window.
  • The gateway MUST keep a (keyid, nonce) cache until expires. A hit returns 401 replay_detected. The nonce is stored only after the signature verifies.
  • On the network leg, the Beckn message_id is derived deterministically from the agent, the idempotency key and the action, so a retry re-sends the identical message; BACP-aware receivers MUST NACK a duplicate message_id within its ttl.
  • Each closed payment mandate MAY be consumed at most once, and at most one debit is allowed per checkout_hash.

docs.title: Atomic reservation and budget TOCTOU
docs.text:
A budget check that reads "spent so far" and then debits is a time-of-check-to-time-of-use race: two concurrent complete calls can both see the same remaining budget and both settle. BACP closes the race with a reservation ledger.

  1. Reservation ledger. For every open payment mandate the gateway MUST keep (a) settled spends, derived only from PSP-signed receipts, and (b) in-flight reservations keyed by closed payment mandate id, each with an amount and a time. Exposure for a budget window is settled spends plus reservations in that window. Exposure against an open checkout mandate's budgets is the settled spends and reservations of every open payment mandate under it.
  2. Atomic section. For complete, the following MUST run as one atomic, linearisable operation keyed on the root open checkout mandate id: the split-order check; the authoritative mandate evaluation (including the positive-amount rule) against exposure; consumption of the closed payment mandate; creation of the reservation; and the session's move to complete_in_progress. The root open checkout mandate is the open checkout mandate named by the open payment mandate's checkout_mandate_ref, followed through parent_mandate_id to the top of any delegation chain. Keying on it, not on the payment mandate id, serialises sibling open payment mandates under one checkout mandate (for example one Reserve Pay block per seller), whose only common cap is the checkout mandate's budgets. A split-tender payment plan MUST reserve every tender in one atomic section. A lock keyed on the root open checkout mandate id, or compare-and-reserve on a store with equivalent guarantees, satisfies this. The rail debit MUST run after the atomic section, never inside it.
  3. What counts. Budgets, max_executions, every rail-cap pre-check (period caps, first-24-hour caps, remaining block) and split-order detection MUST count reservations as spent. Each Reserve Pay block counts as reserved spend at its full attested amount until its revocation is confirmed or it expires, and the gateway applies the activation of a sibling block in the same atomic section, so that an issuance and a complete never take the same headroom (Usage ledger).
  4. Resolution. A reservation becomes a settled spend only when a PSP-signed success receipt is applied. It MUST be released on a PSP-signed failure receipt or a refused debit, and kept while the payment is in_doubt. Once every payment on a mandate has resolved, no reservation may remain.
  5. The rail is not the backstop. A gateway MUST NOT rely on rail-enforced limits to bound BACP budgets: the rail authority may legitimately exceed the BACP caps, and the multi-seller rails (UPI Circle, agentic card tokens) are exactly the loose ones.
  6. Replicas. A gateway running as several instances MUST share a ledger that is linearisable per root open checkout mandate. A per-process lock is not enough. Atomicity is per root inside one gateway, and one open mandate belongs to one gateway (agent.bap_id), so there is no cross-gateway section to take; a mandate moves between gateways only by a successor root (Porting a mandate, Q-36, settled).
  7. Negotiation exposure. The guard's cross-session exposure check, and the emission of the firm COUNTER, ACCEPT or bid it guards, MUST run in the same kind of atomic section, keyed on the principal. Each outstanding firm commitment holds a reservation until it is rejected, expires, is withdrawn or superseded, or is paid.
  8. Lock order. There are two levels, the principal (K1) and the root open checkout mandate (K2), and a gateway MUST take them in this order and never the reverse. The idempotency in-flight marker is written before K1 and is a write, not a held lock. A K1 section that guards several roots takes their K2 sections in ascending mandate_id order. Inside K2, the ledger's chain-head compare-and-swap and the receipt-uniqueness insert-if-absent do not block: if either fails, the whole K2 operation aborts with nothing reserved. No rail, Beckn or webhook I/O runs inside either level. K2 does not see a K1 reservation by taking K1: the guard writes each firm ACCEPT, counter-offer or bid it emits into the root's ledger as a reservation keyed by offer_hash, so that exposure in K2 counts it, and a complete of the negotiated deal converts that reservation in K2 in one step. The per-root check that no reservation or settled debit exists for a checkout_hash also runs in K2 (Deterministic evaluation, step 4).
  9. Split-order scope. Split-order detection is per (root open checkout mandate, seller) within 10 minutes and MUST count completed and in-flight orders. The seller is identified by the tax id in the BPP-signed terms, else by the payee VPA, else by the pair bpp_id and provider_id; two orders are the same seller when any of these identifiers match. The covers[] legs of a summary-approved basket are exempt. Cross-seller velocity is bounded only by the budgets (Q-50, settled).
  10. Pre-checks. The PUT /sessions/{id} pre-check is advisory and MUST NOT create reservations. A step-up or a rejection MUST NOT create a reservation.

Conformance requirement. N concurrent complete calls on one open mandate MUST NOT settle more than any budget allows, even when the rail authority is far larger than the budget, and MUST NOT leave reservations behind.

docs.title: Positive-amount rule
docs.text:
• The first step of mandate evaluation: the payable amount MUST be an integer number of paise greater than zero (a boolean is not an integer). Otherwise the result is 403 amount_not_positive, before any other step and before any reservation.
  • Every tender in a payment plan MUST be greater than zero, even when the tenders sum correctly.
  • Every value-bearing credit-ledger posting MUST be greater than zero; direction is carried by the entry type, never by the sign.
  • Schemas keep Amount (minimum: 0) where zero is legitimate (a free-goods line, a remaining budget). Payable amounts (a closed mandate's amount, a payment or refund Receipt's amount, a payment-plan tender's amount) use PositiveAmount from common.json (value minimum: 1).

docs.title: Data minimisation and over-sharing
docs.text:
• Data shared with a seller MUST be a subset of the mandate's data_scopes and MUST be covered by a ConsentReceipt for that recipient. Anything else gets 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at the session update.
  • No personal data travels through the Beckn gateway (BG); search carries only context and intent.
  • The payment leg to the PSP is basket-blind.
  • The InstructionLog keeps content encrypted at the operator. Only hashes and references leave it, and content is released only inside an evidence bundle to a party entitled to it.
  • Receipts and evidence MUST NOT contain any value a handler descriptor lists under never_collect (UPI PIN, OTP, card number, CVV, expiry, Aadhaar number, biometrics, net-banking credentials).
  • An Aadhaar number is never collected; age or identity attributes use selective disclosure.

docs.title: Reservation-price DLP
docs.text:
• The buyer's reservation price and total_max live only in the negotiation mandate and in the gateway's guard. The schema fixes disclosure: never.
  • The seller verifies only a signed within_bounds attestation from the buyer's credential provider. No seller-facing message, response, webhook or log may carry reservation, total_max or a payment range maximum.
  • TermSheets are closed objects, so an undeclared field cannot smuggle a bound out.
  • The leak check MUST be provenance-aware: a number the counterparty sent first and the buyer side merely echoes is not a leak. Only buyer-originated content is judged.
  • Guard log entries record constraint ids only, never values.

docs.title: Resource limits
docs.text: Limit Rule Body size Every agent endpoint and /trusted-surface/events MUST refuse a body above 256 KiB with 413 request_too_large, checked on raw bytes before signature verification, digest computation or JSON parsing. A gateway MAY set a lower limit. Proposed: publish it in /.well-known/bacp as limits.max_body_bytes. Per-agent idempotency quota Per agent (AgentCredential.sub), at most 10,000 live keys and 64 requests in flight by default. Exceeding either returns 429 quota_exceeded with Retry-After. The store MUST NOT evict a live key early to make room. Signature lifetime expires − created ≤ 300 s; the nonce cache is bounded by that window. Upstream waits A missing on_* callback MUST end the wait with 504 bpp_timeout (or the payment saga states), never an unbounded wait.

docs.title: URL fetch hygiene
docs.text:
BACP fetches a document from a URL in a few places: a gateway's /.well-known/bacp profile, a key set (keys, a registry key set), the profile that a UCP-Agent header names and any documentation URL that a participant publishes. A URL that a counterparty supplies is untrusted input. The rules below are at the strength of UCP's own fetch rules (as of 18-10-2026): three are MUST and four are SHOULD, and the body bound is a SHOULD because a MUST would be BACP's own choice and would break fetchers that exist today. They do not apply to a Beckn registry lookup, which has its own signed form (Registry lookup).

# Rule Level 1 The URL MUST be https. A fetcher MUST NOT fetch an http URL. MUST 2 A fetcher MUST NOT follow a redirect (3xx). MUST 3 A fetcher SHOULD set connect and total timeouts. SHOULD 4 A fetcher SHOULD NOT cache a document for less than 60 seconds (a floor, not a time to live). SHOULD 5 A fetcher MUST resolve the host and refuse an address that is not globally routable (RFC 6890 special-purpose ranges, including loopback, private, link-local such as 169.254.169.254, and unique-local addresses), checking the resolved address and not only the name. MUST 6 A fetcher SHOULD force one refresh when a signature or digest check fails against a cached copy, and no more. SHOULD 7 A fetcher SHOULD accept a body of at least 128 KiB and SHOULD refuse a larger one that it does not need. SHOULD

The split is UCP's: its rules 1, 2 and 7 (rules 1, 2 and 5 here) are MUST, and its rules 3, 4, 6 and 8 (rules 3, 4, 6 and 7 here) are SHOULD. A fetched document is data. It never changes a version, an amount, a payee, a handler, a mandate or a signer, and a gateway never derives a key or an extension schema from it without the checks that the registry rules state. Inbound request bodies are already capped at 256 KiB (request_too_large).

docs.title: Field-scoped webhooks
docs.text:
1. A webhook body MUST NOT embed a signed receipt. Every embedded receipt MUST be replaced by a ReceiptRef: receipt_id, receipt_hash (sha-256 over the JCS form of the full signed receipt), receipt_type, result and, where present, amount, refund_state and rail{type, rrn, status, original_rrn}.
  2. The full signed receipt MUST be available by authenticated GET on its owning resource (session, order or return) to the party of record.
  3. An agent that needs the receipt SHOULD fetch it and MUST check that its hash equals receipt_hash.
  4. Webhooks remain gateway-signed, full-state snapshots in every other respect.
  5. A webhook MUST NOT carry personal data outside the receiving agent's mandate data_scopes, nor any negotiation bound.

See REST for delivery and signing.

docs.title: Server state under concurrency
docs.text:
• A gateway MUST NOT return a server error because of concurrent access to its own state. Iterations over shared registries take a snapshot under the owning lock.
  • Production gateways SHOULD keep idempotency records, the nonce cache and budget reservations in a shared atomic store, so that every instance sees the same state.
  • A seller's order id is unique only within that seller, so the gateway keys orders by (bpp_id, order_id). An order-scoped request that is ambiguous without bpp_id gets 400 invalid_request at $.bpp_id. See REST.

docs.title: Privacy under the DPDP Act and Rules
docs.text:
Not legal advice

This section describes how BACP carries the artefacts that DPDP duties need. It is not legal advice and does not establish that any deployment complies with the DPDP Act or Rules. Dates and penalties are taken from the Gazette texts cited here and may change by later notification. Each participant remains responsible for its own compliance and should take advice from qualified counsel.

BACP treats every seller that receives the buyer's personal data as a separate Data Fiduciary, and the agent operator and buyer app as Fiduciaries for their own processing. The protocol carries the artefacts each of them needs to show compliance; it does not replace their own notices and policies.

docs.title: Commencement
docs.text:
Provisions Applies from Notes DPDP Rules 1, 2 and 17–21 (the Data Protection Board); Act s.1(2), s.2, ss.18–26, 35, 38–43, 44(1) and 44(3) 13-11-2025, on publication (Rules: G.S.R. 846(E); Act commencement: G.S.R. 843(E), both of 13-11-2025) In force. Rule 4 and the First Schedule (Consent Managers); Act s.6(9) (Consent Manager registration) and s.27(1)(d) 13-11-2026 (one year after publication) See Consent Manager role. Rules 3, 5–16, 22 and 23 (notice, security, breach, retention, children, Significant Data Fiduciaries, rights, cross-border transfer); Act ss.3–5, 6(1)–(8) and 6(10), 7–17, 27 (except 27(1)(d)), 28–34, 36, 37 and 44(2) 13-05-2027 (eighteen months after publication) The Act's duties and its penalties (s.33 and the Schedule) commence on the same date as these Rules (G.S.R. 843(E)). RBI direction on Storage of Payment System Data (06-04-2018) In force See Data localisation. CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28-04-2022): 6-hour incident reporting, 180-day log retention in India, NTP clock synchronisation In force Not a DPDP instrument; see Breach notice and Retention.

Dates may move

A MeitY consultation in January 2026 reportedly proposed shortening some of the eighteen-month periods to twelve months; reports differ on whether it covers all the duties or only Rule 13. It is reported in secondary sources only, and no amending notification had been found as of 17-10-2026. A corrigendum to the Rules (G.S.R. 892(E), 10-12-2025) and the DPDP (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 (S.O. 5458(E), Order dated 05-10-2026, Gazette issue 06-10-2026) change wording only and move no date. A further corrigendum, G.S.R. 113(E), is listed by a secondary source (reported, not verified as of 17-10-2026). See Q-53.

docs.title: Notice and consent
docs.text:
• Consent is captured only on the Trusted Surface, by an explicit affirmative action (tap, PIN, biometric or passkey), never inferred by an agent. The capture records a device signature; voice captures add the audio and transcript hashes and the translation model.
  • A ConsentReceipt is issued per recipient Fiduciary per mandate. It records the Rule 3 notice (an itemised description of the data, the specified purpose and the goods or services, and the means to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board), together with the recipient, the notice language (English or an Eighth Schedule language, Act s.5(3) and s.6(3)), and the legal basis (consent_s6 or legitimate_use_s7a for delivery data the buyer provided for that order).
  • Withdrawal MUST be as easy as giving consent. The receipt carries a withdrawal URI and an erasure signal.
  • When the seller is unknown at mandate setup, a class receipt (recipient *) scoped to the mandate's categories is issued. It only pre-authorises: a per-seller receipt MUST be minted at init before any data is released to that seller, and no data is released on the strength of a class receipt alone (settled in Q-12).
  • Fail-safe default until Q-12 is settled: from 13-05-2027, the first release of personal data to a seller not named in any receipt the principal approved MUST be confirmed by the principal on the Trusted Surface (see Mandates and Consent).
  • Purchase consent is never recorded automatically: no confirmation without a covering mandate or an explicit buyer confirmation, and pre-ticked add-ons are declined.
  • Marketing consent is off unless a receipt says otherwise. With no active marketing receipt for a seller, every marketing purpose is granted: false, whatever a seller's default, a UCP buyer.consent member or any other receipt says. A business default is never consent (DPDP Act, 2023, s.6(1) asks for a clear affirmative action by the principal; the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, r.4(9) forbids recording consent automatically). Marketing consent is never asked inside a payment step-up. The standalone receipt for it is Proposed (Marketing consent, Q-101).

docs.title: Purpose limitation
docs.text:
• Every mandate carries a purpose code. The purpose fixes the categories, maximum validity, monetary bounds and data scopes the mandate may request (registry table in Mandates and Consent; settled in Q-47).
  • Data shared under a mandate MUST stay within its data_scopes and the order's needs.
  • Separate consent for model training and for health data is not yet modelled (forward compliance).

docs.title: Consent Manager role
docs.text:
The Mandate Manager turns Trusted Surface approvals into signed mandates and ConsentReceipts, keeps their status and publishes a status list. It is designed to be data-blind: it stores mandates and logs, never order or payment payloads. Whether it registers as a DPDP Consent Manager or integrates with one, and how that fits a Mandate Manager co-located with the payer PSP, is open: Q-16.

Act s.6(9) (registration of Consent Managers with the Board) and Rule 4 apply from 13-11-2026. Under the First Schedule, a Consent Manager is a company incorporated in India with a net worth of at least ₹2 crore. Until Q-16 is settled, these fail-safe rules apply (stated normatively in Mandates and Consent):

  • A Mandate Manager MUST NOT act, or describe itself, as a Consent Manager unless it is registered with the Board. On ConsentReceipts issued on or after 13-11-2026, cm_registration_no MUST be the Board registration number when the MM acts as a Consent Manager, and MUST be null otherwise.
  • An MM that acts as a registered Consent Manager MUST NOT also perform the credential-provider role (re-verifying closed mandates, issuing within_bounds attestations); that role runs as a logically separate component with its own registry key.
  • The MM keeps records of consents, notices and sharing for at least 7 years and MUST give them to the Data Principal on request, on the Trusted Surface, in machine-readable form (First Schedule Part B item 4). A REST export endpoint is not part of this version.

docs.title: Data localisation
docs.text:
RBI requires payment system data to be stored only in India; data for the foreign leg of a transaction may also be stored abroad. RBI's FAQ on the directive allows processing abroad if the data returns to India within one business day or 24 hours. Where an agent operator's own language model may process payment data is open: Q-15. Until it is settled, BACP applies a fail-safe default that is stricter than the FAQ:

  • A gateway, Mandate Manager or PSP adapter MUST store mandates, receipts, the InstructionLog and evidence bundles that contain payment data only in India.
  • These components MUST NOT send payment data to a language model, log store or other processor outside India, even transiently.
  • The AgentCredential and registry MAY declare data_residency{payment_data: "IN", llm_region, log_region, transfer_basis}. A gateway MUST NOT treat a missing or incomplete declaration as permission for payment-data egress outside India.

Cross-border transfer of other personal data follows DPDP s.16 and Rule 15 from 13-05-2027: transfer is restricted only to countries the Central Government notifies. A Significant Data Fiduciary may also be required to keep specified data in India (Rule 13(4)).

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
• From 13-05-2027, DPDP Rule 8(3) requires personal data, traffic data and processing logs to be kept for at least one year; the ConsentReceipt records retention.legal_minimum (default one year) and the recipient's maximum.
  • Erasure on withdrawal or once the purpose is served (s.8(7)) is reconciled with that minimum.
  • Already in force: participants subject to the CERT-In Directions (28-04-2022) MUST keep the logs of their ICT systems, which include gateway, InstructionLog and signing-service logs, for a rolling 180 days within India, and produce them to CERT-In on request. This is a floor; the DPDP one-year minimum above applies on top of it from 13-05-2027.
  • Mandate records at the Mandate Manager are kept for 7 years.
  • Negotiation transcripts are kept for at least the proposed limitation period of two years for B2C, longer for B2B and public procurement (Q-56).
  • A retention table for the InstructionLog, receipts and evidence bundles is still to be written (Q-17).

docs.title: Breach notice
docs.text:
Applies now: CERT-In reporting. Under the CERT-In Directions issued under s.70B(6) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28-04-2022), service providers, intermediaries, data centres and body corporates must report the cyber incidents the Directions list (including data breaches, data leaks and unauthorised access to IT systems or data) to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them or being told of them. Participants subject to the Directions MUST make that report themselves; a BACP message never satisfies it on their behalf, and no other participant or the BACP maintainers can make it for them. The 180-day log duty that supports the report is described under Retention.

From 13-05-2027: DPDP breach notice. In addition, Act s.8(6) and DPDP Rule 7 require a Fiduciary that becomes aware of a personal data breach to inform each affected Data Principal without delay, and the Board without delay, followed by a detailed report within 72 hours of becoming aware of it (or a longer period the Board allows on a written request). Failure to notify can attract a penalty of up to ₹200 crore. In a BACP flow a breach at one participant can affect data held by others. Proposed: a cross-participant bacp.breach_signal message carrying detection and notification times (Q-17). Because the CERT-In clock is 6 hours, the signal is meant to be sent as soon as a participant detects an incident affecting others; receiving a signal can be the moment another participant "notices" an incident and starts its own 6-hour clock. The signal carries times and references only, and the logs it points to are the ones kept for the 180-day CERT-In period.

docs.title: Forward compliance
docs.text:
These DPDP duties start on 13-05-2027 and are not yet designed in. Proposed message designs are tracked in Q-17:

Duty Proposed Downstream erasure after withdrawal, with acknowledgement and an SLA bacp.erasure_request Accuracy and correction propagation to recipients (s.8(3)) bacp.correction Breach signalling (Rule 7) bacp.breach_signal Children: verifiable parental consent; no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising (s.9, Rules 10 and 12) principal.minor_status, parental_consent_ref, and a minor mode that turns off personalised ranking and drops items whose sponsorship.status is sponsored or undeclared (BACP policy; DPDP s.9(3) applies from 13-05-2027 to targeted advertising) Separate consent for model training and for health data Separate purpose classes with a no-training default

Grievances: the operator's grievance officer is named in the AgentCredential, and DPDP grievances must be answered within 90 days (Rule 14(3)); e-commerce grievances follow the shorter timelines described in Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: Penalties
docs.text:
The Schedule to the DPDP Act (s.33(1)) sets the maximum penalties the Board may impose. They apply from 13-05-2027.

Breach Maximum penalty Failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach (s.8(5)) ₹250 crore Failure to notify the Board or affected Data Principals of a breach (s.8(6)) ₹200 crore Breach of the additional obligations for children (s.9) ₹200 crore Breach of the additional obligations of a Significant Data Fiduciary (s.10) ₹150 crore Breach of a Data Principal's duties (s.15) ₹10,000 Breach of a voluntary undertaking accepted by the Board (s.32) Up to the penalty for the original breach Breach of any other provision of the Act or the Rules ₹50 crore

docs.title: Trade Profiles
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. Several thresholds rest on secondary sources; every regulatory number MUST be configurable.

India trades in many ways at once: a quick-commerce order paid by UPI, a kirana's monthly khata, a distributor's "buy 10 get 1" scheme, an RFQ that ends in a net-30 purchase order, a GeM reverse auction, an eNAM lot sold to the highest bidder. A trade profile is a named, conformance-testable bundle of defaults over the negotiation module and the payment handler registry. It fixes, for one trade model:

  • the extra roles that take part;
  • the allowed negotiation modes;
  • the eligible payment handlers, by presence;
  • the credit terms and documents that apply;
  • the validators and human-presence gates that run.

docs.title: Declaring a profile
docs.text:
• A BAP or BPP declares the profiles it supports in /.well-known/bacp (profiles[]). See Discovery and Profiles.
  • A session declares exactly one profile in context.bacp (profile) and in its negotiation tags. The profile is fixed when the session opens, and a later message that declares another is refused with capabilities_incompatible.
  • Who declares it. The buyer side declares profile and acting_for at session open, in a buyer-signed message, and both are pinned (NegotiationSession.profile and acting_for_kind are read-only). The buyer gateway fills them from the mandate. A model-supplied NegotiationCreate.profile that differs from the mandate's is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch. A consumer marker always wins.
  • Refusing a profile. Either party MAY refuse with capabilities_incompatible, param $.context.bacp.profile, reason profile_not_supported or profile_misdescribed. Nothing becomes LIVE, and a seller never reclassifies a session. A GSTIN does not end consumer status: the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.2(7), Explanation (a) keeps a person who buys goods for commercial purpose that is not within the exclusion a consumer. Whether a sole proprietor's livelihood purchase is a consumer purchase despite a signed declaration of commercial purpose is open (Q-52).
  • A profile narrows. It never widens a mandate: the principal's checkout mandate and negotiation mandate still apply, and the stricter bound wins.
  • A participant that claims a profile MUST pass the conformance cases of the levels that profile needs (see Conformance). No attestation covers an experimental profile (Maturity).

docs.title: Handler classes
docs.text:
The handler columns below use the binding classes of the handler registry:

Class Meaning O Open: a standing authority whose limits the rail, the issuer or both parties enforce. Can back an agent payment with the human not present (HNP). C Closed: each payment is authorised by the human (UPI PIN, card AFA, net-banking login). Human present (HP) only. A Assisted: a human operator (VLE, BC agent) completes the payment for the principal D Cash or UPI on delivery N Not a payment at checkout: financing, guarantees, deposits and settlement constructs

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Every term sheet names its parties. One transaction can name a different ordering entity, consignee and paying authority.

Role Who in India How BACP represents it buyer, seller The principals parties.buyer / parties.seller; each may act through an agent under a mandate ordering_entity GeM buyer organisation, enterprise department parties.ordering_entity consignee GeM consignee who issues the CRAC, a receiving warehouse parties.consignee; issues the GRN or CRAC paying_authority PAO / DDO, enterprise accounts payable parties.paying_authority; the checker in maker–checker broker Arhtiya, property broker, customs house agent, salesman intermediaries[] with acts_for; commission disclosed in commission[]; needs its own scoped mandate aggregator Marketplace, B2B app, GeM, eNAM, ONDC apps Marketplace or merchant-of-record flag. Collecting money for others requires an authorised payment aggregator's escrow. financier Bank, NBFC, BNPL lender, TReDS financier, e-NWR pledgee, LC bank Class N or credit handlers; becomes the new payee on the ledger after discounting logistics 3PL, courier (COD collector), transporter holding the e-way bill Fulfilment party; COD remitter assurer Assayer, inspector, hallmarking centre, RERA or BIS registry Issues assay certificates, inspection reports and HUIDs as document references or verifiable credentials arbiter Grievance officer, ODR provider, MSEFC, APMC committee, GeM incident management, consumer commission The escalation chain on the IGM issue; MSEFC for MSMED disputes assisted_operator CSC VLE, bank BC, kirana operator AI agent → human operator → principal chain. Principal consent, operator id and fee are logged, and the receipt goes to the principal. The operator is an assisted_operator entry in Session.participants[], REQUIRED on channel: assisted, and the principal approves with the principal's own factor (Assisted channel). reseller Social-commerce reseller Two prices and two parties; the reseller margin settles after the return window auctioneer Neutral auction platform Runs the clock; never affiliated with a seller (Auctions)
