Maturity says how far a profile is settled in BACP 2026-10-18 and whether a participant can be attested for it (as of 18-10-2026). It labels the profile and changes no rule inside it.

Maturity Profiles Meaning launch b2c.ecom (marketplace and quick commerce), kirana.khata, subscription, ticketing Stable and attestable. The profile's rules are the ones this release launches with. proposed fmcg.distribution, b2b.procurement, services, social In this release and attestable. The rules MAY change in a later dated release. experimental gem, agri, crossborder, high_value, c2c.rental, assisted.rural Described for review only. Outside the conformance scope of this release: no conformance attestation covers it, and the profile MAY change or be removed in a later dated release.

A party MAY refuse an experimental profile with capabilities_incompatible, reason profile_not_supported (Declaring a profile). A participant is never required to support a profile, whatever its maturity.

Waiver permitted says whether a firm offer in a session of that profile may carry acceptance_revocation: waived, always with a signed waiver_basis (Acceptance revocation). "No" marks a consumer profile: its trade has consumer buyers, so waived is refused in it. A session that declares no profile, or whose buyer side acts for an individual (acting_for.kind: individual) or sends no acting_for, is treated the same way whatever profile it declares, and the profile is fixed when the session opens (Consumer sessions). In this version no profile permits allowed_until_receipt. In agri the acceptor is the farmer or FPO selling a lot, or a bidder buying one, and the profile describes no consumer buyer, so agri is a business profile; the farmer's explicit acceptance of a bid (eNAM and mandi) still applies.

Credit-backed overlays such as TReDS invoice discounting and OCEN purchase finance are not separate profiles. They attach to the profiles above and are described under Financing overlays.

docs.title: B2C retail
docs.text:
Profile b2c.ecom: organised B2C e-commerce and quick commerce.

  • Negotiation. There is no bargaining on the base price. The buyer optimises across coupons, bank offers, no-cost EMI, exchange offers, delivery slot and fee, and membership pricing, using scheme mode: the buyer asserts machine-readable schemes with eligibility proofs and the seller agrees or disagrees per scheme. Ticketed or flash prices use posted_dynamic. Conditional cashback never counts toward all_in_total.
  • Payment handlers. HNP orders MAY use Reserve Pay (one block per seller, payable to that seller's collection VPA), UPI Circle, agentic card tokens or a gift PPI. Everything else is HP. COD and UPI on delivery are allowed only if the mandate sets cod_allowed.
  • Credit. Card EMI and BNPL are credit-funded. They require credit_funding_allowed on the governing mandate, full disclosure (lender, APR, KFS, no_cost: false when interest is charged), and a human-present loan acceptance. Whether checkout BNPL fits the digital-lending end-use rules is open (Q-32).
  • COD. A seller MAY accept or refuse COD per order. The mandate's cod_max_open_orders caps open COD orders, and a COD order placed without the principal counts against the placing agent's id. The final payment mode at the door (cash or UPI on delivery) is recorded. Whether an RTO fee may be charged to a consumer is open (Q-37); it is never charged unless disclosed in round 1 and allowed by the mandate.
  • Compliance. The drip-pricing, basket-sneaking, false-urgency and personalised-pricing validators run on every offer (Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023). An e-way bill is needed above ₹50,000 per consignment; returns produce a credit note and a refund to source.

docs.title: Kirana, khata and mol-bhav
docs.text:
Profile kirana.khata: the neighbourhood kirana, phone and WhatsApp ordering, and the household khata.

  • Negotiation. fixed for packaged MRP goods: an offer MAY discount below MRP and MUST NOT exceed it. alternating (mol-bhav) for loose staples, fruit and vegetables and bulk quantities, priced by weight (unit: kg). scheme for passed-on brand schemes. Voice-note or photographed lists become structured lines; free text from the shop is untrusted data. A loose item MUST carry a measure (Units, quantity and weighed goods), so that "1.5 kg of atta in 250 g steps" is a quantity of 1500 with unit KGM, scale 3 and increment 250, and the Hindi unit label travels as display_text (किलो). A heavier bag cannot raise the bill: after delivery the amount can only fall unless the principal agreed an adjustment_band and a hold exists (Weighed goods).
  • Payment handlers. The khata is a bacp.credit_ledger shared by buyer and seller. HNP top-ups MAY use a Reserve Pay block payable to that kirana. Repeat Reserve Pay debits after the first follow the 24-hour pre-debit notice by default, until the notice question is settled (Q-03). HP payments use UPI intent or UPI 123PAY on feature phones; 123PAY is capped per transaction, and the exact cap is open (Q-05).
  • Credit terms. Interest-free trade credit with a credit limit, due dates and ageing. Every entry MUST be acknowledged by both parties. Whatever the channel (tap, SMS, voice), an acknowledgement MUST end in a counterparty signature, and the channel is recorded as the method. An unacknowledged entry is flagged disputed. A ledger payment entry MUST cite a PSP-signed receipt (RRN or UTR); a screenshot is never proof. Treating interest-free khata as trade credit outside the digital-lending rules is a working position (Q-27).
  • Documents. Parchi or estimate, ledger confirmation; a GST invoice on request where the shop is registered.

docs.title: Distributor schemes
docs.text:
Profile fmcg.distribution: brand → C&F → super-stockist → distributor → wholesaler → retailer.

  • Negotiation. scheme for trade schemes: quantity purchase schemes ("buy 10 get 1"), slab discounts, display incentives and target-linked incentives. fixed for tier price lists (retailer, wholesaler, distributor), and alternating for bulk deals. A scheme follows an accrual → claim → credit note lifecycle linked to the qualifying invoices; free goods appear as a zero-priced line or an equivalent credit note.
  • Payment handlers. Credit ledger and NACH debit for HNP; NEFT, UPI intent, a dealer credit line from a financier, and positive-pay cheques for HP; COD to the retailer.
  • Credit terms. Credit days per counterparty with days-past-due tracking. Where the selling party is a micro or small manufacturing or services enterprise, the MSMED 45-day cap applies.
  • Compliance. The MRP ceiling binds wholesale dealers too, so it runs on retail packs even in B2B. IRN e-invoicing applies when the seller's aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year since 2017-18, an e-way bill above ₹50,000, and delivery challans for stock transfers.

docs.title: B2B procurement: RFQ → PO → net terms
docs.text:
Profile b2b.procurement: SME and enterprise purchasing.

  • Negotiation. rfq_sealed and rfq_iterated for multi-seller sourcing with landed-cost comparison, alternating for technical and commercial rounds, and reverse_l1 where the buyer's policy calls for it. See RFQ. Negotiable issues include unit price and price-variation clauses, quantity and MOQ, delivery schedule and Incoterm (or FOR_DESTINATION), freight, advance %, credit days, warranty, liquidated damages, PBG and retention.
  • Flow. RFQ → quotation or proforma → negotiation → PO (confirm) → order acknowledgement (on_confirm) → dispatch with tax invoice, e-way bill and challan → GRN and inspection → three-way match (PO, GRN, invoice) → payment on net-N → TDS certificate. The purchase order MUST NOT alter accepted terms.
  • Payment handlers. HNP: credit ledger and NACH debit. HP with maker–checker: the agent prepares a NEFT, RTGS or IMPS instruction (or a BBPS B2B invoice payment) and a human checker approves it in corporate banking. N: TReDS and e-BG.
  • Credit terms. Tranches such as "30% advance, 70% net-45 from GRN". The MSMED cap (at most 45 days from acceptance, 15 days with no written agreement) applies to micro and small manufacturing and services suppliers; traders are warned only (Q-21). The clock runs from acceptance, which under the Act is the day of delivery unless the buyer objects in writing within 15 days; a buyer-signed GRN records both. The ledger computes the statutory due date, MSMED interest on late payment, and the income-tax deduction exposure on unpaid MSE dues. Exposure from firm commitments counts against the checkout mandate's budgets as well as total_max (Q-46).
  • Compliance. IRN and signed QR for sellers whose aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year since 2017-18, with a 30-day reporting flag where AATO is ₹10 crore or more (GSTN advisory, from 01-04-2025; primary text not verified as of 17-10-2026); e-way bill above ₹50,000; TDS obligations displayed. Companies with turnover above ₹250 crore must be onboarded on TReDS (see Financing overlays). Trade documents and ledgers are service-level interfaces whose REST binding is still open (Q-44).

docs.title: GeM
docs.text:
Profile gem: government procurement on the Government e-Marketplace.

  • Roles. Ordering entity, consignee and paying authority are separate parties; GeM is the auctioneer and its incident management is an arbiter.
  • Negotiation. fixed for direct purchase, rfq_sealed for L1 purchase and e-bids, reverse_l1 for reverse auctions after technical evaluation, and english for forward (disposal) auctions. Price is negotiated only through the reverse auction. Quantity MAY vary under the ± option clause (option_clause_pct). Ties MAY use msme_preference or make_in_india_preference. On GeM itself these preferences are wider than a tie-break: under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, an MSE quoting within L1 + 15% may match the L1 price and supply at least 25% of the tendered value when L1 is not an MSE, and the Make in India order gives a 20% purchase-preference margin to Class-I local suppliers. A BACP tie-break does not model these bands; the buying platform applies them.
  • Mode thresholds. The buying organisation chooses the mode by value and records procurement_mode_reason. The default thresholds under GFR Rule 149 as amended in July 2024 are listed in Reverse L1: direct purchase up to ₹50,000; L1 purchase above ₹50,000 up to ₹10 lakh among sellers of at least three different manufacturers; above ₹10 lakh, bids are mandatory, through online bidding or reverse auction. They MUST be configurable.
  • Payment handlers. Payment runs through the GeM handler (PFMS and the GeM pool account), which the agent does not trigger directly. EMD MAY be paid by UPI collect or furnished as an e-BG; performance security as an ePBG. The UPI limit for GeM payments, including EMD, was raised to ₹5 lakh per transaction from 15-09-2025, as reported by the public broadcaster (reported, not verified against the NPCI circular or a GeM page as of 17-10-2026).
  • Credit terms. Payment terms are fixed by the GeM general terms and conditions and are not negotiable. The buyer MUST pay within 10 days of the CRAC (including auto-generated CRACs). Late payment attracts penal interest of 1% per month, pro-rated, which is deposited in an account maintained by GeM rather than paid to the seller; MSMED interest is additional. The ledger tracks this clock.
  • Compliance. Every agent action produces an audit trail fit for CAG and CVC review: who acted, under which mandate, and the comparison set. Suspended sellers are excluded from new bids.

docs.title: eNAM and mandi
docs.text:
Profile agri: APMC mandis, eNAM, FPOs and warehouse receipts.

  • Negotiation. english for open auctions and eNAM e-auctions, dutch for perishables, rfq_sealed for FPO tenders. Lots carry assay attributes (moisture, grade, foreign matter) as document references.
  • Seller acceptance. The highest bid is sent to the farmer, who accepts or rejects it. Only the farmer's or FPO's explicit acceptance awards the lot. eNAM states that once the auction is completed, the farmer "can either choose to accept it or reject it". BACP lets a rejected lot be re-auctioned; whether eNAM re-auctions a rejected lot is not confirmed in an official source, and state APMC rules vary (English auctions).
  • Payment handlers. NEFT, RTGS or UPI collect direct to the farmer's account (HP); the arhtiya's advance on the credit ledger; e-NWR pledge finance as class N.
  • Credit and deductions. Payout = accepted bid × weighed quantity − farmer-borne charges. Commission, market fee and loading are itemised lines, each tagged with the party that bears it. An arhtiya's pre-season loan is interlocked credit: its repayment is a separate line deducted at sale (commission[].deducted_at_source), shown to the farmer. The seller agent can compare selling now with storing against an e-NWR and a pledge loan.
  • Documents. Gate entry, assay certificate, auction slip, weighment slip, sale bill (state-specific form), e-NWR.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Profile services: home services, healthcare over UHI, mobility, education, gig work.

  • Negotiation. fixed fares and fees; alternating on scope; two-phase inspect-then-quote (scope.inspection_then_quote, inspection_fee); slot negotiation with slot.hold_until. A slot hold expires at its time and releases capacity. A change of scope after acceptance requires a new offer (change_order_policy: new_offer_required). A no-show policy is a term-sheet issue.
  • Payment handlers. HNP: UPI Circle, or a UPI one-time mandate captured after the job. HP: UPI intent, card token, card EMI. Milestones are schedule[] tranches; milestone escrow uses an authorised payment aggregator's escrow.
  • Compliance. Health data travels only under an ABDM consent artefact.

docs.title: Subscriptions
docs.text:
Profile subscription: OTT and digital plans, utility bills via BBPS, daily milk and newspaper delivery, SaaS.

  • Negotiation. fixed plans and scheme bundles. No price bargaining.
  • Payment handlers. Recurring debits are mandates: UPI AutoPay, card e-mandates, NACH debit, BBPS UPMS, NETC and NCMC top-ups, and a credit ledger for a monthly milk khata. One-off bills use BBPS fetch-then-pay.
  • Rules. A pre-debit notice at least 24 hours before each debit, with opt-out; additional authentication for a debit above ₹15,000 (₹1 lakh for the categories the RBI lists). Subscriptions MUST support pause, skip, resume, quantity change per cycle and one-step cancellation with proof, which revokes the mandate. For eNACH caps see Q-29.

docs.title: Social and conversational
docs.text:
Profile social: WhatsApp and Instagram sellers, resellers, live commerce.

  • Negotiation. alternating for DM bargaining, fixed for catalogue prices. Chat stays advisory: an acceptance typed in chat MUST be mapped to a signed accept linked to the chat thread, because acceptance must follow the prescribed manner (Acceptance).
  • Payment handlers. HNP: Circle. HP: UPI intent or collect. COD and UPI on delivery. A partial advance for custom orders is a tranche.
  • Rules. Payment is confirmed only by a PSP or bank callback or a signed rail reference, never by a screenshot. The payee name comes from the bank's records, not from the chat. A reseller's margin is recorded separately from the end-buyer price and settles after the return window.

docs.title: Assisted rural
docs.text:
Profile assisted.rural: CSC village-level entrepreneurs, bank BC agents, AePS operators, feature-phone users.

  • Negotiation. fixed. The operator's service fee is the only negotiated item.
  • Payment handlers. Assisted handlers (AePS, POS dynamic QR) and UPI 123PAY (IVR) for HP. Channel limits are enforced: UPI 123PAY (Q-05) and UPI Lite (₹1,000 per transaction).
  • Rules. The principal's consent (biometric or OTP), the operator's id and the fee are logged, and the receipt goes to the principal's phone in their language.

docs.title: Exports and cross-border
docs.text:
Profile crossborder: MSME exports and imports.

  • Negotiation. rfq_sealed and alternating over Incoterm, currency and payment instrument. Every cross-border offer MUST carry an Incoterm, a currency, a payment instrument (advance TT, LC at sight or usance, D/P, D/A, open account with ECGC cover) and the required document set. A foreign-currency price is shown through the fx disclosure view; every settlement amount stays in INR.
  • Payment handlers. C: PA-CB (capped at ₹25 lakh per transaction) and account-to-account transfers. N: LC, e-BG and bacp.trade.export_realisation, which tracks the realisation deadline. Outbound cross-border card-not-present payments need AFA when the acquirer asks.
  • FEMA realisation. The export-realisation tracker records the due date for each export and alerts before it: 9 months from shipment (goods) or invoice (services), and 12 months for exports invoiced or settled in INR, under the FEM (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations 2026, Reg 5(1), as amended with effect from 01-10-2026. The periods have changed several times since 2025 and the AD bank can extend them, so they MUST be configurable. Proceeds unrealised for more than one year past the due date restrict future exports to full advance or an irrevocable LC (Reg 13). See Credit and Split Tender.
  • Compliance. Courier exports have had no value cap since 31-03-2026: CBIC Circular 17/2026-Customs removed the earlier ₹10 lakh limit for commercial export consignments through courier mode. BACP does not redirect a consignment to cargo on value alone.

docs.title: C2C and rentals
docs.text:
Profile c2c.rental: classifieds, recommerce, equipment and furniture rental, tenancy.

  • Negotiation. alternating, with heavy mol-bhav and inspection-based quotes.
  • Payment handlers. A token advance on a UPI one-time mandate with release conditions; rent by UPI AutoPay or NACH debit; HP by UPI intent.
  • Rules. Tokens and deposits carry release conditions and an itemised deduction policy; a deduction is released with its reason. Title checks (IMEI, vehicle RC) and inspection reports are document references. Where a state has adopted the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, deposits are capped at two months' rent (residential) and six months' (non-residential).

docs.title: High-value purchases
docs.text:
Profile high_value: cars, property and gold.

  • Negotiation. alternating over multi-issue bundles (price, accessories, finance, delivery; price per sq ft, floor rise, payment plan, possession date; making charges, wastage, old-gold exchange), plus scheme.
  • Payment handlers. Every commitment is human-present. UPI intent, card token, RTGS and credit handlers; tranches for token, loan and balance.
  • Rules. For property sold by a RERA-registered promoter (an apartment, plot or building), a token or booking amount above 10% of cost needs a linked registered agreement for sale (RERA s.13; NEG_RERA_TOKEN_CAP). A cash receipt of ₹2 lakh or more is refused (Income-tax Act, 1961 s.269ST; Income-tax Act, 2025 s.186 equivalent; NEG_CASH_LIMIT), and PAN is required above the statutory threshold, which secondary sources give as a purchase of any goods above ₹2 lakh per transaction. A "hallmarked" claim requires an HUID.

docs.title: Ticketing
docs.text:
Profile ticketing: rail, air, bus and events.

  • Negotiation. posted_dynamic and fixed. A posted price carries its validity and quota or class. A booking MUST honour the price shown within its validity or reject explicitly; a later price is a new offer, never a silent charge.
  • Payment handlers. HP: UPI intent and card token. HNP: Circle for low-value bus or metro tickets.
  • Rules. Booking windows are respected without anti-bot evasion, tickets are bound to the traveller's id, and the agent refuses unauthorised resellers.

docs.title: Financing overlays: TReDS and OCEN
docs.text: Financing attaches to a profile's credit terms rather than forming a profile of its own.

docs.title: TReDS
docs.text:
TReDS platforms discount an MSME seller's invoices that the buyer has accepted. Handler in.fin.treds (class N).

  • The seller uploads the accepted invoice as a factoring unit, bound to its GST IRN and the buyer's acceptance; financiers bid; the seller accepts a bid and is funded without recourse.
  • After discounting, the ledger records the financier as the new payee, and the buyer pays the financier on the due date, typically by NACH debit.
  • A buyer-side agent can accept invoices within an approval policy and keep them inside the MSMED 45-day window. A seller-side agent can upload invoices and accept bids within a rate floor. Both act within the corporate's platform entitlements with human signatory approval.
  • Companies with turnover above ₹250 crore, and all CPSEs, are required to onboard on TReDS (Ministry of MSME notification of 07-11-2024, as reported by PIB). Since 30-06-2026, operating CPSEs must also settle MSME invoices through a TReDS platform. See Credit and Split Tender for sources.
  • Applies to: b2b.procurement, fmcg.distribution, gem sellers.

docs.title: OCEN
docs.text:
OCEN offers credit at the point of purchase through a regulated lender or loan service provider. Handler in.fin.ocen (with in.fin.dealer_line for dealer credit). OCEN is an industry protocol stewarded by iSPIRT (current version OCEN 4.0) and is in production, for example on GeM Sahay. It has no RBI recognition of its own, so every OCEN loan falls under the lender's own RBI directions, including the Digital Lending Directions. The in.fin.ocen handler binding is at registry status pilot.

  • An agent MAY present OCEN loan offers only through a regulated lender or LSP arrangement.
  • Every offer MUST carry the lender, APR, tenure, EMI, penal charges, the KFS reference, a cooling-off period of at least one day and the repayment payee. Offers are shown unbiased, never pre-selected.
  • Loan acceptance is always human-present (credit_acceptance_requires_hp for an agent attempt). Repayments go to the lender only.
  • Applies to: fmcg.distribution, b2b.procurement, and credit-funded checkouts in b2c.ecom and high_value where the mandate sets credit_funding_allowed.

See Credit and Split Tender for the loan-offer schema and the credit ledger.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
Profiles differ mostly in which documents they need. Documents are typed references (doc_type, id, parent_ids[], issuer, issued_at, hash, and irn or ewb_no where relevant) that link into a graph:

flowchart LR
    RFQ[RFQ] --> Q[Quotation or proforma]
    Q --> PO[PO is Beckn confirm]
    PO --> ACK[Order ack is on_confirm]
    PO --> INV[Tax invoice with IRN]
    INV --> EWB[e-way bill above ₹50,000]
    INV --> DC[Delivery challan]
    DC --> GRN[GRN or CRAC or weighment slip]
    PO --> GRN
    GRN --> M3{Three-way match}
    INV --> M3
    M3 --> PAY[Payment advice and receipt]
    INV --> CN[Credit or debit note]
    PAY --> TDS[TDS certificate]
    GRN --> LED[Ledger due date and MSMED clock]

A GRN, CRAC or weighment slip records delivery and acceptance, which start the MSMED clock, or starts the GeM 10-day clock (CRAC). How a buyer-issued GRN or CRAC travels on Beckn is open (Q-33). Domain credentials (e-NWR, HUID, RERA registration, assay certificate, inspection report, ABDM consent artefact, e-ticket) are document references whose uri points to a verifiable credential.

docs.title: Who acted on a trade document
docs.text:
A GRN, a CRAC and an MSMED written objection start or move a money clock, and so does a credit-ledger acknowledgement. Each such act carries a typed actor (Actor in common.json), the same object as a ledger acknowledgement's actor in credit-ledger-entry.json:

Field Required Meaning kind yes human or agent role yes principal (the party itself or its authorised human), seller_operator (seller staff such as a munim or a sales officer), assisted_operator, agent (the party's own AI agent) or sub_agent. A human acts only as principal, seller_operator or assisted_operator; an agent only as agent or sub_agent participant_ref yes The acting participant's participant_id, or the agent id for an agent mandate_ref no (REQUIRED for an agent's order-less ledger act) The mandate under which an agent acted. It records the mandate; it does not authorise the act. For an order-less ledger act it also names the Mandate Manager that issues the step-up (Step-up signers)
  • A GRN, CRAC, objection or acknowledgement by an agent (actor.kind: agent) MUST carry hp_proof of the principal's confirmation on the Trusted Surface: a post_order step-up whose ts_render names the act (Presence proof). No mandate scope authorises an agent's trade act. The seller app or the gateway rejects any agent act without hp_proof, and the ledger schema rejects an agent acknowledgement without it.
  • A ledger acknowledgement other than one taken automatically from a rail receipt (auto_from_rail_receipt) carries actor; the schema rejects one without it.
  • A gateway that lists in.bacp.trade_document or in.bacp.ledger binds these acts at POST /trade-acts (Seller-side and trade acts). The request names its subject (an order, a ledger entry by ledger_ref, or a ledger statement by ledger_range), so a ledger entry with no order_id (an opening balance, a payment or an adjustment) is named by ts_render.subject_ref, not by an order. Every trade-act ts_render carries subject_hash. A GRN carries its lines (line_ref, quantities received, accepted and rejected, an enum reason), and seller-posted delivery evidence (proof_of_delivery, lorry_receipt) dates acceptance only if the buyer counter-signs it or it carries a third-party reference the buyer can check. Whether an objection sent by an agent is an objection "in writing" under the MSMED Act is open (Q-21).

docs.title: Sessions and Checkout
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

A checkout session is the gateway's synchronous, authoritative view of one purchase in progress. The agent talks to the gateway with UCP-style session verbs. The gateway translates each call into signed Beckn/ONDC actions, waits for the on_* callbacks, evaluates the mandate, moves money on the payment rail, and returns the full session state every time.

This page covers discovery, the session lifecycle, complete, and the payment saga. Mandates are described in Mandates and Consent. What happens after an order exists is in Orders and Post-order. The REST operations are defined in the BACP OpenAPI document (services/bacp.openapi.yaml) and summarised in REST.

docs.title: Flow overview
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP Gateway (BAP)
    participant BG as ONDC Gateway
    participant S as Seller (BPP)
    participant P as Payer PSP
    A->>G: POST /discover (bacp-browse)
    G->>BG: search with context.bacp
    BG->>S: search
    S-->>G: on_search catalogue
    G-->>A: results flagged within_mandate, ranking parameters
    A->>G: POST /sessions with items (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: select
    S-->>G: on_select quote with TTL
    G-->>A: 201 incomplete with quote
    A->>G: PUT /sessions/id with fulfilment, data_share, handler
    G->>S: init
    S-->>G: on_init BPP-signed quote and disclosures
    G->>G: Strip add-ons, hash disclosures, mandate pre-check
    G-->>A: 200 ready_for_complete with checkout_hash
    A->>G: POST /sessions/id/complete with closed mandates (bacp-pay)
    G->>G: Authoritative mandate evaluation and budget reservation
    G->>P: Basket-blind debit
    P-->>G: PSP-signed Receipt
    G->>S: confirm with payment PAID
    S-->>G: on_confirm order id
    G-->>A: 200 completed with order, receipt and budget_after

docs.title: Verbs and Beckn mapping
docs.text:
BACP verb REST Beckn / ONDC action Mandate action_scope Signature tag bacp.discover POST /discover search → on_search (through the ONDC gateway and registry lookup) DISCOVER (optional) bacp-browse bacp.checkout.create POST /sessions select → on_select (quote with TTL) QUOTE bacp-browse bacp.checkout.update PUT /sessions/{session_id} select when items change; init → on_init for fulfilment, billing and payment terms ORDER, SHARE_DATA bacp-browse bacp.checkout.get GET /sessions/{session_id} none (gateway state) n/a bacp-browse bacp.checkout.complete POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete rail debit through the PSP, then confirm → on_confirm with payment.status = PAID and the rail reference ORDER, PAY bacp-pay bacp.checkout.cancel POST /sessions/{session_id}/cancel none (no order exists yet) n/a bacp-browse bacp.human_handoff POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff support → on_support n/a bacp-browse (request; release before acceptance); bacp-handoff (acceptance and release by a human support operator)

Every committing Beckn message the gateway sends (init, confirm, and post-order update, cancel, issue) carries context.bacp with the agent, presence, idempotency_key, ai_disclosure: true, the current InstructionLog log_head, and the mandate_ref (required on init, confirm, update, cancel and issue). The Beckn binding, including the message.order.tags[] mirror for networks that reject unknown context keys, is in Beckn / ONDC Binding.

The gateway derives each Beckn message_id as UUIDv5(message_id_namespace, agent_id | idempotency_key | action), so a retried call re-sends an identical message. A BACP-aware receiver MUST NACK a duplicate message_id within its ttl, and the gateway treats that NACK as "already received".

docs.title: Discover
docs.text: POST /discover sends a Beckn search and aggregates on_search results until max_wait_ms. Each result is flagged within_mandate when the request names a mandate_ref. Every item carries its own sponsorship (sponsored, not_sponsored or undeclared) and, where the seller sent them, mrp, tax_inclusive and prior_price, and every result carries a source_digest. The response carries the ranking parameters in descending order of importance (for example distance, price and seller rating), and ranking.sponsored is true if and only if some item is sponsored. A result also carries needs_principal_factor: true when the seller accepts no handler that a human-not-present payment can use, and requires_principal_confirmation when the seller declares that it wants the principal to confirm certain orders. The default ranking never uses the seller's payment rungs, merchant discount rate or finder fee (Ranking by payment rungs). Discovery moves no money and shares no personal data. See Discovery and Profiles.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
POST /sessions names the seller (bpp_id, provider_id), the items, the presence and optionally the mandate_ref, channel, language, participants and webhook_url. The gateway sends select and returns 201 with the quote from on_select. With channel: assisted, participants[] MUST contain an assisted_operator entry; otherwise the gateway returns 400 invalid_request at $.participants (Assisted channel). A session that is one leg of a multi-seller basket also carries the basket's basket_id.

  "bpp_id": "bpp.kirana.example.in",
  "provider_id": "P-112",

docs.title: Update (PUT)
docs.text:
PUT /sessions/{session_id} is a full replace of the agent-editable fields: items, fulfilment, billing, data_share and payment.handler. A PUT whose items differ from the current ones triggers a new select. A PUT with fulfilment triggers init. On on_init the gateway:

  1. verifies that the quote is signed by the BPP's registry key, and computes checkout_hash = sha-256(JCS(quote)) over that BPP-signed quote (checkout_hash);
  2. checks data_share against the mandate's data_scopes, SHARE_DATA scope and active ConsentReceipt (Data minimisation), before any data leaves for the seller;
  3. checks that payment.handler, after alias resolution, is the open mandate's rail binding (403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.payment.handler otherwise);
  4. declines every pre-ticked add-on, re-runs init without it, and reports preticked_addon_removed (warning, recoverable). A seller that keeps a declined add-on is treated as a NACK;
  5. compares prices against on_select. A changed unit price or a new fee line (packing, convenience, COD fee or other charge) gives drip_pricing_detected (requires_buyer_review). A fee line whose first_disclosed_round comes after the round that the handler intersection consumed is drip pricing under this rule. It then runs the convenience-fee consistency check across the debit modes the seller accepts: a payment_mode_fee_inconsistent warning (a SHOULD, never a refusal), which in HNP also raises a confirm step-up with reason constraint_unresolved. It fills recipient on each line from the BPP's signed value, or from the Beckn mapping (an unmapped type gives recipient: other and the warning charge_recipient_unmapped), and copies the buyer finder fee and np_fees unchanged into intermediary_compensation[] (Buyer finder fee);
  6. compares each line's unit_price in the on_select quote with the unit price that the discover response of the session's transaction_id showed for the same item (discovered_unit_price). A higher price gives discovery_price_changed. Where that item was shown with a prior_price, the message is requires_buyer_review and the session moves to requires_escalation with a confirm step-up. Where it was not, the message is recoverable, the session does not escalate on its account, and the agent MUST tell a present principal the new price. A lower price gives no message. drip_pricing_detected keeps its meaning: it compares on_select with on_init;
  7. requires the mandatory disclosures: seller_name, total_price, return_terms, cancellation_terms, country_of_origin, expected_delivery and price_breakup (seller_address and grievance_officer SHOULD be present). For a session whose items came from POST /discover it also fills catalogue[] with one entry per line item, copied unaltered from the discover response: item_id, sponsorship, discovered_unit_price and source_digest, and mrp, tax_inclusive and prior_price where the item had them. It hashes all of it, and the session's typed policies[] (Typed policies), into disclosures.hash, and raises policy_text_mismatch for a typed value that contradicts the binding return_terms or cancellation_terms. A missing mandatory disclosure gives disclosures_missing (requires_buyer_review). It then adds one type: disclosure message for each catalogue[n] whose sponsorship.status is sponsored (sponsored_listing) or undeclared (sponsorship_undeclared), and one prior_price_claim message for each that has a prior_price, each at param: $.disclosures.catalogue[n] with resolution: recoverable. The gateway MAY also put the item name in args[] with origin: counterparty; an agent that presents the message takes the name from the session line, never from args (Message object). An agent presents a catalogue[] entry that qualifies even when no message names it;
  8. runs split-order detection and the advisory mandate pre-check (Deterministic evaluation). The pre-check MUST NOT reserve budget.

Outcomes: ready_for_complete when everything passes; requires_escalation with a confirm step-up when drip pricing, a discovery_price_changed on an item shown with a prior_price, missing disclosures, a split order or a step-up threshold is found (the session MUST NOT reach ready_for_complete with missing disclosures); a 403 error when the mandate rejects; incomplete with quote_mismatch when the seller's quote does not match the requested quantities.

    {"id": "I-MILK-1L", "quantity": 1},
    {"id": "I-TOOR-500G", "quantity": 1}
  ],

docs.title: Units, quantity and weighed goods
docs.text:
A catalogue item MAY carry a measure, a QuantityUnit {unit, scale, increment, display_text}: unit is a UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 code, one step is 10^-scale of the unit, and increment is the ordering granularity in steps. A line echoes the item's measure. With no measure the item is sold by the piece (unit C62, scale 0, increment 1). measure is REQUIRED for loose goods in the kirana.khata profile and RECOMMENDED elsewhere.

  • ItemRef.quantity stays an integer of at least 1. With the default measure it is a count, as before. For an item whose measure has scale above 0 it is a count of 10^-scale units, and it MUST be a multiple of increment: 1500 with {unit: KGM, scale: 3, increment: 250} is 1.5 kg in six steps of 250 g. An off-increment quantity (1600) gets 400 invalid_request at $.items[n].quantity and is never rounded.
  • On ONDC Retail the gateway sends quantity.count = quantity / increment, and only where the seller's own pack measure equals the increment; otherwise it refuses and does not convert (Quantity and units).
  • display_text is counterparty text, spoken only as a labelled value.

Weighed goods. A line sold by weight can end up heavier or lighter than quoted. BACP keeps the principal from paying more than she was quoted unless she heard "up to ₹X" and a hold exists:

  1. By default a post-order weight adjustment can only reduce the amount, as a refund in adjustments[]. An upward adjustment with no adjustment_band is refused, and the order stands at the quoted total (Weighed goods).
  2. A line MAY carry adjustment_band{max_up, max_down}. It is not a mandate constraint, so it adds no new family of bounds, and it is hashed into checkout_hash (below). The gateway accepts a max_up only when (a) the Trusted Surface reads it as "up to ₹X" and the principal confirms, (b) the quote total plus the sum of max_up over all lines is within the approved amount and the mandate's caps, (c) max_up is at most the quoted price of one increment of the line's measure, and (d) the rail holds the amount at payment, the extra is collected only from that hold, and there is no second debit and no cash-on-delivery top-up. Where the rail has no such hold, the band is absent and an adjustment can only reduce the amount. A session whose total plus the sum of max_up is above the mandate cap escalates with confirm, and the Trusted Surface shows "up to ₹X".
  3. substitution{policy} is none (the default), same_brand or ask. A substitute line arrives only through a new quote with a new checkout_hash, never inside the same quote or on on_confirm (Seller refusals and substitution).

Whether an upward adjustment after a human-not-present payment is a new supply that needs fresh consent, whether the GST invoice must show the final weighed quantity, and whether a one-time UPI block can be captured in part are open (Q-101, Q-102); the down-only default applies until they are answered.

docs.title: Fulfilment options and minimum order
docs.text:
The session carries fulfilment_options[], projected from on_select and on_init: each is {id, type, label, slot, tat, charge, pickup_location}. type is Delivery or Self-Pickup, slot is {start, end}, tat is the seller's time to fulfil (from its time_to_ship tag), charge is an Amount in integer paise and pickup_location is the place of collection for a Self-Pickup option. Location has no capability of its own: it is folded into pickup_location. label and pickup_location are counterparty text, and the Trusted Surface shows them only as labelled seller values.

  • The agent chooses by fulfilment.option_id on PUT /sessions/{session_id}. The choice is hashed into checkout_hash. An id that the session did not offer gets 400 invalid_request at $.fulfilment.option_id.
  • A seller's Order MAY carry fulfilments[]{id, type, state} (SHOULD, where the seller reports several), and fulfilment_state is kept.
  • A provider's or item's min_order{value, item_qty} (SHOULD, where the seller sets one) is checked when the session is created and updated. A basket below it is refused with 400 invalid_request at $.items.

docs.title: Line provenance
docs.text:
Each LineItem carries added_by, one of principal, agent, seller and assisted_operator. The gateway assigns it from the signer and the source and never from the request: a request that sets added_by is not believed, and the gateway records what it observed (an agent-signed request gives agent). It is principal only for a line that the principal confirmed on a Trusted Surface or by a human-present render. A line that a seller's quote adds is seller, and a line that an assisted-channel operator adds is assisted_operator.

  • The agent MAY send principal_requested: true on an ItemRef. The claim decides only how the Trusted Surface reads the line: the Trusted Surface reads in full every agent, seller and assisted_operator line that the agent has not marked principal_requested (ts_render.unrequested_lines[], named in render_required[] whenever it is not empty), and counts the rest ("and 11 items you asked for"). The claim never changes added_by. added_by is fixed when the line first appears in the session and does not change when the agent re-sends the line. principal_requested has effect only on a line whose added_by is agent; on a seller or assisted_operator line it is ignored, and the line is always in unrequested_lines[].
  • A zero-price line that a seller scheme adds is read out and does not block. A paid line that a seller added needs a new quote, so a new checkout_hash.
  • An ItemRef MAY carry its own transaction_id and source_digest, so that a re-quote from an old list still runs the discovery_price_changed check against the price that list showed.
  • Seller view: the line's added_by is projected to the seller's view of the order where the network can carry it (Q-102).

docs.title: Extension members
docs.text: SessionCreate, SessionUpdate and Session carry an optional ext member: an object keyed by the reverse-DNS id of a declared third-party capability (a key never starts with in.), each value an object that the capability's registry schema governs (Capability declarations). An ext member whose capability is not listed in the profile's capabilities, or whose declaration is not active, is refused with 400 capability_unsupported at $.ext["<id>"], and the session is unchanged. An ext member that touches an amount, the payee, presence, a mandate or a disclosure is critical: it is refused unless its capability is listed and the amount also appears as a line of the base totals, and it is never a mandate constraint. Until an extension-registry review exists (Q-94) no third-party declaration is active, so every ext member is refused.

docs.title: checkout_hash binding
docs.text:
checkout_hash is sha-256 over the JCS form of the BPP-signed quote returned in on_init. When the session also carries a chosen fulfilment.option_id, an adjustment_band or a substitution policy on a line, which are choices of the principal and not part of the seller's quote, the hash is sha-256(JCS({"quote": <the quote>, "selection": {"fulfilment_option_id": ..., "lines": [{"id": ..., "adjustment_band": ..., "substitution": ...}]}})), naming only the members that are present. lines holds only the lines that carry at least one of these members, sorted by id in ascending order of UTF-16 code units (as RFC 8785 sorts keys). With none of them the hash is the one above, so every hash computed before this release stays valid. It is the anchor that binds every later artefact to one basket and one price:

  • the agent copies it into both closed mandates (Closing), together with the exact quote total;
  • complete MUST carry the same checkout_hash; any difference returns 403 mandate_scope_mismatch at $.checkout_hash;
  • if accepted_disclosures_hash is sent, it MUST equal disclosures.hash;
  • the payment leg to the PSP carries checkout_hash instead of the basket, and the PSP's Receipt repeats it;
  • the gateway allows at most one debit per checkout_hash (under a payment plan, at most one per tender, and never more in total than all_in_total; see Wire binding of plans);
  • the evidence bundle recomputes it from the BPP-signed quote and, where the session recorded one, the principal's selection (Evidence).

checkout_hash is the hash of the quote, not of an accepted negotiation offer. Nothing in BACP asserts that checkout_hash equals an offer_hash.

docs.title: Seller refusals and substitution
docs.text: When a seller NACKs, Error.seller_reason carries the reason that its BPP-signed NACK states. A retry of the same item at a total no higher than the one the principal was shown is recoverable. A substitute item or seller at a higher total than the last BPP-signed quote of the session needs a new confirm step-up, in human-present and in human-not-present sessions alike (Seller refusals and substitution). A substitute never arrives in the same quote and never on on_confirm without a new checkout_hash: a line's substitution.policy is none by default, so a substitute is not accepted, and with same_brand or ask a substitute still comes only in a new quote (Units and weighed goods). A BPP-signed seller_confirmation tag raises a confirm step-up with reason seller_confirmation, at most one per checkout_hash.

docs.title: Fees on the payer's screen
docs.text:
BACP makes normative what the principal pays and to whom. It leaves informative how sellers, payment aggregators and banks split their own costs (Who pays).

Payer-borne lines. Every quote line the principal pays, other than goods, carries a code or type, an amount in integer paise and a recipient (seller, logistics, buyer_app, agent_operator, assisted_operator, government or other). The recipient is the value that the seller's side signed. The gateway never infers it from the line's code; for a charge that arrives over Beckn it uses the published mapping. A convenience_fee or cod_fee line MAY carry applies_to_handlers, the handlers it applies to; a line without it applies to every handler, and a fee that applies to several handlers but not all is one line that lists them. The intersect response's comparison[] records, for each option, a gateway-computed method_charge: the sum of the scoped payer-borne lines for that option. A method_charge from a counterparty is ignored, and no view labels it as "who pays". recipient: government is valid only on a line of type tax, and a tax line's recipient is government. A line of the seller's quote never carries agent_operator or assisted_operator. On BACP-native lines either breach is schema-invalid. On Beckn the gateway ignores a stated bacp.charge recipient that breaches it, applies the table, and adds the warning charge_recipient_invalid (recoverable); a line that named the agent or assisted operator is also treated as an operator charge that the notice does not cover.

What never reaches the principal. The merchant discount rate (MDR), the payment aggregator's commission, the finder fee and net-settlement amounts MUST NOT appear in a payer line, in all_in_total, in a comparison[] total, in ts_render, in any principal-facing message or in rail.evidence of a receipt. They are not in the charge vocabulary, and BACP adds no payer field, because every quote line is borne by the buyer. NPCI's FAQ (15-10-2026) Q34 says that on-boarded merchants cannot pass MDR on to customers on UPI; it is an FAQ, not a circular.

Operator charges. A per-order fee that the principal pays to the agent operator, an assisted operator or the buyer app is a gateway-asserted line in the session's operator_charges[] ({code, amount, recipient}, code agent_fee or service, recipient agent_operator, assisted_operator or buyer_app). It is never inside the BPP quote: the quote total and all_in_total stay equal to Beckn quote.price.

  • The ts_render total and the amount evaluated against the mandate's budgets and step-up thresholds are the quote total plus the sum of operator_charges[].
  • The closed Payment Mandate's amount, and every debit to the seller's payee, are the quote total (or, under a payment plan, the tender amounts, which add up to all_in_total). An operator charge is never part of a debit to the seller's payee.
  • The gateway MUST check the session's operator charges against operator_compensation in the notice of the mandate's ConsentReceipt. They are covered only when a from_principal entry has basis: per_order and their sum is at or below its amount.
  • An uncovered operator charge raises a confirm step-up with reason constraint_unresolved, in HP and in HNP. Its render says that the fee is not in the terms the principal approved for this agent. The gateway logs the charge at stage disclosure.

This line discloses a fee; it is not a licence to charge one. NPCI's FAQ Q17 says that UPI application providers shall not charge a platform fee or any other charge, and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 r.5(7) (from 01-01-2027) restrict a bundled fee of a marketplace e-commerce entity. Whether either reaches an agent operator is open (Q-79). How the operator collects its charge is outside BACP, and BACP never moves it.

Intermediary compensation. The gateway copies the ONDC buyer finder fee and np_fees unchanged into the session's intermediary_compensation[], writes them to the InstructionLog at stage disclosure, and gives them to the principal on request. They are never read out per order on the Trusted Surface and never added to a total. The label for the principal is "fee paid by the seller to the buyer's app", never "seller's cost".

Convenience-fee consistency (SHOULD, never a refusal). NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 binds the Payee PSP, not the seller, the agent or the gateway. It asks that no surcharge is levied on users for UPI transactions, and that any convenience fee is disclosed upfront and remains consistent across the available debit payment modes (net banking, debit card, UPI and credit card). The gateway SHOULD warn when this is not so. Let D be the debit-mode handlers the seller accepts in this option set: the in.upi.* family including credit-funded UPI, in.card.* and in.netbanking. The gateway SHOULD give the warning payment_mode_fee_inconsistent (warning, requires_buyer_review) when a payer-borne scoped line (any code except cod_fee on in.cod) applies to a strict subset of D, or when the scoped amounts differ between any two handlers in D. It does not fire on a uniform unscoped fee. COD is outside the test, and PPI wallets and in.cod.upi stay outside D until counsel answers (Q-78). In human-present checkouts the Trusted Surface shows the fee before the factor. In HNP the warning raises a confirm step-up with reason constraint_unresolved, and no money moves until the principal decides. The text cites para 7.5 first, then the Payment Aggregators Master Direction 2025 para 10(c) ("charges, other than the price ... distinctly displayed to the payer prior to the transaction"), and NPCI's FAQ Q17 and Q34 as an FAQ; RBI's Card Directions 2025 para 77 is context (it binds issuers). It MUST NOT cite S.O. 5067(E) against merchants, because that order binds a "bank or system provider". Whether a Trusted Surface reading meets "to the User ... prior to the selection of the payment mode" is open (Q-78); the mandate constraint convenience_fees records the principal's consent in HNP.

Splitting. An agent SHOULD NOT split one intended order into several payments to change the fee a seller bears. Enforcement rides on the existing suspected-split-order confirm trigger (Split-order detection); BACP adds no new trigger.

docs.title: Discounts
docs.text:
BACP carries discount codes in the shape of the UCP Discount extension: codes go in, and the discounts that the seller applied (by code or automatically) and the codes it rejected come out. The capability is in.bacp.discounts, which extends in.bacp.checkout. A gateway that supports it lists it in capabilities (Capabilities). An agent SHOULD NOT send discounts to a gateway that does not list it. A gateway that does not list it refuses a request that carries discounts with 400 capability_unsupported at $.discounts and creates or changes nothing, and never ignores the member (Capabilities).

  1. Codes in. POST /sessions and PUT /sessions/{session_id} accept discounts: {codes[]}. The list replaces the earlier one. Because PUT already replaces every agent-editable field, an omitted discounts clears the codes, as does codes: []. The seller decides how codes match (for example, case).
  2. The seller's quote is the source of truth. The gateway forwards the codes on select and init (Beckn mapping). It derives discounts.applied[] only from offer lines in the BPP-signed quote, and never computes, adds or keeps a discount the seller did not sign. applied[].amount equals the line's magnitude, the discount total is the sum of applied[], and the payable amount is the BPP-signed quote total. The gateway MUST NOT submit a code, or select an offer, that the agent did not send in discounts.codes[], except offers the seller marks automatic. Every applied[] entry with a code MUST match a submitted code under the seller's case rule; an agent that sees any other records discount_source_unknown and tells a present principal.
  3. Rejected codes out. Each submitted code that is not in applied[] gets exactly one type: warning message at param: $.discounts.codes[n] with resolution: recoverable and one of discount_code_expired, discount_code_invalid, discount_code_already_applied, discount_code_combination_disallowed, discount_code_user_ineligible (UCP's names) or discount_code_unsupported (the seller or network takes no codes). A gateway MAY report every rejection as discount_code_invalid, so that the answers do not reveal which codes exist. The agent MUST tell a present principal.
  4. Automatic discounts have automatic: true and no code. The agent cannot remove them.
  5. No provisional discounts on a plain session. Discounts that depend on the payment instrument or on a buyer assertion (bank, card-BIN and UPI-app offers, loyalty, segment) stay in TermSheet scheme mode (Negotiation). A discount that carries provisional or eligibility is invalid, so that a producer of another protocol that sends them fails loudly instead of being half-mapped (Q-74). A provisional loyalty benefit never enters total, all_in_total or charge_lines[], and the agent says it with the loyalty_provisional sentence (Disclosure phrases). A paid membership that a seller adds is a line with added_by: seller, and the principal hears it as a line she did not add (Line provenance). The loyalty capability is parked (Q-98).
  6. Cashback is not a discount. It is never in applied[], and the agent never describes it as lowering the price (Rail bindings).
  7. Display. An applied discount is shown only as a discount line with the fixed discount_applied sentence (Disclosure phrases) and its amount. It is never shown as a new item price, a strike-through, or a percentage of an item price, unless the item carries a verified prior_price. title is seller text: it is shown only as labelled counterparty text, and no figure or percentage in it is voiced. A discovery offer's figures are rendered only for kind discount or slab, only after the source is verified (Verifying discovery results), and only as cart-level terms ("₹50 off orders above ₹499"; "10% off the order, up to ₹100"). Any other or unknown kind is rendered as "offer" with its title as labelled seller text and no figure. An item-scoped offer (item_ids present) is rendered without figures unless the item has a verified prior_price. Whether a coupon or a cart-level offer is an announced price reduction under r.4(13) is a question for counsel (Q-66).
  8. Mandate checks run on the payable. Every amount check of Deterministic evaluation (step 0, step 4, step 5, step 7 and step 8) runs on the BPP-signed quote total after discounts. No new mandate constraint is added. A discount that makes the payable zero is refused by step 0 (amount_not_positive) (Q-75). A line that an offer adds (freebie, buyXgetY) is a line item, and mandate step 5 applies to it.
  9. Changes after the quote. A discount that is applied at on_select and gone at on_init raises the total. It gives drip_pricing_detected (requires_buyer_review) together with the message of the code. Any change to checkout_hash re-runs step 8, so an approval given for a discounted quote never covers an undiscounted one.
  10. Refunds. The refund for a cancelled or returned line comes from the seller-signed revised quote, never from a gateway computation (Refunds). A refund never exceeds what was paid for that line, which is the line total minus the allocations on that line. The discount itself is never paid out as money.
  11. Codes the agent itself brings. An agent whose operator earns when a code is used (an affiliate code) MUST NOT submit it when no human is present. When a human is present it MUST first tell the principal, with the discount_affiliate sentence. The agent records the source of every code (principal or agent) in the InstructionLog at stage cart, with the code as an HMAC-SHA-256 under a per-session key that the operator holds and never as a bare hash (Instruction log).
  12. Limits. codes has at most 10 entries, each 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters. These are BACP design values against code enumeration, not regulatory limits, and are open to review. The gateway MUST rate-limit rejected codes per agent, per agent operator and per seller, and answers an excess with 429 quota_exceeded.

The gateway never funds a discount that is not in the seller's signed quote. A discount funded by the gateway or the buyer app is not supported, because it would break "amount equals the quote total" (Q-76).

docs.title: Session state machine
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> incomplete: create (select)
    incomplete --> incomplete: items changed (select), quote_mismatch
    incomplete --> ready_for_complete: on_init OK and pre-check OK
    incomplete --> requires_escalation: disclosure, drip pricing, split order or step-up
    ready_for_complete --> requires_escalation: complete over step-up or AFA threshold
    requires_escalation --> ready_for_complete: step_up.approved (confirm)
    requires_escalation --> complete_in_progress: step_up.approved with HP payment
    requires_escalation --> cancelled: step_up declined or expired
    ready_for_complete --> complete_in_progress: complete accepted
    ready_for_complete --> incomplete: quote expired
    complete_in_progress --> completed: debit OK and on_confirm OK
    complete_in_progress --> cancelled: debit failed, no money moved
    complete_in_progress --> complete_in_progress: payment in_doubt or reversal_pending
    complete_in_progress --> cancelled: refund credit settled (payment reversed)
    incomplete --> cancelled: cancel, TTL, mandate stopped
    ready_for_complete --> cancelled: cancel, TTL, mandate stopped, pre-debit opt-out
    requires_escalation --> cancelled: cancel, TTL, mandate stopped
    incomplete --> human_handoff: handoff requested
    ready_for_complete --> human_handoff: handoff requested
    requires_escalation --> human_handoff: handoff requested
    human_handoff --> cancelled: cancel, TTL, mandate stopped
    human_handoff --> incomplete: handoff released
    completed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]
From Event To Messages and notes (none) POST /sessions, on_select received incomplete ai_disclosure incomplete PUT with new items (select) incomplete quote_mismatch if the seller's quote differs from the request incomplete PUT, on_init signed, disclosures complete, pre-check allows ready_for_complete preticked_addon_removed, pre_debit_notice where applicable incomplete PUT finds drip pricing, a discovery_price_changed on an item shown with a prior_price, missing disclosures, a split order, or a step-up threshold requires_escalation drip_pricing_detected, discovery_price_changed, disclosures_missing, split_order_suspected, step_up_required ready_for_complete complete over a step-up threshold, AFA threshold, or split order requires_escalation step_up_required ready_for_complete complete after the quote's expires_at has passed incomplete quote_expired (re-select) ready_for_complete complete before a pre-debit notice matures ready_for_complete pre_debit_notice; no money moves requires_escalation step_up.approved without payment (confirm) ready_for_complete step_up_approved; agent completes with step_up_id requires_escalation step_up.approved with HP closed mandates and PSP receipt complete_in_progress continues to confirm requires_escalation step_up.declined, or complete after expires_at cancelled step_up_declined or step_up_expired; no money moves ready_for_complete complete accepted by the atomic evaluation complete_in_progress payment.status: initiated complete_in_progress Debit succeeds and on_confirm arrives completed budget_after complete_in_progress PSP refuses or fails the debit (one tender) cancelled payment_failed; reservation released complete_in_progress Under a payment plan, a later tender fails after an earlier one was captured complete_in_progress earlier tenders released or refunded to source; cancelled only when every unwound tender is released or refunded and its credit has settled complete_in_progress Under a payment plan, one tender is in_doubt complete_in_progress no other tender is released or refunded until the outcome is known complete_in_progress PSP times out complete_in_progress payment_in_doubt; reservation kept complete_in_progress Debited, on_confirm still missing after re-send complete_in_progress debited_not_confirmed; payment.status: reversal_pending complete_in_progress PSP reports the refund credit as settled cancelled payment.status: reversed any open state POST /sessions/{id}/cancel cancelled session_cancelled any open state Mandate revoked, paused or expired cancelled mandate_revoked, mandate_paused, mandate_expired; rail_binding_not_open_eligible for a gateway pause of an ineligible binding (Handler binding) ready_for_complete Principal opts out of a pre-debit notice cancelled pre_debit_opt_out (requires_buyer_input); no rail traffic incomplete, ready_for_complete, requires_escalation POST /sessions/{id}/handoff (action: request) human_handoff handoff.requested_at set; InstructionLog stage handoff human_handoff Acceptance signed by a human support operator under bacp-handoff human_handoff handoff.accepted_by and accepted_at set, by compare-and-set, only while accepted_by and ended_at are absent human_handoff Agent PUT or complete human_handoff 409 session_state_conflict at $.status human_handoff step_up.approved from the Trusted Surface human_handoff held, not applied, until release human_handoff action: release by the accepted_by key (bacp-handoff), or by the agent (bacp-browse) while accepted_by is absent incomplete handoff.ended_at set; InstructionLog stage handoff; a held approval then applies only if unexpired and its checkout_hash still matches human_handoff action: release by any other key human_handoff nothing changes any, with handoff.ended_at set action: accept unchanged 409 session_state_conflict at $.status; nothing changes human_handoff Cancel, TTL, mandate revoked, paused or expired cancelled as for the other open states; handoff is kept

The open states are incomplete, ready_for_complete, requires_escalation and human_handoff. Calling complete on an incomplete session returns 409 session_state_conflict; the agent MUST PUT the session first. Cancelling a session that is complete_in_progress or completed also returns 409 session_state_conflict; the agent cancels the order instead.

docs.title: Payment sub-states
docs.text:
Inside complete_in_progress, payment.status follows the payment saga:

payment.status Meaning not_started No debit attempted yet. initiated The atomic evaluation passed; the debit has been sent. debited A PSP-signed success receipt has been applied. confirmed on_confirm received; the session is completed. in_doubt The PSP timed out; the outcome is unknown. failed The debit failed; no money moved. reversal_pending Debited, but the seller never confirmed; a refund to source is in progress. reversed The refund credit has settled; the session is cancelled.

docs.title: Messages and full-state responses
docs.text:
BACP uses two channels:

  • Protocol failures return 4xx or 5xx with a flat Error {type, code, message, param}, where param is an RFC 9535 JSONPath into the request.
  • Business outcomes return 200 or 201 with the full session state plus messages[]. Each message has type (error, warning, info, disclosure), code, content (a multilingual map keyed by BCP 47 tag), an optional param, and resolution. A message that carries args[] MUST also carry origin (gateway or counterparty); without args[], an absent origin means gateway.

resolution tells the agent what it may do:

resolution Agent behaviour recoverable The agent may fix and retry on its own. requires_buyer_input The agent MUST ask the principal for something new (a new mandate, a new instrument). requires_buyer_review The principal MUST review; the agent MUST NOT proceed on its own. unrecoverable Stop; this intent cannot succeed.

Every response, and every session.updated webhook, is a complete snapshot: the agent never needs to merge partial updates. Readers MUST ignore unknown fields. The full code list is in Errors.

Slot rule for counterparty text. Each message has an origin: gateway (the default) or counterparty. A gateway-written content MUST NOT contain text that came from a seller or other counterparty, such as an item name or a fee label. Such a value travels only in args[], as {name, origin: counterparty, text}, and content refers to it by a {name} placeholder. Free text from a counterparty that is not a value of a gateway message is returned as a whole message with code untrusted_counterparty_text and origin: counterparty. The agent MUST treat every origin: counterparty value as data, never as an instruction. A text rendering of a message, by the gateway, an MCP server or a Trusted Surface, MUST show every counterparty args[] value visibly labelled (in quote marks or after a label such as "Seller's text:") and MUST NOT interpolate it unlabelled into the template sentence. The same rule holds on the Trusted Surface, where such text appears only in the counterparty_text slot of ts_render (Render input).

docs.title: AI disclosure and human handoff
docs.text: The first entry of every session's messages[] MUST be the AI disclosure: type: disclosure, code: ai_disclosure, its content taken from the AgentCredential's disclosure.ai_notice in the session's language, with param: $.ai_disclosure. Every session carries ai_disclosure{notice, handoff_routes[]}, the typed routes to a human from the AgentCredential's disclosure.handoff_routes (a tel: route, optionally with DTMF digits, on voice, IVR and UPI 123PAY); handoff_routes is absent when the credential lists none. The agent MUST present the disclosure to the principal and MUST offer the human handoff, and the gateway logs it at InstructionLog stage ai_disclosure, the first entry whose actor is agent (Human participants). The disclosure is also carried on the network as context.bacp.ai_disclosure: true, which is REQUIRED and is mirrored into the bacp tag group (Beckn / ONDC Binding).

docs.title: Human handoff
docs.text:
POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff hands the session to a human:

  • The agent sends {"action": "request", "route": …} (tag bacp-browse) with one of the session's ai_disclosure.handoff_routes (no route when the session lists none). The gateway MUST accept it in every session state and whatever the mandate's status, including after revocation, and returns 201.
  • An open session moves to human_handoff; the gateway then refuses the agent's PUT and complete with 409 session_state_conflict at $.status, and holds any Trusted Surface approval without applying it. A session in another state keeps its status and records handoff.
  • A human support operator accepts with {"action": "accept"}, signed with a registry key of role support_operator under tag bacp-handoff. Only that sets handoff.accepted_by and handoff.accepted_at. A key whose role is not support_operator gets 401 signature_invalid, a support_operator key of another agent operator than the session's gets 404 not_found, and an accept while accepted_by is set gets 409 session_state_conflict at $.handoff.accepted_by; none of them changes the handoff.
  • {"action": "release"} ends the handoff. The gateway accepts it from the accepted_by key under bacp-handoff, or from the agent under bacp-browse only while accepted_by is absent. The session returns to incomplete and handoff.ended_at is set. A release by any other key changes nothing: 401, 404 or, for a key of the same agent operator that is not accepted_by and for an agent release after acceptance, 409 session_state_conflict at $.handoff.accepted_by.
  • accept and release are each one compare-and-set on handoff.accepted_by and handoff.ended_at: an agent's release applies only while accepted_by is still absent, and an accept after ended_at is set gets 409 session_state_conflict. A race between them ends either released with no accepted_by, or connected in human_handoff, never both.
  • Every act is logged at InstructionLog stage handoff. On the network a handoff maps to Beckn support → on_support.

Session.handoff is {route, requested_at, accepted_by, accepted_at, ended_at}. See Human participants.

docs.title: Complete
docs.text:
POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete (tag bacp-pay) is the only call that moves money.

{
  "presence": "HNP",
  "checkout_mandate": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUuY2hlY2tvdXQuMSJ9.c2ln",
  "payment_mandate": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln",
  "checkout_hash": "sha-256:vRBpqmLq4AipYw1ZNnIL3trdLVrcHQAQ0g5RurJB4CQ",
  "accepted_disclosures_hash": "sha-256:vq4x2opsK4KIM-scKiTGRWd4Fzxs-GBx7lO8Glgm_U4"
}

checkout_mandate and payment_mandate are the closed mandates as attached compact JWS (Closing). After an approved confirm step-up the body also carries step_up_id. The agent MAY add kb_jwt.

The gateway, in order:

  1. Decodes the closed mandates and checks they are signed by the session agent's cnf key (HNP) or by the principal key that signed the parent (HP), and narrow the session's open mandates (403 mandate_invalid_signature or mandate_scope_mismatch).
  2. Checks the session state. A cancelled session returns its state (or the mandate error that cancelled it). A session that is already complete_in_progress or completed re-runs the closed-mandate checks and then returns 403 mandate_scope_mismatch (one debit per checkout). An open step-up that is not approved returns the unchanged requires_escalation state; an expired one cancels the session with step_up_expired.
  3. Checks the quote TTL. If the quote's expires_at has passed, the session returns to incomplete with quote_expired and nothing else happens.
  4. Checks the collector and bindings: the collecting party is an authorised PA or bank, and checkout_hash, disclosures hash, closed-mandate amounts and auth_binding all match. The amount of the closed Payment Mandate is the quote total; under a payment plan, the amount of each tender's closed Payment Mandate is that tender's amount (Fees on the payer's screen). A closed Payment Mandate whose amount does not match gets 400 invalid_request at $.payment_mandate (under a plan, at $.payment_plan.tenders[i].payment_mandate) and nothing changes.
  5. Verifies the InstructionLog chain (403 log_chain_invalid).
  6. Runs the atomic section, keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate: split-order detection, the authoritative evaluation against exposure, consumption of the closed Payment Mandate, the budget reservation, and the move to complete_in_progress (Usage ledger).
  7. Debits the rail after the atomic section. The debit instruction is basket-blind: payee, amount, closed-mandate reference and hash, checkout_hash, transaction_id.
  8. Applies the PSP-signed receipt to the ledger, computes budget_after, sends the payment.receipt webhook (with a ReceiptRef), and sends Beckn confirm with payment.status: PAID, the rail reference, and context.bacp.mandate_ref.
  9. On on_confirm records the order and returns completed.

Response (200, abridged):

{

  "transaction_id": "6f1c2a8e-0c7b-4f7e-9d0e-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "status": "completed",
  "presence": "HNP",
  "order_id": "ORD-KIR-88231",
  "line_items": [
    {"id": "I-ATTA-2KG", "quantity": 1,
     "unit_price": {"value": 11000, "currency": "INR"},
     "total": {"value": 11000, "currency": "INR"}}
  ],
  "totals": [{"type": "total", "amount": {"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"}}],
  "payment": {
    "handler": "in.upi.reservepay",
    "collected_by": "BPP",
    "type": "ON-ORDER",
    "status": "confirmed",
    "receipt": {
      "receipt_id": "rcpt_PAY0000000001",
      "receipt_type": "payment",
      "iss": "psp.example.in",
