docs.title: Timeout, in-doubt and reconciliation
docs.text:
If the PSP does not answer the debit, the outcome is unknown:

  • payment.status becomes in_doubt and the session stays complete_in_progress with message payment_in_doubt (recoverable). The budget reservation is kept.
  • The gateway MUST NOT attempt a new debit until the outcome is known. It reconciles with the PSP by the debit's idempotency key and applies the PSP-signed result: success continues to confirm; failure releases the reservation and cancels the session with payment_failed.
  • The agent MUST NOT retry with a new Idempotency-Key. It calls GET /sessions/{id} or waits for session.updated. A retry with the same key returns the same state and never re-debits.
  • Under a payment plan the same rules apply tender by tender. A tender in in_doubt freezes the plan: the gateway MUST NOT release or refund any other tender while it is unresolved, and a complete that carries a different plan for the same checkout_hash gets 409 plan_conflict or 409 session_state_conflict and debits nothing. When the in-doubt tender resolves as success, the session completes under the original plan.

docs.title: Debited but not confirmed
docs.text:
If the debit succeeds but on_confirm does not arrive, the gateway re-sends the identical confirm (same message_id) once. If it is still missing:

  • the session MUST stay complete_in_progress with payment.status: reversal_pending, reversal_deadline set to the debit time plus 5 days, and message debited_not_confirmed (warning, recoverable);
  • for refund_route: gateway_collector the gateway MUST start a refund to source immediately, citing the original rail reference (original_rrn for UPI); for seller_collector it MUST request that refund from the seller's collector through IGM at once. Issuing the refund Receipt does not by itself end the session;
  • when the PSP reports the refund credit as settled, payment.status MUST become reversed and the session MUST become cancelled;
  • payment.reversal_basis and payment.refund_route MUST be set. reversal_basis is rbi_tat when the payer PSP reports the debit as pending or as deemed (a credit-side timeout after a successful debit; NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular para 32.3), bacp_policy when the PSP reports the payee credit as completed and only the seller's on_confirm is missing, and unknown when the PSP's response does not say. refund_route is gateway_collector when the gateway's own payment aggregator collected the money, and seller_collector when the seller's collector holds it;
  • the debited_not_confirmed message MUST follow the basis. For rbi_tat it states the rail's turnaround time (T+5) and the compensation of ₹100 a day beyond it (RBI/2019-20/67, Annex, row 4(b): "Account debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location"). For bacp_policy it MUST NOT state an RBI compensation entitlement: reversal_deadline is then BACP's own policy of the debit time plus 5 days. For unknown it names the routes that certainly exist, namely the refund to source, a complaint through UDIR in the payer's UPI app (Consolidated Circular para 32.2) and, after 30 days, the RBI Integrated Ombudsman, and adds: "if your bank shows this payment as failed or pending, RBI's automatic-reversal and compensation rules apply". Whether row 4(b) reaches a payment that the rail completed, where only the seller's confirmation is missing, is not verified as of 18-10-2026 and is asked of counsel and RBI, so BACP promises no statutory remedy that may not exist;
  • the message MUST say what the gateway actually did. For gateway_collector the gateway's refund has "started". For seller_collector the gateway MUST request the refund from the collector through IGM, citing original_rrn, and tell the principal how to raise a complaint through UDIR, and the message says "requested", never "started" (on UPI a refund is an acquirer function: NPCI OC 165);
  • a late on_confirm, after the reversal has begun, is answered with a Beckn cancel, logged, and never debited again.

When the refund is settled, the spend is released only under the exception to "refunds do not restore budget", and while the reversal is unresolved the gateway makes no further human-not-present debit to that seller under the root. The signal that confirms refund settlement, and the saga for rails other than UPI, are open (Q-49); the rule above states which evidence releases the budget once it exists.

docs.title: Deferred settlement after a pre-debit notice
docs.text:
Some rails require the payer to be told about a debit at least 24 hours before it happens. This applies when the binding's effective pre_debit_notice is required_24h (e-mandate rails such as UPI AutoPay) or bacp_policy_24h (NACH). It also applies, until the legal position is settled (Q-03), to the second and every later unattended debit on a UPI Reserve Pay or one-time-mandate binding whose notice requirement is unknown; the first debit is covered by the block-creation authorisation. A deployment MAY switch that last default off per rail only by an explicit, logged policy decision, and conformance runs MUST keep it on.

Such sessions follow a notice-gated checkout:

  1. When the session first becomes ready_for_complete, the gateway MUST issue the notice and relay it as the webhook pre_debit.notice and the message pre_debit_notice. The session shows payment.scheduled_debit_at.
  2. A complete before the notice matures MUST move no money. It returns 200 with message pre_debit_notice (recoverable, param: $.payment.scheduled_debit_at).
  3. After the notice matures the agent MUST re-quote (PUT the session). The gateway MUST reuse the matured notice only if the new amount is at most the notified amount; otherwise a new notice is needed.
  4. If the principal opts out on the Trusted Surface (rail.debit_opt_out), the gateway MUST cancel the session with pre_debit_opt_out (requires_buyer_input) and send nothing to the rail.

The agent MUST relay a pre-debit notice to the principal and MUST NOT dismiss it. See Rail Bindings.

docs.title: Multi-seller basket
docs.text:
A session names one seller (bpp_id), binds one BPP-signed quote and allows one debit per checkout_hash. A purchase from several sellers is therefore a basket of sessions, one per seller, each of them a leg with its own quote, closed mandates, debit and receipt. BACP gives no atomicity across sellers: each leg completes or fails on its own.

  • basket_id. The agent groups the sessions with basket_id (pattern ^bkt_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,40}$) on POST /sessions. All sessions with one basket_id MUST have the same principal, presence and root open Checkout Mandate; otherwise the gateway returns 400 invalid_request at $.basket_id. basket_id is gateway-local: it MUST NOT appear in context.bacp, in Beckn tags or on the payment leg, so that no seller and no PSP learns the rest of the basket.
  • No payment spans sellers. No human-present payment and no BAP-collected payment covers more than one seller. Each leg pays its own payee. A complete whose payment would cover several sellers is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.
  • Plan before pay. Before the first debit in a basket, the gateway plans a payment for every leg under the per-leg rule. If any leg has no HNP handler, it raises one summary step-up (confirm, reason rail_fallback) covering every leg, and no leg is debited until that step-up is decided. A summary approves the plan; each human-present leg is then paid with its own closed mandates and its own factor (Step-up).
  • Headroom check. Before the first debit, the gateway MUST check every Reserve Pay leg: the block's remaining amount (attested block_amount less matched debits) covers the leg, the block has not expired, and the exposure of every block and leg fits the root's budgets (Usage ledger). If any check fails, no leg is debited and the gateway raises a rail_fallback step-up.
  • Partial failure. If one leg's debit fails (payment_failed), its reservation is released and the other legs keep their receipts. The failed leg does not move again without a new step-up: the principal chooses to drop it (the default when the step-up expires), pay that seller human-present, or hand off to a human (Human handoff). The gateway never re-routes a failed or in_doubt leg to another handler on its own, and never offers a new block after a failed payment.
  • Records. Each leg keeps its own RRN and receipts. The gateway keeps the basket_id with the sessions in its own records, and logs the rung chosen and skipped for each leg in comparison[].

The Trusted Surface rules for a basket (the number of sellers stated first, one line per seller) are in Human participants.

docs.title: Idempotency, retries and races
docs.text:
Every POST and PUT MUST carry an Idempotency-Key of 22 to 64 printable ASCII characters, which SHOULD carry at least 122 random bits. Keys are scoped to (agent, canonical operation, path parameters).

Situation Result No key, or a key of the wrong length 400 idempotency_key_required Same key, same body (semantic equality, null ≠ absent) The stored response, with header Idempotent-Replayed: true Same key, different body 422 idempotency_conflict; use a new key only for a new intent Same key while the first request is still running 409 idempotency_in_flight with Retry-After; retry with the same key Idempotency store unavailable 503 idempotency_store_unavailable; writes fail closed Per-agent key or in-flight quota exceeded 429 quota_exceeded with Retry-After

Keys are kept at least 24 hours (48 hours recommended). 5xx responses are never stored.

Lost responses. After a lost or timed-out response the agent MUST call GET /sessions/{session_id} first, and MUST retry complete only with the same key. A new key means a new purchase intent and is evaluated afresh. A 504 bpp_timeout leaves the session retrievable; the agent GETs it and retries with the same key.

Exactly one winner. However many complete calls race:

  • With the same key, exactly one executes; the others get 409 idempotency_in_flight or the replayed response.
  • With different keys on the same session, at most one debit happens: the closed Payment Mandate is consumed atomically and the gateway allows one debit per checkout_hash. The losers get 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.
  • Across different sessions under one open mandate, the atomic section serialises evaluation and reservation, so the settled total never exceeds any budget; the calls that would exceed it get 403 mandate_exhausted and move no money.

A gateway MUST NOT return a server error because of concurrent access to its own state, and SHOULD keep idempotency, nonce and reservation state in a shared atomic store when it runs as several instances.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text: The gateway sends session.updated (full session snapshot), payment.receipt, pre_debit.notice, mandate.status_changed and step_up.updated (the state of a step-up that the agent's request caused, with its ts_event_hash once approved) to the agent's webhook_url. Webhooks are signed by the gateway (RFC 9421) with Standard Webhooks headers and retried with backoff. A webhook body MUST NOT embed a signed Receipt: it carries a ReceiptRef (receipt_id, receipt_hash, receipt_type, result, and where present amount, refund_state and rail). The agent fetches the full receipt with GET /sessions/{id} and MUST check that its hash equals receipt_hash before relying on it (Evidence: Receipts).

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
Status Codes 400 invalid_request, idempotency_key_required, mandate_schema_invalid, receipt_invalid 401 signature_invalid, replay_detected, agent_unregistered, agent_credential_revoked 403 mandate errors (Mandates), rail_limit_exceeded, collector_not_authorised, log_chain_invalid 404 not_found 409 idempotency_in_flight, session_state_conflict (also any agent PUT or complete while human_handoff, a handoff accept after the handoff ended, the handoff operator-binding cases at $.handoff.accepted_by, a step-up inside the decline cool-off and a replacement past the re-prompt cap, Limits on step-ups) 413 request_too_large (body above 256 KiB) 422 idempotency_conflict 429 quota_exceeded 502 bpp_nack 503 idempotency_store_unavailable, trusted_surface_unavailable 504 bpp_timeout

See Errors for the full registry.

docs.title: Orders and Post-order
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

Once complete succeeds, the seller (BPP) owns an order. The order's state stays Beckn's authoritative state machine; the gateway mirrors it and adds an append-only adjustments[] read model. Every write after the order exists (cancel, return, raising and acting on an issue) is mandate-scoped: it passes the same deterministic gate as checkout, with its own signature tag bacp-post-order.

These are the paths that agentic checkout protocols generally leave out: cancelling, returning and complaining on behalf of a principal.

docs.title: Order addressing
docs.text:
Beckn order ids are unique only within the BPP that issued them. The gateway therefore keys every order by the pair (bpp_id, order_id).

  • When an agent holds only one order with a given order_id, it MAY address the order by order_id alone.
  • When the agent holds the same order_id from two or more BPPs, every order-scoped request MUST name the BPP:
    • in the request body as bpp_id on cancel (POST /orders/{order_id}/cancel), return (POST /orders/{order_id}/returns) and issue (POST /issues) requests;
    • as the query parameter ?bpp_id= on GET /orders/{order_id} and GET /orders/{order_id}/returns/{return_id}.
  • If the order is ambiguous and bpp_id is missing, the gateway MUST return 400 invalid_request with param: $.bpp_id. It MUST NOT pick one of the orders.
  • A bpp_id that matches none of the agent's orders with that id returns 404 not_found.
  • The query string is covered by the request signature: whenever the target URI has a query component, the RFC 9421 signature MUST cover @query (Identity and Request Signing).

For example, GET /orders/ORD-KIR-88231?bpp_id=bpp.kirana.example.in is signed with @query in its covered components, so the bpp_id cannot be changed in transit.

docs.title: Order state and tracking
docs.text:
GET /orders/{order_id} returns the Order: state, fulfilment_state, line_items, totals, invoice, adjustments[], return_window_ends, payment and mandate_ref.

  • state is the Beckn order state: Created, Accepted, In-progress, Completed, Cancelled.
  • fulfilment_state is the ONDC fulfilment state code (for example Order-delivered). An order with several fulfilments MAY also carry fulfilments[]{id, type, state} (SHOULD, where the seller reports them), each with its own state.
  • adjustments[] is append-only: cancellation, return, refund, replacement, dispute and weight_charge entries, each with status, at, and where relevant amount and receipt_id. Nothing is rewritten.
  • return_window_ends comes from the seller's @ondc/org/return_window.

The seller pushes changes as unsolicited on_status, on_update and on_cancel callbacks. The gateway accepts a callback only if it verifies against the BPP's registry key, is addressed to this BAP, and names an order it knows by (bpp_id, order_id); anything else is ignored and logged. It then sends the agent a webhook:

Webhook When Body order.updated Every order state or fulfilment change (on_status, on_cancel, on_update) Full order snapshot return.updated Every return or refund state change {order_id, return} payment.receipt A payment or refund receipt is issued ReceiptRef, never the signed receipt issue.updated A respondent action on an IGM issue Full issue snapshot

Tracking uses the same model: fulfilment progress arrives as order.updated with the new fulfilment_state. Beckn track → on_track maps to the bacp.order.track verb.

Order snapshot (abridged to one line item):

{
  "id": "ORD-KIR-88231",
  "transaction_id": "6f1c2a8e-0c7b-4f7e-9d0e-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "bpp_id": "bpp.kirana.example.in",
  "provider_id": "P-112",
  "state": "Completed",
  "fulfilment_state": "Order-delivered",
  "line_items": [
    {"id": "I-MILK-1L", "quantity": 1,
     "unit_price": {"value": 6800, "currency": "INR"},
     "total": {"value": 6800, "currency": "INR"}}
  ],
  "totals": [{"type": "total", "amount": {"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"}}],
  "adjustments": [],
  "return_window_ends": "2026-10-22T21:00:00+05:30",
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3"
}

docs.title: The post-order mandate gate
docs.text:
Every post-order write (cancel, return, raise issue, issue action) MUST pass this gate before any Beckn message is sent:

  1. Tag and idempotency. The request is signed with tag bacp-post-order and carries an Idempotency-Key.
  2. Mandate. The mandate_ref that a cancel, return or issue request carries MUST be the mandate the order was placed under (403 mandate_scope_mismatch otherwise). An issue action is checked against the mandate of the issue's order.
  3. Scope. The action (CANCEL, RETURN or RAISE_ISSUE) MUST be in the mandate's action_scope (403 mandate_scope_mismatch).
  4. Status. The mandate MUST be ACTIVE; or REVOKED, PAUSED, EXPIRED or EXHAUSTED with presence: HP, for every pause reason (principal_paused, binding_ineligible, reissue_required and unmatched_rail_debit). A write on a revoked, paused, expired or exhausted mandate without HP returns 403 presence_not_allowed. A PENDING or REJECTED mandate returns 403 mandate_required.
  5. Presence. presence MUST be in the mandate's presence_allowed (403 presence_not_allowed), plus the per-action presence rules below. A write with presence: HP that carries a valid hp_proof is exempt from this check, because the principal is present: otherwise a mandate whose presence_allowed is only HNP could never return goods. A grievance, dispute, cancellation or return write is never refused with mandate_exhausted or mandate_expired; for example an HP RAISE_ISSUE on an EXHAUSTED mandate returns 201.
  6. Presence proof. A write with presence: HP MUST carry hp_proof{ts_event_hash, step_up_id}: a step-up of kind post_order whose ts_render names this write (action, order_id and, for an issue action, issue_id and, for RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED or RESOLUTION_REJECTED, the subject_hash of the issue's resolution as shown), and the hash of its signed step_up.approved event, not used for another write. Without hp_proof the gateway returns 403 presence_not_proven (requires_buyer_review) carrying step_up (kind post_order, reason presence_proof) for the principal to confirm, and the same pending step-up on a repeat; with a proof for another action, order or issue, one already used, or one for an issue (RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED or RESOLUTION_REJECTED) whose current resolution does not hash to its subject_hash, the same code. The gateway consumes the proof inside the atomic section keyed on the order's root Checkout Mandate. No Beckn or IGM message is sent until the proof passes (Presence proof).

An ended or paused mandate does not strand an order. Revoking, pausing, expiring or exhausting a mandate stops new commitments only. Cancel, return and issue on orders already placed under it stay allowed, with the principal present, whatever the reason: a principal must always be able to cancel, return or dispute an order that is already paid, and the seller's take-back and refund duties continue. A pause for a lapsed conformance attestation or any other binding reason is a gateway condition and never blocks the principal's protective write.

docs.title: Cancel
docs.text:
POST /orders/{order_id}/cancel:

{
  "reason_code": "001",
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "presence": "HP",
  "hp_proof": {"ts_event_hash": "sha-256:Rk3mW8qZ1tY5vB9nC2xL6pD0sH4jF7gA3eU8iO1kM5w", "step_up_id": "stp_01HZPOCAN01q8W3nK5vRt7YcLm2"},
  "note": {"hi-IN": "गलती से ऑर्डर हो गया", "en-IN": "Ordered by mistake"},
  "bpp_id": "bpp.kirana.example.in"
}
  • reason_code comes from the seller's Beckn get_cancellation_reasons.
  • An HNP cancel is allowed only when the order amount is within the mandate's step_up.above_amount; above it the cancel MUST be presence: HP (403 presence_not_allowed).
  • The gateway sends Beckn cancel {order_id, cancellation_reason_id} and waits for on_cancel. If the seller refuses under its cancellation terms (@ondc/org/cancellable, cancellation_terms), the gateway returns 403 cancel_not_allowed (requires_buyer_review) with the seller's error.
  • On success the order becomes Cancelled, a cancellation adjustment is appended, and the gateway refunds the amount to the original method (Refunds). Cancelling an already-cancelled order returns its current state.
  • A seller-side cancel arrives as an unsolicited on_cancel. The gateway appends a cancellation adjustment with status SELLER_CANCELLED and refunds in the same way.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
POST /orders/{order_id}/returns:

{
  "items": [{"id": "I-MILK-1L", "quantity": 1}],
  "reason_code": "002",
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "presence": "HP",
  "hp_proof": {"ts_event_hash": "sha-256:M4pQ8rT2vX6zB1dF5hJ9kL3nP7sW0yA4cE8gI2mO6qU", "step_up_id": "stp_01HZPORET01q8W3nK5vRt7YcLm2"},
  "evidence": [
    {"type": "image",
     "hash": "sha-256:KArKH3tsITnbzaQ_h7yf91N2zdrnaEcfKy5IDFOJd7A",
     "uri": "https://agents.vaani.example.in/e/1.jpg"}
  ],
  "refund_to": "original_method"
}
  • Returns are presence: HP: the principal confirms the return on the Trusted Surface, through the post_order step-up that the first attempt returns, and the request carries hp_proof of that confirmation (gate step 6). An HNP return gets 403 presence_not_allowed; an HP return without valid hp_proof gets 403 presence_not_proven.
  • The request MUST be made before return_window_ends. After it, the gateway returns 403 return_not_allowed.
  • Partial quantities are allowed. Each item MUST be on the order, and for each item the quantity in this request plus the quantities in earlier returns on the same order MUST NOT exceed the ordered quantity. Otherwise 403 return_not_allowed at $.items[i].
  • The refund amount is the item's unit price times the returned quantity, plus the charge lines the order's terms refund and less any charge line the terms disclosed as retained. The refund record carries charges_refunded[] and charges_retained[]; a retained line carries the refund_rule that was disclosed before commitment. A refund that is below the amount paid and does not match charges_retained[] gets the message refund_short_of_terms (Refunds).
  • reason_code comes from the seller's get_return_reasons. Evidence is carried as hashes and URIs; the media stays with the agent operator.
  • The gateway sends Beckn update with update_target: item and returns 202 with a ReturnRecord in RETURN_INITIATED.
{
  "return_id": "ret_01HZXC",
  "order_id": "ORD-KIR-88231",
  "status": "RETURN_INITIATED",
  "items": [{"id": "I-MILK-1L", "quantity": 1}],
  "refund": {"status": "PENDING", "amount": {"value": 6800, "currency": "INR"}, "to": "original_method"}
}

The seller moves the return through on_update:

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> RETURN_INITIATED: update sent
    RETURN_INITIATED --> RETURN_APPROVED: on_update Return_Approved
    RETURN_INITIATED --> RETURN_REJECTED: on_update Return_Rejected
    RETURN_APPROVED --> RETURN_PICKED: on_update Return_Picked
    RETURN_APPROVED --> LIQUIDATED: on_update Liquidated (no pickup)
    RETURN_PICKED --> RETURN_DELIVERED: on_update Return_Delivered
    RETURN_DELIVERED --> [*]
    LIQUIDATED --> [*]
    RETURN_REJECTED --> [*]

The return refund MUST be issued exactly once, on the first of Liquidated or Return_Delivered. refund.status then moves PENDING → INITIATED → SUCCESS (with the refund receipt) or FAILED. A rejected return sets refund.status: FAILED. Each change appends a return adjustment and sends return.updated.

A rejected return also carries the message return_refused, and a seller's unsolicited on_cancel of an order carries seller_cancelled on the order. Each has resolution: requires_buyer_review and names the operator's grievance_contact in args[]. Neither ends the principal's route: a seller's refusal to take back goods that the principal reports as defective is not lawful (Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, r.6(3)), and cancellation charges are to be symmetric (r.4(8)), so the principal can raise an issue (Errors).

docs.title: Refunds to the original method
docs.text:
• The refund for a line of an order that carried discounts comes from the seller-signed revised quote, never from a gateway computation, and never exceeds what was paid for that line: the line total minus the allocations on that line (Discounts).
  • A refund MUST go back to the instrument that paid (refund_to: original_method), through the same handler, as a credit referencing the original payment.
  • The refund Receipt is PSP-signed and MUST identify the original payment (original_rrn, original_utr, or an original_* key in rail.evidence) and carry a refund_state. The default for a completed refund to source is refunded_to_source.
  • Card, UPI and net-banking payments are never refunded into a prepaid wallet (PPI), even on request (403 refund_to_ppi_forbidden). A refund to another payer-owned mode needs the payer's explicit instruction (403 refund_not_to_source otherwise).
  • Card refunds, split-tender allocation and credit-funded refunds have handler-specific states such as pending_cardholder_consent and adjusted_against_dues; see Payments and Credit and Split Tender.
  • A refund MUST NOT restore any mandate budget (Mandates).
  • A refund below the amount paid MUST match the lines in charges_retained[] (the same rule on a cancellation adjustment); otherwise the gateway returns refund_short_of_terms (requires_buyer_review, with the IGM route) and does not block or hold the refund. A refund is never reduced by the merchant discount rate or the aggregator's fees (Refunds).
  • Every refund appends a refund adjustment with its receipt_id and sends payment.receipt with a ReceiptRef. A failed refund appends a refund adjustment with a FAILED status.

docs.title: Weighed goods
docs.text:
A line sold by weight or measure (Units, quantity and weighed goods) can be packed heavier or lighter than quoted. The order stands at the quoted total unless a rule below moves it:

  1. Down only by default. A post-order weight adjustment can only reduce the amount: the gateway records it as a refund in adjustments[], to the original method, under the rules above. A weight adjustment that raises the amount, when the line carries no adjustment_band, is refused: the order stands at the quoted total, nothing is collected and the gateway records the refusal in the InstructionLog.
  2. A band, only with a hold. A line whose adjustment_band has a max_up (accepted only when all four conditions of Units, quantity and weighed goods hold) allows an upward adjustment of at most max_up, recorded as a weight_charge adjustment. The extra is collected only from the hold that was placed at payment: there is no second debit and no cash-on-delivery top-up. Where the rail has no hold, or the hold cannot be captured in part, the band was never accepted and the adjustment is down only. An upward adjustment above max_up, or on a rail without a hold, is refused and the order stands.
  3. Budget. A downward adjustment is a partial refund after fulfilment and releases no budget (Usage ledger).

docs.title: Issues and grievances (IGM)
docs.text: BACP raises complaints through the ONDC Issue and Grievance Management (IGM) flow, with the agent as an AI_AGENT complainant acting on behalf of the principal, and with a signed, verifiable evidence bundle attached.

docs.title: Raising an issue
docs.text:
POST /issues (tag bacp-post-order, RAISE_ISSUE in scope):

{
  "order_id": "ORD-KIR-88231",
  "category": "PAYMENT",
  "sub_category": "PMT02",
  "description": {
    "hi-IN": "दूध वापस किया, पर रिफ़ंड नहीं आया",
    "en-IN": "Returned milk, refund not received"
  },
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "rrn": "629318004417",
  "bpp_id": "bpp.kirana.example.in"
}
  1. The gateway passes the post-order gate. presence defaults to HNP; on an order whose mandate is not ACTIVE (REVOKED, PAUSED, EXPIRED or EXHAUSTED) it MUST be HP.
  2. It assembles the transaction's evidence bundle and runs the verification (the five AP2 steps and step 6, Trusted Surface events) and the InstructionLog chain check (Evidence bundle). If the bundle does not verify fully, it returns 422 evidence_unverifiable and sends nothing. A failure of only the catalogue checks of step 6 does not stop the issue: the gateway sends it with the result recorded in verification. A gateway MUST NOT refuse to raise an issue because of a catalogue check.
  3. It sends Beckn IGM 2.0 issue with the agent as an actors[] entry of type AI_AGENT (Proposed, see below) whose id is the issue's complainant_id, the agent id and operator, on_behalf_of set to the principal's pseudonymous principal_ref, the mandate_ref, the payment references (RRN or UTR), the evidence_bundle_ref URI and the evidence_bundle_hash, and mirrors the actor type in a bacp tag group.
  4. For a PAYMENT issue with an RRN, the gateway also lets the payer PSP pick the complaint up through UPI's dispute channel (UDIR), cross-referenced by RRN and the IGM issue id.
  5. It returns 201 with the Issue in status OPEN and level ISSUE. The seller's on_issue is only an acknowledgement; PROCESSING arrives later as an unsolicited on_issue.

Whether ONDC registers AI_AGENT as an IGM 2.0 actor type is open (Q-11): the IGM 2.0 enum has AGENT, which is not an AI agent. Until then it is a namespaced extension value mirrored in tags. BACP targets IGM 2.0, which has only issue and on_issue; GET /issues/{issue_id} returns the gateway's snapshot and makes no network call (the IGM 1.x issue_status / on_issue_status actions are not used).

docs.title: Status, actions and levels
docs.text:
Issue.status is one of OPEN, PROCESSING, RESOLVED, CLOSED. Everything the parties do is an entry in actions[] (with actor_type and time), never a status: OPEN, PROCESSING, INFO_REQUESTED, INFO_PROVIDED, INFO_NOT_AVAILABLE, RESOLUTION_PROPOSED, RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED, RESOLUTION_REJECTED, RESOLUTION_CASCADED, RESOLVED, CLOSED (the IGM 2.0 action codes), plus ESCALATED, a BACP agent action that raises the issue level (ISSUE → GRIEVANCE) rather than an IGM 2.0 action code. A proposed remedy is carried in resolution (action_triggered: REFUND, REPLACEMENT, RETURN, CANCEL, NO-ACTION, and refund_amount).

Respondent action (on_issue) Effect on status PROCESSING, INFO_REQUESTED, RESOLUTION_PROPOSED, RESOLUTION_CASCADED PROCESSING RESOLVED RESOLVED

The agent acts with POST /issues/{issue_id}/actions (INFO_PROVIDED, RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED, RESOLUTION_REJECTED, ESCALATED, CLOSED), through the same gate:

  • RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED and RESOLUTION_REJECTED MUST be presence: HP, with hp_proof (gate step 6): only the principal accepts or rejects a remedy, and only the remedy the principal was shown. If the seller revises the resolution after the principal confirmed, the proof no longer applies (403 presence_not_proven). RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED is followed by CLOSED, and the issue becomes CLOSED.
  • Acting on a CLOSED issue returns 409 session_state_conflict.
  • ESCALATED moves the issue from level ISSUE to level GRIEVANCE, handled by the grievance redressal officer (GRO). The escalation carries the same evidence bundle, identified by its hash.

IGM in its current version has no dispute level. Online dispute resolution (ODR) is referenced out of protocol as odr_reference (Q-06).

docs.title: Timelines
docs.text:
On opening, the gateway sets expected_response_by to at most 48 hours after the issue is raised and expected_resolution_by to at most 30 days after it, or to the shorter durations the respondent declares in the IGM 2.0 expected_response_time and expected_resolution_time. The 48-hour acknowledgement and one-month redress limits come from the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, Rule 4(5), and ONDC restates them for buyers: the buyer app "must come back to you within 48 hours", and a complaint "has to be resolved within 30 days" (ONDC complaint page). The IGM 2.0 schema carries these clocks as per-issue ISO 8601 durations and sets no network default; ONDC's reference SDK uses PT1H and P1D as example values. If the respondent misses expected_response_by, the agent SHOULD offer the principal an escalation to GRIEVANCE.

Proposed

Whether the gateway escalates automatically when a clock is missed, and what the ONDC Network Policy IGM chapter adds, are open (Q-57).

docs.title: Negotiation
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

The negotiation module lets an agent bargain, request quotations and bid on behalf of a principal, the way trade happens in India today: mol-bhav at a kirana or a weaver's shop, DM bargaining on social commerce, RFQ → quotation → PO in B2B procurement, and reverse auctions on government platforms. It sits before checkout. A negotiation ends in an agreed term sheet that the seller then binds in its signed on_init quote, and only that signed quote enters the checkout session and the payment flow.

RFQs and auctions build on this page and are specified in RFQ and Auctions. Which modes, payment handlers and validators apply to each kind of trade is set by the trade profiles.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Only structured, signed and expiring messages bind. Chat, voice, counterparty free text and LLM rationale are advisory. They carry binding: false, are logged as hashes, and never change a term sheet.
  2. The model proposes and a deterministic engine decides. A guard outside the LLM evaluates every outgoing firm counter-offer, acceptance, bid and award, and every incoming offer, against the principal's negotiation mandate. The model sees only a verdict.
  3. The reservation price never leaves the principal's side. The seller verifies only a signed within_bounds attestation. No message, error, webhook or log line sent to anyone else carries the reservation price or the ceiling.
  4. Indian law is enforced as validators, not left as guidance. MRP ceilings, the MSMED credit cap, the dark-pattern rules of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), cash limits and bid-rigging screens are checks that block, escalate or flag.
  5. Contract-law alignment. Offer, revocation, lapse and acceptance follow the Indian Contract Act, 1872, ss.4–7 (see Indian Contract Act timing).
  6. Silence is never acceptance. A negotiation that receives no reply ends TERMINATED at its deadline, never AGREED.

docs.title: Negotiation modes
docs.text:
Every session declares its mode up front. The enum is negotiation-session.json#/$defs/Mode.

mode How trade does it today Mechanics in BACP Acceptance or award fixed Catalogue checkout, MRP goods One firm offer (the on_select quote). The buyer may only accept, reject or let it lapse. Buyer accept posted_dynamic Rail flexi-fare, airline buckets, Tatkal A firm offer with short validity and a quota or class. A price change after expiry is a new offer, never a silent charge. Buyer accept within validity alternating Mol-bhav, DM bargaining, car dealers, B2B price rounds Alternating firm or indicative offers. One live offer at a time, max_rounds, absolute deadline. Either side accepts the live offer rfq_sealed B2B RFQ, GeM e-bid, sealed tenders Structured RFQ to N sellers, sealed commit–reveal quotations with a deposit, landed-cost comparison Award after response_by (RFQ) rfq_iterated Shortlist and "best and final" rfq_sealed, then alternating rounds with a shortlist. Each shortlisted seller is its own bilateral session under the parent rfq_id. As above english Mandi open outcry, eNAM, disposal auctions Ascending price-only bids on a neutral auctioneer's clock with anti-sniping Highest valid bid at close, then the seller's explicit acceptance (Auctions) reverse_l1 GeM reverse auction after technical evaluation Descending bids. Bidders see the current L1 price only, never who bid it. Lowest bid at close dutch Perishables, end-of-day clearance Published non-increasing price ticks First conforming acceptance in the auctioneer's chain order scheme Bank offers, coupons, QPS "buy 10 get 1", slab and target schemes No bargaining. The buyer asserts machine-readable schemes with eligibility proofs. The seller agrees or disagrees per scheme, and stacking rules apply. Seller Agree per scheme, then a normal accept

A coupon code on a plain checkout session is not scheme mode: it is a code that the seller applies or rejects (Discounts). Discounts that depend on the payment instrument or on a buyer assertion stay in scheme mode.

A sealed_first_price auction is negotiated under mode rfq_sealed, and a mandate that allows sealed auctions MUST list rfq_sealed in modes_allowed.

docs.title: Capability advertisement
docs.text:
A BPP advertises bacp.negotiation as a provider tag in on_search, mirrored into its profile. The BAP declares its own set in /.well-known/bacp (see Discovery and Profiles). The schema is negotiation-session.json#/$defs/Capability:

Field Meaning negotiable_issues[] JSON Pointers into the term sheet, e.g. /lines/*/unit_price, /payment/credit_days modes[] Supported modes max_rounds, round_timeout Round limits min_offer_validity Shortest validity the advertiser will issue sig_algs[], firm_quote_supported Signing algorithms; whether firm quotes are offered accepted_handlers[] Payment handlers the seller accepts, which feed the handler intersection pricing_ai_vendor Any third-party pricing or negotiation AI the participant uses

Rules:

  • A session MUST use the intersection of the two adverts.
  • Any issue not in the intersected negotiable_issues is fixed. A counter-offer that changes a fixed issue MUST be refused with NEG_ISSUE_NOT_NEGOTIABLE.
  • max_rounds defaults to 10 for B2C and 30 for B2B.
  • min_offer_validity has a floor of PT5M in every profile. A counterparty's advert MAY lengthen it and MUST NOT shorten it: the effective value is the larger of PT5M and the declared value.
  • An empty mode intersection returns capabilities_incompatible, and the agent falls back to fixed.

docs.title: The negotiation mandate
docs.text:
A negotiation is bounded by a negotiation mandate that is separate from the checkout mandate described in Mandates and Consent.

Why separate. AP2- and Verifiable-Intent-compatible verifiers fail closed on constraint types they do not know. Adding negotiation constraints to the checkout or payment mandate would make those verifiers reject it. BACP therefore carries the bacp.neg.* constraints in their own mandate:

  • vct: in.bacp.mandate.negotiation.1, kind: negotiation, schema mandate-negotiation.json;
  • signed by the principal on the Trusted Surface and countersigned by the Mandate Manager, like every other mandate;
  • for role: buyer, linked to the open checkout mandate by checkout_mandate_ref, which MUST be present. For role: seller (a reverse-auction bidder, a farmer selling a lot), checkout_mandate_ref MUST be absent, because a seller has no checkout mandate.

Both mandates are evaluated, and the stricter bound wins: the checkout mandate's budgets, allow-lists and step-up rules still apply to a negotiated deal.

Autonomous acceptance. process.accept_confirmation says what happens when the guard returns acceptable and the agent calls accept.

  • ask is the meaning of an absent key. The gateway raises a confirm step-up with reason accept_confirmation, whose ts_render carries offer_hash, and sends nothing seller-visible before negotiation.step_up.approved.
  • autonomous lets the gateway send the accept without the principal. It takes effect only if the mandate also carries a usable process.notice_route (type mm_event, tel or sms, and ref) that the Mandate Manager writes from a number or reference it has verified as the principal's own (for tel and sms, the number the Trusted Surface holds for the principal, as for voice), and never from a request. A MandateRequest whose proposed constraints carry notice_route is refused with 400 invalid_request at that path (mandate-request.notice-route.invalid.json). mm_event is not usable until BACP defines the event. Otherwise the gateway treats the mandate as ask and records autonomous_unavailable_no_notice_route (info). The only gateway-to-Trusted-Surface channel that BACP defines is the content-free app_push of a step-up (ts_notify_url), which carries a step_up_id and an expiry and never the text of a notice, so it is not a notice_route. BACP defines no gateway-to-Trusted-Surface notice event (Q-61), so a route the gateway itself uses (tel or sms) is the way to meet the condition until one is defined; if one is defined, it becomes an allowed mm_event value and the fallback fires less often.
  • Never preselected. The Mandate Manager MUST write the key on every mandate it issues from the effective date of this version. The notice that the principal approves on the Trusted Surface at set-up MUST present ask and autonomous with equal weight and preselect neither, MUST say that under autonomous the agent may accept a firm offer without the principal when the guard returns acceptable, and MUST give the fixed consequence sentence of each acceptance_revocation value (Render input), so that the principal knows what such an acceptance means before any is sent. In a consumer session this is also the explicit and affirmative action that Rule 4(9) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 asks for ("no such entity shall record such consent automatically"). Whether one Trusted-Surface-signed mandate is consent for each later purchase is open (Q-52).
  • agri seller. In an agri session a seller gateway treats the key as ask whatever the mandate says, so that a farmer always taps their own acceptance. This is a BACP gateway rule, not a legal requirement.
  • Legacy mandates. A mandate with no accept_confirmation is read as ask. A verifier that fails closed on unknown constraint keys refuses a mandate that carries the key until it supports it.
  • No hold. BACP has no accept_hold. The stops are the withdrawal of a purchase offer (Withdrawal) and the principal's decline of an AGREED or BOUND deal (Decline).

The negotiation mandate is verified only by the principal's own guard and credential provider. It is never disclosed to the counterparty. It travels to the seller only as a within_bounds attestation (see Binding to checkout).

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
constraints.negotiation ($defs/NegotiationConstraints) holds every bound. Unknown keys fail closed.

Required for sellers. price.unit_max[], price.unit_min[] Per-item bounds price.reservation The walk-away price. See Reservation price. Required for buyers. price.max_increase_pct_after_first_quote Drip-pricing tripwire. Default 0 for B2C. quantity[] Minimum, maximum and largest acceptable MOQ per item delivery.* deliver_by_latest, allowed slots and Incoterms, whether partial delivery is allowed, maximum delivery charge payment.* handlers_allowed[], max_advance_pct, credit_days_min / credit_days_max, max_delay_interest_pa_pct, emi_allowed, credit_funding_allowed, cod_allowed, cod_max_open_orders, collected_by_allowed[], credit_ledger{ledger_id, max_outstanding} after_sales.* Minimum return window, minimum warranty, installation, allowed return types quality.* Allowed grades; whether inspection or hallmarking is required commission.*, deposit.*, schemes.* Commission cap and who may pay it; deposit cap and refundability; allowed scheme funders. schemes.count_conditional_cashback is the constant false. process.* max_rounds, deadline, counterparty_allowlist, auction_max_bid, rfq_min_responses, rfq_min_window, award_rule, firm_counter_allowed, accept_confirmation, notice_route step_up.* any_violation, between_reservation_and_max and agreed_issue_reopened are the constant true. new_counterparty_above and drip_pct are set per mandate.

revocation.on_revoke is the constant withdraw_live_firm_offers: when the mandate is revoked, the gateway MUST send withdraw for every live firm offer of that principal (see Mandate revocation).

docs.title: Reservation price
docs.text:
The reservation price is the principal's private walk-away value.

  • price.reservation is an SD-JWT selectively disclosable claim with sd: true, disclosure: "never" (a constant) and held_by ∈ policy_engine | trusted_surface.
  • It MUST NOT be disclosed to the counterparty, to any seller-side verifier, to a payment processor or to the LLM. The model receives only the guard verdict.
  • Its relation to total_max is:
Offered all_in_total (buyer) Guard outcome At or better than reservation acceptable. The agent may accept without the principal. Between reservation and total_max needs_escalation, reason negotiation_between_reservation_and_max. The principal decides on the Trusted Surface. Beyond total_max needs_escalation, reason negotiation_out_of_mandate. The agent MUST NOT emit a firm counter-offer or bid at this value. A principal approval here is a fresh closed approval with an RBI-compliant factor.

For a seller mandate the directions are reversed (total_min is the floor).

A mandate that sets disclosure to anything other than never, or a buyer mandate without a reservation, is invalid:

docs.title: Presence of a negotiation
docs.text: The gateway derives the presence of a negotiation from the session in which the principal reached the agent, or from an hp_proof (Presence proof); it does not take it from the presence field of NegotiationCreate as the agent states it. A NegotiationCreate that asserts presence: HP without a valid hp_proof is refused with 403 presence_not_proven (requires_buyer_review), and nothing is sent to the seller. HNP needs no proof.

docs.title: Term sheet
docs.text:
Every binding offer carries a multi-issue term sheet, schema termsheet.json. Amounts are integer paise in INR.

Issue envelope. Every negotiable issue is wrapped as {value, negotiable, status, proposed_by}, where status ∈ Assert | Agree | Disagree | Terminate. This generalises ONDC's per-term status handshake for payment terms to every issue. The envelope and the groups are closed (additionalProperties: false), so a reservation value, a utility weight or any undeclared field cannot ride inside a term sheet. Extra issues go only under namespaced extensions, and the guard fails closed on any extension issue that is not in Agree.

Group Issues Price lines[], charges[], all_in_total unit_price; tax_inclusive; gst_rate_pct; read-only mrp; retail_package_mrp_required; price_breaks[]; line_total; every charge with mandatory and first_disclosed_round. all_in_total is required from round 1 and MUST equal Beckn quote.price. pricing_basis ∈ list, volume, negotiated, personalised, auction, scheme, posted_dynamic. Quantity lines[] quantity, unit (each, kg, quintal, set, hour, …), moq, tolerance_pct, option_clause_pct (GeM-style ± quantity option), price_breaks[] Fulfilment delivery.* fulfilment_type; deliver_by or slot{start, end, hold_until}; tat; incoterm (plus FOR_DESTINATION, Indian domestic practice and not an Incoterm); named_place; partial_allowed; delivery_charge; late_delivery_penalty Payment payment.* options[], each with its own all_in_total (e.g. prepaid against COD); selected_option_id; schedule[] tranches with an amount or pct and due{event, offset_days}; advance_pct; credit_days; credit_reference_event; early_pay_discount; delay_interest_pa_pct; emi; collected_by; settlement_basis and settlement_window; withholding_amount; cod{allowed, fee, rto_fee}; cross_border_instrument; credit_ledger Returns returns.* Window, type (refund, replace, credit note, exchange only), restocking fee, return-shipping payer, open-box delivery Warranty and penalties warranty_penalty.* Warranty months and type, extended-warranty price, liquidated damages (% per week, cap), PBG %, retention %, maximum liability, arbitration, jurisdiction Quality quality, lines[].quality Spec reference, grade, assay, inspection, rejection terms, HUID required Scope scope.* Deliverables, milestones, inspect-then-quote, inspection fee, revisions, change-order policy, no-show policy Schemes schemes.applied[] Funder, benefit type, eligibility proof (as a hash), stacking group, exclusivity, conditional (conditional cashback never counts in all_in_total), claim lifecycle Commission commission[] Broker, arhtiya, VLE or reseller commission: basis, value, who pays, deducted_at_source Deposit deposit Token, booking, security, EMD, refundable deposit or caution money; refundability; deduction policy; holder; linked_agreement_ref Cancellation, tax and documents, conditions ONDC-style cancellation.terms; tax_docs (e-invoice, e-way bill, TDS section); conditions_precedent[]; optional fx disclosure view (settlement stays INR) Parties parties.* buyer, seller and, where they differ, ordering_entity, consignee, paying_authority, intermediaries[]

A tranche structure such as "30% advance, 70% net-45 from GRN" is two schedule[] entries: one on_order, one on_acceptance with offset_days: 45.

docs.title: Credit terms and MSMED limits
docs.text:
If the seller is a Udyam micro or small enterprise in manufacturing or services, every credit offset (credit_days and every tranche offset_days) MUST be at most 45 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance. MSMED Act, 2006, s.15 says the period agreed in writing "in no case … shall exceed forty-five days from the day of acceptance or the day of deemed acceptance". The term-sheet schema encodes this rule, and the validator also runs in code.

  • Where no written agreement exists, payment is due within 15 days of acceptance: before the "appointed day" of s.2(b).
  • The day of acceptance is the day of actual delivery, or, if the buyer objects in writing within 15 days of delivery, the day the supplier removes the objection. With no written objection within 15 days, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery (s.2(b), Explanation).
  • Medium enterprises are never covered: the Act's "supplier" is a micro or small enterprise (s.2(n)).
  • Traders. The Ministry of MSME Office Memorandum of 02-07-2021 lets retail and wholesale traders register on Udyam but says their benefits "are to be restricted to Priority Sector Lending only". BACP therefore does not apply the cap to a trader seller, and the validator only warns. Whether that memorandum excludes traders from s.15 as a matter of law is open (Q-21).
  • A firm offer that breaches the cap is blocked with NEG_MSMED_CREDIT_CAP. A buyer's own draft only warns.
  • A buyer-signed GRN, or seller-posted delivery evidence that the buyer counter-signed or that carries a third-party reference the buyer can check, dates acceptance for the on_acceptance event and for every MSMED-applicable sale; seller-only evidence dates nothing (MSME late-payment interest). The acceptance date that starts the clock is the delivery date, or the date an objection recorded within 15 days of delivery was removed. How an objection travels on the network is open (Q-21); the rule is pending counsel (Q-83).
  • The credit ledger computes the statutory due date, compound interest at three times the bank rate on overdue amounts (s.16), and the income-tax deduction flag for late payments to micro and small enterprises. See Credit and Split Tender.

An interest-bearing EMI MUST carry no_cost: false, and EMI, BNPL and credit-funded options MUST carry the lender, APR and KFS reference (termsheet.emi-nocost.invalid.json fails the schema). Loan acceptance itself is always human-present (see Credit and Split Tender).

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
All negotiation messages are defined by offer.json, a oneOf discriminated by type.

type Sent by Purpose offer Either side A fresh offer (no in_reply_to) counter_offer Either side Rejects the live offer and makes a new one. MUST cite the live offer in in_reply_to. bid Bidder An auction bid (auction_id required) accept Offeree Absolute acceptance of exactly one live offer. Carries no terms. reject Offeree Rejects the live offer with a typed reason_code. final: true ends the negotiation. withdraw Offeror Revokes the offeror's own offer before acceptance is complete terminate Either side or auctioneer Ends the negotiation (max_rounds, deadline, principal_instruction, mandate_revoked, no_agreement, auction_closed_no_award, rfq_not_awarded) request_extension Offeree Asks the offeror to extend expires_at. Silence means no extension. accept_revoke Acceptor Revokes an acceptance before it reaches the proposer, only where the offer allows it bid_commit, bid_reveal, bid_retract Bidder Sealed-bid commitment and reveal; open-outcry retraction (Auctions)

docs.title: Common envelope
docs.text:
Every message carries msg_id, negotiation_id, transaction_id (the Beckn context.transaction_id), round, dispatched_at, received_at (filled by the receiver), from{role, np_id, agent_id, offeror_kind}, signatures[] and, once received, counter_signature. Every firm offer, bid, accept, withdraw, accept_revoke, bid_commit and bid_reveal also carries sender_log_seq, sender_log_prev and protocol_terms{version, hash} inside its signed bytes (Signed seller acceptance and clock skew). The gateway fills them; a model never supplies them. An "offer" for these rules includes a bid and an RFQ quotation, on receipt as well as on draft.

  • Signing. A message MUST carry the sending network participant's registry signature (role: bap or bpp): a detached JWS over the JCS of the message without signatures, counter_signature and received_at. The gateway MUST NOT hold or use an agent's key. The agent's own act is evidenced by its RFC 9421 request signature under the tag bacp-negotiate, which the gateway verifies before parsing and records in the transcript (see Identity and Request Signing). A message MAY also carry an agent signature entry. Whether agents SHOULD sign message bodies is open (Q-48).
  • Hashes. msg_hash and offer_hash are sha-256 over JCS of the message minus signatures, counter_signature and received_at, so the hash does not change on receipt. dispatched_at, sender_log_seq, sender_log_prev and protocol_terms are inside the hashed bytes.
  • Receipt. The receiver returns a CounterSignature, a compact JWS by its registry key whose payload is a CounterSignaturePayload (msg_hash, negotiation_id, received_at, log_seq, log_entry_hash, prev_entry_hash, all REQUIRED), in the synchronous response to the exchange. The CounterSignature is a BACP artefact, not a Beckn signed acknowledgement, and BACP does not require Beckn 2.0 signed acknowledgements on the network leg (settled in Q-43). A counterparty that does not return valid CounterSignatures is treated as not supporting firm negotiation: the gateway MUST send it only non-firm offers (firm: false).
  • Agent disclosure. from.offeror_kind ∈ agent | human MUST be present on every message and MUST be shown to the principal.
  • Advisory text. Free text travels only in advisory{binding: false, text_hash, chat_ref}. Counterparty free text reaches the agent only as a messages[] entry with code untrusted_counterparty_text, which the agent framework MUST treat as data. It MUST NOT invoke tools, change mandates or trigger an acceptance.

docs.title: Offers: firm and non-firm, expiry
Acceptance
docs.text:
An accept carries no terms: the schema forbids term_sheet and in_reply_to. It carries:

  • offer_hash, which MUST equal the hash of the live offer exactly;
  • negotiation_mandate_ref{id, hash}, whose content is never disclosed;
  • legal_effect ∈ acceptance (the accepted offer was firm) | purchase_offer (it was non-firm);
  • bound_attestation, the within_bounds attestation (see Binding to checkout).

An accept MUST NOT carry a step_up_id or any other field that reveals that the deal needed the principal's approval.

Notice of an autonomous act. After every accept that the gateway dispatches without a step-up, for buyer and seller roles alike, the gateway emits to the principal the message agreed_by_agent (type: info, resolution: recoverable). For a consumer purchase offer, where the accept is of a non-firm offer, the message is purchase_offered_by_agent. These are info and not requires_buyer_review so that a model does not read them as an instruction to stop and turn autonomous back into ask by its own branching. The notice:

  • is built from gateway templates in the principal's language, never from agent prose, and reaches the principal by the mandate's notice_route, never through the agent's own output;
  • states the seller or buyer name, offeror_kind, the all-in total (in ₹ with Indian grouping, and spoken in words on a voice surface), the quantity and unit, the current-stage cancellation charge, the stop route available in that state, revoke_route, grievance_contact and a content_hash;
  • carries no URI other than those routes and no urgency text (Render input);
  • is recorded in the evidence bundle as notice_renders[], the gateway-signed render with the receipt of its delivery (Evidence).

The stop button of a purchase_offered_by_agent notice appears only where a carrier exists that can honour it. On a Beckn leg no carrier exists in this version (Beckn / ONDC Binding), so the notice there MUST NOT show a stop control, because a control that cannot work is a misleading interface.

docs.title: Withdrawal, rejection and termination
Decline of an AGREED or BOUND deal
docs.text:
No exit from AGREED or BOUND exists on the agent's instruction, and none is added: an agent path would let an agent cancel many formed contracts and leave the charges with the principal. The principal declines on the Trusted Surface with the distinct event negotiation.agreed.declined, signed with its Presentation (Presentation record). The event name differs from negotiation.step_up.declined, because one verb with two consequences cannot be told apart on a voice channel or in the bundle. An agent terminate after AGREED without that event is refused with 403 presence_not_proven.

  • The render MUST show the current-stage charge under the term sheet's cancellation.terms before the factor is taken.
  • The edges are AGREED → CANCELLED and BOUND → CANCELLED, reason principal_declined.
  • It is not a breach when the terms permit cancellation at that stage: it is performance of a term. A breach is flagged, as a claim only and never as a finding, when the terms make that stage non-cancellable or the charge goes unpaid. If the terms are silent on the stage before CONTRACTED, the record carries principal_declined with the flag no_stage_term and no fee is computed.
  • A session already in BREACH_FLAGGED keeps its no-penalty buyer cancel.
  • For a consumer, Rule 4(8) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (parity) bears on any charge; whether it limits a charge before CONTRACTED is open (Q-52). The Rules give no cooling-off right.

A reject carries a typed reason_code (price, delivery, payment_terms, quality, not_negotiable, mrp_exceeded, msmed_credit_cap, terms_drift, out_of_mandate, incoterm_not_supported, other) and MAY carry an ONDC error code such as 50005. It MUST NOT carry the reservation value.

docs.title: Extension requests
docs.text:
Expiry is a signed term, so an extension is a new offer: the offeror re-issues identical terms with a later expires_at and extends: <old hash>, and the old offer becomes SUPERSEDED. If the offeror does not answer, there is no extension.

request_extension is sent only on the principal's or agent's explicit instruction: a Trusted Surface negotiation.request_extension event, or an explicit agent message. The gateway MUST NOT send it automatically when a negotiation is escalated (see Anti-leak rules). Whether a seller can answer within ONDC's PT30S TTL is open (Q-34).

docs.title: State machines
docs.text: BACP tracks the state of each offer and the state of the negotiation separately. Each offer has its own lifecycle in NegotiationSession.offers[].state. The schema is negotiation-session.json.

docs.title: Offer state
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> LIVE: signed offer countersigned by receiver
    LIVE --> SUPERSEDED: counter-offer received or extension re-issued
    LIVE --> ACCEPTED: conforming accept dispatched before expires_at
    LIVE --> WITHDRAWN: withdraw received before accept dispatched
    LIVE --> REJECTED: reject received
    LIVE --> EXPIRED: expires_at passed with no accept
    LIVE --> LAPSED_CONDITION: condition precedent failed
    LIVE --> ACCEPT_REVOKED: sunset only, matched accept_revoke and accept
    ACCEPTED --> ACCEPT_REVOKED: sunset only, proposer countersigns accept_revoke_honoured
    ACCEPTED --> WITHDRAWN: earlier-received withdraw processed late
    WITHDRAWN --> LIVE: our withdraw lost the crossing to an earlier accept
    ACCEPTED --> [*]
    SUPERSEDED --> [*]
    WITHDRAWN --> [*]
    REJECTED --> [*]
    EXPIRED --> [*]
    LAPSED_CONDITION --> [*]
    ACCEPT_REVOKED --> [*]
  • One live offer. At most one offer is LIVE per negotiation. A counter-offer MUST cite the live hash in in_reply_to, otherwise it is refused with NEG_STALE_OFFER (409). Accepting a superseded offer is also NEG_STALE_OFFER.
  • The two crossing edges (ACCEPTED → WITHDRAWN, WITHDRAWN → LIVE) follow the committed-order rule of Contested crossings and are annotated in the offer's history. A contested crossing takes neither edge: the offer stays as it was and the session is ESCALATED.
  • ACCEPT_REVOKED is dormant in this version. Both edges into it exist only under acceptance_revocation: allowed_until_receipt, which every receiver refuses, so no offer reaches ACCEPT_REVOKED. The edges are defined by the sunset text: the matched pair (LIVE → ACCEPT_REVOKED, the proposer's view) and the proposer's countersigned accept_revoke_honoured (ACCEPTED → ACCEPT_REVOKED, the acceptor's view).

docs.title: Negotiation state
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> OPEN: capability intersection OK
    OPEN --> AWAITING_OFFER: RFQ or select sent
    OPEN --> NEGOTIATING: first offer sent or received
    AWAITING_OFFER --> NEGOTIATING: quotation received
    AWAITING_OFFER --> TERMINATED: response_by passed with no quotation
    NEGOTIATING --> NEGOTIATING: counter or fresh offer or extension
    NEGOTIATING --> ESCALATED: guard verdict needs_escalation
    ESCALATED --> NEGOTIATING: principal declines or link or offer expires
    ESCALATED --> ACCEPT_PENDING: principal approves and accept dispatched
    NEGOTIATING --> ACCEPT_PENDING: accept dispatched on live firm offer
    NEGOTIATING --> AGREED: counterparty accepts our live firm offer
    NEGOTIATING --> PURCHASE_OFFERED: accept dispatched on non-firm offer
    ACCEPT_PENDING --> AGREED: receipt countersigned and no earlier withdraw
    ACCEPT_PENDING --> NEGOTIATING: earlier withdraw wins or accept revoked
    PURCHASE_OFFERED --> BOUND: seller on_init echoes the accepted terms
    PURCHASE_OFFERED --> NEGOTIATING: seller on_init differs and is a counter-offer
    PURCHASE_OFFERED --> REJECTED: seller declines with typed reason
    PURCHASE_OFFERED --> NEGOTIATING: buyer withdraw before on_init
    AGREED --> BOUND: on_init terms equal accepted terms
    AGREED --> BREACH_FLAGGED: on_init drift
    BOUND --> CONTRACTED: confirm then on_confirm
    BOUND --> BREACH_FLAGGED: confirm or on_confirm drift
    AGREED --> CANCELLED: principal_declined (TS event and hp_proof)
    BOUND --> CANCELLED: principal_declined (TS event and hp_proof)
    BREACH_FLAGGED --> CANCELLED: buyer cancels without penalty
    BREACH_FLAGGED --> NEGOTIATING: buyer treats drifted terms as a new seller offer
    NEGOTIATING --> REJECTED: final reject
    NEGOTIATING --> TERMINATED: max_rounds or deadline or mandate revoked or terminate
    ESCALATED --> TERMINATED: deadline or mandate revoked
    ESCALATED --> AGREED: contested, both principals confirm
    ESCALATED --> CANCELLED: crossing_unconfirmed or formation_disputed
    CONTRACTED --> [*]
    CANCELLED --> [*]
    REJECTED --> [*]
    TERMINATED --> [*]
  • ESCALATED has two causes: a guard verdict (needs_escalation, or an acceptance that needs the principal's confirmation under accept_confirmation) and a contested crossing (reason crossing_contested, see Contested crossings). The edges ESCALATED → AGREED and ESCALATED → CANCELLED belong to the second.
  • NEGOTIATING with no live offer is legal (every offer expired). A fresh offer may follow while round < max_rounds and now < negotiation_deadline. A message for round max_rounds + 1, or after the deadline, ends the negotiation TERMINATED.
  • Silence ends at the deadline as TERMINATED, never AGREED.
  • From BREACH_FLAGGED, a buyer who treats the drifted terms as a new seller offer sends them through the guard and validators like any incoming offer. The breach record stays either way.
  • Cancelling after CONTRACTED is not a negotiation transition. It is the order cancel path under the agreed cancellation.terms (see Orders and Post-order). A seller-side cancel of a firm contract is a firm-offer breach event.
  • BOUND opens the checkout session in ready_for_complete with the BPP-signed quote. CONTRACTED corresponds to the checkout session's completed.
