docs.title: The guard
docs.text:
The guard is a deterministic, non-LLM policy engine inside the gateway's trust zone. The model proposes and the guard decides. It runs on every outgoing firm counter-offer, acceptance, bid and award, and on every incoming offer, where it computes the verdict shown to the model. It fails closed, and the first failing step wins. Step-ups are collected so that the principal's diff card shows every out-of-bound issue.

Step Check On failure N-1 Request signature with tag bacp-negotiate, agent credential, both mandates ACTIVE, presence allowed 401 / 403 as for checkout N-2 Schema validation of the message and the term sheet. Unknown constraint keys and extension issues not in Agree fail. NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID. Where the failing schema rule encodes a validator (MSMED cap, no-cost EMI), the validator's code is reported instead (NEG_MSMED_CREDIT_CAP, NEG_EMI_NO_COST_FALSE). N-3 Capability: mode in the intersection and in modes_allowed; changed issues within negotiable_issues; round ≤ max_rounds; now < deadline capabilities_incompatible, NEG_ISSUE_NOT_NEGOTIABLE, or TERMINATED N-4 Offer liveness: in_reply_to or offer_hash is the live hash; the offer has not expired NEG_STALE_OFFER, NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED N-5 Validators Per validator: block, step-up or flag N-6 Every per-issue bound in constraints.negotiation; counterparty allow-list needs_escalation; mandate_scope_mismatch for a counterparty outside the allow-list N-7 Exposure across all of the principal's concurrent negotiations needs_escalation with NEG_EXPOSURE_EXCEEDED N-8 Price against the reservation needs_escalation N-9 Checkout-mandate rules: category, merchant and PIN code allow-lists, step_up.above_amount, step_up.new_merchant, and the negotiation mandate's new_counterparty_above needs_escalation N-10 Payment feasibility: the handler intersection is non-empty for the selected payment option at this presence handlers_incompatible N-11 Write a guard entry to the instruction log with constraint IDs only, never values. Request the within_bounds attestation. n/a

docs.title: Outcomes
docs.text:
The guard produces one of three verdicts, and the verdict is the only signal about the mandate that reaches the model (live_offer.guard):

Guard result Verdict shown to the model Meaning pass acceptable Within every bound and at or better than the reservation. The agent may act without the principal. escalate needs_escalation Outside a bound, between the reservation and the ceiling, over exposure, or a step-up rule fired. Only the principal can approve. fail not_acceptable A validator blocked, or a hard rule failed. The agent MUST NOT accept.

Counter-offers follow two rules:

  • An agent MUST NOT emit a firm counter-offer outside the mandate, because the counterparty could accept it.
  • If the guard returns needs_escalation, the agent MAY still send the counter-offer, but only with subject_to_principal_approval: true, which forces firm: false. If process.firm_counter_allowed is false, every outgoing counter-offer is non-firm.

docs.title: Step-up to the Trusted Surface
docs.text:
A negotiation step-up is created only on an outgoing accept or firm-counter attempt. An incoming verdict only sets live_offer.guard; it creates no step-up, so that fifty incoming offers cannot send the principal fifty prompts. On needs_escalation for such an attempt, or on acceptable under accept_confirmation: ask, the session moves to ESCALATED and carries a step_up object with kind: confirm and reason ∈ negotiation_out_of_mandate | negotiation_between_reservation_and_max | accept_confirmation. In the A2A binding this maps to the task state TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED (A2A 1.0), and in MCP to insufficient_scope (see MCP and A2A).

  • The diff card (issue, offered value, the principal's own bound, all-in total, offer expiry) is rendered only on the Trusted Surface. The agent and the counterparty never receive the bound. In the REST view, step_up.diff[] carries only issue_path, offered and within_bounds.
  • The step-up's ts_render carries the offer_hash of the offer to approve and, for a firm offer, its acceptance_revocation value, which the Trusted Surface shows only as a fixed consequence sentence followed by the cancellation terms (Render input).
  • The Trusted Surface posts the principal's approval as a negotiation.step_up.approved event, never step_up.approved. Its presentation MUST carry offer_hash and MUST NOT carry checkout_hash, because no quote exists yet. The gateway refuses the event with 403 ts_render_mismatch unless presentation.offer_hash equals the ts_render's offer_hash and the offer the step-up names (Presentation record).
  • The principal approves with an RBI-compliant factor such as the UPI PIN or a device biometric. The Mandate Manager then issues a one-off within_bounds attestation bound to that exact offer_hash.
  • The step-up link lives for min(15 minutes, expires_at − now). An offer that expires while the negotiation is ESCALATED cannot be revived by the approval. The approval can then be used only for a fresh offer, and an acceptance attempt returns NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED.
  • Fatigue limits.
    • At most one pending negotiation step-up exists per negotiation_id. It is marked superseded when its offer is superseded, and an event for it gets 409 NEG_STALE_OFFER.
    • At most one step-up is presented at a time per principal. Others queue and expire with their offers.
    • The gateway caps the step-ups it creates per principal. The cap, a count over a window, is declared in /.well-known/bacp (negotiation.step_up_cap); BACP sets no number. Beyond it the gateway answers the agent 429 with Retry-After, and nothing is visible to the seller: a capped offer lapses by silence. The cap also counts the fee-line review prompts of TS-3 and a BACP step-up for the convenience-fee disclosure that NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 requires (Mandates and Consent).
    • negotiation.step_up.declined MAY carry end_negotiation: true, which sends terminate with reason principal_instruction, so that declining stays as easy as approving.
    • The Central Consumer Protection Authority's Dark Patterns Guidelines name "nagging" as "repeated and persistent interactions … unless specifically permitted by the user", and from 01-01-2027 Rule 4(15) of the E-Commerce Rules makes compliance and a yearly self-audit a duty of the entity.
  • An offer that lapses while the principal approves produces offer_expired_during_approval in the ts_render language ("the offer ran out while you were approving"), never "you declined".
  • A negotiation approval that names a checkout step-up is refused with 403 ts_render_mismatch, and the session is unchanged.
  • A seller's acceptance of the buyer's non-firm offer is the seller's purchase offer, not a contract. It escalates, and it binds only after the principal approves on the Trusted Surface and the terms are within the mandate's bounds.

docs.title: Anti-leak rules
docs.text:
The principal's bounds MUST NOT leak through any channel:

  1. No seller-visible escalation signal. Escalation MUST NOT emit anything the seller can see. In particular the gateway MUST NOT send an automatic request_extension when it escalates, and an accept MUST NOT carry a step_up_id or any approval reference. An extension is requested only on an explicit principal or agent instruction.
  2. Nothing seller-facing carries a bound. No offer, reject reason, error, webhook, Beckn message or evidence bundle shared with the counterparty carries reservation, total_max, total_min, utility weights, or an AP2 amount_range.max. The seller verifies only the within_bounds attestation.
  3. The model does not see the bound. The reservation lives in the policy engine or on the Trusted Surface. The model receives only acceptable, not_acceptable or needs_escalation.
  4. Logs carry IDs, not values. Guard entries carry constraint IDs only. Gateways and registries MUST NOT log term-sheet contents in the clear.
  5. Data-loss prevention. Participants SHOULD scan every buyer-originated outgoing message, response, webhook and log line for the reservation and ceiling values. The scan MUST be provenance-aware: a number that the counterparty sent first and that the buyer side merely echoes (for example, a seller's COD total that happens to equal the reservation) is not a leak. Only buyer-originated content is judged. Conformance runs apply this scan after every case (see Conformance).

docs.title: Validators
docs.text:
Validators run at three places: at the BPP before it sends, at the BAP gateway on receipt (guard step N-5), and at the network's log-validation layer, which extends ONDC's search-time MRP check to select, init, confirm and update. Error codes follow the two-channel rule.

ID Validator Rule Outcome and code V-01 MRP ceiling For a line with retail_package_mrp_required: true, the unit price including tax MUST NOT exceed mrp per sale unit, at every offer, bid, on_select, on_init, confirm and update, in B2B and B2C. Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011, Rule 18(2) bars any retail dealer or other person, including a manufacturer, packer, importer or wholesale dealer, from selling a packaged commodity above its retail sale price (as confirmed in a Lok Sabha answer of 26-03-2025). English auctions are capped at MRP. Not applied to loose goods or to packs exempt under Rule 3, which per a consolidated text are: packages of more than 25 kg or 25 L; cement, fertiliser and agricultural farm produce in bags above 50 kg; and packs meant for industrial or institutional consumers. The Rule 3 wording is from a secondary consolidation and was not checked against the Gazette. The rules define the retail sale price as the maximum price "inclusive of all taxes" and say nothing about fees; whether fees count toward MRP, and the current Rule 3 text, are open (Q-20). Fail-safe default until Q-20 is settled: (1) in B2C, every line that carries an mrp is checked, whatever its retail_package_mrp_required value; the Rule 3 exemption (retail_package_mrp_required: false) is honoured only in B2B; (2) for the lines checked, the sum of unit price including tax times quantity, plus every mandatory packing and convenience charge, MUST NOT exceed the sum of mrp times quantity; delivery and other charges stay separate disclosed charges. block, NEG_MRP_EXCEEDED V-02 MSMED credit cap See Credit terms and MSMED limits block for a firm offer, warn otherwise; NEG_MSMED_CREDIT_CAP V-03 Drip pricing all_in_total present from round 1 and equal to quote.price. A charge with first_disclosed_round > 1 forces re-consent. A rise above max_increase_pct_after_first_quote between on_select and on_init or confirm triggers step-up. Payment-method fees appear in payment.options[] from round 1. step-up, NEG_DRIP_PRICING V-04 Terms drift See Drift detection breach, NEG_TERMS_DRIFT V-05 False urgency expires_at − valid_from ≥ effective min_offer_validity (floor PT5M) block, NEG_FALSE_URGENCY V-06 Basket sneaking A counter-offer MUST NOT add lines or charges the buyer did not assert, unless they are put to the buyer as Assert and the buyer agrees block, NEG_BASKET_SNEAK V-07 Personalised pricing pricing_basis declared. If personalised, the factors are listed. Device, OS and other irrelevant attributes are prohibited. block, NEG_PERSONALISED_PRICING V-08 Collusion screen No seller sees another seller's quote or bid. Third-party pricing AI is declared. Network screens look for identical and near-identical bids and bid rotation. flag, NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN (details) V-09 Shill bidding No bids by the seller or its affiliates; neutral auctioneer block, NEG_SHILL_BID (details) V-10 Agent disclosure offeror_kind on every message block V-11 Prompt-injection isolation Counterparty free text is untrusted data. Only structured messages reach the guard. flag, NEG_INJECTION_SUSPECTED V-12 Cash and high-value gates A cash tranche of ₹2 lakh or more is refused (Income-tax Act, 1961 s.269ST; Income-tax Act, 2025 equivalent: s.186 per secondary sources, not verified as of 17-10-2026). PAN is required for jewellery above the statutory threshold. A RERA token or booking amount above 10% needs a linked_agreement_ref. High-value categories always need a human-present commitment. block, NEG_CASH_LIMIT, NEG_RERA_TOKEN_CAP V-13 Credit disclosure EMI, BNPL and credit-funded options carry the lender, APR, KFS reference, and no_cost: false when interest is above zero block, NEG_CREDIT_DISCLOSURE_MISSING, NEG_EMI_NO_COST_FALSE V-14 Document gates IRN for B2B invoices from sellers whose aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year since 2017-18; e-way bill before dispatch above ₹50,000; the 30-day IRN reporting flag where AATO is ₹10 crore or more block at dispatch, NEG_EINVOICE_IRN_MISSING, NEG_EWB_MISSING

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text:
After acceptance, the seller's BPP-signed on_init (and later confirm / on_confirm) MUST carry exactly the accepted terms, apart from payment-rail endpoints. The receiving gateway MUST check this from content, not from claims:

  1. Recompute the term-sheet hash from the term sheet carried in on_init and compare it with the hash of the accepted offer's term sheet. A claimed hash is checked too, but a matching claim is never sufficient.
  2. Compare every line of the bound term sheet with the accepted one on (item_id, unit, quantity, unit_price, currency).
  3. Compare every line item of the BPP-signed quote with the accepted lines on (item, quantity, unit_price, line total).
  4. Compare the quote total with the accepted all_in_total.

A difference in any one of these is drift, even when the totals still match: a seller that halves the quantity and doubles the unit price, or switches kg for quintal, has drifted.

Accepted offer On drift Firm The accepted firm offer is a contract, so drift is a breach, not a return to negotiation. The session moves to BREACH_FLAGGED with message NEG_TERMS_DRIFT (requires_buyer_review). The gateway raises an IGM 2.0 issue with the agent as an AI_AGENT actor (Proposed, Q-11) and the evidence (accepted hash, claimed and recomputed hashes, the list of differences, both totals). The buyer MAY cancel without penalty (cancelled_no_penalty). A post-acceptance "out of stock" on a firm offer is also a breach. Whether a breach carries a network penalty is open (Q-22). Non-firm (purchase offer) The differing on_init is the seller's counter-offer. The accepted offer becomes SUPERSEDED, the session returns to NEGOTIATING, and the buyer gets seller_counter_at_init (requires_buyer_input).

The gateway records bound_term_sheet_hash as the hash it computed from the bound content, never the hash the seller claimed.

docs.title: Signed seller acceptance and clock skew
docs.text:
Transcript positions decide contract formation. Times are recorded, and never decide it.

A rule that compared timestamps stamped by the offeree itself would leave the offeree a free option inside the 5-second band: it could sign an acceptance, hold it, watch the market, and send it late. BACP therefore decides a crossing only on a signed admission by the party that loses by it, read inside that party's own chain, so no comparison of two parties' clocks decides anything.

  • One chain per participant. Each participant keeps one linearisable hash chain per negotiation_id, like the exposure store. A gateway that runs as several instances MUST share a linearisable chain. Two receipts at one log_seq that name different entries are equivocation: evidence_unverifiable, treated as contested and reported to NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN.
  • Positions in the signed bytes. A sender logs a firm message and takes its position before it dispatches it. The message carries sender_log_seq (its position in the sender's own chain) and sender_log_prev (the hash of the entry before it) inside its signed bytes. Genesis. At position 1 of either chain, sender_log_prev and the receipt's prev_entry_hash are the genesis hash, sha-256 of the negotiation_id as UTF-8 bytes, written sha-256:<base64url>; this mirrors the InstructionLog genesis. Both chains use the same value, so a verifier recomputes it from the negotiation_id alone.
  • The receipt. Every receiver returns, in the synchronous response to the exchange, a CounterSignature whose payload is a CounterSignaturePayload: {msg_hash, negotiation_id, received_at, log_seq, log_entry_hash, prev_entry_hash}, every field REQUIRED. prev_entry_hash lets a fork be proved from two receipts alone. log_entry_hash changes from MAY to REQUIRED.
counter-signature-payload.json
{
  "msg_hash": "sha-256:udhTqGUfMOyYjXn08oDUyndhNq27sfBt7HeM4FPXa1c",
  "negotiation_id": "neg_SAREE7Q2W9",
  "received_at": "2026-10-13T11:05:11+05:30",
  "log_seq": 42,
  "log_entry_hash": "sha-256:cWq_rdLVyoidbmszti6flYZ196mpjNjLChZH4gkdQcI",
  "prev_entry_hash": "sha-256:vq4x2opsK4KIM-scKiTGRWd4Fzxs-GBx7lO8Glgm_U4"
}
Invalid: receipt without log_seq (counter-signature-payload.no-log-seq.invalid.json) 
{
  "msg_hash": "sha-256:lJRtoHUIQckYFk7BASGC6sKjJ-XUVuGwnPAf-YDVEAs",
  "negotiation_id": "neg_SAREE7Q2W9",
  "received_at": "2026-10-13T11:05:11+05:30",
  "log_entry_hash": "sha-256:puM6b3R7BrQTlpr9p56R-_uigPyPOQaTc6_KCeiDQRU",
  "prev_entry_hash": "sha-256:vq4x2opsK4KIM-scKiTGRWd4Fzxs-GBx7lO8Glgm_U4"
}

  • The negotiation chain and log_entry_hash. The chain of a participant for one negotiation_id is its own chain. It is not the InstructionLog of any session: the InstructionLog is keyed on a session_id and numbers seq from 0, whereas this chain is keyed on the negotiation_id and numbers log_seq from 1. It holds, in the order in which the participant logged them, both the firm messages that it sent and the messages that it received. Its genesis hash is the sha-256 of the negotiation_id as UTF-8 bytes. An entry is the JSON object {msg_hash, negotiation_id, received_at, log_seq, prev_entry_hash} for a message that the participant received (the CounterSignaturePayload without log_entry_hash), and {msg_hash, negotiation_id, dispatched_at, log_seq, prev_entry_hash} for a message that it sent, with the message's own dispatched_at. prev_entry_hash is the log_entry_hash of the entry at log_seq − 1, and the genesis hash at log_seq 1. log_entry_hash is sha-256: followed by the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) form of the entry, those five members and nothing else, so that it covers neither itself nor any signature.

    Worked example, the receipt of offer.accept-genesis.json at position 1 of the receiver's chain for neg_SAREE7Q2W9. The JCS form of the entry is {"log_seq":1,"msg_hash":"sha-256:udhTqGUfMOyYjXn08oDUyndhNq27sfBt7HeM4FPXa1c","negotiation_id":"neg_SAREE7Q2W9","prev_entry_hash":"sha-256:pviiX-jSkdM0fNAvXPzGSPN94ZCAIVDowcD6eqGUGlM","received_at":"2026-10-13T11:05:11+05:30"} and its sha-256 is sha-256:1qt_DRfJWFUxIc0WGpwXSRXacc5T0wMnTeTNpy-toHk, the log_entry_hash of counter-signature-payload.genesis.json. The msg_hash there is the sha-256 over the JCS form of offer.accept-genesis.json without signatures, counter_signature and received_at. scripts/validate.py recomputes both. - When a receipt counts as an order proof. A receipt counts only if it (i) is a CounterSignature by the counterparty participant's registry key, which verifies as a JWS on its own, (ii) comes in the synchronous response of the same exchange (a REST response, an MCP JSON-RPC result, a blocking A2A response, or on Beckn a bacp.receipt TagGroup in the Ack; see Beckn / ONDC Binding), and (iii) arrives within 5 seconds of the sender's dispatch, measured on the sender's own monotonic clock. The 5 seconds reuse the freshness bound below and are not a new limit. Because it reads one clock, this passes the clock-invariance property in Conformance. A receipt that is slower, missing or unverifiable is recorded but does not prove order, and a crossing that depends on it is contested. - Idempotent re-delivery. A receiver that has already countersigned a msg_hash MUST return the byte-identical CounterSignature, with the same log_seq, and MUST NOT re-run the freshness or expiry checks on that message. A different CounterSignature for the same msg_hash is equivocation. An honest retry (for example a Beckn confirm re-sent with the same message_id) therefore needs no looser freshness. - Freshness only. For every inbound message, |received_at − dispatched_at| MUST be at most 5 seconds, or the message is refused with NEG_CLOCK_SKEW (422) and is not processed. This is a freshness bound and a BACP choice; no Indian instrument gives a tolerance. It never decides order. A refused message is not re-signed and retried, because a new signature is a new message. - dispatched_at. It MUST equal the created parameter of the sender's RFC 9421 signature exactly. RFC 9421 created is an integer with no sub-second precision, so dispatched_at carries no fraction (offer.dispatched-at-fraction.invalid.json fails the schema). Retries re-send identical bytes, so msg_hash removes duplicates. Under the committed-order rule dispatched_at is evidence only.

Invalid: dispatched_at with a fraction (offer.dispatched-at-fraction.invalid.json)

      "value": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJiYWNwIjoidjEifQ.c2lnbmF0dXJl"
    }

}
  • Instants, not strings. Every comparison of times is a comparison of instants: …T10:00:05+05:30 equals …T04:30:05Z, and any rewrite between the two happens outside signed bytes.
  • Monotonic received_at. A participant records the clock reading it truly saw. A decrease of received_at along a chain MUST carry clock_step_observed on the transcript entry. A verifier treats an unflagged decrease as evidence_unverifiable. Order is by log_seq only, so a flag costs nothing.
  • Clock traceability. Participants MUST keep clocks traceable to NIC or NPL time sources (CERT-In Directions of 28-04-2022, direction (i)) and, from the commencement of the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 761(E), r.6(4)-(5) and r.8(4)), to IST from an authorised source. As of 18-10-2026 those Rules are notified and not in force; they commence 180 days after publication, which is about 24-02-2027 (the exact day is not verified). This is a duty on each clock and never an ordering input.
  • IST in BACP-owned times. BACP-owned wall-clock values in negotiation messages and evidence (received_at, expires_at, dispatched_at as rendered, transcript entries) SHOULD carry the offset +05:30. Beckn context.timestamp follows ONDC and keeps Z. Every time shown or told to a person on the Trusted Surface is in IST, in the person's language (Render input). Whether Rule 7 of those Rules reaches machine timestamps is open (Q-84).
  • A seller's acceptance of a buyer offer counts only if the buyer gateway countersigned it, and is subject to the same expiry rules below.

docs.title: Contested crossings
docs.text:
Write W for the offeror's withdraw and A for the offeree's accept. Each comparison sits inside one party's own chain.

Outcome Condition Code Who proved it Withdraw wins The offeree's CounterSignature for W has log_seq below A's sender_log_seq (the offeree logged W before it dispatched A) accept_void_withdrawn (seller acceptor: seller_accept_void) The offeree, the loser Accept wins The offeror's CounterSignature for A has log_seq below W's sender_log_seq (the offeror received A before it sent W) withdraw_lost_crossing The offeror, the loser Contested Neither holds (each sent before it received), or a needed receipt is missing, late or unverifiable crossing_contested Nobody; humans decide Impossible Both hold evidence_unverifiable, treated as contested and reported to NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN Equivocation

Why contested is the only rule that does not reward holding. A genuine crossing (A sent at position 5, W sent at position 10 a moment before A arrives) produces the same four integers as an acceptance that the offeree signed and logged, did not send, and sent later after seeing W: no signed artefact tells them apart. Any rule that decides the genuine case for one side therefore also rewards the hold. A contested outcome gives the holder a review and never a contract.

Residual risk, disclosed. An offeror that holds the CounterSignature for A, sends W, and only then logs A turns a contract it owed into a contested review. The payoff is "no deal, no breach", the window is the 5-second receipt bound, and it cannot be prevented without a third-party sequencer. Every contested record carries late_receipt_party, and gateways report per-participant contested counts to the collusion screen. BACP sets no threshold.

What a contested crossing does. BACP evidence does not settle formation; neither gateway proceeds; the protocol records no breach event. BACP does not say "no contract", because a protocol term under the Information Technology Act, 2000, s.13 can fix when a record is despatched and received but cannot declare that no contract exists; whether one formed is a question of fact under ICA ss.4-5.

  • Each side's session goes to ESCALATED with reason crossing_contested, and both principals are asked on their own surfaces. The seller gateway MUST raise the case to its principal and MUST NOT auto-confirm (the fail-safe of Indian Contract Act timing is two-sided).
  • Both confirm → AGREED, and the deal proceeds.
  • Neither confirms (declined or silent) by the earlier of the offer's expires_at and the end of the step-up link → CANCELLED, reason crossing_unconfirmed. No breach event, no protocol-computed charge, and the exposure reservation is released once (Principle 6; TS-2, "expiry means decline").
  • One confirms, the other declines or is silent → CANCELLED, reason formation_disputed, carrying the grievance_contact of both sides. No breach event and no protocol-computed charge. Whether a contract formed is for ODR or the courts. Silence is a decline, so a deal never proceeds on one confirmation.
  • The message is crossing_contested with resolution requires_buyer_review on a buyer-side gateway and requires_seller_review on a seller-side gateway (Errors). The agent MUST stop and MUST NOT resend.
  • On Beckn a message is ordered only when its Ack carries a verifying receipt, so every crossing that depends on an unreceipted Beckn message is contested. Non-crossing deals are unaffected.

docs.title: Expiry and the acceptor's margin
docs.text:
expires_at is a receipt deadline at the offeror, stated in the protocol terms and in the offer semantics. An accept received after expires_at returns NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED. Two guards stop an offeror from escaping its own offer at the expiry edge:

  • Acceptor's margin. The acceptor's gateway MUST NOT dispatch an accept when expires_at − now is under 5 seconds on its own clock. It refuses locally with NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED and sends nothing, and the principal sees offer_expired_during_approval. An honest acceptor loses the last 5 seconds of each offer's validity. This margin is the acceptor's own, not an extra check at the offeror.
  • Dispatch before expiry. An accept that is refused as expired, whose dispatched_at is not after expires_at, and which passed freshness, is crossing_contested, not expired. A self-asserted time can move this case only to contested, never to bound. An accept received with dispatched_at after expires_at is NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED.

Whether a court reads an acceptance dispatched before expires_at but received after it as in time (ICA s.4, s.6(2)) is open (Q-52).

docs.title: Per-principal exposure
docs.text:
An agent that sends firm counter-offers to several sellers at once could commit the principal several times over. The guard therefore counts exposure (step N-7):

  • Exposure is the sum of all_in_total over the principal's outstanding firm counter-offers, ACCEPT_PENDING acceptances, AGREED-but-unpaid deals and lodged standing accepts (each at max_price × qty), across all of that principal's negotiation mandates and concurrent negotiations, including every session under the same rfq_parent_id, plus the message being guarded.
  • Exposure MUST be at most total_max and at most every remaining checkout-mandate budget period, whatever the payment handler. A credit-ledger deal counts against the budgets and against credit_ledger.max_outstanding only when a gateway complete books it (Q-46, settled).
  • Over the limit, the verdict is needs_escalation with NEG_EXPOSURE_EXCEEDED.
  • Atomicity. Computing exposure and emitting the firm message it guards MUST run as one atomic, linearisable operation keyed on the principal. Each outstanding commitment holds an exposure reservation. A standing accept's reservation is keyed on its standing_accept_id (it has no offer_hash) and is released when its auction closes or the standing accept is used or withdrawn. Any other reservation is released when its offer reaches REJECTED, EXPIRED, WITHDRAWN, SUPERSEDED, TERMINATED or LAPSED_CONDITION, or ACCEPT_REVOKED on the proposer's countersigned accept_revoke_honoured, and converted when the deal is paid. Release is idempotent: it is keyed on the offer's offer_hash (a standing accept's, on its standing_accept_id) and happens at most once per reservation, however often the event that releases it is delivered or replayed. While the outcome of an accept_revoke is contested (the proposer has not countersigned an outcome), the reservation is held. If the outcome is still contested when the offer's expires_at passes, the gateway surfaces it to the principal (requires_buyer_review) and the reservation stays counted. A gateway that runs as several instances MUST share a linearisable exposure store. Exposure across two different gateways serving one principal is not counted: each open mandate belongs to one gateway (agent.bap_id), and a move to another gateway is a successor root (Q-36, settled).
  • The session view reports only amounts (exposure.principal_outstanding_firm, counted_against[]), never the bound.

docs.title: Binding to checkout
docs.text:
Negotiation hands over to checkout through a chain of hashes. BACP does not treat the accepted offer as the checkout:

  1. The buyer accepts offer_hash. The accept carries the within_bounds attestation.
  2. The seller's BPP-signed on_init echoes the identical term sheet, and the gateway's recomputed hash becomes bound_term_sheet_hash. The session is BOUND.
  3. The checkout session opens in ready_for_complete with the BPP-signed quote. Its checkout_hash is the hash of that signed quote.
  4. The closed checkout and payment mandates bind to checkout_hash, as in Sessions and Checkout.

checkout_hash MUST NOT be asserted to equal offer_hash or bound_term_sheet_hash: they are hashes of different objects (the quote, the offer and the term sheet).

The within_bounds attestation (offer.json#/$defs/BoundAttestation) is {type: bacp.neg.bound_attestation, mandate_ref, offer_hash, result: true, iss, iat, signature}, issued by the buyer's credential provider (the Mandate Manager). Before issuing it, the credential provider MUST re-verify the deal against the open checkout mandate and the negotiation mandate. The seller BPP MUST verify only this attestation against the issuer's registry key. If the credential provider refuses, the acceptance is not sent and the agent gets NEG_ATTESTATION_REFUSED. Whether a zero-knowledge range proof should replace the attestation is open (Q-24).

On Beckn, the acceptance is an init carrying bacp.neg.accept, BOUND is the on_init echo, the PO is confirm referencing offer_hash, and PO acceptance is on_confirm (CONTRACTED). The PO MUST NOT alter accepted terms. See Beckn / ONDC Binding.

docs.title: Indian Contract Act timing
docs.text:
Legal basis pending review

The statutory rules cited below are taken from the text of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, ss.2 and 4–7. The timing rules in this section are normative as protocol terms that participants agree to, in the sense of the Information Technology Act, 2000, s.13, and every firm message names them through protocol_terms. Whether courts would treat them, and the crossing rule, which is a BACP design choice, as the time of dispatch and receipt is open (Q-52). Fail-safe default until Q-52 is settled: when a deal's formation is decided by the crossing rule, neither gateway proceeds to init, complete or confirm on it automatically. The buyer gateway escalates to the buyer principal on the Trusted Surface (requires_buyer_review), the seller gateway escalates to the seller principal (requires_seller_review) and MUST NOT auto-confirm, and each proceeds only on its principal's confirmation (Contested crossings). The crossing outcome is still recorded in the transcript.

Rule Statute BACP behaviour Proposal (s.2(a), (b)) A person who signifies willingness to do or abstain from something, "with a view to obtaining the assent of that other", makes a proposal. A proposal, when accepted, becomes a promise. firm: true is a proposal. firm: false is an invitation to treat. That term is not in the Act; it comes from case law. Accepting a non-firm offer has legal_effect: purchase_offer: it is the buyer's proposal, and the seller's echoing on_init or on_confirm is the acceptance. Communication (s.4) A proposal is communicated "when it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made". An acceptance is complete against the proposer "when it is put in a course of transmission to him, so as to be out of the power of the acceptor", and against the acceptor "when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer". A proposal is communicated when the offeree's CounterSignature exists. Acceptance is complete against the proposer on dispatch (dispatched_at), and against the acceptor on receipt (received_at). Communication of a revocation (s.4) The communication of a revocation is complete "as against the person who makes it, when it is put into a course of transmission to the person to whom it is made, so as to be out of the power of the person who makes it", and "as against the person to whom it is made, when it comes to his knowledge". A withdraw or an accept_revoke is dispatched at its dispatched_at and received at the receiver's received_at. Revocation of a proposal (ss.5, 6(1)) A proposal "may be revoked at any time before the communication of its acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards". A proposal is revoked "by the communication of notice of revocation by the proposer to the other party". The offeror may withdraw only until the offeree dispatches an acceptance. A withdraw takes effect on receipt. Revocation of an acceptance (s.5) "An acceptance may be revoked at any time before the communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards." Governed by the offer's acceptance_revocation term. See Acceptance revocation. Proposal kept open (s.5, Explanation, Uttar Pradesh) Inserted by the Uttar Pradesh Act 57 of 1976: "Where an invitation to a proposal contains a condition that any proposal made in response to such invitation shall be kept open for a specified time and a proposal is thereupon made accepting such condition, such proposal may not be revoked within such time." BACP has no rule for it and does not refuse a withdraw on that ground. Whether it binds a quotation made in response to an RFQ is open (Q-19). Crossing (BACP rule) The Act gives no tie-break. When a withdraw and an accept cross, the outcome comes from the four cases of Contested crossings: the withdrawal wins on the offeree's own receipt of it, the acceptance wins on the offeror's own receipt of it, and otherwise the crossing is contested. No timestamp decides it, and there is no tie rule. A losing withdrawal is a breach event and is reported (withdraw_lost_crossing). A losing acceptance is void (accept_void_withdrawn, seller_accept_void). A contested crossing records no breach event. Lapse (s.6(2), (3), (4)) A proposal is revoked "by the lapse of the time prescribed in such proposal for its acceptance", "by the failure of the acceptor to fulfil a condition precedent to acceptance", and "by the death or insanity of the proposer, if the fact of his death or insanity comes to the knowledge of the acceptor before acceptance". An offer lapses at expires_at, which is a receipt deadline at the offeror (Expiry), and silence leads to EXPIRED. A counter-offer that cites an expired offer is refused with NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED. Either party MAY send a fresh offer while rounds and the deadline remain. If a conditions_precedent[] entry fails (e.g. lc_opened), the offer becomes LAPSED_CONDITION. Treating every condition precedent as one of the kind s.6(3) describes is a BACP choice. BACP has no message for the case of s.6(4). Absolute acceptance (s.7(1)) The acceptance must "be absolute and unqualified". An acceptance mirrors offer_hash and carries no terms. A changed term is a counter-offer. That a counter-offer rejects the prior offer comes from case law, not from the text of s.7. Manner of acceptance (s.7(2)) If an acceptance is not made in the prescribed manner, the proposer "may, within a reasonable time after the acceptance is communicated to him, insist" on that manner, "but if he fails to do so, he accepts the acceptance". Every offer prescribes acceptance_manner: bacp.neg.accept. Any other form is non-conforming and is refused promptly with NEG_ACCEPT_NONCONFORMING, so that the proposer insists on the prescribed manner within a reasonable time.

The Information Technology Act, 2000, s.13 fixes when an electronic record is despatched and received "save as otherwise agreed" between originator and addressee. The protocol terms that every firm message names (protocol_terms{version, hash}) are such an agreed rule. They state the committed-order rule, the receipt window, the contested outcome, that expires_at is a receipt deadline, and the stipulation of s.12(2) that unless an acknowledgement has been received the electronic record is deemed never to have been sent. An individual's agreement is shown on what the person sees: the mandate and the ConsentReceipt cite the terms. Whether a hash an agent sends is the principal's agreement for s.13 (s.11 attribution), and whether a consumer's approval citing the terms is "otherwise agreed", are open (Q-19).

The protocol-terms text and its hash. The protocol-terms text of a version is the file protocol-terms/<version>.txt published with that version (protocol-terms/2026-10-18.txt for this one), UTF-8 with LF line ends and no byte order mark. hash is sha-256: followed by the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the exact bytes of that file, with no canonicalisation. A gateway computes it from the published file and never from its own copy of the wording, and a receiver refuses a firm message whose hash differs with capabilities_incompatible. scripts/validate.py checks that every example carries the digest of the file of its version.

Invalid: protocol_terms.hash that is not the digest of the file (offer.protocol-terms-hash-stale.invalid.json)

docs.title: Acceptance revocation
docs.text:
Legal basis pending review

Whether an offer, an earlier agreement between the parties or a protocol term can validly exclude the acceptor's right under s.5 is open (Q-19). BACP permits waived only under the conditions below. Showing the term to a principal does not make the exclusion valid.

The Indian Contract Act, 1872, s.5 says: "An acceptance may be revoked at any time before the communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards." Under s.4 that communication is complete as against the acceptor "when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer". Neither section says "unless otherwise agreed". The Information Technology Act, 2000, s.10A covers "the revocation of proposals and acceptances" expressed in electronic form. Section 13 fixes only when an electronic record is despatched and received, "save as otherwise agreed"; it does not mention knowledge or revocation. BACP takes the proposer's receipt time (received_at) as the time of that knowledge. Whether s.13 receipt is s.4 knowledge is open (Q-19, Q-52).

Here "acceptance" means acceptance of a proposal (ICA ss.4–5), not acceptance of goods under MSMED s.15.

The term. Every firm offer MUST carry acceptance_revocation. There is no default, and a gateway MUST NOT insert or normalise the value before hashing, so the term is always inside the signed bytes and offer_hash. A firm offer without it is refused with 400 NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID and never becomes LIVE.

  • allowed_until_receipt. The acceptor may revoke an acceptance until the proposer receives it. In this version no receiver honours this value: every receiver refuses it, on every binding and in every trade profile (table below). The value stays in the schemas so that a later version can lift the refusal without a schema change; the rules that would then apply are the sunset text.
  • waived. The offer excludes that right. It MUST carry waiver_basis: the signed contract between the parties (doc_type: contract) or the buyer's own RFQ (doc_type: rfq, see Award), with its hash. Inside offer_hash this is a commitment to the document, not proof of it. The acceptor's gateway MUST NOT accept a waived offer without the principal unless it holds the document that hashes to waiver_basis.hash; otherwise it escalates to the principal (requires_buyer_review). "Holds" means all three of: the gateway obtained the document from its own principal before the offer arrived; the document names the offer's counterparty, by its np_id or its GSTIN; and the principal marked the document as a waiver basis. If any of the three is missing, the gateway escalates to the principal (requires_buyer_review). A document fetched from waiver_basis.uri, taken from the offer, or supplied by the counterparty in any other way does not count.

Consumer sessions. The value rules depend on the session's trade profile (context.bacp.profile, see Trade Profiles). A consumer profile is one that the profile table marks "waiver permitted: no". The profile is fixed when the session opens; a later message of the session that declares another profile is refused with capabilities_incompatible and changes nothing. A session is a consumer session, whatever profile it declares, if it declares no profile, if the buyer side's context.bacp.acting_for.kind is individual, or if the buyer side sends no acting_for. The buyer side declares the profile and acting_for at session open in a buyer-signed message, and the buyer gateway fills them from the mandate; a seller refuses a profile that misdescribes the trade as set out in Declaring a profile.

Where each value is permitted. The rules also depend on the binding that carries the offer between the parties. In this version:

Leg Session allowed_until_receipt waived with waiver_basis waived without waiver_basis REST, MCP or A2A Business Refused, capabilities_incompatible Permitted. The acceptor's gateway accepts without the principal only if it holds the hashed document as a waiver basis naming the counterparty. Refused, NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID REST, MCP or A2A Consumer Refused, capabilities_incompatible Refused, capabilities_incompatible Refused, NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID Beckn / ONDC Business Refused, capabilities_incompatible Permitted, with the same hash rule Accepted only by a human shown the consequence sentence Beckn / ONDC Consumer Refused, capabilities_incompatible Accepted only by a human shown the consequence sentence, as in the next column Accepted only by a human shown the consequence sentence: the buyer through a Trusted Surface step-up, never autonomously (requires_buyer_review); a human seller in the BPP app
  • Refused means that the receiving gateway answers the offer with the code shown (capabilities_incompatible with param $.acceptance_revocation). The offer never becomes LIVE, and the negotiation state does not change. The gateway also refuses its own principal's draft with the same value and code (403), and sends nothing.
  • No firm offer in a consumer session off Beckn. In a consumer session on REST, MCP or A2A no value is permitted in this version. A seller there makes only non-firm offers (firm: false), and the buyer's acceptance of one is a purchase offer (legal_effect: purchase_offer, Acceptance).
  • The Beckn rows are a network limit. No Beckn carrier exists for accept_revoke in this version (Beckn / ONDC Binding).
  • waived without a basis on Beckn. Such an offer fails the schema. On a Beckn leg only, the receiving gateway excuses exactly one schema error: the missing waiver_basis of a firm offer with acceptance_revocation: waived. It refuses an offer with any other schema error, including one that also lacks waiver_basis, with NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID. It records an offer whose only error is the missing basis, and no agent may accept it. In a consumer session on Beckn it treats a waived offer that carries a basis in the same way.
  • Broadcast RFQ. For a broadcast RFQ the waiver basis is the RFQ itself: waiver_basis{doc_type: rfq, hash} carries the hash of the published RFQ, which the seller's gateway fills, replacing "the document names the counterparty" for that case. Rfq.acceptance_revocation_required: waived is for business sessions only and is refused in consumer sessions. An RFQ that an agent creates with it needs a confirm step-up with reason rfq_prescribes_waiver, because it waives the principal's own s.5 right (Award).
  • Human acceptance on Beckn. The buyer gateway escalates such an offer to the principal with a confirm step-up (reason constraint_unresolved) whose ts_render carries acceptance_revocation and offer_hash, and sends the acceptance only after a negotiation.step_up.approved event whose presentation.offer_hash is that offer's (Step-up to the Trusted Surface). On the seller side only a human may accept it, in the BPP app, after the app shows the consequence sentence.
  • Never "cannot cancel". Neither value restricts cancellation, and a value MUST NOT be rendered or relied on as a restriction on cancellation. Cancelling after CONTRACTED follows the agreed cancellation.terms only (Negotiation state). The Trusted Surface shows the value only as its fixed consequence sentence, followed by the cancellation terms (Render input).

accept_revoke in this version. Because no offer with allowed_until_receipt is live, the proposer countersigns, logs and refuses every accept_revoke with accept_revoke_not_allowed. Nothing else changes, and the acceptance stands. The message keeps its schema: accept_msg_hash (the msg_hash of the acceptance) and offer_hash (the offer it names) are REQUIRED.

Bids. accept_revoke never governs bid_retract. A bidder's retraction follows the auction's retraction rules whatever the bid's acceptance_revocation value. An award is an acceptance; a revoked award is handled under Award and Who may run and award.

accept_revoke and withdraw are always sent under the signature tag bacp-negotiate, and an accept_revoke of an acceptance that the principal approved on the Trusted Surface needs hp_proof (Operations).

docs.title: Sunset text for allowed_until_receipt
docs.text:
Proposed (sunset)

The rules in this subsection are not in force in this version. They state when a later version may lift the refusal of allowed_until_receipt and how the value is then honoured. The conformance cases that need a live offer with allowed_until_receipt are published as data in the Proposed (sunset) block.

Conditions for lifting the refusal. A later version lifts the refusal on a binding only when all of these hold:

  • (a) The revoke names its acceptance and offer. accept_revoke carries accept_msg_hash and offer_hash, and a revoke whose dispatched_at is earlier than the dispatched_at of the acceptance it names is void. (Specified in this version.)
  • (b) The receiver commits to receipt order before it sees the next message. In force in this version for every firm negotiation message (Signed seller acceptance and clock skew). The receiver returns its CounterSignature, carrying log_entry_hash and log_seq, in the synchronous response to each negotiation message, before it appends any later message of that negotiation to its transcript. The outcome of an accept_revoke is a separate message. A CounterSignature that reaches the sender more than 5 seconds after the sender's dispatch, on the sender's own monotonic clock, is recorded but does not count as an order proof. A verifier that holds a CounterSignature naming transcript position n for one message and a transcript with a different message at n reports evidence_unverifiable.
  • (c) The matched-pair rule below is implemented, with the hold kept in the transcript.
  • (d) Exposure release on a countersigned accept_revoke_honoured is idempotent (Per-principal exposure). (Specified in this version.)
  • (e) Beckn. A Beckn carrier for accept_revoke exists, or Beckn legs keep refusing the value (Q-22).
  • (f) Tested. The 16 sunset-block cases (T3-08 to T3-37) pass in a harness that loads the conformance YAML. Not met as of 18-10-2026: no implementation passes them yet. It can be met only after an implementation provides the committed-order rule, synchronous receipts, accept_revoke and the matched pair. Even then (e) stays open until a Beckn carrier exists.

Revocation under allowed_until_receipt (sunset). Call the acceptance A and the revocation R.

  1. R carries accept_msg_hash (the msg_hash of A) and offer_hash (the offer A names). R's dispatched_at MUST NOT be earlier than A's dispatched_at; otherwise R is void.
  2. The proposer orders the two by its transcript (receipt order is chain order), and commits to that order under condition (b): its CounterSignature on each message, with log_entry_hash, is in the synchronous response to that message.
  3. If R is received first, the proposer appends R to the negotiation's transcript on receipt and holds it, keyed on accept_msg_hash, until the offer's expires_at, ordered by chain. Every instance of the proposer that handles A reads the transcript for a held R. If A (same msg_hash and offer_hash) arrives within the hold, the pair matches: the offer moves LIVE → ACCEPT_REVOKED, the negotiation stays in or returns to NEGOTIATING, and the outcome is accept_revoke_honoured. If A does not arrive, R is discarded at the end of the hold and the discard is logged. Discarding an earlier revocation sooner would be narrower than ICA s.5 and its Illustration, so the hold runs to expires_at, ordered by chain, and is not a separate revocation window.
  4. If A is received first, the acceptance stands (AGREED), and the outcome is accept_revoke_after_receipt.
  5. The proposer countersigns and logs every R, whatever the outcome, and sends the outcome code as a separate message. A receipt of A or R without log_entry_hash is not recorded (evidence_unverifiable), and the negotiation does not move to AGREED on it.
  6. The acceptor's offer moves ACCEPTED → ACCEPT_REVOKED, and its negotiation from ACCEPT_PENDING to NEGOTIATING, only on the proposer's countersigned accept_revoke_honoured. Until then the outcome is contested, and the exposure reservation is held.

docs.title: Mandate revocation
docs.text: When the negotiation mandate is revoked, the gateway MUST send withdraw (reason mandate_revoked) for every live firm offer of that principal, within the 60-second revocation target set in Mandates and Consent, and end open sessions TERMINATED. An acceptance that crosses one of these withdrawals follows the crossing rule. If the counterparty accepted earlier, the deal stands, and the principal is told with agreed_by_counterparty (requires_buyer_review).

docs.title: Legal effect and evidence
docs.text:
• An accepted firm offer is an agreement on terms: a contract, subject to its conditions_precedent. A non-firm offer binds no one until the seller accepts the buyer's purchase offer.
  • Every firm message names the protocol_terms that govern it, and the session names them at open. A mismatch between the two sides is capabilities_incompatible; a firm message with none is NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID.

  • Every negotiation produces an append-only, hash-chained transcript. Every message, CounterSignature, guard verdict (constraint IDs only), validator flag, step-up event and award is appended to the instruction log under the stages negotiation and guard, and NegotiationSession.transcript[] holds each entry's msg_hash and log_entry_hash. Tampering with any entry breaks chain verification. See Evidence and Instruction Log.
  • Advisory chat and model rationale are logged with binding: false and appear in the transcript only as advisory.text_hash.
  • The transcript is encrypted to the parties plus a regulator escrow key. Who governs the escrow key is open (Q-23).
  • The evidence bundle for a transaction adds the transcript, the accepted offer, the within_bounds attestation and the bound on_init. These let a grievance officer or ODR provider verify what was offered and what was agreed without seeing the reservation price.
  • Retention: at least the Consumer Protection Act limitation period, proposed as 2 years for B2C, and longer for B2B and public procurement (kept for CAG/CVC review). The period is open (Q-56).

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Each operation is defined once and bound to REST, MCP and A2A (see REST and MCP and A2A).

REST MCP tool Signature tag POST /negotiations bacp_negotiation_open bacp-browse GET /negotiations/{id} bacp_negotiation_get bacp-browse POST /negotiations/{id}/offers (offer, counter_offer, reject, withdraw, terminate, request_extension, accept_revoke) bacp_offer_send bacp-negotiate for firm messages, withdraw and accept_revoke; otherwise bacp-browse POST /negotiations/{id}/accept bacp_offer_accept bacp-negotiate POST /rfqs, GET /rfqs/{id}, POST /rfqs/{id}/award bacp_rfq_create, bacp_rfq_get, bacp_rfq_award bacp-negotiate (award) POST /auctions, GET /auctions/{id}, POST /auctions/{id}/bids, POST /auctions/{id}/standing-accepts, POST /auctions/{id}/standing-accepts/{standing_accept_id}/withdraw, POST /auctions/{id}/award bacp_auction_create, bacp_auction_get, bacp_auction_bid, bacp_standing_accept_lodge, bacp_standing_accept_withdraw, bacp_auction_award bacp-negotiate
  • Tag rule. A withdraw or an accept_revoke changes whether a contract exists, so it is always signed under bacp-negotiate, whether or not the offer it concerns is firm. One signed under any other tag is refused with 401 signature_invalid (Signature tags).
  • Decline. There is no agent-callable decline of an AGREED or BOUND deal. The principal declines by the Trusted Surface event negotiation.agreed.declined (Decline), and withdraws a purchase offer by negotiation.purchase_offer.withdrawn or by the agent's withdraw with accept_msg_hash.
  • Tool use. The agent reads offers[].state and the message crossing_contested, and never resends a message after a crossing. On NEG_CLOCK_SKEW it does not re-sign and retry. On crossing_contested it stops, and the principal decides. After a refusal to accept because the state is ESCALATED, it calls accept again with step_up.step_up_id once the state leaves ESCALATED; the id goes to the agent's gateway only.
  • Revoking an approved acceptance. If the principal approved the acceptance on the Trusted Surface, an accept_revoke of it MUST carry hp_proof (Presence proof); without one it is refused with 403 presence_not_proven and nothing is sent. No operation in this version lets an agent obtain a step-up that names an accept_revoke, so such a revoke is refused.

MCP results return the NegotiationSession in structuredContent. A2A 1.0 task states map as: TASK_STATE_WORKING (waiting on the counterparty), TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED (a counter-offer to answer), TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED (ESCALATED, including the ask confirmation and a contested crossing), TASK_STATE_COMPLETED (CONTRACTED), TASK_STATE_CANCELED or TASK_STATE_FAILED (REJECTED, TERMINATED, CANCELLED). Versions of A2A before 1.0 use the lowercase names working, input-required, auth-required, completed, canceled and failed. These are A2A's own values and are used verbatim; BACP's own spelling is "cancelled", so A2A TASK_STATE_CANCELED (or canceled) maps to the BACP negotiation state CANCELLED and to the checkout session status cancelled. Agent-to-agent negotiation over A2A without a network participant's signature can produce only firm: false offers.

docs.title: RFQ and Auctions
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. This page extends the negotiation module. Everything there (term sheets, signed messages, the guard, exposure, drift detection, contract timing) applies to RFQs and auctions too.

Two families of multi-party negotiation are covered here:

  • RFQs: a buyer asks N sellers for structured quotations and awards one, then issues a purchase order. This is how B2B procurement, IndiaMART-style leads and GeM e-bids work.
  • Auctions: bidders compete on a published price clock run by a neutral auctioneer. This covers GeM-style reverse auctions, mandi and eNAM forward auctions, Dutch clearance of perishables and sealed-bid tenders.

Both rest on two rules: the rules are signed and published before the first response, and no participant sees another's quote or bid before the rules allow it.

docs.title: RFQ
docs.text:
An RFQ is a signed Rfq object (negotiation-session.json#/$defs/Rfq). It replaces ONDC's free-text BUYER_TERMS with a structured draft term sheet. Each invited seller gets its own bilateral negotiation session under the parent rfq_id, so every message, guard check and transcript of the negotiation module applies per seller.

Field Rule rfq_id Parent identifier. Every child negotiation carries it as rfq_parent_id, which drives exposure counting. mode rfq_sealed or rfq_iterated term_sheet_draft The structured requirement (lines, quantity, delivery, payment terms, quality, deposit) issues_negotiable[] JSON Pointers sellers may quote on. A counter-offer on any other issue is refused with NEG_ISSUE_NOT_NEGOTIABLE. invitees[] / broadcast Named sellers, or a category and city broadcast. Suspended sellers MUST be excluded. response_by REQUIRED. The time after which quotations are compared min_responses REQUIRED. The minimum number of valid quotations before an award (for example 3 for an L1 purchase) award_rule l1_landed_cost, qcbs or best_score, with scoring_rule_ref where needed acceptance_revocation_required Optional, the constant waived. Business sessions only. See Award. state DRAFT → PUBLISHED → COLLECTING → CLOSED → REVEALED → SHORTLISTED → AWARDED, or CANCELLED comparison[] Every valid quotation normalised to landed cost, with rank. Kept for audit. awarded The winning negotiation, offer hash and reason

A request without response_by or min_responses MUST be refused with 400 invalid_request. If the buyer's negotiation mandate sets process.rfq_min_window, a response_by closer than that window is refused with mandate_scope_mismatch.

docs.title: Sealed RFQ
docs.text:
In rfq_sealed, quotations are sealed with commit–reveal:

  1. Before response_by, each seller sends bid_commit with commit_hash = sha-256(JCS(bid) ‖ salt) and a bid_deposit_ref.
  2. Neither the gateway nor any other seller sees a quotation before response_by. While collecting, GET /rfqs/{id} MUST expose only the number of commitments and MUST omit comparison.
  3. After response_by, the gateway requests reveals. Each seller sends bid_reveal with the bid and salt, and the gateway checks that the hash matches the commitment. A reveal before close is refused with NEG_EARLY_REVEAL.
  4. A seller that never reveals forfeits its bid and its deposit (bid_not_revealed).
  5. The gateway normalises every revealed quotation to landed cost (freight, payment terms, taxes) and ranks them.

A sealed RFQ MUST carry a deposit in its draft term sheet. A sealed RFQ without one is refused with NEG_DEPOSIT_REQUIRED. See Deposits and EMD.

docs.title: Iterated RFQ
docs.text: In rfq_iterated, the sealed round is followed by alternating rounds with a shortlist ("best and final"). Each shortlisted seller's session continues as a bilateral alternating negotiation under the same rfq_id. Firm counter-offers to several shortlisted sellers count together against the buyer's exposure, so the guard escalates once their sum would exceed the mandate.

docs.title: Award
docs.text:
• No early award. The buyer MUST NOT award before response_by unless every invitee has responded. An early award is refused with NEG_EARLY_AWARD. This counters the first-proposal bias of LLM negotiators.
  • Minimum responses. An award with fewer valid quotations than min_responses is refused with NEG_AWARD_RULE.
  • Award rule. Under l1_landed_cost, the award MUST go to the L1 landed-cost quotation. Any other choice is refused with NEG_AWARD_RULE.
  • Award is acceptance. An award is an accept of the winning quotation's offer_hash, signed under the tag bacp-negotiate, guarded like any acceptance and carrying the within_bounds attestation. The quotation's acceptance_revocation term applies to the award as to any acceptance; BACP fixes no value for RFQ modes.
  • Frozen comparison set. The award rule is evaluated over the comparison set frozen when the RFQ closes; under rfq_iterated that is the close of the final shortlist round. Nothing that arrives later joins it, and it does not change when an award is revoked.
  • Revoked award. An award can be revoked only under the sunset text for allowed_until_receipt; in this version every accept_revoke of an award is refused (accept_revoke_not_allowed). If an award is revoked (accept_revoke_honoured), the RFQ moves to CANCELLED and is flagged NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN for review. It is not awarded again: any later award on it is refused with NEG_AWARD_RULE. A buyer that still wants the goods publishes a new RFQ.
  • Buyer-prescribed waived. A buyer that wants its awards to be final MAY set Rfq.acceptance_revocation_required: waived in its own RFQ, so that quotations carry acceptance_revocation: waived with a waiver_basis of doc_type: rfq, the RFQ's id and the hash of the published RFQ. The seller's gateway fills waiver_basis. The buyer then gives up its own right to revoke the award, on terms it set itself. It is for business sessions only and is refused in consumer sessions with capabilities_incompatible. An RFQ that an agent creates with it needs a confirm step-up with reason rfq_prescribes_waiver, because it waives the principal's own ICA s.5 right. The profile rules of Acceptance revocation still apply.
  • Losers. Every other child negotiation receives terminate with reason rfq_not_awarded, and its deposit is released.
  • Audit trail. The comparison set is kept with the award (for example, offers from at least three different manufacturers for an L1 purchase), together with who awarded it, under which mandate and why.

docs.title: Purchase order
docs.text:
After award, the RFQ follows the ONDC B2B (RET 2.0.2) sequence, as bound in Beckn / ONDC Binding:

Step BACP Beckn / ONDC carrier RFQ Rfq select with a bacp.neg.rfq tag group; one select per seller under one rfq_id Quotation Firm offer (or bid_commit / bid_reveal) on_select; quote.price MUST equal all_in_total; a proforma on on_status Negotiation rounds Counter-offers Repeated select / on_select in the same transaction_id Acceptance accept init carrying bacp.neg.accept Bound terms BPP-signed quote echoing the term sheet on_init Purchase order PO referencing offer_hash confirm with BAP_TERMS.ACCEPT_BPP_TERMS PO acceptance Order acknowledgement on_confirm → CONTRACTED

The PO MUST NOT alter accepted terms. Any drift between the accepted term sheet and on_init, confirm or on_confirm is handled by drift detection. For credit sales, the contract opens a credit-ledger entry instead of a checkout session, and the GRN, invoice and payment follow Credit and Split Tender. A typical B2B order is net-30 from GRN with an early-payment discount, and an MSE seller's credit is capped as described in Credit terms and MSMED limits.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Buyer procurement agent
    participant G as BACP gateway (BAP)
    participant CP as Buyer credential provider
    participant S1 as Seller 1 BPP
    participant SX as Other invited sellers
    A->>G: POST /rfqs rfq_sealed with response_by, min_responses 3, award l1_landed_cost
    G->>S1: select with bacp.neg.rfq
    G->>SX: select with bacp.neg.rfq
    S1-->>G: on_select bid_commit hash and deposit ref
    SX-->>G: on_select bid_commit hashes and deposit refs
    Note over G: Sealed until response_by. No quote is relayed to any seller.
    G->>S1: reveal request after response_by
    S1-->>G: bid_reveal
    G->>SX: reveal request
    SX-->>G: bid_reveal
    G->>G: Normalise to landed cost, rank, keep the comparison set
    A->>G: POST counter_offer to seller 1 on credit days
    G->>G: Guard, MSMED cap, exposure across RFQ sessions
    G->>S1: select round 2 counter
    S1-->>G: on_select firm counter net-30 from GRN
    A->>G: POST /rfqs/{id}/award with offer_hash
    G->>CP: Request within_bounds attestation
    CP-->>G: Signed attestation
    G->>S1: init with bacp.neg.accept
    S1-->>G: on_init with identical terms so BOUND
    G->>S1: confirm as purchase order referencing offer_hash
    S1-->>G: on_confirm accepts the PO so CONTRACTED
    G->>SX: terminate rfq_not_awarded and release deposits

docs.title: Auctions
docs.text:
Every auction starts with an AuctionSpec (negotiation-session.json#/$defs/AuctionSpec):

Field Meaning type english, reverse_l1, dutch or sealed_first_price auctioneer, auctioneer_neutrality Who runs the clock. affiliated_with_any_seller MUST be false. operator_type ∈ network_auction_service, government_platform, exchange, regulated_market. clock_source names the authoritative clock. lots[] Lot, item, quantity, unit, optional assay document and MRP reserve_price, reserve_disclosed, start_price, increment, decrement_schedule[] Price rules opens_at, closes_at, extension_rule{window, extend_by, max_extensions} Clock and anti-sniping visibility sealed, price_only or open tie_break earliest_bid, lottery, msme_preference, make_in_india_preference. In a Dutch auction always earliest_bid, the earliest position in the auctioneer's chain. standing_accepts_enabled Optional. Dutch only. Whether the auctioneer takes principal-signed standing accepts (Dutch auctions). bid_deposit{amount, instrument, forfeit_on[]} Required for sealed auctions retraction_rule no_retraction, before_close_outside_window, obvious_error_only eligibility Bidder allow-list, technically qualified only, licence required; exclude_suspended is the constant true award_rule highest_price, l1, first_accept, qcbs fixed_terms, scoring_rule_ref Non-price issues fixed for every bidder, or scored by a published rule procurement_mode_reason Why this mode was chosen, for example the value threshold

Publication. The creator submits an AuctionSpec draft. Any signature on the draft is the requester's own and is not relied on. The neutral auctioneer MUST sign the published spec and freeze its spec_hash, which is authoritative. The rules MUST NOT change after the first bid. The auctioneer's chain positions (the log_seq of its CounterSignatures) fix bid order, and its own clock fixes the close.

Bidders see an AuctionState view: spec_hash, state (SCHEDULED, OPEN, EXTENDED, CLOSED, REVEALED, AWARDED, NO_AWARD, CANCELLED), the current price where visibility allows, the caller's own rank, a bid count and closes_at. It never shows other bidders' identities or sealed bids. A bid outside OPEN or EXTENDED is refused with auction_not_open.

Anti-sniping is mandatory. A bid received within extension_rule.window before closes_at extends the close by extend_by, up to max_extensions.

A price-only lot auction carries each bid as a single line of quantity 1 with unit set, priced at the lot total, with the lot quantity in the line name, so that lot totals never have to be split into fractional paise per unit.

docs.title: Reverse L1 (GeM-style)
docs.text:
The reverse auction follows GeM practice: after technical evaluation, qualified sellers revise prices downward in a faceless online L1 negotiation.

  • Visibility is price_only: bidders see the current L1 price and their own rank, never who bid it.
  • A bid MUST be at or below start_price and MUST improve on the bidder's own previous bid by at least increment. It need not beat the current L1. A bid that does not improve is refused with 409 bid_not_improving.
  • The default retraction rule is no_retraction.
  • At close by the auctioneer's clock, the award goes to the L1 bid. Award is an accept of the winning bid's hash, with the buyer's within_bounds attestation.
  • A seller-side guard checks each bid against the seller mandate's floor (total_min, or auction_max_bid read as a floor for sellers).
  • GeM separates the ordering entity, the consignee and the paying authority, and the term sheet names all three. Payment terms on GeM are fixed and not negotiable (see GeM profile).

Procurement-mode thresholds. A buying organisation configures its own value thresholds for direct purchase, L1 purchase and bid or reverse auction, and every RFQ or auction records procurement_mode_reason. Under GFR Rule 149 as amended by DoE OM F.1/3/2024-PPD (10-07-2024), the default thresholds are:

Value Mode Up to ₹50,000 Direct purchase from any GeM seller meeting quality, specification and delivery period Above ₹50,000, up to ₹10 lakh L1 purchase from the GeM seller with the lowest price among the sellers of at least three different manufacturers. The online bidding and reverse auction tools may also be used. Above ₹10 lakh Bids are mandatory, obtained through online bidding (e-bid) or the reverse auction tool. GeM gives a normal bid duration of 10 to 45 days.

The values are from GFR 2017 Rule 149 as consolidated by the Department of Expenditure. Direct purchase has no ceiling for automobiles. Scientific ministries and research institutes have a ₹1 lakh direct-purchase limit (DoE OM F.20/42/2021-PPD, 18-07-2024). Rule 149 forbids splitting a demand to avoid L1 buying, bidding or reverse auction. The values MUST be configurable, not hard-coded.

docs.title: English (forward) auctions
docs.text:
Used for mandi and eNAM lots, FPO sales and disposal auctions.

  • A bid MUST beat the current highest by at least increment, otherwise bid_not_improving.
  • For packaged goods that must bear MRP, bids are capped at MRP (NEG_MRP_EXCEEDED).
  • The default retraction rule is before_close_outside_window.
  • The seller's explicit acceptance is required. For a farmer's or FPO's lot, the highest bid at close is not a sale until the seller accepts it. Only the seller (the auction creator) may award a forward auction. A rejected highest bid allows the same lot to be re-auctioned.
  • The farmer's payout is the accepted bid times the weighed quantity, minus itemised charges (commission, market fee, loading), each tagged with the party that bears it (see agri profile).

docs.title: Dutch auctions (perishables)
docs.text:
Used for perishables and end-of-day clearance.

  • The decrement_schedule[] is published in the spec, and its ticks MUST be non-increasing. A spec or runtime tick that rises is refused with NEG_DUTCH_PRICE_INCREASE.
  • A bidder accepts the current tick by sending an acceptance at that tick's price. An acceptance at any other price is refused with NEG_STALE_OFFER.
  • The first conforming acceptance in the auctioneer's chain order wins, and the award is final. It is never replaced. The bidder's tick message is legally a bid, and the award completes the sale (Sale of Goods Act, 1930, s.64(2)).
  • tie_break is the constant earliest_bid, meaning the earliest position in the auctioneer's own hash chain. A chain has no ties, so msg_hash stays only as a defensive last key. dispatched_at and received_at are recorded and never decide an award.
  • Receipt and tick_close. The auctioneer returns a synchronous CounterSignature with log_seq for every tick acceptance. At award it signs tick_close{tick, accepts[{log_seq, msg_hash}], log_head} and publishes it to every bidder at that tick (AuctionState.tick_close). The tick boundary is a chain entry, not a clock reading: an acceptance belongs to tick k when its receipt position precedes tick_close{k}. A validator rejects a tick_close whose accepts repeat a log_seq, because JSON Schema cannot.
  • A bidder whose countersigned position is missing from tick_close, or appears at another position, holds a signed contradiction: evidence_unverifiable with NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN, or a NEG_AWARD_RULE dispute.
  • A winner that dispatched after a loser (a dispatch inversion) is flagged to the collusion screen.
  • Later acceptances for the awarded tick MUST still be recorded in chain order. Each receives auction_closed_no_award.
  • Residual risk. A rogue auctioneer can still choose the processing order of near-simultaneous arrivals. The log makes a later reordering provable and does not prevent the first (Q-25).

Standing accept (optional). An auctioneer MAY set AuctionSpec.standing_accepts_enabled: true. A principal then lodges, before the auction opens, a principal-signed standing_accept{standing_accept_id, auction_id, lot_hash, valid_until, max_price, qty, mandate_ref, sender_log_seq, sender_log_prev, protocol_terms, signature}; every member is REQUIRED. A standing accept is lodged through the principal's gateway as a firm bid under tag bacp-negotiate, by POST /auctions/{auction_id}/standing-accepts, and withdrawn, while the auctioneer has not used it, by POST /auctions/{auction_id}/standing-accepts/{standing_accept_id}/withdraw (409 once it is used). The guard evaluates it at max_price × qty and holds that exposure reservation until the auction closes or the accept is used or withdrawn, and keys that reservation on standing_accept_id. An auctioneer MUST refuse a standing accept whose auction_id or lot_hash is not this auction's, or whose valid_until has passed, and uses each standing_accept_id at most once. The principal's gateway MUST refuse, with NEG_AWARD_RULE, and record no AGREED for, an award that cites a standing accept it did not lodge for that auction_id and lot_hash, whose valid_until has passed, or whose standing_accept_id it has already seen used or released; it makes no new exposure reservation for it. lot_hash is the sha-256 of the JCS form of the AuctionSpec lots[] entry that the standing accept is for, and valid_until MUST NOT be later than the auction's closes_at. A standing accept run in another auction is NEG_AWARD_RULE. At the first tick whose price is at or below max_price the auctioneer runs standing accepts ahead of live accepts at that tick, in the chain order in which they were placed. A slow human bidder, for example one on IVR, then competes on price and not on reflexes, with no randomness. Absent the flag, only the base rule applies and slow bidders lose speed contests to agents. Whether a standing accept is the principal's own acceptance under ICA s.7 is open (Q-85).

docs.title: Sealed-bid auctions
docs.text:
A sealed_first_price auction, or any auction with visibility: sealed, uses the same commit–reveal as a sealed RFQ:

  • bid_commit with commit_hash and bid_deposit_ref before close; bid_reveal after close. A reveal before close is NEG_EARLY_REVEAL.
  • An unrevealed bid is excluded and its deposit forfeited.
  • It is negotiated under mode rfq_sealed, so the bidder's mandate MUST allow rfq_sealed.
  • A sealed auction without bid_deposit is refused with NEG_DEPOSIT_REQUIRED:
Invalid: sealed auction with no deposit (auction.sealed-no-deposit.invalid.json)

docs.title: Deposits and EMD
docs.text:
Sealed RFQs and sealed auctions MUST require a bid deposit. The instrument (bid_deposit.instrument) is one of emd (earnest money deposit), ebg (electronic bank guarantee), upi_otm_block (a UPI one-time-mandate block) or pa_escrow (payment-aggregator escrow).

  • A bid_deposit_ref counts only if the holder of the deposit confirms a live deposit, held for that bidder, of at least the published minimum. Otherwise the commitment is refused with 403 NEG_DEPOSIT_INVALID (reasons: not found, not held for this bidder, below minimum). A reference string alone proves nothing.
  • A bidder that does not reveal forfeits its deposit. Losing bidders' deposits are released at award, when they receive terminate with rfq_not_awarded or auction_closed_no_award.
  • A deposit is a deposit issue in the term sheet with type: emd, refundable, deduction_policy and held_by (pa_escrow, bank_guarantee, gem_pool_account, …). Collecting a deposit on behalf of others requires an authorised payment aggregator's escrow.

docs.title: Who may run and award
docs.text:
• Neutral auctioneer. The auctioneer is a network auction service, a government platform, an exchange or a regulated market. It MUST NOT be the seller's BPP or anyone affiliated with a seller, because of the conflict of interest and the shill risk. A spec with affiliated_with_any_seller not equal to false is refused: seller-run auctions are refused. Gateways join only the network-designated neutral auctioneer. Who operates that auctioneer on ONDC is open (Q-25).
Invalid: seller-run auction (auction.seller-run.invalid.json)
