  • Award authority. Only the auction's creator or the neutral auctioneer itself may award. Any other caller gets NEG_AWARD_RULE. An award MUST be signed under the tag bacp-negotiate.
  • Award timing and rule. Except in Dutch auctions, an award is possible only after close by the auctioneer's clock (NEG_EARLY_AWARD otherwise), and only to the bid that the award_rule selects at close (NEG_AWARD_RULE otherwise).
  • Forward auctions. Only the seller's explicit acceptance awards a forward auction.
  • Revoked award. The award rule is evaluated over the bids standing at close, frozen then. In every auction type, if an award is revoked (accept_revoke_honoured, possible only under the sunset text), the auction moves to CANCELLED and is flagged NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN for review. It is not awarded again: an award to the next bid, or any later award on it, is refused with NEG_AWARD_RULE. A lot that is still for sale goes to a new auction.
  • Seller-paced messages (ticks, a seller counter-offer after silence) travel as unsolicited on_select within the transaction, with buyer polling as a fallback. Whether ONDC validators accept this is open (Q-26).

docs.title: Retraction
docs.text:
The retraction_rule decides whether a bidder may retract a bid with bid_retract:

Rule Retraction allowed Default for no_retraction Never reverse_l1, sealed before_close_outside_window Before close and outside the anti-sniping window english obvious_error_only Only with reason obvious_error, before close and outside the window —

Under every rule, a retraction inside the anti-sniping window, or after close, is refused with NEG_RETRACTION_REFUSED.

Not an acceptance revocation. accept_revoke never governs bid_retract. A bid's retraction follows the retraction_rule above whatever the bid's acceptance_revocation value, and an accept_revoke cannot retract a bid.

Retraction isolation. A retraction voids only the retracting bidder's own bid. Other bidders' bids stand. The previous best bid is not re-published as the standing price: the standing price stays hidden until the next bid. Repeated retractions by one bidder are flagged to the shill and collusion screens.

Proposed

Proposed: the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, s.64(2) says that an auction sale "is complete when the auctioneer announces its completion by the fall of the hammer or in other customary manner; and, until such announcement is made, any bidder may retract his bid". BACP does not treat this right as overriding no_retraction in e-auctions. Whether it applies is open (Q-35). The quoted text is from a bare-act reproduction and was not checked against the official India Code text as of 17-10-2026.

Section 64 also bears on shill bidding: unless the sale is notified as subject to the seller's right to bid, the seller may not bid or employ anyone to bid (s.64(4)), and a sale in which the seller uses "pretended bidding to raise the price" is voidable by the buyer (s.64(6)).

docs.title: Shill and affiliate detection
docs.text:
A bid by the seller, or by anyone acting for the seller, inflates the price. The auctioneer judges bidder independence by three identities, not by the network participant alone:

  1. the principal behind the bidder's negotiation mandate;
  2. the agent operator, the registry subscriber operating the agent (the did:web host of its agent id);
  3. the key fingerprint of the agent's signing key.
Situation Result The bidder is the auction creator (the seller), a declared affiliate of the seller, or shares the seller's principal, operator or key Refused with NEG_SHILL_BID Two different bidders share a signing key Flagged (NEG_SHILL_BID, screen) Two different bidders share an agent operator Flagged Two bidders reach the network through the same BAP Not a shill signal. A shared network BAP is normal. One bidder retracts repeatedly Flagged

docs.title: Collusion screens
docs.text:
Under the Competition Act, 2002, s.3(3)(d), an agreement between enterprises "engaged in identical or similar trade" that "directly or indirectly results in bid rigging or collusive bidding" is presumed to have an appreciable adverse effect on competition. The proviso added in 2023 extends that presumption to an enterprise not in that trade if it "participates or intends to participate in the furtherance of such agreement". BACP prevents collusion structurally and screens for it statistically:

  • No seller-to-seller channel. The protocol offers no way for one seller to obtain another's live or sealed quote or bid. Gateways MUST NOT cache or relay on_select term sheets across BPPs. Bidder-to-bidder messaging is not supported.
  • Pricing-AI disclosure. Participants declare any third-party pricing or negotiation AI (pricing_ai_vendor). A shared vendor is a hub-and-spoke risk signal under the Competition Act, 2002, s.3(3) and its 2023 proviso.
  • Screens. The auctioneer and the network run screens that flag and never block (NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN, requires_buyer_review):
    • identical prices from different bidders;
    • distinct bidders within 0.5% of each other;
    • bid rotation: across 3 or more auctions with a recurring ring of bidders, the winners take turns.
  • Flags go to the buyer and, through the network operator, to the competition regulator as appropriate. They are evidence for review, not a verdict.

docs.title: Bharat Agentic Commerce Protocol (BACP) Specification
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. Each one links to the relevant entry in Open Questions.

BACP is an open protocol that lets an AI agent run the full Indian commerce lifecycle on behalf of a person or a business: discover, negotiate, check out, pay, track fulfilment, return, get refunds and raise grievances. It does this on rails that already exist and are already regulated: ONDC/Beckn for commerce, UPI and the other Indian payment rails for money, Account Aggregator–style consent artefacts for authority, and the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act for personal data.

This page is the normative entry point. It defines the conventions that apply to every other page, the layering and actor model, the core artefacts, the lifecycle, and the rules for versioning and extensibility.

docs.title: Requirements language
docs.text: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL in this specification are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

docs.title: Data conventions
docs.text: Convention Rule Amounts Every amount is an Amount object: an integer value in paise (INR minor units) and currency: "INR". ₹302 is {"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"}. Every settlement amount MUST be in INR. A foreign-currency figure MAY appear only as a disclosure view (fx.json). Payable amounts A payable amount (a closed mandate's amount, a payment receipt's amount, a tender's amount) MUST be an integer number of paise greater than zero. Values that may legitimately be zero, such as a remaining budget or a free-goods line, MAY be zero. Date and time Timestamps are RFC 3339 date-time strings, for example 2026-10-12T10:15:00+05:30. Where a rule depends on a calendar period (a budget month, an AFA period), the period is computed in IST (UTC+05:30). BACP-owned timestamps SHOULD carry the offset +05:30; Beckn context fields follow ONDC, which requires Z, and are relayed unchanged. Every comparison of times is a comparison of instants, so …T10:00:05+05:30 and …T04:30:05Z are equal. The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 761(E)), Rule 7, require IST for any time reference from their commencement (notified, not in force as of 18-10-2026; about 24-02-2027, exact day not verified). Whether Rule 7 reaches machine timestamps is open (Q-84). Durations ISO 8601 durations, for example P30D or PT5M. Signature timestamps RFC 9421 created and expires parameters are integer seconds since the Unix epoch. Canonical JSON Signed and hashed JSON is canonicalised with JCS (RFC 8785). Hashes Written as alg:base64url. sha-256 is mandatory. blake2b-512 is allowed only for Beckn digests. Text shown to people Multilingual maps keyed by BCP 47 tag, for example {"hi-IN": "...", "en-IN": "..."}. Hindi display text under hi-IN is written in Devanagari. Romanised Hindi (for example a voice transcript) is tagged hi-Latn-IN. Schemas JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Schemas are identified by their $id under https://bacp.dev/schemas/, and tools MUST resolve $refs by $id, not by file path.

docs.title: The problem BACP solves
docs.text:
India already has interoperable commerce (ONDC/Beckn), instant interoperable payments with standing authorities (UPI Reserve Pay, UPI Circle, AutoPay), a consent-artefact model (Account Aggregator and DEPA), and a data-protection law (DPDP). None of them was designed for a software agent acting for a person. Each lacks the same four things:

  • Who the agent is. Today only the platform is identified on the network, never the agent or the legal entity that operates it.
  • Under whose authority, and within what limits. Nothing expresses "buy groceries for me, up to ₹3,000 a month, never more than ₹1,500 an order, and ask me above ₹1,200".
  • Whether a human was present. Payment and consumer rules differ sharply between a person approving a payment and an agent acting alone.
  • What the person agreed to share, with whom, for what purpose.

BACP adds these four things as a thin, namespaced agent layer, together with a hash-chained instruction log and rail-anchored receipts so that any dispute can be reconstructed from the person's instruction to the bank reference number. BACP does not fork ONDC/Beckn, UPI or any other rail.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
1. The model proposes, a deterministic engine decides. An LLM interprets intent, searches, builds carts and drafts offers. It never verifies anything that matters. Every commitment (paying, accepting an offer, placing a bid, cancelling, returning) passes a deterministic, non-LLM check that fails closed. The agent is treated as untrusted: prompt injection cannot be prevented, so it is contained. See the section below.
  2. The rail is authoritative. Payment rails enforce their own limits. BACP limits MUST be at or below the rail's, and BACP re-checks them. BACP never relies on the rail to bound its own budgets.
  3. An agent is never an authentication factor. The agent never sees or relays a UPI PIN, OTP or card credential, and never activates a mandate. Approval and authentication happen only on a non-agentic Trusted Surface.
  4. Consent is explicit and never inferred. Purchase consent and DPDP consent come from an affirmative action by the person, never from silence.
  5. Minimum disclosure. The payment leg is basket-blind. The seller never sees the payment instrument or the buyer's negotiation bounds. The bank never sees the basket.
  6. Evidence by default. Every step is signed and logged so that liability can be decided from evidence. BACP makes no claim about how the law allocates liability for agent error (Q-01).
  7. Bharat-first. Multilingual text, voice and IVR channels, voice-consent evidence, GST lines and cash on delivery are first-class.

docs.title: Layering
docs.text:
BACP is an agent layer over Beckn/ONDC, not a replacement for it. Each layer reuses an existing primitive.

flowchart TB
    subgraph T["Transport bindings"]
        REST["REST, RFC 9421 signed"]
        MCP["MCP tools"]
        A2A["A2A extension"]
    end
    subgraph F["BACP session facade (at the BACP gateway)"]
        SES["Checkout, negotiation and post-order sessions"]
        VER["Deterministic verifier and negotiation guard"]
        LOG["Instruction log, receipts, evidence bundle"]
    end
    subgraph N["Beckn / ONDC backbone"]
        BKN["search, select, init, confirm, status, cancel, update"]
        IGM["IGM 2.0 issue and on_issue"]
        CTX["context.bacp extension"]
    end
    subgraph P["Indian payment rails"]
        OPEN["Standing authorities for human-not-present use"]
        CLOSED["Per-transaction 2FA for human-present use"]
    end
    subgraph C["Consent (AA / DEPA style)"]
        MM["Mandate Manager and Trusted Surface"]
    end
    subgraph I["Identity"]
        REG["Registry, AgentCredential, status lists"]
    end
    T --> F
    F --> N
    F --> P
    N -.->|"payment terms and bank reference"| P
    C -.->|"mandates verified by"| F
    C -.->|"rail binding attestation"| P
    I -.->|"keys and credential status"| T
    I -.->|"subscriber keys"| N

Solid arrows are call paths. Dotted arrows are trust dependencies. Consent and identity are cross-cutting: every call depends on them. The facade talks to the payment rails through the payer PSP rather than through Beckn, because Beckn carries only payment terms: money moves off-network.

Layer What BACP reuses What BACP adds Transport bindings REST (OpenAPI 3.1), MCP tools with structuredContent, A2A DataPart and the TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED task state. One operation set, bound three ways. UCP binds its own operations four ways (REST, MCP, A2A and an embedded binding), and BACP does not adopt the embedded one. RFC 9421 agent signatures with separate tags for browsing, paying, post-order writes and negotiation. Step-up mapped to A2A TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED and MCP insufficient_scope. See REST and MCP and A2A. Session facade UCP checkout lifecycle and status names; ACP full-state responses, flat errors, messages[].resolution and idempotency; AP2's Trusted Surface and fail-closed constraint evaluation. A synchronous session over asynchronous Beckn; the deterministic verifier; the instruction log; an in-doubt payment saga. See Sessions and Checkout. Beckn/ONDC backbone Beckn {context, message}, ACK plus on_* callbacks, Ed25519/BLAKE2b network signing, registry lookup, ONDC payment and settlement fields, IGM. The context.bacp extension, mandatory idempotency and a replay cache, and an IGM actors[] entry of type AI_AGENT (Proposed: Q-11). Agent semantics stay in a namespace that network participants can ignore. See Beckn / ONDC Binding. Payment rails Live Indian rails: UPI Reserve Pay, UPI Circle, UPI AutoPay, card e-mandates, eNACH, PPIs, COD and others, with their own regulatory limits. Payment authority bound to a live rail primitive with a PSP-signed attestation; a basket-blind payment leg; rail-anchored receipts. See Payments. Consent AA/DEPA consent-artefact semantics: immutable, purpose-coded, use-counted, revocable. AP2-style open and closed mandates. Periodic budgets, allow-lists, step-up thresholds, post-order action scopes, a separate negotiation mandate, revocation within 60 seconds, DPDP consent receipts. See Mandates and Consent. Identity ONDC registry onboarding and key lookup, W3C verifiable credentials and status lists, AP2 cnf key binding. The AgentCredential: the agent, its operator's legal entity, its BAP binding, AI disclosure and human handoff. See Identity and Request Signing.

docs.title: The layering decision
docs.text:
BACP makes four choices about how it sits on existing infrastructure:

  1. An agent layer over Beckn/ONDC. Beckn already provides a signed asynchronous grammar, registry PKI, post-order writes (cancel, return), grievance handling (IGM), reconciliation and settlement (RSF), and a production network. BACP carries agent semantics in context.bacp and follows UCP checkout's lifecycle and status names (BACP spells cancelled and adds human_handoff). BACP is not wire-compatible with UCP: paths, totals and the sign of discounts, the ucp envelope, the complete payload and payment authority, and the MCP argument shape differ (BACP and other protocols). BACP is neither a UCP profile only (UCP has no network discovery, post-order writes, Indian rails or DPDP) nor an ONDC domain specification only (that would lose global-agent interoperability and the AP2 mandate format).
  2. Mandates in AP2 style with AA/DEPA consent semantics. A mandate has the structure of an AP2 open or closed Checkout Mandate or Payment Mandate, and the life of an Account Aggregator consent artefact: immutable once signed, tied to a purpose code, use-counted, and revocable at any time.
  3. Payment bound to live Indian rails. An open (human-not-present) payment mandate MUST bind to a standing authority that a live rail already enforces, such as a UPI Reserve Pay block or a UPI Circle delegation. A closed (human-present) payment is authorised by a fresh per-transaction factor on the Trusted Surface. BACP does not wait for a future rail: as of 17-10-2026, NPCI has not published an agent-payment specification for UPI, so the handler in.upi.uap is reserved.
  4. RFC 9421 agent signatures. Every agent request is signed with RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures under the key bound in the AgentCredential, with a tag that limits what the request may do. The network leg keeps the network's own signing.

docs.title: Actor model
docs.text:
Actor Role in BACP Trust Principal The person or business on whose behalf the agent acts (the DPDP Data Principal and, for payments, the payer). Sets up, pauses and revokes mandates; answers step-ups; receives notices. Trusted to authorise. Consent is always an explicit, affirmative action on the Trusted Surface, never inferred. Agent The LLM runtime (voice or text) that interprets intent, discovers, builds carts, negotiates and closes open mandates with its cnf key. Untrusted. It never verifies anything that matters, never holds a PIN or OTP, never signs consent and is never an authentication factor. Agent operator The legal entity that runs the agent and holds its AgentCredential. Keeps the operator signing key out of the agent's reach, runs the instruction log, appoints a grievance officer, keeps an AI inventory, and provides AI disclosure and a human handoff. Accountable and identified through registry onboarding. BACP gateway The BACP endpoint that agents call. It is co-located with, or runs on behalf of, a registered Buyer App (BAP), so the BAP subscriber is the network-visible party. It verifies agent signatures and credentials, runs the deterministic mandate verifier and negotiation guard, translates calls into signed Beckn actions, holds the replay cache, idempotency store and reservation ledger, and is the interfacing network participant for IGM. Trusted to enforce policy deterministically, but audited by conformance tests and evidence rather than trusted on its word. Seller / BPP The seller and its Seller App (BPP). Provides catalogue, signed quotes, fulfilment, cancel and return handling, GST invoices, and responds to IGM issues. A BACP-aware BPP verifies context.bacp and, in negotiation, the buyer's within_bounds attestation. Honest but curious. Its content is untrusted input to the agent (dark patterns, prompt injection). Mandate Manager Turns an approval on the Trusted Surface into signed, immutable mandates and consent receipts. Keeps status, usage and revocation, publishes a status list and notifies counterparties within 60 seconds. Acts as, or for, a DPDP Consent Manager. Data-blind: stores mandates and logs, never order or payment payloads. Trusted Surface The non-agentic surface, typically the payer's UPI app, where the principal reads notices in their language, approves mandates and step-ups, and enters a PIN or biometric. Non-agentic by requirement. Trusted for consent capture and authentication. PSP / rail The payer PSP and the rail behind it (for UPI, NPCI and the issuer bank). Creates the standing authority (block, delegation, mandate), issues the rail_binding attestation, executes debits and refunds, and signs receipts with the rail reference (RRN, UTR or equivalent). Authoritative for money movement and limits. Sees only payee, amount, mandate reference and checkout hash, never the basket. Registry The ONDC registry or another accredited registry. Publishes subscriber keys for BAPs, BPPs, Mandate Managers and PSPs; issues AgentCredentials and their status lists; records conformance attestations and payment-aggregator authorisation. Root of trust for keys. Which body anchors agent identity is open (Q-02).

Other parties appear in specific flows: the Beckn gateway (BG), which multicasts search and is routing-only; grievance redressal officers and ODR providers; payment aggregators; logistics providers; and, for trade profiles, roles such as consignee, paying authority, broker, financier and a neutral auctioneer (see Trade Profiles).

Co-location

In BACP 2026-10-18 the Mandate Manager is operated by, or co-located with, the payer PSP that also provides the Trusted Surface, so that consent capture and PIN entry happen on one non-agentic surface. The roles stay logically separate so that an independent DPDP Consent Manager can take over. An MM that acts as a registered Consent Manager does not also act as credential provider; that role runs as a separate component (Q-16).

docs.title: Core artefacts
docs.text:
Artefact Purpose Schema AgentCredential Identifies the agent, its operator and its BAP; binds the agent's signing key (cnf); lists the signature tags it may use; carries the AI disclosure and human-handoff link. An SD-JWT VC, vct: in.bacp.agent.1. agent-credential.json Mandate The principal's signed authority, AP2-compatible: open or closed, Checkout or Payment, with budgets, allow-lists, step-up thresholds, action and data scopes, and a rail or auth binding. mandate.json Negotiation mandate A separate mandate (vct: in.bacp.mandate.negotiation.1) holding negotiation bounds, including a reservation price that is never disclosed. mandate-negotiation.json ConsentReceipt The DPDP record of what personal data goes to which recipient, for what purpose, in which language, with the withdrawal and grievance routes. One per recipient per mandate. consent-receipt.json Receipt A PSP-signed payment or refund receipt anchored to the rail reference (RRN, UTR or other rail evidence). Budgets decrement only from these. receipt.json InstructionLog entry A signed, hash-chained record of prompt → intent → cart → mandate → payment reference, held by the operator. instruction-log-entry.json context.bacp The extension carried in the Beckn/ONDC context of every BACP-originated network message. beckn-context-bacp.json TermSheet The multi-issue terms under negotiation: price, quantity, delivery, payment, returns, warranty and more. termsheet.json Offer and negotiation messages Signed, expiring offers, counter-offers, bids, ACCEPT, REJECT, WITHDRAW and related messages. offer.json NegotiationSession The state of a negotiation, RFQ or auction, and the negotiation capability advert. negotiation-session.json Handler descriptor Data describing one Indian payment handler: binding class, presence rules, limits, AFA, refund route, settlement evidence. handler-descriptor.json PaymentPlan A split-tender or multi-tranche payment plan. payment-plan.json Credit ledger entry A hash-chained B2B credit (khata) posting. credit-ledger-entry.json LoanOffer A regulated credit offer with its key fact statement reference and cooling-off period. loan-offer.json FX view A disclosure view of a foreign-currency amount; settlement stays in INR. fx.json Common types Amount, Hash, Jws, Jwk, Signature, Presence, LangText, HandlerRef and others. common.json

The evidence bundle, which packages mandates, the BPP-signed quote, receipts and the instruction-log chain for a dispute, is defined in the REST binding (EvidenceBundle in the OpenAPI document listed under Reference) and described in Evidence and Instruction Log.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
A BACP transaction moves through seven stages. Mandate setup happens once, before the first stage, on the Trusted Surface. Negotiation is optional: a fixed-price catalogue purchase goes straight from discovery to checkout.

flowchart LR
    M["Mandate setup<br/>on the Trusted Surface"] --> D
    D["Discover<br/>POST /discover<br/>Beckn search"] --> NG
    D --> C
    NG["Negotiate (optional)<br/>signed offers under<br/>a negotiation mandate"] --> C
    C["Checkout<br/>POST and PUT /sessions<br/>Beckn select and init"] --> P
    P["Pay<br/>POST complete<br/>verifier, rail debit,<br/>Beckn confirm"] --> F
    F["Fulfil<br/>GET /orders<br/>Beckn status"] --> R
    F --> G
    R["Return and refund<br/>POST returns<br/>Beckn update,<br/>refund to source"] --> G
    G["Grievance<br/>POST /issues<br/>ONDC IGM as AI_AGENT"]
Stage Agent call Signature tag Network or rail action Defined in Mandate setup POST /mandates bacp-browse None on the network. The Mandate Manager and PSP create the mandate and the rail authority after the principal approves on the Trusted Surface. Mandates and Consent Discover POST /discover bacp-browse Beckn search → on_search through the Beckn gateway, with registry lookup Discovery and Profiles Negotiate /negotiations, /negotiations/{id}/offers, /negotiations/{id}/accept, /rfqs, /auctions bacp-browse for non-binding messages; bacp-negotiate for firm offers, ACCEPT, auction creation, bids and awards select / on_select rounds carrying negotiation tags Negotiation Checkout POST /sessions, PUT /sessions/{id} bacp-browse select → on_select (quote), then init → on_init (signed quote, payment terms) Sessions and Checkout Pay POST /sessions/{id}/complete bacp-pay Basket-blind debit through the payer PSP, then confirm → on_confirm with the rail reference Payments Fulfil GET /orders/{id} and webhooks bacp-browse status and unsolicited on_status (track is proposed) Orders and Post-order Return and refund POST /orders/{id}/returns, POST /orders/{id}/cancel bacp-post-order update (return) or cancel, then a refund to the original source Orders and Post-order Grievance POST /issues, POST /issues/{id}/actions bacp-post-order IGM 2.0 issue / on_issue with an AI_AGENT actor (Proposed) and an evidence bundle Evidence and Instruction Log

Revocation can happen at any point. A revoked mandate stops new commitments within 60 seconds. Protective actions on orders already placed under it (cancel, return, grievance) remain allowed with the principal present (presence: HP).

Getting Started walks through one complete transaction.

docs.title: The model proposes, a deterministic engine decides
docs.text:
BACP separates proposing from deciding.

  • The agent, and any LLM behind it, MAY propose anything: a search, a cart, a counter-offer, a return.
  • A deterministic, non-LLM engine inside the gateway trust zone decides whether a proposal becomes a commitment. For checkout this is the mandate verifier, which runs authoritatively on every complete and as an advisory pre-check on every PUT /sessions/{id}. For negotiation it is the negotiation guard, which runs on every outgoing firm counter-offer, ACCEPT, bid and award, and on every incoming offer.
  • The engine MUST fail closed: any failure, unknown constraint or unevaluable input rejects the commitment. The first failing check wins.
  • The engine's outcome is limited to pass, reject or escalate to the principal. When the engine escalates, the decision moves to the principal on the Trusted Surface, never back to the LLM. In negotiation the LLM sees only the verdicts acceptable, not_acceptable or needs_escalation, never the principal's bounds.
  • Free text from counterparties (product descriptions, seller chat) is untrusted input. It is returned to the agent only as data and can never widen a mandate.
  • Budgets, usage counts and rail caps are evaluated against an atomic reservation ledger, so concurrent requests cannot together exceed a budget.

The detailed evaluation order is defined in Mandates and Consent and Negotiation.

docs.title: Protocol versioning
docs.text:
BACP versions are calendar dates in the form YYYY-MM-DD. A dated version is a snapshot of the whole protocol: the specification pages, the JSON Schemas, the OpenAPI document, the handler registry and the conformance manifest, published together.

  • The current dated release is 2026-10-18. The working version on main is draft, which has no date and may change without notice.
  • A gateway publishes the versions it supports in its profile (bacp.version and bacp.supported_versions). An agent MUST use a version that the gateway lists.
  • Schema $ids under https://bacp.dev/schemas/ resolve to the latest release. Pinned copies live under https://bacp.dev/YYYY-MM-DD/schemas/.

The release process, URL scheme and breaking-change policy are defined on the Versioning page.

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
BACP is designed to be extended without breaking existing participants, with one deliberate exception: authority is never extended silently.

  1. Unknown fields are ignored; a member of an unlisted capability is refused. A receiver MUST ignore fields it does not understand in requests, responses, webhooks and network messages, unless the schema for that object forbids additional properties. A network participant that does not speak BACP ignores context.bacp. The exception is a request member that a capability owns, where the receiver's version defines the capability but the receiver does not list it: the receiver MUST refuse it with 400 capability_unsupported at the member's path, MUST create or change nothing, and MUST NOT ignore it. An ignored discounts member would let an agent tell the principal that a coupon was applied when it was not. Fields from a version that the receiver does not implement are ignored as before. See Capabilities.
  2. Unknown mandate constraints fail closed. A verifier that meets a constraint key it does not understand, in any mandate, MUST reject the mandate (constraint_unknown). An unknown constraint might be the very limit the principal relied on.
  3. New constraints go in new mandates. Because existing AP2-compatible verifiers fail closed on unknown constraints, a new family of bounds is carried in a separate mandate type, as negotiation bounds are, rather than added to Checkout or Payment Mandates.
  4. Closed objects stay closed. Objects whose schema forbids additional properties (for example the mandate constraints object, context.bacp and the term-sheet issue groups) MUST NOT carry extra fields. Extra negotiable issues go only under namespaced extensions, and the negotiation guard fails closed on any extension issue that is not agreed.
  5. Error codes are registered. A new error code MUST be registered with its HTTP status and resolution before use. A client that meets an unregistered code MUST act on the HTTP status class and MUST NOT retry a 4xx with a new Idempotency-Key. See Errors.
  6. Unknown handlers fail closed. A payment handler reference that does not resolve in the handler registry MUST be treated as not eligible. Resolving a handler does not make it eligible: reserved and deprecated handlers MUST NOT back a payment.
  7. Namespaces. Indian rails and instruments use in.<family>.<variant> handler ids. BACP-native constructs use bacp.<construct>. Capabilities use in.bacp.*. The in.* ids are governed by the BACP registries and are not bound to a DNS name: nothing about a domain such as bacp.in, which an unrelated party holds (as of 18-10-2026), makes an in.* id or a schema URL under it trustworthy. BACP never declares an in.* id together with a schema in a profile that a UCP platform reads, and a BACP gateway MUST NOT accept or fetch a schema for an in.* id from any source.
  8. Extensions come from a digest-pinned registry and are never fetched. A third-party extension is declared in capability_declarations by registry reference and schema digest (Capability declarations), and its payload travels under ext.<id>. A gateway MUST NOT fetch an extension's schema at run time. An ext member that touches an amount, the payee, presence, a mandate or a disclosure is critical: it is refused unless its capability is listed and the amount also appears as a line of the base totals, and it is never a mandate constraint.

docs.title: Payments Overview
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

BACP does not move money itself. Money moves on Indian payment rails (UPI, cards, net banking, NACH, PPIs, BBPS, e-RUPI and others), operated by NPCI, the card networks, NBBL, banks and payment aggregators under RBI regulation. Beckn/ONDC carries only the payment terms of an order. The BACP gateway talks to the rail through the payer's PSP and records the result as a signed, rail-anchored receipt.

This page defines the payment model that every rail binding shares:

  • payment handlers, their classes and how mandates bind to them;
  • the handler intersection between buyer and seller;
  • receipts, refunds and failed-payment handling;
  • the reserved NPCI UAP slot and handler naming.

The other payment pages cover the details:

Page Content Handler Registry The descriptor format, governance, alias resolution and the full table of 57 handlers Rail Bindings One subsection per rail family, with every limit and the regulation it comes from Credit and Split Tender Payment plans, BNPL and loan offers, the khata credit ledger, MSME interest, TReDS and FX disclosure

Mandates themselves are defined in Mandates and Consent, and the checkout session that drives a payment in Sessions and Checkout.

docs.title: Handlers, instruments and tokens
docs.text:
A payment handler is one way of paying that a rail or instrument offers, such as in.upi.autopay (UPI AutoPay) or in.card.mandate (a card e-mandate). Each handler has a descriptor in the handler registry that states, as data:

  • who operates and regulates it;
  • whether a human must be present for each payment, or a standing authority may be used;
  • the limits, the AFA (additional factor of authentication) model and the pre-debit-notice rule;
  • where refunds go, how disputes are raised and what settlement evidence the rail returns;
  • which fields may cross the payment leg, and which must never be collected.

An instrument is the payer's account, card, wallet, voucher or credit line that a handler debits. An opaque token is the reference by which BACP names an instrument or a standing authority without holding the credential behind it: a UPI Circle delegation id, an SBMD block id, a UMN, a UMRN, a card-on-file token reference, or a voucher reference held in a vault.

Credential rules. These apply to every participant, and to the agent in particular.

  • An agent, a BACP gateway and a buyer app MUST NOT collect, store, log or relay a UPI PIN, an OTP, a card PAN, CVV or expiry date, net-banking credentials, an Aadhaar number or biometric data. Every handler descriptor lists these under data_minimisation.never_collect.
  • An agent is never an authentication factor. A PIN, OTP, passkey, biometric or 3-D Secure step is completed by the human on their own device or on the payer PSP's Trusted Surface.
  • For cards, only the issuer and the card network may store card-on-file data (RBI CoFT circular RBI/2021-22/96). Other parties MAY retain only the last four digits and the issuer name.
  • Gift-card and voucher codes are held in the Trusted Surface or a PSP-adapter vault. The agent never sees them, and the gateway's PSP adapter redeems them.
  • Net banking is implemented only as a redirect to the bank's own page.

Basket-blind payment leg. The request that reaches the payer PSP and the rail carries only {payee, amount, mandate_ref, checkout_hash}. Line items, product names and other basket data MUST NOT be sent on the payment leg.

docs.title: Handler classes
docs.text:
Every descriptor carries binding.class. The class decides whether a handler may run with no human present (HNP) under a standing authority, or needs a human present (HP) for each payment.

Class Meaning Presence Examples O (open-eligible) A standing authority whose limits the rail, the issuer or both parties enforce. It MAY back an open (HNP) payment mandate, but only through a primitive whose limits the rail or the issuer enforces, listed in binding.open_primitives. HP or HNP in.upi.reservepay, in.upi.circle (not open-eligible while Q-77 is open), in.upi.autopay, in.upi.otm, in.card.mandate, in.nach.debit, in.ppi.gift, in.erupi (pilot) C (closed, HP only) Needs a human-completed 2FA or approval bound to this one transaction. It backs only a closed, HP payment mandate. HP in.upi.intent, in.card.token, in.netbanking, in.a2a.neft, in.credit.bnpl A (assisted or device-bound) HP on the payer's own device or at an assisted touchpoint. Never usable by a remote agent. HP, assisted in.upi.lite, in.card.present, in.pos.tap, in.aeps.assisted D (deferred) The order may be placed HNP, but payment happens later with a human (cash or UPI at the door). Order HNP, payment HP in.cod, in.cod.upi N (non-paying) Financing, verification or tracking. Never satisfies a payment mandate. — in.fin.treds, in.fin.lc, in.gov.gem, in.pa.settlement

The full assignment of all 57 handlers is in the registry table.

Why only class O is open-eligible. The RBI Authentication Directions 2025 (RBI/2025-26/79) require every digital payment to be authenticated with at least two factors, at least one of them dynamic for every payment other than a card-present one. The exemptions in Annexure-1 include recurring e-mandate debits after the first one, small-value contactless and offline payments, gift PPIs and PPI-MTS, and UPI Tap & Pay. So an unattended agent debit is lawful only when it runs under a standing authority that the rail or issuer recognises and enforces, such as an AFA-registered e-mandate, a UPI Circle delegation or an SBMD block. Class O names exactly those handlers. Every other payment needs a fresh, human-performed 2FA, which makes it class C or A.

The descriptor schema enforces three consistency rules:

  • binding.open_eligible: true implies presence.hnp: rail_enforced;
  • binding.open_eligible: true implies a non-empty binding.open_primitives;
  • presence.device_bound: true implies binding.open_eligible: false.

in.store_credit, in.loyalty and bacp.credit_ledger are class O, but their limits are enforced by the merchant or by BACP, not by a rail or issuer. In BACP 2026-10-18 they have open_eligible: false and presence.hnp: none, and do not back open (HNP) payment mandates. Opening them is closed in this release (Q-59 and Q-46, settled); the conditions for opening them later are Proposed text in Q-59. in.upi.circle is class O but has open_eligible: false while Q-77 is open, even when a conformance attestation lists it.

docs.title: Binding mandates to handlers
docs.text:
A payment mandate is either open (a standing HNP authority the agent may draw on) or closed (authority for exactly one payment). See Mandates and Consent.

Mandate Carries Rule Open payment mandate rail_binding{type, primitive, rail_ref, attestation, registry_version, pre_debit_notice} type MUST resolve to a class O handler whose descriptor has open_eligible: true and status: live, or status: pilot only when the gateway's conformance attestation lists that pilot. primitive MUST be in the descriptor's binding.open_primitives. rail_ref is the delegation id, SBMD block id, UMN, UMRN or equivalent. attestation is a PSP-signed statement of {rail_ref, type, primitive, limits, expiry, payee, funding} (and custody for a gift PPI), hashed into the mandate. registry_version records the dated registry release the Mandate Manager checked at issuance. Eligibility is re-checked against the current registry at every complete (Handler binding). Closed payment mandate (HNP) auth_binding{type: parent_rail_binding} The debit executes under the parent open mandate's rail binding. Closed payment mandate (HP) auth_binding{type} with type in the handler's binding.closed_auth E.g. upi.pin, card.3ds, netbanking.login_otp, maker_checker, kfs_esign. Created on the Trusted Surface.

The rules below apply after the handler reference has been resolved to its canonical id (alias resolution).

  1. Open eligibility. An open payment mandate whose rail_binding.type resolves to a class C, A, D or N handler MUST fail schema validation and MUST be refused. A reserved or deprecated descriptor MUST NOT back a payment, and a pilot descriptor only when attested. A rail_binding.primitive that is not in the descriptor's binding.open_primitives, or a descriptor with open_eligible: false, gets rail_binding_not_open_eligible.
  2. Rail limits are authoritative. The mandate's constraints (per-transaction amount, budgets, validity) MUST be at or below the descriptor's rail limits. The Mandate Manager rejects a mandate whose constraints exceed its rail binding.
  3. Class C. A class C handler backs only a closed, HP payment mandate whose auth_binding.type is in binding.closed_auth. An HNP request gets presence_handler_mismatch.
  4. Class A. A class A handler needs presence HP, an assisted channel and an assisted-session binding: operator id, terminal id, and an order hash shown to the payer before capture. A remote agent is refused.
  5. Class D. A COD order needs an open checkout mandate with cod_allowed: true and a cod_max_open_orders cap. No payment mandate is created at order time. See COD.
  6. Class N. A class N handler never satisfies a payment mandate. Credit-funded handlers need credit_funding_allowed: true on the governing mandate (otherwise credit_funding_not_allowed) and an HP loan acceptance. See Credit and Split Tender.
  7. Credit on UPI. in.upi.credit_line and in.upi.rupay_cc are class C. They MAY run HNP only through a class O primitive on the credit account (AutoPay, Reserve Pay or OTM), and the payment-plan leg then carries funding: credit, with the user's prior consent recorded as credit_funding_allowed on the mandate.
  8. AFA thresholds. A debit above ₹15,000 (₹1,00,000 for insurance premiums, mutual-fund subscriptions and credit-card bills) under UPI AutoPay, a card e-mandate or a PPI e-mandate needs AFA (RBI E-mandate Framework 2026). The gateway returns requires_escalation with step_up.kind = rail_auth. Thresholds are evaluated on the total of a payment plan, never per tender.
  9. Other rail caps. Exceeding any other rail cap (per-transaction, period, block balance, first-24-hour, channel caps) gives 403 rail_limit_exceeded with resolution: requires_buyer_review, step_up_kind: rail_auth and every reason listed.
  10. Budgets do not rely on the rail. A gateway MUST NOT rely on rail-enforced limits to bound BACP budgets, because the rail authority may be larger than the mandate's budget. Budgets are enforced atomically by the gateway (see Mandates and Consent).

Pre-debit notice. The descriptor's afa.pre_debit_notice gives the rule for each handler:

Value Meaning Handlers required_24h Notice at least 24 hours before the debit, with opt-out (RBI E-mandate Framework 2026) in.upi.autopay, in.card.mandate, in.ppi.wallet (e-mandate), in.bbps.upms bacp_policy_24h BACP's own 24-hour notice with opt-out, because the framework does not state that it covers NACH in.nach.debit exempt No pre-debit notice; a post-debit notice MUST be sent in.ppi.netc_topup, in.ppi.ncmc_topup unknown Not settled in.upi.reservepay, in.upi.otm

Until Q-03 is answered, unknown MUST be treated as required_24h for the second and every later unattended debit on a Reserve Pay or OTM binding. The first debit is covered by the block-creation authorisation. A deployment MAY switch this off for a rail only by an explicit, logged policy decision, and conformance runs MUST keep it on.

A 24-hour notice cannot fit inside a short quote TTL, so a notice-gated checkout works as follows:

  1. The gateway issues the notice when the session first becomes ready_for_complete, and relays it as webhook pre_debit.notice and message pre_debit_notice.
  2. A complete before the notice matures moves no money and returns 200 with message pre_debit_notice.
  3. After maturity the agent re-quotes. The matured notice is reused only if the new amount is at or below the notified amount. Otherwise a new notice is required.
  4. An opt-out on the Trusted Surface cancels the session with pre_debit_opt_out and no rail traffic.

docs.title: Handler intersection and preference
docs.text:
Before a payment, the gateway computes the set of handlers that every party accepts, deterministically:

eligible = registry handlers with status live (or pilot, when attested)
         ∩ the buyer app's profile payment_handlers
         ∩ the seller's accepted handlers
         ∩ the handlers of the selected TermSheet payment option and tranche
         ∩ the handlers allowed by the negotiation, checkout and payment mandates
         ∩ presence filter
         ∩ amount filter (descriptor limits, UPI P2M category caps, remaining block or balance)
         ∩ instruments the Trusted Surface reports as available (including card CNP enablement)

The presence filter is:

Presence Classes allowed HNP O, plus D for placing an order HP O, C, D HP on an assisted channel O, C, D, A

The eligible set is then ordered by:

  1. the user's own designated preference. The order MUST NOT be steered by incentives to the platform, network or PSP;
  2. the lowest all-in total, counting only the payer-borne lines that apply to the handler (a COD fee or a convenience fee scoped to it by applies_to_handlers, an unscoped line, and the session's operator charges), and discounts. The seller's own costs are never in the total (Fees on the payer's screen);
  3. the lowest authentication friction at this presence.

Every excluded handler is reported with a reason, for example not_in_registry, pilot_not_attested, not_accepted_by_seller, not_in_mandate, presence_handler_mismatch, above_limit, instrument_unavailable, card_not_enabled_for_cnp, reservepay_block_wrong_payee, cod_open_orders_cap or credit_funding_not_allowed. The response also carries a comparison[] of every option and its total, and the comparison is written to the instruction log so that the user can see why a method was chosen. Each entry may carry a method_charge: the sum of the scoped payer-borne lines for that option, computed by the gateway. A method_charge or fee_bearer value that a counterparty supplies is ignored, and the value is a log value that no view labels as "who pays". The gateway MUST NOT put the merchant discount rate, the payment aggregator's commission, the finder fee or a net-settlement amount in a comparison[] total, and gives the warning payment_mode_fee_inconsistent where convenience fees differ across debit modes.

  • An empty intersection returns 200 with message handlers_incompatible (requires_buyer_input). The same code is a 403 when it blocks the caller's own ACCEPT.
  • A Reserve Pay block is payable only to one seller. The intersection MUST exclude in.upi.reservepay unless a block payable to this seller exists. A seller that lacks only a block keeps its rank and is offered a human-present payment; it is not dropped.
  • Multi-seller baskets. For each leg of a multi-seller basket the fallback rungs of the per-leg rule (the seller's existing payee-bound instrument, a gift PPI the principal designated, one planned human-present step) rank below the principal's designated preference (rule 1); no rung, and no any-merchant primitive, ranks above it. For every leg the comparison[] records the option chosen (chosen: true) and every option skipped, each with its reason.
  • If a card is excluded because card-not-present use is disabled on it, the agent MUST NOT silently try another card.

The REST binding of the intersection is POST /payment-handlers/intersect. It takes a negotiation_id (the inputs come from the negotiated TermSheet) or, on a gateway that lists in.bacp.payment_plan, a session_id alone for a plain checkout session (Q-45, settled 18-10-2026). A gateway that does not list the capability still requires the negotiation_id and refuses a session_id with 400 capability_unsupported at $.session_id.

For a plain session:

  • the gateway covers only the session's own sellers: a bpp_id that is not a seller of the session gets 404 not_found;
  • excluded[].reason is the closed enum of the OpenAPI document, with no amount, no bound and no text written by a counterparty, and each exclusion carries resolution and, for a session with several sellers, bpp_id;
  • the gateway counts a per-agent rate limit before it looks the session up (429 quota_exceeded);
  • excluded[] is for the buyer's own agent and is never forwarded to a seller, and an eligible handler is never authority: complete always re-evaluates the mandate, the rail limits and the seller's terms.
excluded[].reason resolution not_in_registry, not_offered_by_bap, not_accepted_by_seller, not_in_term_sheet, pilot_not_attested unrecoverable above_limit recoverable (choose a payment plan from payment.plan_options[], or accept a step-up) instrument_unavailable, card_not_enabled_for_cnp, cod_not_allowed, cod_open_orders_cap, credit_funding_not_allowed, reservepay_block_wrong_payee requires_buyer_input not_in_mandate, presence_handler_mismatch requires_buyer_review

A plain-session agent that does not use this learns an ineligible handler only from a failed debit, which can cost money.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP Gateway
    participant R as Handler registry
    participant S as Seller BPP
    participant T as Trusted Surface
    A->>G: Request intersection for negotiation and presence HNP
    G->>R: Load descriptors and resolve aliases
    G->>S: Read accepted handlers from the catalogue
    G->>T: Ask which instruments are available
    G->>G: Intersect, filter by presence and amount, order by preference then total
    G-->>A: eligible, excluded with reasons, comparison

docs.title: Receipts
docs.text:
Every money movement is evidenced by a receipt signed by the party that acted, normally the payer PSP (schema).

  • receipt_type is payment or refund (or mandate, checkout). result is success, failure or in_doubt.
  • rail.type is a handler reference. Producers SHOULD emit the canonical id. rail.rail_ref and rail.status are required.
  • UPI family (in.upi.*, in.cod.upi, in.pos.tap, in.pos.dynamic_qr and their aliases): a successful receipt MUST carry a 12-digit rrn, and MUST carry utr whenever the descriptor's settlement.evidence_refs lists utr. in.upi.lite and in.upi.intl list RRN only.
  • Other handlers: a successful receipt MUST carry at least one of rrn, utr or rail.evidence. The keys of rail.evidence MUST come from the descriptor's settlement.evidence_refs, for example arn and auth_code for cards, umrn for NACH, voucher_id for e-RUPI, loan_id for credit, ledger_entry_id for store credit and the credit ledger, bconnect_txn_id for BBPS, cbdc_txn_id, uetr and pa_order_id.
  • rail.evidence MUST NOT contain anything in the descriptor's never_collect list.
  • A receipt that the principal can see, and rail.evidence, never carry the merchant discount rate, the payment aggregator's commission or a net-settlement amount. This follows from the rule that evidence keys come from settlement.evidence_refs, and no descriptor lists a fee key. payee_mcc, the merchant category code of the UPI merchant tag, is an optional evidence key that a UPI merchant-payment descriptor may list; it lets a receipt show whether the payee was categorised as a small merchant. An absent value means unknown. Whether a payer PSP can see the tag is not verified as of 18-10-2026.
  • Cash COD moves no money through a rail, so it has no payment receipt. The order records the collection against the AWB, with no escrow reference.
  • The remaining mandate budget (budget_after) is computed by the gateway after it applies a signed receipt, and is returned unsigned on the session. It MUST NOT appear inside a signed receipt.
  • Webhooks never embed a signed receipt. They carry a ReceiptRef with receipt_hash, and the agent fetches the full receipt and checks the hash. See Evidence and Instruction Log.
  • A cross-border payment MAY carry an fx disclosure view. Settlement amounts stay in INR. See FX disclosure.

A refund receipt MUST identify the original payment (original_rrn, original_utr, or an original_* key in rail.evidence such as original_arn) and MUST carry a refund_state:

refund_state Meaning refunded_to_source Default: the refund reached the original instrument released_block A UPI OTM block was released before capture adjusted_against_dues A card refund made before the bill was paid, adjusted against the dues (RBI Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions 2022, "Credit Card MD", para 10(g)) pending_cardholder_consent A card refund waiting for the cardholder's consent (see below) reversed_to_bank_account No consent within 7 days, so the issuer reversed the amount to the cardholder's bank account credit_note_issued An unpaid credit-ledger sale was reduced by a credit note; no money moved

docs.title: Refunds
docs.text:
Default: to the original method. A refund goes back to the instrument that paid (RBI PA Master Direction 2025 para 10(f)), routed through the PA escrow. A refund goes to store credit or to another mode owned by the payer only on the payer's explicit instruction; otherwise the gateway refuses it with refund_not_to_source. Refunds do not restore a mandate budget.

What a refund returns. BACP states what the principal gets back as charge lines, not as a rate.

  • A reversal (debited_not_confirmed, a failed debit) MUST credit the full debit.
  • A cancellation or return refund below the amount paid MUST match lines in charges_retained[] of the refund record. Each retained line was disclosed before commitment, carries a refund_rule (always, before_dispatch or never), and is a retention that the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 permit. The record also carries charges_refunded[]. The gateway checks each charges_retained[] line against the order's committed terms: the quote bound by the closed Checkout Mandate's checkout_hash, or the TermSheet. The line needs the same code, an amount at or below the disclosed amount, and the refund_rule that was disclosed, and its event must be one the rule allows: always is never retained, before_dispatch is retained only after dispatch, and never is retained. A line that fails any check is not a match, and the shortfall gets refund_short_of_terms. A retention on a return whose reason is a defect, a deficiency, a wrong item or late delivery gets refund_short_of_terms, whatever the line says.
  • Otherwise the gateway returns the message refund_short_of_terms (requires_buyer_review, with the IGM route). The gateway never blocks the refund or holds the money: refund routing is the aggregator's and the banks' duty (PA Master Direction 2025 para 8(b)).
  • A refund is never reduced by the merchant discount rate or the aggregator's fees.
  • Rules 6(3) and 7(4) of the Rules bar a refusal to refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods, and rule 4(8) makes cancellation charges symmetric. Whether a disclosed non-refundable payment charge (convenience, payment_handling, platform) may be kept at all, including on a return for a defect, is open with counsel (Q-81). Until it is answered, no conformance case passes a retained payment-related charge as valid, and none passes a retention on a return for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods.
  • This holds whatever NPCI decides about MDR on refunds. No public NPCI or RBI text found says whether MDR is reversed on a refund (not verified as of 18-10-2026).

Never into a PPI where the PPI rules forbid it. Refunds of card, UPI or net-banking payments MUST NOT be credited to an RBI-regulated PPI (wallet, PPI card, gift PPI), even if the user asks (PPI Master Direction 2021 para 14.3 has no consent exception). The gateway refuses with refund_to_ppi_forbidden. In the other direction, a refund of a PPI-funded payment MUST go back to the same PPI immediately, even if this takes it above the PPI's limits (para 14.3).

Card refunds above the consent threshold. Where the card bill has already been paid and a refund would leave a credit balance above the lower of 1% of the credit limit or ₹5,000, the issuer must seek the cardholder's consent within 7 days; without consent the issuer reverses the amount to the cardholder's bank account (Credit Card MD para 10(h)). The refund receipt goes through pending_cardholder_consent and then either refunded_to_source or reversed_to_bank_account, and BACP MUST NOT promise an "instant refund to card" in that case. A refund made before the bill is paid is adjusted against the dues (adjusted_against_dues) and does not pass through pending_cardholder_consent.

The refund route of each handler is the descriptor's refund.route:

Paid with Route Notes UPI (intent, Circle, AutoPay, Reserve Pay, credit line) source To the source VPA or account with original_rrn. A credit-line payment goes back to the credit line. Whether a refund restores a Reserve Pay block is not verified. UPI OTM release_block_or_source Before capture, release the block. After capture, a normal UPI refund. Cards (token, e-mandate, agentic, RuPay credit card on UPI) source_with_card_credit_consent To the card, with the consent rule above Card EMI, BNPL, cardless EMI, OCEN lender To the lender, reducing the loan. The cooling-off exit is separate. PPI wallet, PPI card, gift PPI, transit PPI same_ppi Back to the same PPI immediately Net banking source To the source account IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, NACH debit new_credit_push A new credit to the payer's bound account, with a UTR Cash COD user_elected_account Cash cannot be refunded to source: to the UPI or bank account the user chooses, or store credit only if the user elects it COD paid by UPI at the door source UPI refund to the source VPA Store credit, loyalty, UPI Lite same_balance Back to the same balance e-RUPI, programmable e₹, NETC and NCMC top-ups issuer_or_sponsor Unredeemed or expired value reverts to the issuer or sponsor bacp.credit_ledger ledger_credit_note Unpaid: a credit_note entry. Paid: a refund to the instrument that settled it. Split tender per tender Last in, first out by default. See split tender.

A return refund is issued exactly once, on the first of the return reaching Liquidated or Return_Delivered. Refund disputes go to the descriptor's dispute.channels: UDIR for UPI, the card issuer's 30-day billing dispute, the PPI issuer (48 hours preferred, 30 days at most), and the Bharat Connect complaint system for BBPS. An IGM issue about a refund carries the RRN or UTR. See Orders and Post-order.

docs.title: Failed payments: TAT and auto-reversal
docs.text:
RBI's harmonised turnaround-time circular (RBI/2019-20/67) requires automatic reversal of failed transactions within a fixed time, and ₹100 per day of compensation beyond it, paid without a claim, where a row of its Annex applies. Whether row 4(b) applies to a UPI payment that the rail completed and only the seller's own confirmation is missing is not verified as of 18-10-2026 (asked of counsel and RBI), so BACP states the compensation only where the PSP reports the debit as pending or deemed:

Failure TAT UPI P2M: account debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location (row 4(b)) T+5 UPI P2P T+1 IMPS beneficiary not credited T+1 auto-reversal NACH debit after mandate revocation T+1 Card-present POS, and card-not-present (e-commerce) debited without merchant confirmation T+5 Card-to-card transfer T+1 PPI on-us T+1 (off-us follows the underlying rail) AePS or Aadhaar Pay debited without merchant confirmation; ATM or micro-ATM cash not dispensed T+5

The circular has no net-banking row. NEFT and RTGS follow their own return rules: NEFT credits within 2 hours of batch settlement or returns, RTGS credits within 30 minutes or returns within 1 hour, with penal interest at repo + 2% for delay (Rail Bindings).

Inside the checkout session, a payment moves through initiated, debited and confirmed. The failure paths are:

  • in_doubt. The PSP timed out. The gateway reconciles by idempotency key and PSP status, and MUST NOT attempt a new debit until the outcome is known. The budget reservation stays in place until reconciliation. An in_doubt payment MUST NOT be re-routed to another handler, in a single session or in a leg of a multi-seller basket, until reconciliation resolves it. On UPI Reserve Pay, NPCI treats a timeout on a block debit as a decline that is reversed in real time and not settled, and for timeouts only the acquiring entity may retry at most 3 times in 24 hours (NPCI UPI OC 228); a gateway still reconciles with the PSP before it treats the leg as failed. A credit-side timeout after a successful debit is deemed (NPCI OC 200 para (d); Consolidated Circular para 32.3) and follows TAT row 4(b).
  • Debited but not confirmed. If the debit succeeded and the seller's on_confirm is still missing after the confirm is re-sent, the session MUST stay complete_in_progress with payment.status = reversal_pending, reversal_deadline = debit time + 5 days, and message debited_not_confirmed (recoverable). For refund_route: gateway_collector the gateway MUST start a refund to source with original_rrn at once; for seller_collector it MUST request that refund from the seller's collector through IGM at once. Issuing the refund receipt does not by itself end the session. When the PSP reports the refund credit as settled, payment.status becomes reversed and the session becomes cancelled. payment.reversal_basis (rbi_tat, bacp_policy or unknown) and payment.refund_route (gateway_collector or seller_collector) MUST be set. The message states the T+5 turnaround and the ₹100 per day compensation only for rbi_tat, never for bacp_policy, and for unknown names the refund to source, UDIR and, after 30 days, the RBI Integrated Ombudsman, with the conditional sentence that RBI's rules apply if the bank shows the payment as failed or pending. For seller_collector the gateway requests the refund through IGM and says "requested", not "started" (Debited but not confirmed). What signal confirms refund settlement is open (Q-49).
  • Failed debit. No money moved. The session is cancelled, the budget reservation is released, and the message is payment_failed.

docs.title: NPCI UAP: the reserved slot
docs.text:
NPCI's Unified Agent Protocol (UAP) for agentic UPI payments has been reported in the press (Business Standard, July 2026; Reuters, September 2026, the latter not verified as of 17-10-2026), but as of 17-10-2026 no public specification, circular or NPCI press release for UAP exists. NPCI's Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 press release does not mention it. What is live as of 17-10-2026 is UPI Circle delegation to IoT or software secondaries (with AI chatbots in a closed-user-group pilot), UPI Reserve Pay and UPI AutoPay, and BACP binds to those.

BACP reserves a slot so that UAP can be added without breaking clients:

  • Canonical id in.upi.uap, with status reserved and class O, but open_eligible: false.
  • The glob aliases upi.uap.* and in.upi.uap.* resolve to it. The exact alias upi.uap.pin resolves to in.upi.intent, not to UAP (alias resolution).
  • The AgentCredential reserves a uap_agent_id field for an NPCI agent registry id (Identity and Request Signing).
  • A reference that resolves to in.upi.uap is schema-valid as a rail binding, but MUST NOT back a payment while the status is reserved.

When NPCI publishes UAP, the descriptor will be filled in from the published text and its status changed through the registry process. Obtaining the member-only NPCI circulars is tracked as Q-07, and the identity anchor as Q-02.

docs.title: Handler ids and legacy aliases
docs.text:
Settled

The naming scheme below is settled in Q-28. Registry changes follow the proposal process, and legacy aliases stay accepted for the deprecation window set in the versioning policy.

  • in.<family>.<variant> names an Indian rail or instrument, e.g. in.upi.reservepay, in.card.mandate, in.nach.debit.
  • bacp.<construct> names a BACP-native construct, e.g. bacp.credit_ledger, bacp.trade.export_realisation.
  • Earlier names (upi.reservepay.block, upi.circle.delegate, upi.autopay, rupay.token, erupi, cod, and the bacp.pay.*, bacp.fin.*, bacp.gov.* forms) are kept as aliases for one deprecation window.
  • Producers MUST emit canonical ids in new artefacts. Consumers MUST accept any handler reference and MUST compare handlers only after resolution.

The resolution rules and the full alias list are in the Handler Registry.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The payment-specific codes are listed in Errors. The ones this page refers to are:

Code HTTP when surfaced Resolution presence_handler_mismatch 403 requires_buyer_review rail_binding_not_open_eligible 400 requires_buyer_input; recoverable for reasons: [registry_copy_stale] reservepay_block_wrong_payee 403 requires_buyer_input rail_limit_exceeded 403 requires_buyer_review handlers_incompatible 200 message (intersect) or 403 (ACCEPT) requires_buyer_input card_not_enabled_for_cnp 200 message requires_buyer_input credit_funding_not_allowed 403 or 200 message (intersect) requires_buyer_input cod_not_allowed, cod_open_orders_cap 403 requires_buyer_input collector_not_authorised 403 unrecoverable refund_to_ppi_forbidden 403 unrecoverable refund_not_to_source 403 requires_buyer_input pre_debit_notice_too_late 403 recoverable payment_in_doubt, debited_not_confirmed 200 message recoverable

Collector check. Before any money moves, complete MUST verify that the party in collected_by is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank, using a verified rbi_pa or bank entry in the regulatory_status of its registry record (a declared entry does not count). Otherwise the gateway returns 403 collector_not_authorised with no rail traffic. The PA-to-merchant settlement timeline is whatever the PA–merchant agreement says; the RBI PA Master Direction 2025 sets no T+1 or other T+N (para 16(a)).

docs.title: Credit and Split Tender
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page covers the ways an order is paid other than one tender in full at checkout:

  • split tender: several tenders now, or tranches over time;
  • credit at checkout: BNPL, cardless EMI, card EMI and point-of-purchase loans, with lender-signed loan offers;
  • the khata credit ledger for seller credit between known parties;
  • MSME late-payment interest, trade credit, TReDS and GeM;
  • the FX disclosure for cross-border payments.

The general payment model, handler classes and refund rules are in the Payments Overview.

Wire binding by capability

Payment plans, credit ledgers and trade documents are bound on REST, MCP and A2A (Q-44, settled 18-10-2026), each behind a capability id that a gateway lists in its profile: in.bacp.payment_plan, in.bacp.ledger and in.bacp.trade_document. The rules marked as MUST for a capability bind only a gateway that lists it. A gateway that lists none of the three keeps the earlier behaviour: a complete that carries payment_plan is refused with 400 capability_unsupported at $.payment_plan and is never ignored in favour of a single tender, and it exposes no MCP tool or A2A DataPart for these interfaces. Splitting an order into tranches over time is accepted only in the form below.

docs.title: Split tender: payment plans
docs.text:
A payment plan (schema) says how one accepted all-in total is paid. There are two kinds of split:

  • Split in space (tenders): for example a gift card for ₹1,000 plus UPI for ₹1,160 on a ₹2,160 order.
  • Split in time (tranches): for example a booking token by UPI now, a loan disbursal by the lender later, and the balance at delivery. Each tender points to a TermSheet payment.schedule[] tranche through tranche_id.
Field Content plan_id plan_ followed by 8 to 40 characters plan_hash The sha-256 over the JCS form of the tenders: the array of {tender_id, handler, amount, sequence} objects (with tranche_id when present) in ascending sequence, without payment_mandate and without any response-only field checkout_hash The hash of the BPP-signed quote. The same value for every tender. It is not the negotiation offer_hash, and nothing in BACP may assert that the two are equal. all_in_total The accepted all-in total, in paise tenders[] One to four tenders: tender_id, handler, amount, sequence (capture order), and optionally tranche_id, presence, closed_payment_mandate_ref, auth_binding_type, rail_ref, funding, receipt_id; status is planned, held, captured, in_doubt, reversal_pending, failed, released, refunded or partially_refunded; on the wire a tender record also carries reversal_deadline and psp_key (both set by the gateway) refund_allocation lifo (default), pro_rata or tender_specific atomicity saga afa_evaluated_on plan_total

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. One checkout, many payment mandates. A plan has one closed checkout mandate (one checkout_hash), and one closed payment mandate and one receipt per tender. Each tender is debited at most once.
  2. Positive amounts. Every tender amount MUST be an integer number of paise greater than zero. A zero or negative tender MUST be refused with amount_not_positive, even when the sum matches.
  3. Exact sum. The tender amounts MUST add up to all_in_total exactly. The gateway checks this and refuses a mismatch with plan_sum_mismatch. A plan has at most four tenders. Operator charges are not tenders and are not in all_in_total.
  4. Capture order and atomicity. Capture runs as a saga. Stored-value tenders (gift PPI, store credit, loyalty, e-RUPI) go first, held where the issuer supports holds, then rail tenders. If a later tender fails, the earlier ones are released or refunded to source at once. A refund of a failed, returned, rejected or cancelled PPI tender is applied to the PPI immediately (RBI Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments, para 14.3(a), as updated 30-09-2026); the T+1 of the RBI turnaround-time circular (RBI/2019-20/67, 20-09-2019; later amendments not verified as of 18-10-2026) for an on-us PPI failure is a separate deadline. A plan whose sequence breaks this order gets plan_order_invalid.
  5. Thresholds on the total. Step-up thresholds, the ₹15,000 AFA threshold, contactless and Tap & Pay exemptions, and split-order detection are evaluated on the plan total. A plan that keeps each tender under a threshold while the total is above it gets requires_escalation with reason split_tender_afa_on_total.
  6. Presence per tender. Each tender's handler MUST be eligible at that tender's presence (see handler classes). For example a gift PPI may be captured HNP, but an HP card-token tender in the same plan needs a Trusted Surface approval, and that approval shows and covers the whole plan.

  7. Code custody. The agent never sees gift-card or voucher codes. They are held in the Trusted Surface or the PSP-adapter vault, and the gateway's PSP adapter redeems them. A gift PPI backs an open mandate only when the PSP attestation states custody: principal_side, that is, that the vault is on the principal's side (the Trusted Surface or the payer PSP); with a gateway-side vault the Mandate Manager refuses issuance and the gift PPI stays human-present (Handler binding).

  8. Every tender carries an amount. An open-amount tender is refused with 400 invalid_request at $.payment_plan.tenders[i].amount.

  9. At most one tender without a hold primitive, and it comes last. A handler with no hold or void primitive cannot be unwound before the debit, so at most one tender of a plan may use one, and it MUST have the highest sequence; otherwise the plan gets plan_order_invalid. This is a BACP design rule that refuses some plans and never debits wrongly; a verified hold or void primitive for UPI P2M outside Reserve Pay and one-time-mandate blocks would relax it.
  10. An in-doubt tender freezes the plan. While any tender is in_doubt, the gateway MUST NOT release or refund any other tender, and the session stays complete_in_progress. The gateway reconciles the tender with the PSP by its derived key and applies the PSP-signed result.
  11. Cancelled only after the credit settles. When a later tender fails, the session becomes cancelled only when every unwound tender is released or refunded and its refund credit has settled. Until then the session stays complete_in_progress and the principal is told that the earlier amount "is being returned; it can take up to one day", never that "no money moved", because the issuer's own message shows two legs.
  12. One PSP key for each tender. The idempotency key that the gateway sends to the PSP for a tender MUST be derived deterministically from the gateway's own id, the session_id, the Idempotency-Key of the complete request and the tender_id (for example, the sha-256 of their JCS array), so that two sessions never share a PSP key, and so that a replay of complete never re-debits any tender and the PSP, which never sees the tender_id, can still de-duplicate. The key is recorded in the tender's psp_key, with rail_ref and reversal_deadline (the debit time plus the rail's turnaround time: T+5 for a UPI P2M debit that did not confirm, T+1 for a PPI on-us failure; RBI/2019-20/67, 20-09-2019, later amendments not verified as of 18-10-2026), so that support staff can answer a call from one record. The gateway applies a PSP result to a tender only when the receipt's closed-mandate reference and amount are that tender's.
  13. Refund allocation on the wire. A plan names lifo or tender_specific. pro_rata is refused with 400 invalid_request until Q-40 is settled.

docs.title: On the wire: in.bacp.payment_plan
docs.text:
A gateway that lists in.bacp.payment_plan (which requires in.bacp.checkout) MUST support everything in this section.

  • Offering. The session carries payment.plan_options[]. Each PlanOption has a plan_id, a plan_hash, a read-only tenders[], the all_in_total and a one-sentence description that the gateway writes from its own templates, for example hi-IN "₹1,000 गिफ्ट कार्ड से और ₹1,160 UPI से" (in English: "₹1,000 from gift card and ₹1,160 by UPI"). A voice channel reads it unchanged. No option is marked as a default or is preselected, and the gateway records in the evidence bundle the order in which it showed the options, because a gateway that also issues the PPI may be tempted to prefer its own stored value.
  • Choosing. complete carries either payment_mandate (one tender, the whole total) or payment_plan (a PlanRequest), never both. The request is sent in full: plan_id and, for each tender, tender_id, handler, amount, sequence, payment_mandate (and tranche_id where one applies).
  • Offered or Trusted-Surface-confirmed only. The tenders MUST hash to the plan_hash of an entry of payment.plan_options[], or to the plan_hash of a plan that the principal confirmed on the Trusted Surface (an approved step-up whose ts_render.plan carries it). A plan that matches neither gets 400 plan_not_offered at $.payment_plan and nothing is debited. A plan_id that names an offered option while the tenders hash differently gets 403 mandate_scope_mismatch, and no tender is captured. The agent composes no tender amount of its own: it cannot see gift-card balances, hold capability or the AFA total across tenders, which are known only to the vault, the issuers and the gateway. This version defines no agent operation that proposes a custom split to the Trusted Surface. Until such an operation exists, a plan counts as Trusted-Surface-confirmed only when it is also an entry of the session's payment.plan_options[], and the approved step-up is of this session at its current checkout_hash. A gateway MUST NOT put in ts_render.plan a plan that is not an entry of plan_options[].
  • P1, one live plan. For one checkout_hash the gateway holds at most one live plan. A complete with a different plan while one is live gets 409 plan_conflict, or 409 session_state_conflict while the session is complete_in_progress; nothing is debited and no mandate usage changes.
  • P2, never over the total. Inside the atomic section keyed on the root Checkout Mandate, the sum of held, captured and in-doubt tender amounts MUST NOT exceed all_in_total.
  • P3, each mandate names its tender. Each closed payment mandate carries tender{plan_hash, tender_id}, and its amount is that tender's amount (not the quote total). A mandate that carries tender MUST NOT pay a complete without payment_plan, and a tender's mandate whose tender does not match the plan is refused with 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.
  • P4, the principal sees the whole plan. A step-up over a plan carries ts_render.plan{plan_hash, tenders[]}; the Trusted Surface shows every tender and its amount, and its approval event carries Presentation.plan_hash and lists plan in Presentation.renders (Presentation record).
  • P5, no credentials in arguments. No MCP tool argument and no A2A DataPart carries a gift-card code, a voucher code or an instrument credential. A call that does gets 400 invalid_request and makes no rail call.

docs.title: Refunds of a split tender
docs.text:
• lifo (default): refunds reverse the capture order, each tender back to its own source under its handler's refund route, capped at what that tender captured.
  • tender_specific: used when lines were bound to a tender, for example a purpose-bound e-RUPI item.
  • A refund above a tender's capture gets refund_exceeds_capture.

Whether LIFO allocation satisfies the refund-to-source rule of PA Master Direction para 10(f) is open (Q-40).

docs.title: Token plus loan
docs.text:
A tranche plan for a high-value purchase (a vehicle, a property booking) combines a token, a loan and a balance:

  • The token tranche is limited by RERA (a booking token of at most 10% without a registered agreement) and by the cash limit of Income-tax Act, 1961 s.269ST (Income-tax Act, 2025 equivalent: s.186 per secondary sources, not verified as of 17-10-2026; cash of ₹2,00,000 or more is refused, NEG_CASH_LIMIT).
  • The loan tranche is an in.credit.* or in.fin.ocen tender with all the credit-at-checkout duties: the KFS shown, HP acceptance, disbursal to the end beneficiary's account, and a cooling-off period of at least one day.

Tranches over the wire. A gateway that lists in.bacp.payment_plan accepts tranche_id on a plan tender and displays the schedule, but a tranche carries no debit authority at complete:

  • only the tranche paid at complete is debited;
  • no later tranche is debited without its own fresh closed payment mandate and the rail's pre-debit notice at execution time (otherwise the debit is refused with no rail call);
  • a delivery tranche is a fresh closed mandate at delivery, never a pre-authorised debit; a delivery debit attempted without one is refused with no rail call;
  • if the principal refuses at delivery, the token is refunded under refund_allocation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A gift card plus a UPI Circle tender. The agent is paying a weaver it has not paid before, so a Reserve Pay block (which belongs to one seller) cannot be used, and the UPI tender runs under a Circle delegation.
