docs.title: Credit at checkout: BNPL and loan offers
docs.text:
Handlers: in.credit.bnpl (alias in.bnpl), in.credit.cardless_emi, in.fin.ocen (registry status pilot), in.fin.dealer_line, and in.card.emi. All are class C, with funding: loan or credit, so credit_disclosure_required is true.

They are governed by the RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025 (RBI/2025-26/36, DOR.STR.REC.19/21.07.001/2025-26, 08-05-2025). These apply to commercial banks, co-operative banks, NBFCs and AIFIs (para 3) and repeal the 2022 and 2023 digital-lending guidelines (para 30). The Key Fact Statement (KFS) and the annual percentage rate (APR) follow DOR.STR.REC.13/13.03.00/2024-25 (15-04-2024). Credit-card EMI is governed instead by the RBI Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions 2022 ("Credit Card MD") para 6(b)(iii) and is outside the Digital Lending Directions; loans on debit cards, including EMI, are inside them (para 29(i)). That PPIs may not be loaded from credit lines, which rules out PPI-based BNPL by non-banks, rests on an RBI letter of June 2022 that is not public and is reported only by secondary sources.

Directions since withdrawn

RBI's list of circulars withdrawn by its Department of Regulation now includes both the Digital Lending Directions 2025 and the KFS circular. They were withdrawn in the November 2025 consolidation into entity-wise directions, such as the Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025. The paragraph numbers on this page are those of the 08-05-2025 text, where every rule cited was checked. The draft consolidated directions carry the same disbursal wording, but the final paragraph numbers have not been checked. Implementers MUST map each rule to the consolidated directions that apply to their lender.

docs.title: Loan offers
docs.text:
Credit offers are carried as an offer list (schema):

Field Rule Source requested_amount The amount the buyer needs financed — offers[] Every matching offer DL Directions para 6(i), from 01-11-2025 unmatched_lenders[] Each lender that did not match, by name, with a reason. The Directions require the names; the reason is a BACP addition. para 6(i) ranking_metric A URI to a publicly pre-disclosed ranking rule (for example APR ascending). Ranking by such a metric "shall not be construed as promoting a particular product". Sponsored ranking is not allowed, because the content must be "unbiased, objective". para 6(iv)

Each LoanOffer MUST carry:

Field Content Source offer_id, lender, lender_regulated_entity The lender and its RBI registration para 6(iii) loan_amount, tenor_months, apr_pct, emi_amount, interest_amount, penal_charges The cost of credit; processing_fee is optional para 6(iii), 8(i) kfs_ref A URI to the KFS, shown before acceptance para 6(iii), 8(i) cooling_off_days At least 1 para 10(i) repayment{payee, mandate_type} The payee is always the lender; mandate_type is in.nach.debit, in.upi.autopay or manual para 9(ii), 9(iii) no_cost true only if the interest is genuinely nil Credit Card MD para 6(b)(iii) preselected Always false: no offer is pre-selected. This is BACP's reading of the bar on content that would "promote or push a product of a particular RE, including the use of dark patterns". para 6(iv) rank Position under ranking_metric para 6(iv)

Lender signature. Each offer is signed by the lender. Because the offer schema is closed, the lender's signature is carried beside the offer, not inside it. The gateway MUST verify it, and MUST reject an offer whose APR, cooling-off period or repayment payee has been altered.

An example offer:

{
  "offer_id": "lof_7Q2K91",
  "lender": "Example Finance Ltd",
  "lender_regulated_entity": "N-14.03512",
  "loan_amount": {"value": 3000000, "currency": "INR"},
  "tenor_months": 6,
  "apr_pct": 24.4,
  "emi_amount": {"value": 527300, "currency": "INR"},
  "interest_amount": {"value": 163800, "currency": "INR"},
  "processing_fee": {"value": 49900, "currency": "INR"},
  "penal_charges": "2% per month on the overdue EMI, as stated in the KFS",
  "kfs_ref": "https://lender.example.in/kfs/lof_7Q2K91",
  "cooling_off_days": 3,
  "repayment": {"payee": "Example Finance Ltd collection account", "mandate_type": "in.upi.autopay"},
  "no_cost": false,
  "preselected": false,
  "rank": 1
}

In this offer apr_pct is the annual percentage rate including the ₹499 processing fee, as the KFS rules require: about 24.4% on the ₹30,000 loan repaid in 6 EMIs of ₹5,273. The annual interest rate alone is 18.5%, and the KFS states it separately. An agent MUST show the APR, not the interest rate, as the cost of credit.

docs.title: Rules for credit at checkout
docs.text:
1. Consent to credit. A credit-funded handler MUST be refused with credit_funding_not_allowed unless the governing checkout or negotiation mandate sets credit_funding_allowed: true. The agent MUST tell the user that the payment is credit.
  2. Human acceptance. Accepting a KFS or loan agreement MUST be a human act on the Trusted Surface: a step-up with kind: confirm and reason credit_acceptance, completed by e-sign or the lender's acceptance flow. An agent that tries to accept gets credit_acceptance_requires_hp. Explicit consent is also required by E-Commerce Rule 4(9).
  3. Full disclosure. Before acceptance the user sees every field above, and every matched offer with the unmatched lenders named.
  4. Cooling-off. During the cooling-off period (set by the lender's board, at least one day) the borrower MUST be able to exit without penalty by repaying the principal and the proportionate APR. A one-time processing fee may be kept if it was disclosed in the KFS (DL Directions para 10). The post-disbursal state carries the end of the cooling-off period and an exit action.
  5. Fund flow. The DL Directions require disbursal to the borrower's bank account (para 9(i)). Their exceptions do not include a general merchant exception; the relevant one is disbursal "for specific end use, provided the loan is disbursed directly into the bank account of the end-beneficiary". A checkout loan that pays the seller MUST fit that exception: the lender documents the end use and pays the end beneficiary directly. Whether this holds when the merchant is the beneficiary is open (Q-32).
  6. Repayment to the lender only. Repayments and refunds MUST go to the lender. No agent platform or lending service provider may pool them (para 9(ii), 9(iii)). A repayment or refund addressed to anyone else gets repayment_payee_not_lender. A merchant refund on a financed purchase goes to the lender and reduces the loan; the exact mechanics are not verified.
  7. No automatic limit increase without the borrower's explicit request (para 7(ii)).
  8. Data. Need-based, explicit, auditable consent; no access to contacts, call logs or media (para 12).
  9. Neutrality. An agent that ranks or selects credit offers is acting as, or for, a lending service provider and inherits the para 6 neutrality duties.
  10. Card EMI. Before converting a card purchase to EMI the agent shows principal, interest and any upfront discount, and never calls an interest-bearing EMI "no cost". A TermSheet that claims no_cost with non-zero interest is refused (NEG_EMI_NO_COST_FALSE).
  11. OCEN and dealer lines. in.fin.ocen offers carry the lender, APR or all-in cost, tenure, repayment mandate type and KFS link, and acceptance is human-present. in.fin.dealer_line drawdowns run under a maker-checker approval and are repaid by NACH. No RBI direction specific to dealer finance was found.

Disputes go to the lender's grievance officer and, after 30 days, to the RBI Integrated Ombudsman (DL Directions para 11(iv)).

docs.title: The khata credit ledger
docs.text:
bacp.credit_ledger is a bilateral, hash-chained, signed ledger for credit between known parties: a kirana's khata, net-N trade credit, distributor credit, and GeM receivables. It is class O, but its limits are enforced by BACP rather than by a rail or issuer, so in BACP 2026-10-18 it is not open-eligible: an open (HNP) payment mandate cannot bind to it (Handler binding). No money moves on a ledger entry. Money moves on another handler, and the ledger records that handler's receipt.

Schemas: credit-ledger-entry.json, with $defs/CreditLedger for the ledger header.

docs.title: Opening a ledger
docs.text:
The CreditLedger header is signed by both parties at opening (at least two signatures). It records:

  • creditor and debtor. The creditor carries settlement_accounts[] (at most 10: a UPI VPA, or a hash of the account number and IFSC), the accounts on which it accepts payment. Only the creditor may add one later, by a signed amendment;
  • kind: khata, trade_credit, distributor_credit or gem_receivable;
  • credit_limit and default_credit_days;
  • interest_rule: none, msmed_statutory, contractual or gem_penal_1pct_pm. The header selects exactly one rule;
  • ack_window: how long the counterparty has to acknowledge an entry (ISO 8601 duration);
  • itemise_above (optional): an amount above which an entry is always acknowledged on its own, never inside a statement acknowledgement;
  • head_hash and opened_at.

docs.title: Entries
docs.text:
Entry types are opening_balance, sale, payment, credit_note, debit_note, scheme_credit, interest_msmed, interest_contractual, gem_penal_interest, adjustment, write_off and limit_change. effect is increase_receivable, decrease_receivable or none, from the creditor's side.

  • Positive amounts. Every value-bearing posting MUST have an amount greater than zero. Direction is carried by the entry type and effect, never by the sign.
  • Who posts. Only the ledger's creditor or debtor may post. The poster signs the entry.
  • Hash chain. Entries are chained by prev_hash and entry_hash. entry_hash and the entry signatures cover only the immutable posting. status, acknowledgements and dispute_ref are lifecycle fields kept outside the hash, so acknowledging an entry never rewrites history.
  • Lifecycle events are chained too. Every status change (posted, acknowledged, disputed, settled) is recorded as its own hash-chained event. An entry's current status and dispute_ref MUST equal what its chained events say, and every acknowledgement MUST verify under the counterparty's registry key. A silent change, for example from disputed back to acknowledged, therefore breaks chain verification.
  • A sale requires due_date and credit_terms. A payment or credit_note requires settles[], the sale entries it closes. A payment requires settlement_evidence.
  • Each entry carries ledger_after: balance, credit limit, overdue amount and ageing buckets (0–30, 31–45, 46–60, 61–90 and over 90 days). A balance confirmation can be exported from the ledger.

docs.title: Acknowledgement: the creditor cannot self-confirm
docs.text:
• An entry is acknowledged by the counterparty of the poster, never by the poster. When the seller books a sale, only the buyer can acknowledge it. An acknowledgement by anyone else gets ack_not_by_counterparty.
  • The acknowledgement MUST be signed with the counterparty's key, whatever the channel: a signature, a Trusted Surface tap, an SMS link, a voice confirmation, or an assisted operator. Every channel ends in the counterparty's signature over the entry hash, and the channel is recorded as method.
  • A payment entry is acknowledged automatically from the rail receipt it cites (auto_from_rail_receipt), because the PSP's signature is the evidence, only when the receipt's payee matches one of creditor.settlement_accounts[] (or settlement_evidence.new_payee after TReDS discounting) and the receipt's issued_at is not before the settled sale's at. A receipt without a payee matches no settlement account. A receipt that pays someone else, or that predates the sale, does not settle the sale: the entry is accepted as pending_ack for the creditor, with message settlement_payee_unmatched, and settles nothing until the creditor acknowledges it. A shop may collect on several VPAs, a family member's or a soundbox's, so a mismatch is not refused; it waits for the creditor's tap, SMS link or voice confirmation.
  • Statement acknowledgement. Beside the per-entry form, a gateway that lists in.bacp.ledger SHOULD support acknowledging a range: the subject is ledger_range{ledger_id, through_seq, head_hash}, and one acknowledgement event names the head_hash and covers every pending entry up to through_seq that the other party posted. An entry that the acknowledging party posted is never covered and keeps its status. A payment entry in pending_ack after settlement_payee_unmatched is never covered by a statement acknowledgement. The creditor acknowledges it on its own, on a render that shows the payee it was paid to. The principal sees the count, the closing balance, the oldest unpaid date and every itemised entry first. A statement acknowledgement MUST NOT cover an entry above the ledger's itemise_above or above the 90th percentile of the amounts that the poster has posted on this ledger. The 90th percentile is computed by the nearest-rank method over the amounts of the poster's entries on this ledger that were acknowledged before the range; entries inside the range are not in the set. With fewer than 10 such entries, every entry in the range above the largest earlier acknowledged entry of that poster is acknowledged one by one. Such an entry is acknowledged one by one (422 invalid_request at $.subject.through_seq otherwise, with no change). An entry posted after the render moves the head: the acknowledgement then gets 409 ledger_head_mismatch, and the new entry is not covered. A per-entry dispute after a statement acknowledgement stays possible and moves only that entry. The 90th-percentile limit is a BACP design value against a hidden inflated line, not a legal rule, and has not been tested against trade practice.
  • An entry still unacknowledged when ack_window expires becomes disputed, with a dispute_ref; this applies only where a notice of the entry was delivered to the counterparty, and whether silence after a delivered notice is acceptance or dispute is flagged to counsel (Q-83). A disputed entry does not count toward the balance or ageing, cannot be acknowledged (entry_disputed), and can be settled or credit-noted only after the dispute is resolved.

Entry status values: pending_ack, acknowledged, disputed, settled, partially_settled, overdue, written_off.

docs.title: Booking and settling
docs.text:
• Sale. A sale is booked only within credit_limit − balance and within the negotiation mandate's payment.credit_ledger.max_outstanding. Otherwise it gets credit_limit_exceeded. A sale counts against the checkout mandate's budgets and against max_outstanding only when a gateway complete books it under the buyer's mandate, inside the root's atomic section; a sale that the creditor posts never touches the budgets. A disputed entry keeps its count until it is resolved or credit-noted. A payment that settles a sale counts within the sale, never on top of it, and releases max_outstanding only; a credit_note releases both (Q-46, settled). bacp.credit_ledger is not open-eligible in this release (Q-59, settled as closed), so a sale is booked with the principal present (HP).
  • Payment. A payment entry MUST cite a PSP-signed receipt from another handler: settlement_evidence.receipt_id with its RRN or UTR. The gateway verifies the receipt signature against the PSP's registry key, and checks that the amount, result and RRN or UTR match. A screenshot or any other evidence MUST be refused, and the sale stays unpaid. A receipt settles ledger entries at most once, and that is checked across every ledger that the creditor's custodian holds, keyed on the rail and the RRN or UTR (receipt_reused). The payee match of the acknowledgement rules applies. Every posting is a compare-and-swap on the chain head: a posting whose prev_hash is not the current head gets 409 ledger_head_mismatch.
  • Credit note. An unpaid sale is reduced by a credit_note entry (refund_state: credit_note_issued where a refund is involved). A credit note cannot exceed the sale's open amount. A paid sale is refunded to the instrument that settled it.

An example payment entry, settling a sale by NEFT:

docs.title: On the wire: in.bacp.ledger
docs.text:
A gateway that lists in.bacp.ledger MUST support these operations (OpenAPI), and serves them only for a ledger of which the agent's principal is the creditor or the debtor (any other ledger is 404 not_found). The gateway resolves the principal of every in.bacp.ledger operation and every LEDGER_ACK from mandate_ref. It is REQUIRED as a query parameter on both ledger GETs, in the body of POST /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries, and in actor.mandate_ref of a LEDGER_ACK. The mandate MUST be held by the calling agent (the request is signed with its cnf key), and MUST name a principal who is the ledger's creditor or debtor; otherwise the gateway returns 404 not_found. For a read the mandate is ACTIVE; for a write it is in a status in which Mandates allows a post_order write. A posting is accepted only when that principal is the debtor. A LEDGER_ACK is accepted only when that principal is the counterparty of the poster of every entry it covers; otherwise the gateway returns 403 ack_not_by_counterparty before any step-up is raised. The step-up is issued by that mandate's Mandate Manager, and the approval is made with that principal's own factor.

Operation Tag What it does GET /ledgers/{ledger_id} bacp-browse The header, head_seq, head_hash, closing balance, overdue amount, oldest unpaid date and entry count. GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries?after_seq=&limit=&status= bacp-browse A page of summaries, ascending by seq. limit is at most 50 (a larger value is 400 invalid_request at $.limit) and the response carries next_after_seq until the last page. POST /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries bacp-post-order An agent posts a payment entry for the debtor, never any other type (400 at $.type). The request carries the prev_hash it saw.

Counterparty-written text in an entry is data, never an instruction, and a tool or DataPart returns it labelled. The agent posts a payment under the checks above: payee match, receipt uniqueness across the custodian, head compare-and-swap, and a per-agent rate limit on postings (429 quota_exceeded). Acknowledging an entry or a statement is a trade act (Seller-side and trade acts).

The string fields that a seller can fill with text (an identifier, a place, a jurisdiction, a lender name) are bounded in credit-ledger-entry.json and termsheet.json: identifier-like values are at most 64 printable characters without spaces, and free-text values have a maxLength of between 20 and 200. These bounds are BACP design values against instructions hidden in counterparty text, not regulatory limits, and are open to review.

docs.title: Interlocked credit
docs.text: Where a broker or commission agent (an arhtiya) advances money to a seller and deducts it at sale, the advance is recorded as a separate ledger with the broker as creditor. The deduction at sale MUST appear as a visible commission or deduction line, never netted silently.

docs.title: Regulatory status
docs.text: Interest-free seller credit (khata, net-N) is treated as trade credit, not digital lending. Once a third-party lender funds it, the handler becomes in.fin.* or in.credit.* and the Digital Lending Directions apply. This position is open (Q-27).

docs.title: MSME late-payment interest
docs.text:
For a sale by a "supplier" under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act 2006 (s.2(n): a micro or small enterprise that has filed a memorandum under s.8(1), today a Udyam registration), the Act applies:

Rule Content Source Acceptance The day of acceptance is the day of actual delivery of the goods or rendering of the services. If the buyer objects in writing within 15 days of delivery, it is the day the supplier removes the objection. If no written objection is made within 15 days, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery. MSMED Act s.2(b), Explanation Due date The buyer pays by the date agreed in writing, which "in no case" may exceed 45 days from the day of acceptance or deemed acceptance. Without a written agreement, payment is due before the "appointed day", the day after 15 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance. MSMED Act ss.2(b), 15 Interest On late payment, "compound interest with monthly rests" at "three times of the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank", notwithstanding any agreement MSMED Act s.16 Tax From AY 2024-25, a sum payable to a micro or small enterprise beyond the s.15 time limit is deductible only in the year it is actually paid. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 01-04-2026, the same rule is s.37(2)(g). Income-tax Act, 1961 s.43B(h) (inserted by the Finance Act 2023, w.e.f. 01-04-2024); Income-tax Act, 2025 s.37(2)(g)

The ledger implements this as follows:

  • msmed.statutory_due_date = the earlier of the agreed date and acceptance + 45 days, or acceptance + 15 days when written_agreement is false. For micro and small suppliers the schema caps credit_terms.credit_days at 45. A firm offer of longer credit to such a supplier is refused (NEG_MSMED_CREDIT_CAP).
  • Acceptance date. The acceptance date of an acceptance-dated sale is the delivery date (MSMED Act s.2(b), Explanation (ii): where no written objection is made within 15 days, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery). The delivery date is evidenced by a buyer-signed GRN, or by seller-posted delivery evidence (proof_of_delivery, lorry_receipt) that the buyer counter-signed or that carries a third-party reference the buyer can check (an e-way bill number or a transporter signature); the entry records which as msmed.acceptance_basis (grn, attested_delivery). Seller-only evidence is recorded with acceptance_basis: unattested, no acceptance date or due date is derived from it, and the gateway notifies the debtor when the evidence is posted. A GRN that accepts everything does not move the date. Where a written objection is made within 15 days of delivery, the acceptance date is the date the supplier removed the objection (Explanation (i)). The GRN and delivery dates MUST NOT precede the invoice date or lie in the future, and the acceptance date is never a free parameter of the creditor. This rule replaces an earlier requirement of a buyer-signed GRN for every acceptance-dated sale, and is pending counsel (Q-21, Q-83). How a buyer's objection travels on the network, and whether it can be checked by machine, is open (Q-21, Q-33); until Q-33 fixes the carriage, a GRN, CRAC or objection filed through an agent is recorded and not sent to the seller, and a recorded act never sets or moves the due date (Seller-side and trade acts).
  • Alerts. BACP raises an alert 5 days before the statutory due date and flags the debtor's tax consequence (msmed.tax_flag).
  • Interest without double charging. These are BACP ledger rules, not rules of the MSMED Act:
    • Overdue statutory interest is posted as interest_msmed entries with interest_basis: 3x_rbi_bank_rate_compound_monthly and the bank_rate_pct used.
    • Each interest_msmed entry carries the cumulative interest_accrued for its sale and posts only the increment over interest already accrued for that sale. Re-running the accrual never charges the same interest twice.
    • The ledger header selects one interest_rule. A ledger MUST NOT accrue both statutory and contractual interest on the same overdue amount for the same period. This is BACP policy. Section 16 makes the statutory interest payable "notwithstanding anything contained in any agreement", so a contractual rule never displaces it for a micro or small supplier.
    • Interest stops accruing on the amount settled by a rail-evidenced payment.
  • Traders. The Ministry of MSME Office Memorandum of 02-07-2021 restricts the benefits of Udyam-registered retail and wholesale traders "to Priority Sector Lending only". Whether that excludes them from s.15 as a matter of law is open (Q-21). For a trader, BACP raises a warning only and does not accrue statutory interest.

docs.title: TReDS
docs.text:
Handler: in.fin.treds (class N, non-paying). The Trade Receivables Discounting System is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (Trade Receivables Discounting System) Directions, 2026 (issued 23-06-2026; circular number RBI/DPSS/2026-27/406 not verified as of 17-10-2026), which repeal the 2014 TReDS guidelines. RBI lists five authorised TReDS operators: RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart (A.TReDS), C2treds and DTX (KredX).

  1. The MSME seller uploads an invoice the buyer has accepted, creating a factoring unit. Once it is accepted, the buyer's obligation to pay on the due date is unconditional, with no option of set-off (Directions para 15(i)).
  2. Financiers bid, and the seller accepts a bid.
  3. The financier funds the seller without recourse to the seller (Directions para 20).
  4. The buyer pays the financier on the due date, by a NACH debit.

Binding rules:

  • Each factoring unit MUST be bound to the GST e-invoice IRN and the buyer's acceptance. An invoice whose IRN has already been financed MUST be refused.
  • After discounting, the ledger's settlement_evidence.new_payee is the financier, and the buyer's due-date NACH debit pays the financier.
  • Companies with turnover above ₹250 crore, and all CPSEs, must onboard on TReDS. The Ministry of MSME notification S.O. 4845(E) of 07-11-2024 cut the threshold from ₹500 crore to ₹250 crore, with an onboarding deadline of 31-03-2025 (confirmed by PIB; Gazette text not verified as of 17-10-2026). Under a Ministry of MSME notification of 30-06-2026, operating CPSEs must also route the settlement of invoices from MSMEs through an RBI-authorised TReDS platform (reported by PIB; Gazette text not verified as of 17-10-2026). BACP records the buyer's TReDS onboarding status and SHOULD offer TReDS as a settlement option on MSME invoices for such buyers.
  • Funding is same day (T0) for bids accepted before a cut-off, otherwise T+1, with the buyer's NACH debit on the due date (vendor; the cut-off time is given inconsistently).
  • Buyer-side and seller-side agents act only within the corporate's platform entitlements and with human signatory approval.

docs.title: GeM receivables
docs.text:
A gem_receivable ledger tracks a Government e-Marketplace order:

  • The consignee issues the CRAC (Consignee Receipt and Acceptance Certificate) within 10 days of the submission of proof of delivery; otherwise GeM auto-generates a CRAC, marking all the PRC (Provisional Receipt Certificate) quantities as accepted (GeM FAQ).
  • The buyer pays within 10 calendar days of the CRAC.
  • Late payment carries penal interest of 1% a month, prorated on a 30-day month. This interest is deposited "in an account maintained by GeM" and is not paid to the vendor. It does not cover interest payable under the MSMED Act or the contract. BACP MUST disclose that, and records it as a gem_penal_interest entry with effect: none.
  • For non-PFMS buyers the GeM Pool Account block reference is recorded at order time; an order without one is shown as unfunded.

Sources: Department of Expenditure OM F.6/18/2019-PPD of 03-07-2020, for procurements under GFR Rule 149 from 01-10-2020; GeM FAQ for the CRAC timeline. The GeM GTC clause that carries these terms was not checked. Reports that individual buyers override them with 45, 60 or 90-day terms are not verified.

docs.title: FX disclosure for cross-border payments
docs.text:
All BACP settlement amounts are INR. For a cross-border payment, an fx view (schema) MAY appear on the TermSheet, the receipt and the disclosures, to show the foreign-currency amount, the rate and the markup:

Field Rule currency ISO 4217 code, never INR foreign_amount Integer minor units of currency, at least 1 rate INR per one unit of currency, greater than zero markup_bps Markup in basis points, zero or more inr_total An INR amount in paise: round(foreign_amount × rate × (1 + markup_bps / 10000)) rate_source, quoted_at Optional

The gateway MUST reject an fx view that is inconsistent with its inr_total. Every settlement amount remains INR.

{
  "currency": "USD",
  "foreign_amount": 250000,
  "rate": 84,
  "markup_bps": 100,
  "inr_total": {"value": 21210000, "currency": "INR"},
  "rate_source": "acquirer",
  "quoted_at": "2026-10-13T11:30:00+05:30"
}

Related cross-border rules:

  • Card AFA. A non-recurring, cross-border, card-not-present payment needs AFA when the overseas acquirer asks for it (RBI Authentication Directions 2025 para 10, from 01-10-2026). See Cards.
  • Determining cross-border. A payment that the merchant declares cross-border is treated as cross-border. A declaration that it is not cross-border cannot override merchant, acquirer or FX data that says it is.
  • PA cross-border collections and payments are capped at ₹25,00,000 per transaction (RBI PA Master Direction 2025 para 11(d)).
  • Export realisation. Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 (FEMA 23(R)/2026-RB, in force from 01-10-2026), as amended by FEMA 23(R)/(1)/2026-RB of 22-09-2026, export proceeds are realised within 9 months: for goods from the date of shipment, for services from the date of invoice, and for goods exported to a warehouse outside India from the date of sale from the warehouse. Exports invoiced or settled in INR have 12 months (Reg 5(1)), and the AD bank may extend the period. If proceeds stay unrealised for more than one year past the due date, the exporter may export further only against full advance or an irrevocable LC (Reg 13). These Regulations replace the FEM (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations 2015, under which the period was also 9 months (FEMA 23(R)/(8)/2026-RB, 05-06-2026; not verified as of 17-10-2026). bacp.trade.export_realisation tracks the due date, with an alert 30 days before it.
  • Whether a cross-border transfer of personal data meets the DPDP Act's restrictions is not checked by the FX view.

docs.title: Who pays
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. It is informative: it explains the rules that other pages make normative, and it states each fact with its binding status and an "as of" date. Where it says MUST or SHOULD, it repeats a rule from the page it links.

BACP makes normative what the principal pays and to whom. It leaves informative how sellers, payment aggregators (PAs) and banks split their own costs. So BACP has no mdr, fee_bearer, payer or settlement_eta field, and none of the seller's own costs appears in a quote line, a total, a ts_render, a message to the principal or a receipt.

The normative rules are in Fees on the payer's screen, Fee-bearer change, the handler intersection, Refunds, the Trusted Surface read-out, Ranking by payment rungs and Operator compensation.

docs.title: The charges
docs.text:
"Binding" says what kind of text the rule comes from. A rate that is announced and not in force says so. Nothing on this page is a net figure for any party.

Charge Who sets it Who bears it at the rail Who may re-allocate it Where it appears in BACP Binding source and status (as of 18-10-2026) Merchant discount rate (MDR) NPCI's UPI and Services Steering Committee for UPI; the acquirer's rate card for cards The merchant, paid to its acquiring bank NPCI's FAQ says on-boarded merchants cannot pass it on to customers on UPI Nowhere. It is never a payer line and never in a receipt UPI: 0.4% above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 from ₹75,000, flat ₹5 for listed categories; announced, not in force; the start is "immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately" and no date was found. FAQ and press release, not a circular. Debit cards: RBI/2017-18/105 (06-12-2017) asks banks to ensure merchants do not pass on MDR; in force not verified as of 18-10-2026. PA commission The PA, by agreement with the merchant The merchant, as a permitted debit from the PA's settlement The PA–merchant agreement Nowhere PA Master Direction 2025, Table 1: commission is a permitted debit; settlement is "as per the agreement" and "must transparently mention the settlement timelines". Binding on the PA. Convenience fee The seller, or the party that runs the payment page The buyer NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 asks that it is disclosed upfront and consistent across debit modes; it binds the Payee PSP convenience charge (TermSheet) or convenience_fee total, with a recipient, optionally scoped by applies_to_handlers NPCI circular (18-09-2026), para 7.5; PA Master Direction para 10(c) (charges other than the price "distinctly displayed to the payer prior to the transaction"). RBI Card Directions 2025 para 77 is context for card fees and binds issuers. COD fee The seller The buyer The seller's terms cod_fee, scoped to in.cod Seller's terms; the PA escrow is not operated for cash on delivery (PA Master Direction para 18(b)). Finder fee or channel margin ONDC network terms and the buyer app's agreement with the seller The seller The seller and the buyer app Never a quote line. Carried unchanged in intermediary_compensation[] and logged ONDC buyer_app_finder_fee_type and _amount and np_fees, read from ONDC's validator, not a policy text. RTO (return to origin) fee and other return charges The seller Decided by the seller's disclosed terms, within the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 The seller's terms; the Rules bar a refusal to refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods (rules 6(3), 7(4)) rto_fee, restocking_fee and return_shipping charge codes, with a recipient and a refund_rule BACP policy for the codes. Whether a disclosed charge may be kept is open (Q-81). Operator fee The agent operator, assisted operator or buyer app The buyer, per order None in BACP: the line discloses a fee and is not a licence to charge one operator_charges[], outside all_in_total and inside the amount the principal pays BACP policy. NPCI FAQ Q17 and the Rules' r.5(7) (from 01-01-2027) may reach it; open (Q-79). TCS (tax collected at source) The tax law The e-commerce operator collects it from its payments to the supplier None Not a BACP line CGST Act s.52: 0.25% on the CGST limb, per CBIC notification 15/2024-CT (rate checked; the only copy held is the text before gazette publication, so no date from which it applies is stated). TDS (tax deducted at source) The tax law The e-commerce operator deducts it from its payments to the seller None Not a BACP line Income-tax Act s.194-O. Rate not verified as of 18-10-2026.

The two texts on small-merchant (P2PM) status are quoted on Rail Bindings and not reconciled. The MDR on a refund is unknown: no public NPCI or RBI text found says whether MDR is reversed when a refund is made (not verified as of 18-10-2026). BACP's refund rule does not depend on the answer, and a refund is never reduced by MDR or PA fees.

docs.title: Settlement and the seller's terms
docs.text: BACP does not carry a settlement_eta. The seller's settlement terms are ONDC's settlement_basis, settlement_window and withholding_amount, carried unchanged. The PA marketplace limits (PA Master Direction paras 10(b) and 13(f)) stay open with RBI (Q-51).

docs.title: Money maps
docs.text:
These maps show who receives money from the payer's money, with no net figure.

A kirana counter, paid by UPI at the shop. The payer pays the shop's VPA. The merchant's acquiring bank and the PA, if any, take their costs from the merchant's side under their own agreements. BACP sees only the order total and the receipt's rrn and utr.

An ONDC prepaid order. The buyer app or the seller app collects (collected_by). The payer pays one amount. Settlement between the collector, the seller and any logistics provider follows ONDC's settlement terms. Who bears the collector's P2M MDR when the buyer app collects is open with ONDC (Q-80); this reading is an analysis, not a published rule.

A direct-to-consumer order with a return. The payer pays the total, including any disclosed charge lines. On a return the refund goes back to the original method. It equals the amount paid less only the lines that the terms disclosed as retained and that the Rules permit; a short refund gets refund_short_of_terms, and the money is not blocked.

A B2B order on NEFT with net-30 terms. The payer pays on the due date by NEFT, outside any quote line. MDR does not apply. A credit-ledger entry or a term sheet states the terms (Credit and Split Tender).

docs.title: How a seller or an operator can game the lines
docs.text:
These are the patterns the rules are written to catch.

  • Steering to MDR-free primitives. A seller or a gateway ranks sellers by whether they carry a rail with no MDR. The default ranking must not use rungs, MDR or the finder fee (Ranking by payment rungs).
  • Splitting. An agent splits one order into payments under ₹2,000 to change the fee a seller bears. An agent SHOULD NOT do it, and the suspected-split-order check applies.
  • Uniform-fee recovery after para 7.5. A seller that may not surcharge UPI charges the same convenience fee on every debit mode. That is lawful under para 7.5 when it is disclosed upfront; BACP does not warn on it, and the fee is in the total from round 1. A fee that first appears in a later round is drip pricing.
  • Mode-specific discounts. A discount for one mode is the mirror of a surcharge on the others. Whether it is a negative surcharge under para 7.5 is open with counsel.
  • Discount for lock. A discount offered only if the principal sets up a block or a mandate can nudge her to a rung that costs the seller less. BACP shows an offer with its condition (Discounts) and does not rule on whether such an offer is lawful.
  • Collector incidence. On a buyer-app-collected order, the party that collects may be the P2M merchant. Which party bears the MDR is open (Q-80).
  • Operator incentives. A recommender that is paid by the recommended seller is the main gaming risk. The operator discloses how it is paid in the mandate notice before the principal approves, an item whose selection is paid for is sponsored with by: agent, and the finder fee is never a quote line.

docs.title: What each human sees
docs.text:
• A principal at a screen. The total, each fee line with who receives it, and the remaining figure as one amount, before the factor.
  • A principal on voice, IVR or UPI 123PAY. The same, read in her language from the Trusted Surface's own templates. A feature-phone or IVR principal never sees a payment page and cannot follow a hash, so each fee line is read one at a time. An order with no fee line adds no audio.
  • A principal whose agent pays on its own (HNP). She agreed to the operator's compensation at mandate approval and, if she set convenience_fees, to a convenience fee up to her cap. Anything else raises a confirm step-up first.
  • A seller. A seller's quote has no operator line: the operator's fee sits outside the BPP quote.

docs.title: Informative and normative
docs.text: Every statement above about an NPCI FAQ is about an FAQ, which is not a circular. A statement about a rate in the future says "announced, not in force" until a date is notified. This page is re-checked at each release against the sources, and its dated facts (the MDR start, RBI/2017-18/105, the passage of Bill No. 150 of 2026) are re-verified then.

docs.title: Handler Registry
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

The handler registry lists every Indian payment mode BACP can bind to: 57 handlers across UPI, cards, net banking, account-to-account transfers, NACH, PPIs, credit, COD, BBPS, e-RUPI, e₹, AePS, transit, trade finance, cross-border, GeM, PA settlement, cheques and the BACP credit ledger. Each entry is a handler descriptor: a JSON document that validates against handler-descriptor.json.

Descriptors are data. Limits, AFA models, refund routes and notice rules are configuration that a gateway loads, not code. When a regulator changes a limit, the descriptor changes and the gateway's behaviour follows without a code release.

How handlers are used at payment time is defined in the Payments Overview. The rail-by-rail rules are in Rail Bindings.

docs.title: Descriptor format
docs.text:
A descriptor has the fields below. Required fields are marked R.

Field R Content handler_id R The canonical id: in.<family>.<variant> for an Indian rail or instrument, bacp.<construct> for a BACP-native construct. Pattern common.json#/$defs/HandlerId. aliases[] Legacy ids that resolve to this handler during the deprecation window. A trailing .* makes a glob alias. See alias resolution. name R Display name as language-tagged text, e.g. {"en-IN": "UPI AutoPay (recurring e-mandate)"}. family R Rail family: upi, card, netbanking, a2a, nach, ppi, credit, cod, bbps, voucher, cbdc, aeps, transit, trade_finance, cross_border, government, pa, cheque, ledger, loyalty, store_credit, pos. kind R payment, mandate_registration, financing, security_verification, tracker or ledger. status R live, pilot, reserved or deprecated. See governance. rail R operator (required), network, and params such as qr_type, network, kyc, funding, direction. regulator[] R One or more {body, instrument, ref}, e.g. {"body": "RBI", "instrument": "E-mandate Framework 2026"}. presence R human_presence (required, mandate or none), hp (may run with a human present), hnp (none, rail_enforced or order_only), device_bound, assisted_only. rail_enforced means a standing authority whose limits the rail or issuer enforces. order_only means the order may be placed HNP but payment happens later with a human (COD). binding R class (O, C, A, D or N; see handler classes), open_eligible, open_primitives[] (the mandate_primitives[].type values that may back an open mandate; only primitives whose limits_enforced_by is rail or issuer, and at least one when open_eligible is true), open_requires (a condition in words, e.g. "only with an AFA-registered PPI e-mandate"), and closed_auth[]: the per-transaction authorisations a closed HP payment may use (upi.pin, upi.biometric, card.3ds, card.otp, card.passkey, netbanking.login_otp, maker_checker, aadhaar_biometric, voucher_code, wallet_pin, kfs_esign, dsc, cash_at_door, parent_rail_binding). mandate_primitives[] R The rail object that carries the standing authority: type (e.g. sbmd_block, otm_block, circle_delegation, upi_autopay_umn, card_emandate, agentic_token_intent, nach_umrn, ppi_emandate, balance_cap, voucher, programmability_rules, upms_registration, topup_mandate, loan_sanction, payee_binding, approval_policy, assisted_session, credit_limit, factoring_unit, gpa_block, pps_registration), ref_name (what rail_binding.rail_ref holds, e.g. UMN, UMRN, SBMD block id), limits_enforced_by (rail, issuer, merchant, lender, bacp, none), payee_scope (single_merchant, single_biller, single_creditor, any_merchant, purpose_locked, issuer_contracted, lender, n_a) and multi_capture. issuer_contracted means that a seller accepts the instrument only through a contract with its issuer, as for a gift PPI (RBI Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments, paras 2.6 and 11.4.3), so that a gateway checks the seller's acceptance before it ranks the rung. limits[] R Each limit has a name (per_txn, per_txn_min, per_day, per_month, per_year, first_24h, balance, block_amount, mandate_max, voucher_max, no_afa_debit, no_afa_debit_special_categories, validity, devices, pps_threshold, cash_threshold), one of amount (integer paise), duration (ISO 8601) or count, an applies_to note, a source citation, a verification grade (verified, secondary, vendor, unverified, conflict), a conflict_note where sources disagree, configurable, and an optional bound (min or max) that says whether the value is a floor or a ceiling, for example the one-year minimum validity of a gift PPI. afa R model (per_txn_2fa, at_registration_and_first_debit, at_registration_only, at_block_creation, at_provisioning, exempt, exempt_below_threshold, biometric_assisted, maker_checker, loan_acceptance, voucher_code, none_cash, n_a), threshold and threshold_special (amounts above which AFA is needed), pre_debit_notice (required_24h, bacp_policy_24h, exempt, unknown, not_applicable) verification (optional; how well the source citation was checked, on the scale of limits[].verification, so that an NPCI-layer citation is graded separately from the RBI layer), and rbi_annex1_item (the row of Annexure-1 of RBI/2025-26/79 that exempts the handler: REQUIRED when model is exempt or exempt_below_threshold, FORBIDDEN when it is at_block_creation or at_registration_only, so that Reserve Pay or UPI Circle is never labelled an RBI exemption; the upper bound is kept by the registry, because Annexure-1 says that later additions also apply). refund R route (source, source_with_card_credit_consent, same_ppi, release_block_or_source, lender, user_elected_account, same_balance, issuer_or_sponsor, new_credit_push, ledger_credit_note, n_a, unverified), failed_txn_tat (ISO 8601 duration), compensation_per_day, notes. See refunds. dispute R channels[] (e.g. UDIR, issuer billing dispute, RBI Integrated Ombudsman, Bharat Connect complaints, GeM incident management) and window. settlement R mechanism (free text), evidence_refs[] (the keys a receipt may carry: rrn, utr, umn, umrn, arn, auth_code, bconnect_txn_id, voucher_id, cbdc_txn_id, factoring_unit_id, loan_id, lc_no, ebg_no, gem_order_no, crac_no, pfms_payment_id, pa_order_id, cheque_no, uetr, ledger_entry_id, awb, none), escrow (pa_escrow, none, gem_pool_account, platform, n_a) and timeline_source. The PA-to-merchant timeline follows the PA–merchant agreement; there is no RBI T+N. data_minimisation R payment_leg_fields (by default payee, amount, mandate_ref, checkout_hash), never_collect (always includes pin, otp, card_pan, cvv, card_expiry, netbanking_credentials, aadhaar_number, biometric and basket; vouchers add voucher_code_plaintext), retain_only (cards: last four digits and issuer) and basket_blind. funding R debit, credit, prepaid, cash, voucher, loan, cbdc, trade_credit or n_a. funding_sources[] Every source of funds a payer can bring to the handler, when it is more than funding. It MUST contain funding. UPI Reserve Pay lists debit and credit, because a block can sit on a savings, current or overdraft account or on a RuPay credit card or a pre-sanctioned credit line (NPCI Consolidated Circular para 16.1). The source of a given mandate is the one its payer PSP attests, never the list. credit_disclosure_required MUST be true when funding is credit or loan: the agent discloses that the payment is credit and holds the user's prior consent. segments[] b2c, b2b, g2b, c2c, assisted, cross_border. requirements[] Identifiers of the requirements the descriptor implements (see Regulatory Mapping). sources[] R Citations for the descriptor's content. notes Free text.

The schema enforces these cross-field rules:

  1. binding.open_eligible: true requires presence.hnp: rail_enforced.
  2. binding.open_eligible: true requires a non-empty binding.open_primitives.
  3. presence.device_bound: true requires binding.open_eligible: false.
  4. funding of credit or loan requires credit_disclosure_required: true.
  5. presence.hnp: rail_enforced requires at least one entry of mandate_primitives whose limits_enforced_by is rail or issuer. A descriptor whose limits only a merchant or BACP enforces is hnp: none.
  6. funding_sources, when present, contains funding, and binding.open_primitives never lists none.

That every binding.open_primitives entry is one of the descriptor's own mandate_primitives[].type values with limits_enforced_by rail or issuer cannot be expressed in JSON Schema. scripts/validate.py checks it for the registry, and registry review MUST check it for a proposed descriptor.

An abridged descriptor (the in.upi.autopay entry, with optional fields and the per-field citations shortened) looks like this:

{
  "handler_id": "in.upi.autopay",
  "aliases": ["upi.autopay"],
  "name": {"en-IN": "UPI AutoPay (recurring e-mandate)"},
  "family": "upi",
  "kind": "payment",
  "status": "live",
  "rail": {"operator": "NPCI"},
  "regulator": [{"body": "RBI", "instrument": "E-mandate Framework 2026"}],
  "presence": {"human_presence": "mandate", "hp": true, "hnp": "rail_enforced"},
  "binding": {"class": "O", "open_eligible": true, "open_primitives": ["upi_autopay_umn"], "closed_auth": ["upi.pin"]},
  "mandate_primitives": [{"type": "upi_autopay_umn", "ref_name": "UMN", "limits_enforced_by": "rail", "payee_scope": "single_merchant", "multi_capture": true}],
  "limits": [
    {"name": "no_afa_debit", "amount": {"value": 1500000, "currency": "INR"},
     "source": {"file": "RBI E-mandate Framework 2026", "section": "8", "label": "RBI"}, "verification": "verified", "configurable": false}
  ],
  "afa": {"model": "at_registration_and_first_debit",
          "threshold": {"value": 1500000, "currency": "INR"},
          "threshold_special": {"value": 10000000, "currency": "INR"},
          "pre_debit_notice": "required_24h"},
  "refund": {"route": "source", "failed_txn_tat": "P5D", "compensation_per_day": {"value": 10000, "currency": "INR"}},
  "dispute": {"channels": ["UDIR in payer app", "MyUPI automated chargeback", "RBI Integrated Ombudsman"]},
  "settlement": {"mechanism": "NPCI UPI settlement cycles", "evidence_refs": ["rrn", "utr"], "escrow": "pa_escrow"},
  "data_minimisation": {"payment_leg_fields": ["payee", "amount", "mandate_ref", "checkout_hash"],
                        "never_collect": ["pin", "otp", "card_pan", "cvv", "card_expiry", "netbanking_credentials", "aadhaar_number", "biometric", "basket"],
                        "basket_blind": true},
  "funding": "debit",
  "sources": [{"file": "RBI E-mandate Framework 2026", "section": "8", "label": "RBI"}]
}

docs.title: Registry governance
docs.text:
The registry is maintained in the specification repository as source/handlers/registry.json and is versioned with the specification. Each descriptor has a status:

Status Meaning May back a payment live The rail or instrument is generally available, and its rules are documented. Yes, subject to its class pilot The rail runs as a pilot or closed user group, or has no general availability (e.g. UPI Circle software delegates, network agentic card tokens, retail and programmable e₹, OCEN), or BACP has not verified how agents may use it (e-RUPI, until Q-38 is answered). Only when the gateway's conformance attestation lists that pilot in pilots[] reserved The id is held for a rail that is not yet published or not open to agents (in.upi.uap, in.cbdc.wholesale). No deprecated The handler is being withdrawn. No

Rules for registry content:

  • Every limit MUST cite its source and carry a verification grade. A limit graded conflict MUST carry a conflict_note. Where sources conflict, a gateway SHOULD enforce the stricter value unless the deployment documents a different choice.
  • A limit whose regulator may change it SHOULD be configurable: true.
  • A registry in which an exact alias maps to two descriptors, or a canonical id is also declared as an alias, MUST be rejected at load.
  • Every descriptor MUST validate against handler-descriptor.json.
  • Status changes (pilot to live, reserved to pilot) are registry changes and follow the proposal process.
  • Eligibility is evaluated against the current registry at every complete, not when a mandate was issued. A change that makes an active mandate's binding ineligible (a downgrade from live to pilot, reserved or deprecated, or a primitive removed from binding.open_primitives) pauses the affected mandates (Handler binding). Mandate Managers and gateways take the registry from the dated release, never from a gateway's GET /payment-handlers, and a gateway adopts a downgrade within 24 hours of the published_at of the publication that makes it. There is no registry-signed snapshot: no party holds a registry key.

docs.title: Release manifest
docs.text: Each publication of the registry files has a release manifest, source/handlers/release.json, valid against registry-release.json. It names the registry_version, a strictly increasing registry_serial (backports included), the published_at instant in IST and the sha-256 digest, over the JCS form, of registry.json and of the conformance-authority list. A copy is newer than another when its serial is greater. scripts/validate.py recomputes the digests, and scripts/registry_release.py --write refreshes them after a registry change. The rules that use the serial and published_at are in Handler binding and the versioning policy.

docs.title: Conformance authorities
docs.text:
Who may sign the attestation that admits a pilot handler is data, like the handler status: the public, dated conformance-authority list, published as source/registry/conformance-authorities.json beside source/handlers/registry.json and valid against conformance-authority-list.json.

  • Each entry is scoped to named handlers (scope.pilots, at least one). An attestation that lists a pilot outside the signing entry's scope is refused.
  • The list is the floor and the ceiling: a Mandate Manager MAY narrow it by publishing an exclusion list and MUST NOT add a signer to it.
  • The list ships empty in 2026-10-18. Until an entry is added, no pilot handler can back an open mandate.
  • Adding an entry, and moving any handler from pilot to live, needs the approvals in GOVERNANCE.md.

docs.title: Reference patterns and receipt echo
docs.text: A descriptor's mandate_primitives[].ref_pattern is an OPTIONAL regular expression that a rail_binding.rail_ref of that primitive has to match, so that a Mandate Manager can check the reference's shape. It is set only from a public source that states the format; no descriptor sets one in this version, and putting one on a live descriptor later is a breaking change. A payer-PSP-signed receipt SHOULD echo the mandate primitive and rail.rail_ref (receipt.json), so that the gateway can reconcile it against the mandate's binding.

docs.title: Alias resolution
docs.text:
Settled

The in.* canonical ids, the alias rules below, the governance of handler names and the length of the deprecation window are settled in Q-28.

A handler reference (HandlerRef) is a canonical id, an exact alias, or a string matched by a glob alias. It resolves as follows:

  1. Order. First an exact canonical handler_id, then an exact alias, then a glob alias (prefix.*), longest prefix first.
  2. Exact beats glob. An exact alias always wins over a glob alias. So upi.uap.pin resolves to in.upi.intent, not to in.upi.uap, whose glob alias is upi.uap.*.
  3. Globs never cover canonical ids. A glob alias MUST NOT match any canonical id. It MUST NOT match an exact alias of another descriptor, except the deprecation-window aliases listed below, which MUST be removed when the window closes.
  4. One target. An exact alias MUST map to exactly one canonical id.
  5. Emit canonical. Producers MUST emit canonical ids in new artefacts: receipts, payment state, profiles, intersection results. Consumers MUST accept any handler reference and MUST compare handlers only after resolution, for example a session's handler against its mandate's rail_binding.type.
  6. Unknown fails closed. A reference that does not resolve is not eligible: the intersection excludes it with not_in_registry, and at PUT or complete it gets 403 mandate_scope_mismatch.
  7. Resolution is not eligibility. After resolution, the binding rules still apply: a reserved or deprecated descriptor MUST NOT back a payment, a pilot descriptor only when attested, and an open mandate only through a primitive in binding.open_primitives.
  8. Deprecation window. Legacy aliases are accepted for one deprecation window: at least two dated releases after the release that deprecates them, and at least 180 days after that release, whichever is later (versioning policy). Removing an alias is a breaking change and gets at least 90 days' notice. The registry SHOULD publish each alias's end date (a proposed descriptor field aliases_deprecated_after, not yet in the schema).

The registry declares two exact aliases of in.upi.intent for the deprecation window: upi.pin and upi.uap.pin (listed after the registry table). They identify a human-present one-off UPI payment authorised by UPI PIN. auth_binding.type stays upi.pin.

docs.title: Proposing a new handler
docs.text:
A new handler, or a change to an existing one (a new limit, a status change, a new alias), is proposed as a change to the registry:

  1. Open an issue in the BACP repository titled handler: <proposed id>, with the rail, its operator and regulator, and the primary sources (circulars, master directions, operator product pages).
  2. Choose the id. Use in.<family>.<variant> for an Indian rail or instrument and bacp.<construct> for a BACP-native construct. The id MUST match HandlerId, MUST NOT collide with an existing id or alias, and MUST NOT be matched by an existing glob alias.
  3. Write the descriptor with every required field. Grade each limit honestly. A limit that comes only from a vendor or the press is vendor or secondary; one with no source is unverified.
  4. Classify it. State the class and justify it against the RBI Authentication Directions 2025: a handler is class O only if a standing authority exists that the rail, issuer or both parties enforce, and the descriptor then has hnp: rail_enforced. An open-eligible descriptor lists in binding.open_primitives only primitives whose limits_enforced_by is rail or issuer. A device-bound handler is never open-eligible.
  5. Start at pilot or reserved unless the rail is generally available with published rules.
  6. Add conformance cases. A handler that a gateway claims under a conformance level needs cases for its binding, limits, AFA and refund route. See Conformance.
  7. Validate. The pull request MUST pass schema validation of the whole registry and the alias rules above.

The BACP working group reviews the proposal. A registry change is a normative change under GOVERNANCE.md: it needs a 14-day review and the approval of two maintainers, one of them the payments editor, and ships in a dated release or an approved backport (settled in Q-28).

docs.title: Rail Bindings
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page binds the payment model to each Indian rail family. For every family it gives the handlers, the limits with the regulation or operator text they come from, the authentication model, how a mandate binds, and the refund and dispute path. The descriptors in the Handler Registry carry the same values as data, together with a verification grade for each limit.

How to read the limits.

  • A limit taken from an RBI direction or an NPCI publication that was checked against the primary text is stated plainly.
  • A limit known only from a vendor's documentation or from the press is marked (vendor) or (press). One that sources disagree on is marked (conflict).
  • Amounts are shown in rupees here. On the wire every amount is integer paise (₹15,000 = 1500000).
  • Limits are configurable in the registry. Where sources conflict, the gateway enforces the stricter value unless a deployment documents otherwise.

The rule every rail is judged against. Under the RBI Authentication Directions 2025 (RBI/2025-26/79, issued 25-09-2025, compliance from 01-04-2026), every digital payment needs at least two distinct factors, at least one of them dynamic for every payment other than a card-present one (para 6), and the issuer compensates the customer in full for a loss from a non-compliant transaction. So an agent-initiated debit either runs under an exempted or AFA-registered standing authority, or needs a fresh 2FA performed by the user. The agent is never a factor.

docs.title: UPI
docs.text:
UPI is operated by NPCI under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007 and RBI oversight. Its rules come through NPCI operating circulars, several of them member-only; the UPI Procedural Guidelines are not publicly available from NPCI as of 17-10-2026 (Q-07). The UPI PIN never leaves the payer's UPI app. On every UPI handler the payment leg is basket-blind, receipts carry the RRN (and the UTR where the descriptor lists it), and disputes go to UDIR in the payer app, with MyUPI automated chargeback.

Failed UPI merchant payments are auto-reversed within T+5, with ₹100 per day of compensation after that; a failed P2P transfer is reversed by T+1 (RBI/2019-20/67, Annex rows 4b and 4a).

docs.title: Intent, QR and collect
docs.text:
Handlers: in.upi.intent, in.upi.qr, in.upi.collect. Class C (human present for every payment).

Item Rule Source Flows Intent: a upi://pay deep link opens the payer's UPI app, where the payer enters the PIN. QR: static (fixed VPA, payer types the amount) or dynamic (amount and transaction reference embedded); Bharat QR is also read. Collect: the merchant's PSP pushes a request to the payer's VPA and the payer approves with the PIN. NPCI UPI product page P2M limit ₹1 lakh per transaction (banks may set lower). ₹5 lakh per transaction for verified merchants in notified categories (capital markets, insurance, travel, credit-card bills, GeM and others) from 15-09-2025, with a 24-hour aggregate that differs by category (reported as ₹10 lakh for most and ₹6 lakh for credit-card bills). ₹1 lakh: NPCI UPI Procedural Guidelines (member-only; not verified as of 17-10-2026). Category caps: NPCI circular of 28-08-2025 (press; NPCI text not verified as of 17-10-2026) Collect P2P collect ended on 01-10-2025; merchant (P2M) collect continues. NPCI circular of 29-07-2025 (press) Payee name From 30-06-2025, UPI apps display only the bank-registered name of the ultimate beneficiary. NPCI (press) AFA Device binding (the bank-linked mobile number) plus UPI PIN, or device-native biometric where enabled (launched at the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2025). NPCI UPI product page; NPCI GFF 2026 press release

Binding rules:

  • An HP one-off UPI payment authorised by PIN is identified as handler in.upi.intent with auth_binding.type: upi.pin.
  • BACP MUST NOT emit a UPI collect request to a non-merchant VPA. in.upi.collect is P2M only.
  • Agent-originated in-person or doorstep UPI payments MUST use a dynamic QR (or intent) carrying the exact amount and a transaction reference equal to, or mapped to, the BACP order id. A static QR MUST be rejected for an agent cart, because it breaks the binding between order and payment.
  • The gateway MUST enforce the P2M per-transaction cap by merchant category (₹1 lakh by default, ₹5 lakh for notified categories) and refuse locally above it.

docs.title: Charges on UPI
docs.text:
These rows state what the sources say as of 18-10-2026. BACP does not carry the merchant discount rate (MDR) or the other costs the seller bears; it carries what the principal pays and to whom (Who pays).

Item Rule Source and status MDR on P2M 0.4% on person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction for ₹75,000 and above. A flat ₹5 applies to listed categories (the FAQ names railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel, among others). AutoPay carries no prescribed MDR. Not yet in force: NPCI decided on 13-10-2026 that it starts "immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately", and no date was found as of 18-10-2026. NPCI FAQ updated 15-10-2026, Q3, Q5, Q22, Q33; NPCI press release 13-10-2026. An FAQ and a press release, not a circular. Whether the Q22 AutoPay rule reaches Reserve Pay and OTM is open with NPCI (Q-81). P2PM (small merchant) Two texts that BACP quotes and does not reconcile. The FAQ says small merchants receiving "up to ₹1 lakh per month" get zero MDR, and that those above ₹1 lakh per month for three consecutive months move to P2M (Q24, Q29). The circular says "less than or equal to ₹1 lakh", with no period (para 7.2). NPCI FAQ 15-10-2026; NPCI/UPI/CC/01 (18-09-2026) para 7.2 Convenience fee The Payee PSP ensures that no surcharge is levied on users for UPI transactions, that a convenience fee is disclosed upfront on the merchant payment page prior to the selection of the payment mode, and that it remains consistent across the available debit payment modes (net banking, debit card, UPI and credit card). The duty binds the Payee PSP, not the seller, the agent or the gateway. NPCI/UPI/CC/01 (18-09-2026) para 7.5 No charge by banks and system providers "No bank or system provider shall impose ... any charge" on RuPay debit cards and UPI up to ₹2,000 (Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, s.10A). It binds banks and system providers; its reach to merchants is interpretation. Gazette S.O. 5067(E), 14-09-2026 UPI app fees The FAQ says UPI application providers shall not charge a platform fee or any other charge for a UPI payment. NPCI FAQ Q17 (an FAQ) Merchants and MDR The FAQ says on-boarded merchants cannot pass MDR on to customers on UPI. NPCI FAQ Q34 (an FAQ)

docs.title: UPI Circle delegate
docs.text:
Handler: in.upi.circle (alias upi.circle.delegate). Class O. Status pilot.

UPI Circle lets a primary user delegate UPI payments to a secondary user, or to a device or software, including AI chatbots. For IoT and software secondaries, NPCI publishes these limits:

Limit Value Source Per transaction, per device ₹5,000 NPCI UPI Circle page Per month, per device ₹15,000 NPCI UPI Circle page First 24 hours after linking ₹2,000 NPCI UPI Circle page. Sources conflict: NPCI OC 201 (13-08-2024) item 9 (a daily transaction limit of ₹5,000 in the first 24 hours) and OC 201B (08-10-2025) item 8 (a cumulative transaction limit of ₹5,000 for the first 24 hours) state ₹5,000. The stricter value applies until NPCI confirms which figure the rail enforces (as of 18-10-2026). Devices or software per primary user 5 NPCI UPI Circle page
  • Linking. OTP, then QR or intent, then consent and limit setting in the primary user's UPI app, then PIN or biometric. AFA happens at linking; payments within the limits need no per-transaction PIN.
  • Status. NPCI states that "AI/Software driven IoT Payments are under pilot with limited users as a part of Closed User Group". The handler is therefore pilot, and a gateway MAY use it only when its conformance attestation lists it (and, until Q-77 is settled, not for an open mandate).
  • Full delegation to a human secondary went live on BHIM on 25-11-2025: up to ₹15,000 a month, with expiry from 1 month to 5 years, usable "after a short cooling period" (NBSL press release). The length of the cooling period and any per-transaction cap for human secondaries are not stated in any public NPCI text found as of 17-10-2026 (Q-08).
  • Explicit user action. NPCI OC 201B (NPCI/UPI/OC-201B/2025-26, 08-10-2025), which extends Circle to IoT devices and software, states: "debit transactions using IoT shall be only initiated by explicit user action." Whether a standing open mandate that an agent executes without the principal present is "explicit user action", and whether "IoT" there covers software profiles, is open (Q-77).
  • No open mandate on Circle for now. in.upi.circle backs no open mandate, even when a listed conformance authority's scope includes it and a gateway's attestation lists it, until Q-77 is settled. A Mandate Manager refuses an open mandate request on in.upi.circle with rail_binding_not_open_eligible, and a gateway refuses every human-not-present complete under an open mandate on it; the registry marks the handler open_eligible: false. This does not change today's behaviour, because no Circle open mandate can exist while the conformance-authority list is empty.
  • Payee scope. A Circle delegation is not tied to one merchant. Where it ever backs an open mandate, it ranks below the principal's own preference in a multi-seller basket (per-leg rule).

Binding rules:

  • An open payment mandate bound to Circle MUST have amount_per_txn at or below ₹5,000 and a monthly budget at or below ₹15,000.
  • The first-24-hour cap and the device's remaining monthly limit are pre-checked before complete. A debit that would exceed them returns 403 rail_limit_exceeded, not a step-up.
  • Because Circle's limits are loose relative to most mandates, the gateway's own atomic budget enforcement is what bounds spending.

docs.title: Reserve Pay (single-block-multiple-debit)
docs.text:
Handler: in.upi.reservepay (alias upi.reservepay.block). Class O.

Item Rule Source Basis RBI decided to allow single-block-multiple-debit (SBMD) in UPI on 07-12-2022. RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, 07-12-2022 Launch NPCI launched UPI Reserve Pay on credit accounts on 08-10-2025: the payer blocks part of a credit card or pre-sanctioned credit-line limit for repeat purchases, with blocked and used amounts visible across apps. NPCI GFF 2025 press release Account types All UPI-permitted sources of funds, including savings, current and overdraft accounts, RuPay credit cards and pre-sanctioned credit lines. The extant pricing of RuPay credit cards and credit lines on UPI applies to executed debits. NPCI UPI OC 228 (08-10-2025); NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 (18-09-2026), para 16.1 Merchants To begin with, enabled only for "online verified merchants with low ticket and high frequency transactions". NPCI UPI OC 228, acquiring entities para 1 Block At most ₹10,000 per block, reserved for at most 90 days; the merchant may debit several times up to the blocked amount. One mobile number may hold only one block at a time for a particular merchant; no NPCI text caps blocks per user across merchants. A block is not a guarantee of payment. NPCI UPI Reserve Pay product page; NPCI UPI OC 228, issuer banks paras 4 and 5; Consolidated Circular para 16.4 Creation Payer-initiated, by QR, intent or SDK. NPCI UPI OC 200 (31-07-2024), para b Timeouts A timeout on a debit is treated as a decline, reversed in real time and not settled. For timeouts only, acquiring entities may retry at most 3 times in 24 hours; no retries for other declines. NPCI UPI OC 228, acquiring entities para 3 Notice The payer is notified of block creation, modification, debit, revoke and expiry. No NPCI text found states whether a pre-debit notice applies. NPCI UPI OC 228, issuer banks para 2; Consolidated Circular para 16.11 Revocation The payee PSP and the UPI app must give the payer a facility to revoke the block; the merchant gives a facility to modify its amount or validity. Unused money is released on expiry or cancellation. Consolidated Circular paras 16.9 and 16.10; NPCI UPI Reserve Pay product page AFA UPI PIN at block creation. NPCI UPI Reserve Pay product page

Which issuers support Reserve Pay is open (Q-04). Whether an agent-initiated draw on a block counts as the customer action on the merchant's platform that NPCI describes is open (Q-65).

One block per seller. An SBMD block's payee is one seller's collection VPA, or the seller's PA sub-merchant VPA. A buyer app cannot hold one block for many sellers.

  • An open payment mandate bound to Reserve Pay MUST name the block's payee in payee{vpa, bpp_id}, and payee.vpa MUST equal the VPA in the seller's BPP-signed payment terms, which the gateway holds (or first obtains by a Beckn init it never confirms) for every block, including one set up outside a checkout (Sibling Payment Mandates). A block whose payee is the buyer app does not back an HNP payment (rail_binding_not_open_eligible). A debit against a block whose payee is another seller MUST be refused with reservepay_block_wrong_payee (the rail-level twin is payee_mismatch).
  • A block counts as reserved spend at its full amount in the mandate ledger until its revocation is confirmed or it expires (Usage ledger).
  • Multi-seller agent shopping follows the per-leg rule: per seller, the principal's preference, then the seller's existing block under the basket's root open checkout mandate, then a gift PPI the principal designated, then one planned human-present step before any debit.
  • The handler intersection excludes in.upi.reservepay unless a block payable to this seller exists.

Multi-seller HNP today

As of 17-10-2026, hands-free buying across several sellers works only for sellers for which the principal already holds a block (or another payee-bound mandate) set up in a UPI app, and only where the seller's acquirer has enabled Reserve Pay, which OC 228 limits at first to online verified merchants with low-ticket, high-frequency transactions. Every other leg is human-present: one payment and one UPI PIN per seller. Block creation is by QR, intent or SDK (NPCI UPI OC 200, para b, which adds that other modes of initiation are envisaged later); no NPCI text found as of 17-10-2026 describes block creation over UPI 123PAY or IVR.

Notice on repeat debits. Whether the E-mandate Framework's 24-hour pre-debit notice applies to SBMD debits is open (Q-03). Until it is answered, the second and every later unattended debit on a Reserve Pay block MUST follow the 24-hour notice-gated checkout described in the overview. The first debit is covered by the block authorisation.

Refunds go to the source with original_rrn. Whether a refund restores the block is not verified.

docs.title: AutoPay (UPI e-mandate)
docs.text:
Handler: in.upi.autopay (alias upi.autopay). Class O.

UPI AutoPay is governed by the RBI Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026 (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396, CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S56/02.14.003/2026-27, 21-04-2026, effective immediately). The two identifiers are the RBI reference number and the department circular number of the same document. It consolidates and repeals the earlier e-mandate circulars, and applies to e-mandates on cards, PPIs and UPI.

Item Rule Source AFA At registration, modification and revocation of the mandate, and for the first debit E-mandate Framework 2026 paras 4(a), 4(e), 5(a) No-AFA debit cap ₹15,000 per debit E-mandate Framework 2026 para 8 Special categories ₹1,00,000 per debit for insurance premiums, mutual-fund subscriptions and credit-card bills E-mandate Framework 2026 para 8 Pre-debit notice At least 24 hours before each debit, with an opt-out of the debit or the mandate (itself validated by AFA) E-mandate Framework 2026 paras 6(a), 6(c) Cost Free to the customer E-mandate Framework 2026 para 10(a) Earlier caps (repealed) ₹2,000 (cards, August 2019; UPI, January 2020), ₹5,000 (December 2020), ₹15,000 (June 2022), ₹1,00,000 for the three categories (12-12-2023) RBI circulars listed in para 11 of the 2026 Framework, now repealed Management The issuer must let the customer modify the validity or withdraw the mandate at any time. Mandates can be paused or revoked in the UPI app, and MyUPI shows mandates across apps. E-mandate Framework 2026 para 4(b); NPCI

Binding rules:

  • rail_binding.rail_ref is the UMN. pre_debit_notice is required_24h.
  • An open payment mandate bound to AutoPay MUST have amount_per_txn at or below ₹15,000 unless the purpose is one of the three special categories.
  • A debit above the no-AFA cap returns requires_escalation with step_up.kind = rail_auth and reason above_afa_limit. The user completes AFA on the Trusted Surface.
  • Every debit follows the notice-gated checkout: no money moves before the notice matures, a re-quoted amount above the notified amount needs a new notice, and an opt-out cancels the session with pre_debit_opt_out.
  • AutoPay on a credit line or RuPay credit card is a payment-plan leg with funding: credit, and the governing mandate MUST have credit_funding_allowed: true (the user's prior consent).

docs.title: One-time mandate (OTM)
docs.text:
Handler: in.upi.otm. Class O.

An OTM blocks funds once, for one merchant, amount and validity. The merchant captures once, up to the blocked amount, and the rest is released; or the block is released if the order is cancelled. It suits "buy this when the final price is known, at most ₹X", such as capture after delivery or after a negotiation.

Item Rule Source Basis RBI's SBMD/blocking decision of 07-12-2022. The NPCI OTM circular was not verified as of 17-10-2026. RBI; NPCI text not verified Block Up to ₹1,00,000 per mandate for general merchant categories (vendor: Pine Labs) Validity Up to 60 days from authorisation (Pine Labs, PayU) versus a 14-day execution window (Juspay); Razorpay documents other authorisation-expiry values by merchant category (conflict; vendors only) AFA UPI PIN at block creation; no further AFA at capture. OTM's status under the 2026 framework is not verified. (vendor) Revocation The payer cannot revoke the block in the TPAP and must ask the merchant, per the vendor. (vendor)

Binding rules:

  • The mandate records merchant, maximum amount and expiry. A capture above the blocked amount MUST fail.
  • The agent MUST release the block when the order is cancelled. Before capture a refund is a block release (refund_state: released_block); after capture it is a normal UPI refund.
  • Validity is configurable and the shortest applicable window wins (Q-31).
  • Repeat-debit notice follows the same fail-safe as Reserve Pay (Q-03).

docs.title: UPI Lite
docs.text:
Handler: in.upi.lite (alias upi.lite). Class A, device-bound.

Item Rule Source Limits ₹1,000 per transaction and ₹5,000 in total at any point in time, with no PIN per transaction; the balance is loaded with a PIN RBI/2024-25/93, 04-12-2024, para 2 (announced 09-10-2024) Lite X Offline NFC payments without a PIN. RBI states the uplift for "UPI Lite"; whether NPCI applies ₹1,000 and ₹5,000 to Lite X is not verified (an older NPCI Lite X FAQ gave ₹500 and ₹2,000; that FAQ is not publicly available as of 17-10-2026). NPCI Lite X brand guidelines (no limits stated) AFA Exempt as a small-value offline payment RBI Authentication Directions 2025, Annexure-1 item 5

A remote agent MUST NOT use UPI Lite. The handler is device_bound: true, so it can never be open-eligible, and a request from a remote agent gets presence_handler_mismatch. Only an assisted, on-device agent at a point of sale may use it. Lite receipts carry the RRN only.

docs.title: UPI 123PAY
docs.text:
Handler: in.upi.123pay (alias upi.123pay). Class C.

UPI 123PAY serves feature phones through IVR, missed call, app and sound-based payments, with the UPI PIN on every transaction.

Limit Value Source Per transaction ₹10,000, raised from ₹5,000 ("Necessary instructions will be issued to NPCI shortly") RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, 09-10-2024 Implementation NPCI circular dated 25-10-2024, compliance by 01-01-2025 (press; NPCI text not verified as of 17-10-2026)

The cap is configurable, with a default of ₹10,000, and the gateway MUST refuse an instruction above it, returning 403 rail_limit_exceeded. Confirming the cap from the NPCI circular is tracked as Q-05.

docs.title: Credit on UPI
docs.text:
Handler Rule Source in.upi.credit_line A pre-sanctioned credit line from a scheduled commercial bank (small finance banks added in 2025) may be used on UPI with the individual's prior consent. The bank sets the limit, period and rate. RBI/2023-24/58, 04-09-2023, updated 12-02-2025; NPCI UPI-OC-171 and OC-171A (press) in.upi.rupay_cc RuPay credit cards may be linked to UPI. The refund rule of the RBI Credit Card and Debit Card Directions 2022 ("Credit Card MD") para 10(h) applies. RBI policy statement of 08-06-2022 (press)

Both are class C. They run HNP only through a class O primitive on the credit account (AutoPay, Reserve Pay or OTM), with funding: credit on the payment-plan leg and the user's prior consent recorded as credit_funding_allowed on the mandate.
