The five tools named create_checkout to cancel_checkout are UCP's own tool names. A gateway offers them only if it lists in.bacp.ucp_checkout (UCP checkout projection); they map to the same operations as bacp_checkout_create to bacp_checkout_cancel, and complete_checkout, being mapped to bacp-pay, is absent on stdio like bacp_checkout_complete.

The five tools before them belong to the capabilities in.bacp.trade_document (documents), in.bacp.ledger (ledger reads and postings) and, for bacp_trade_act_record, both. bacp_return_get and bacp_evidence_get were named bacp_refund_status and bacp_dispute_evidence before this release; a server SHOULD keep the old names as aliases for one release. A tool that needs bacp-pay or bacp-post-order is not offered on a transport without RFC 9421 carriage (Authentication).

The inputSchema of bacp_human_handoff limits action to request and release, although the REST request lists accept too, so that a model cannot "accept" for the human and read the resulting 401 as an authentication fault.

Defined verbs without a REST operation yet, and so without a tool: bacp_order_track and bacp_rate. /trusted-surface/events and /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id} are never exposed as tools: only a Mandate Manager or payer PSP may call them. A handoff acceptance (action: accept), and a release by the support operator, is signed by a human support operator under tag bacp-handoff and is never a tool call (Human handoff).

docs.title: Results and errors
docs.text:
• A successful tool call returns the full resource in structuredContent, including messages[] with their resolution. A text rendering MAY accompany it, but the agent MUST act on structuredContent.
  • A step-up returns the resource in requires_escalation with its step_up object. How the MCP server signals it depends on the client's declared capabilities:
    • If the client declared support for URL-mode elicitation and the step-up carries a trusted_surface_url, the server MUST send a URL-mode elicitation whose URL is the step-up's trusted_surface_url (under MCP 2025-11-25, the URLElicitationRequiredError, code -32042; under MCP 2026-07-28, an InputRequiredResult carrying elicitation/create), MUST NOT signal insufficient_scope, and records mcp_signal: url_elicitation. The client opens the URL so that neither it nor the model can inspect it.
    • Otherwise the server signals insufficient_scope and records mcp_signal: insufficient_scope.
    • A step-up with delivery: app_push has no URL: the server signals insufficient_scope and records mcp_signal: insufficient_scope, and the principal is reached by the push.
    • A post_order step-up has no session. On 403 presence_not_proven with Error.step_up, the server binds it the same way: for a client that declared URL-mode elicitation and a step-up that carries a trusted_surface_url, -32042 with one URL elicitation whose url is the trusted_surface_url and whose elicitationId is the step_up_id; otherwise a tool error result whose structuredContent is the Error including step_up, with mcp_signal: insufficient_scope. When the step-up is approved the server MAY send notifications/elicitation/complete with that elicitationId. The notification carries no approval: the agent reads bacp_step_up_status for the state and the ts_event_hash.
    • The capability is declared by the client. A client that under-declares URL-mode elicitation falls back to insufficient_scope, and the agent then relays the trusted_surface_url to the principal itself. This is not a bypass, because only the signed Trusted Surface event approves, but the agent sees the link. Where the signer of the step-up has no conforming origin and has registered a ts_notify_url, the gateway uses StepUp.delivery: app_push, a content-free push that reaches the principal's Trusted Surface without the agent and leaves the step-up with no link (Origins and delivery). The agent SHOULD check that the host of a trusted_surface_url is an origin of the subscriber that StepUp.surface names before it hands the link over, and an MCP client that does URL-mode elicitation shows that host to the user.
  • An elicitation accept means only that the user went to the URL. It is never an approval: the step-up is approved only by the signed Trusted Surface event. The agent directs the buyer to the Trusted Surface; it cannot satisfy the challenge itself.
  • A protocol failure is returned as a tool error result (isError: true) whose structuredContent is the flat Error object (type, code, message, param, resolution), with the same code the REST binding would return. The agent reads the code and param, corrects the argument and calls again; a missing or wrong argument is invalid_request at $.<argument>, and an argument of a capability that the gateway does not list is capability_unsupported at $.<argument>, with capability in structuredContent.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• MCP transport authentication follows the MCP authorization specification: OAuth 2.1 with audience-bound tokens (RFC 8707 resource indicators, RFC 9728 protected resource metadata). The MCP server MUST NOT accept or pass through tokens issued for another audience.
  • An OAuth token authenticates the MCP client. It is not a BACP mandate and never authorises a payment: every binding commitment still needs the mandate, the AgentCredential and the deterministic evaluation.
  • Proposed: over the Streamable HTTP transport, each tool call is an HTTP request that the agent signs with RFC 9421 exactly as in the REST binding (its cnf key, the AgentCredential in BACP-Agent, the signature tag of the mapped REST operation), and the tool arguments carry idempotency_key for every tool mapped to a POST or PUT.
  • No money or trade tool without signatures. How the agent's signature is carried over the stdio transport is not defined. A tool mapped to bacp-pay or bacp-post-order therefore MUST NOT be offered on a transport without RFC 9421 carriage: on stdio the host sees bacp_checkout_complete, the order write tools, bacp_trade_act_record and bacp_ledger_payment_post as absent from tools/list, not as tools that fail at call time. A principal on a local desktop MCP host completes on a remote (HTTP) binding or through a human channel.
  • MCP per version. A gateway that lists more than one version serves one MCP endpoint for each and publishes them as mcp_endpoints{version: uri} in its profile (Fields), because MCP's Streamable HTTP has a single endpoint path and a host may be unable to set the BACP-Version header. A session created on one endpoint and used on another gets 409 version_mismatch.
  • No seller account, OTP or password. No tool asks the agent for, relays or stores a seller's one-time password or account password. No seller-account token, link token or session cookie appears in a tool argument, a tool result, the InstructionLog, an evidence bundle or model context, and a call that carries one is refused with 400 invalid_request and the value is not logged. A link token is never a mandate and never authorises a payment. Linking a buyer's account at a seller is itself parked, with the controls any such capability must meet (Q-96).
  • No credentials in arguments. No tool argument carries a gift-card code, a voucher code or an instrument credential; a call that does is refused with 400 invalid_request, makes no rail call, and the argument is not logged.

docs.title: Agent card and extension
docs.text:
• A BACP gateway that offers A2A publishes an A2A Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json and lists a2a in the transports of its BACP profile.
  • Proposed: the card declares the BACP extension in its capabilities, references the gateway's /.well-known/bacp profile, and is signed as a JWS over its JCS form, as A2A allows. The extension URI carries the version, https://bacp.dev/<version>/a2a (for example https://bacp.dev/2026-10-18/a2a), and the card declares it with required: true, so that a client that does not know the version cannot proceed without noticing. A gateway that lists more than one version lists one extension URI for each, and a task is pinned to the version of the URI it started under (The version of a request).
  • A2A authentication follows the card's declared securitySchemes; as with MCP, it authenticates the client and is never a mandate.

docs.title: Data parts
docs.text:
Each operation is a message carrying one DataPart keyed by its BACP name; results come back as a DataPart on the task.

Operation Request DataPart Result DataPart Checkout session (create, get, update, complete, cancel) Proposed: bacp.session.create, bacp.session.update, bacp.session.complete, bacp.session.cancel bacp.session Open a negotiation bacp.negotiation.open (creates a task) bacp.negotiation Get a negotiation task get bacp.negotiation Send an offer, counter, reject, withdraw, terminate, extension request or accept-revoke bacp.neg.message (the signed message as a JWS inside) bacp.negotiation Accept the live offer bacp.neg.accept bacp.negotiation RFQ create, get, award bacp.rfq bacp.rfq Auction create, get, bid, award bacp.auction bacp.auction Payment handlers list, get, intersect bacp.payment_handlers bacp.payment_handlers Mandates, orders, returns, issues, evidence Proposed: bacp.mandate, bacp.order, bacp.issue, bacp.evidence same Step-up status (the state of a step-up that the agent caused) Proposed: bacp.step_up_status same Trade act: GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection, ledger acknowledgement (in.bacp.trade_document, in.bacp.ledger) bacp.trade_act bacp.trade_act Credit ledger read and payment posting (in.bacp.ledger) bacp.ledger (header read, or a payment posting), bacp.ledger.entries (a page of entries) bacp.ledger, bacp.ledger.entries Input needed on a task in TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED — bacp.input_request {needed_from}: principal when the human must answer (data, a choice, a handoff), agent when the agent can answer itself (a counter-offer)

docs.title: Task states
docs.text:
A2A task state (v1.0 JSON value) Negotiation state Checkout session TASK_STATE_WORKING Waiting on the counterparty complete_in_progress (Proposed) TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED A counter to answer Proposed: incomplete when the buyer must supply data TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED ESCALATED requires_escalation (step-up) TASK_STATE_COMPLETED CONTRACTED completed (Proposed) TASK_STATE_CANCELED or TASK_STATE_FAILED REJECTED, TERMINATED or CANCELLED cancelled (Proposed)

Versions of A2A before 1.0 use the lowercase names working, input-required, auth-required, completed, canceled and failed.

A2A's TASK_STATE_CANCELED and canceled are A2A's own values and are used verbatim. BACP spells its own value "cancelled": these A2A states map to the checkout session status cancelled and the negotiation state CANCELLED.

A task in TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED carries a bacp.input_request DataPart whose needed_from says who must answer, so that a client agent never answers on the principal's behalf what only the principal may answer.

TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED is a signal, not an authorisation: the task resumes only after the Mandate Manager or PSP posts a signed step-up result to the gateway. A post_order step-up, raised by a write on an order or an issue, puts that order or issue task in TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED with the Error.step_up in its status message, and the client agent reads bacp.step_up_status (Proposed name; the A2A form of GET /step-ups/{step_up_id}, with the same access rule) until the state is approved.

Negotiation notices and declines over A2A. A2A has no state for "notice only". The ask confirmation (accept_confirmation) and a contested crossing map to TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED (ESCALATED) as the table shows. The principal's decline of an AGREED or BOUND deal (principal_declined) moves the task to TASK_STATE_CANCELED (CANCELLED). The agreed_by_agent and purchase_offered_by_agent notices are info messages that change no task state: the gateway delivers the notice to the principal by the mandate's notice_route, and a client agent MUST NOT forward, summarise or answer it. The response to every negotiation message sent carries the counterparty's counter_signature for it when one was returned and verified; when it is absent, a crossing that depends on that message is contested. A client agent that sees crossing_contested stops and does not resend.

docs.title: How mandates travel
docs.text:
• Mandates are never created over A2A. bacp.mandate requests a mandate; the buyer approves it on the Trusted Surface.
  • A closed mandate travels exactly as in the REST binding: an attached compact JWS whose payload is the Mandate JSON with its inner signature, inside the bacp.session.complete DataPart (Proposed name), together with the agent's key-binding JWT.
  • Negotiation never carries the negotiation mandate or its bounds. An ACCEPT carries only the offer_hash, the negotiation mandate reference and the within_bounds attestation signed by the buyer's credential provider.

docs.title: How signatures travel
docs.text:
• A negotiation message carries the sending network participant's registry signature as a detached JWS over JCS, inside the bacp.neg.message DataPart. Signed messages are transport-independent, so the same bytes verify whether they arrive over A2A or Beckn.
  • Agent-to-agent negotiation over A2A (buyer agent to seller agent) is allowed. Without a network participant's signature, it can produce at most firm: false offers. For an ONDC order, the accepted offer_hash MUST reappear in the seller-signed on_init; that is the network anchor.
  • The agent's own act is evidenced by its RFC 9421 request signature to its gateway. Whether the agent should also sign the message body with its cnf key, so that messages stay verifiable over A2A without a network participant, is open: Q-48.

docs.title: REST
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

The REST binding is the reference binding of BACP. A BACP gateway, run by or for a registered buyer app (BAP), exposes it to AI agents. Each call is translated into signed Beckn/ONDC actions (see Beckn / ONDC Binding) or into calls to the payer PSP and Mandate Manager, and the gateway returns the authoritative full state of the resource. The same operations are bound to MCP tools and to an A2A extension (see MCP and A2A).

The normative contract is the OpenAPI 3.1 document: https://bacp.dev/latest/services/bacp.openapi.yaml. Where this page and the OpenAPI document differ, this page is authoritative.

docs.title: Base URL and media type
docs.text:
• The base URL is chosen by the gateway, for example https://gw.bap.example.in/bacp. Every path on this page, including /.well-known/bacp, is relative to it. Agents discover a gateway's base URL, transports, capabilities, payment handlers and keys from its profile (see Discovery and Profiles).
  • Requests and responses are application/json encoded in UTF-8.
  • Amounts are integer paise ({"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"} is ₹302.00). Times are RFC 3339 date-times; examples use the IST offset +05:30.
  • Readers MUST ignore unknown fields, except a request member of a capability that the receiver defines but does not list, which it refuses with 400 capability_unsupported (Extensibility rule 1). Unknown mandate constraints MUST fail closed.
  • Business outcomes return 200, 201 or 202 with full state and messages[]; failures return 4xx or 5xx with the flat Error object (see Errors).

docs.title: Request headers
docs.text:
Header Direction Required Meaning Signature-Input, Signature request every call except the public reads RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the agent's cnf key (see Signatures) Content-Digest request every signed call RFC 9530 digest of the raw body (of the empty body on a GET), covered by the signature BACP-Agent request every signed agent call The AgentCredential (SD-JWT VC) with only the disclosures the gateway needs BACP-Version request every agent call when the profile lists more than one version; optional otherwise The BACP version of the request (Version negotiation). Covered by the signature whenever present Idempotency-Key request every POST and PUT 22–64 printable ASCII characters with at least 122 random bits (see Idempotency) Content-Type request every call with a body application/json Idempotent-Replayed response on a replay true when the response is the stored response of an earlier request with the same key Retry-After response with 409 idempotency_in_flight and 429 quota_exceeded Seconds to wait before retrying with the same key

BACP-Agent-Credential, a fallback name for BACP-Agent, was accepted only before the first dated release. From BACP 2026-10-18 it MUST NOT be accepted; agents send BACP-Agent.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
Every agent request MUST be signed with RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures. The full rules, key resolution and the AgentCredential are in Identity and Request Signing. In summary:

  • The signature MUST cover @method, @authority, @path, content-digest and bacp-agent, plus idempotency-key on every non-GET request, and bacp-version whenever the request carries BACP-Version. A request under tag bacp-ts or bacp-handoff carries no BACP-Agent header and does not cover bacp-agent. It MUST also cover @query whenever the target URI has a query, and SHOULD cover content-type. A signature that lacks a required component is rejected with 401 signature_invalid.
  • Signature parameters MUST include created, expires, nonce, keyid and tag. expires − created MUST NOT exceed 300 s; up to 5 s of clock skew is allowed.
  • The gateway verifies the signature on the raw bytes before parsing JSON, after the body-size check. It keeps a (keyid, nonce) replay cache until expires.
  • The signing key is the AgentCredential's cnf key for agents, the registry key for a Mandate Manager or PSP calling /trusted-surface/events or /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id} (only the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP, as defined in Step-up signers; any other gets 404), and the registry key of a human support operator accepting or releasing a handoff (no BACP-Agent header, and bacp-agent is not covered).

docs.title: Signature tags
docs.text:
The tag parameter states what the signature authorises. The tag MUST be the one required by the endpoint, and it MUST be listed in the AgentCredential's purposes; otherwise the gateway returns 401 signature_invalid. The table lists every agent endpoint. An agent endpoint that is not listed gets 401 signature_invalid: there is no default tag. Every operation of the OpenAPI document carries its tag as x-bacp-signature-tag, and scripts/validate.py fails an operation without it.

Tag Authorises Endpoints bacp-browse Reads, discovery, building a cart, mandate requests, non-firm negotiation messages, ledger reads POST /discover, GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}, POST /sessions, GET and PUT /sessions/{session_id}, POST /sessions/{session_id}/cancel, POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff (action: request, and action: release before acceptance), POST /checkout-sessions, GET and PUT /checkout-sessions/{id}, POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel, POST /mandates, GET /mandates/{mandate_id}, POST /mandates/{mandate_id}/relinquish, GET /orders/{order_id}, GET /orders/{order_id}/returns/{return_id}, GET /orders/{order_id}/documents, GET /issues/{issue_id}, GET /evidence/{transaction_id}, GET /evidence/{transaction_id}/summary, GET /step-ups/{step_up_id}, POST /negotiations, GET /negotiations/{negotiation_id}, GET /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers, non-firm messages other than withdraw and accept_revoke on POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers, POST /rfqs, GET /rfqs/{rfq_id}, GET /auctions/{auction_id}, POST /payment-handlers/intersect, GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}, GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries bacp-pay Moving money POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete and POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete, including a payment_plan (Wire binding of plans) bacp-post-order Protective writes on an existing order, trade acts and ledger postings POST /orders/{order_id}/cancel, POST /orders/{order_id}/returns, POST /issues, POST /issues/{issue_id}/actions, POST /trade-acts, POST /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries bacp-negotiate Binding negotiation acts: firm offers and counters, ACCEPT, bids, awards, and the acts that undo them (WITHDRAW, ACCEPT_REVOKE) POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers when the message is firm or is a withdraw or accept_revoke, POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/accept, POST /rfqs/{rfq_id}/award, POST /auctions, POST /auctions/{auction_id}/bids, POST /auctions/{auction_id}/award bacp-ts Trusted Surface events and render fetches, signed by the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP, never by an agent POST /trusted-surface/events, GET /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id} bacp-handoff A human support operator accepting or releasing a handoff, signed by a registry key of role support operator, never by an agent POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff with action: accept or release bacp-mm-event A gateway reporting a mandate event to the Mandate Manager, signed by the registry key of the gateway's BAP, never by an agent The webhook mandate.event, delivered to the mandate's audit_uri (Mandate events); it is not an operation of this API

GET /.well-known/bacp, GET /payment-handlers and GET /payment-handlers/{handler_id} are public and need no signature.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
# Rule 1 Idempotency-Key is REQUIRED on every POST and PUT. A missing or malformed key returns 400 idempotency_key_required. Keys are scoped to (agent, canonical operation, path parameters): the operation, not the URL string, and the values of its path parameters. For every operation that exists today this is the same scope as (agent, method, path), and an MCP tool or an A2A DataPart that maps to the operation shares its keys, as does the /checkout-sessions twin of a /sessions operation. 2 Body equality is semantic: null is not the same as an absent field. 3 Same key and same body: the gateway returns the stored response with Idempotent-Replayed: true. 4 Same key and a different body: 422 idempotency_conflict. 5 Same key while the first request is still in flight: 409 idempotency_in_flight with Retry-After. 6 Keys are kept at least 24 hours; 48 hours is RECOMMENDED. 5xx responses are never stored. 7 If the idempotency store fails, writes fail closed with 503 idempotency_store_unavailable. 8 After a lost response, a timeout or a 5xx, the agent MUST call GET on the resource first, and MAY retry only with the same key. A new key is a new purchase intent and is evaluated against the mandate afresh. 9 A write refused with 403 presence_not_proven is retried with hp_proof under a new key: the body differs, so the same key gets 422 idempotency_conflict, whose message names a new key. 10 Across a projection twin (an operation and its /checkout-sessions form), the stored request is compared in its canonical BACP form, and a replay returns the stored outcome in the shape of the path that was called.

complete is protected twice: by the idempotency key and by the rule that a closed payment mandate is consumed at most once and a checkout_hash is debited at most once (see Sessions and Checkout).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• A request body larger than 256 KiB is refused with 413 request_too_large, checked on raw bytes before signature verification. A gateway MAY set a lower limit. Proposed: it publishes the limit in its profile as limits.max_body_bytes.
  • Per agent, a gateway keeps at most 10,000 live idempotency keys and 64 requests in flight by default. Beyond that it returns 429 quota_exceeded with Retry-After.
  • A missing seller callback ends the gateway's wait with 504 bpp_timeout; the resource stays retrievable by GET.

Every operation with a request body documents 413 and 429. See Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Order ids
docs.text: A seller's order id is unique only within that seller, so the gateway keys orders by (bpp_id, order_id). If an agent holds the same order id from two sellers, an order-scoped request without bpp_id returns 400 invalid_request with param: "$.bpp_id". The agent passes bpp_id in the body of cancel, return and issue requests, or as the ?bpp_id= query parameter on GET /orders/{order_id} and GET /orders/{order_id}/returns/{return_id}. A request with a query string MUST cover @query in its signature.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Only GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries is paginated, by keyset: after_seq (return entries whose seq is greater), limit (1 to 50, default 50; a larger value is 400 invalid_request at $.limit) and status. The response carries next_after_seq until the last page and the ledger's head_seq and head_hash. The other list responses (GET /payment-handlers, GET /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers) return the complete list. GET /payment-handlers accepts the filters presence, class, kind, segment and status.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
The gateway pushes state changes to the agent's webhook URL, given as webhook_url in POST /mandates (so that mandate.status_changed can reach the agent before any session exists) and in POST /sessions.

Event When mandate.status_changed The mandate became ACTIVE, PAUSED, REVOKED, EXPIRED or EXHAUSTED, or the set of pause reasons (pause_reasons[], beside the single reason) of a PAUSED mandate changed. Delivered within 60 s of the Trusted Surface event, with the affected sessions. session.updated Full session snapshot, for example step-up required or approved, or a payment resolved after being in doubt. payment.receipt A payment or refund receipt was applied (as a ReceiptRef). order.updated Full order snapshot after an unsolicited on_status, on_cancel or on_update. return.updated A return or refund changed state. issue.updated An IGM respondent action arrived (PROCESSING, INFO_REQUESTED, RESOLUTION_PROPOSED, RESOLUTION_CASCADED, RESOLVED). pre_debit.notice A pre-debit notice was issued. The agent MUST relay it to the buyer and MUST NOT dismiss it. step_up.updated A step-up that the agent credential's request created reached a final state (approved, declined, expired, voided or superseded). data is the StepUpStatus, with ts_event_hash once approved (Presence proof). It carries no render and no text for the principal.

Each delivery is a WebhookEvent: event_id, type, created_at and data.

A MandateEvent is not one of these deliveries: the gateway sends it to the mandate's audit_uri, the endpoint of the Mandate Manager, under the tag bacp-mm-event (Mandate events). The agent never receives it, and the Mandate Manager refuses one whose signer's BAP is not the mandate's agent.bap_id.

Signing and delivery.

  • Every delivery MUST be signed by the gateway with an RFC 9421 signature under the gateway's registry key, covering at least @method, @authority, @path, content-digest and the Standard Webhooks headers webhook-id (equal to event_id) and webhook-timestamp. Proposed: the signature tag is bacp-webhook, and the gateway lists its tags in its profile (Q-58). Until that is settled, a receiver MUST NOT reject a webhook only because its signature has no tag or an unknown one.
  • The receiver MUST verify the signature against the gateway's published key and SHOULD de-duplicate on webhook-id. A 2xx response acknowledges the event; otherwise the gateway retries with backoff.
  • Webhooks are full-state snapshots, but field-scoped: a body MUST NOT embed a signed receipt. Receipts travel as a ReceiptRef (receipt_id, receipt_hash, receipt_type, result, and where present amount, refund_state, rail{type, rrn, status, original_rrn}). The agent fetches the full signed receipt by GET on the owning session, order or return and MUST check that its hash equals receipt_hash.
  • A webhook MUST NOT carry personal data outside the receiving agent's data_scopes, nor any negotiation bound. See Security and Privacy.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Every operation in the OpenAPI document. Tag is the OpenAPI tag; Signature tag is the RFC 9421 tag the endpoint requires. This table is generated from source/services/bacp.openapi.yaml.

Method Path Tag Signature tag Idempotency-Key Summary GET /.well-known/bacp profile none (public) — Gateway profile (UCP /.well-known pattern) POST /discover discovery bacp-browse required Network discovery (Beckn search / 2.0 discover via gateway and registry) GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest} discovery bacp-browse — Fetch the BPP-signed on_search callback behind a discovery result, as {body, authorization}. Served only to the agent whose search produced the transaction. POST /sessions session bacp-browse required Create checkout session (UCP create_checkout, Beckn select) GET /sessions/{session_id} session bacp-browse — Get session (UCP get_checkout). Use for lost-response recovery before any retry. PUT /sessions/{session_id} session bacp-browse required Update session, full replace (UCP update_checkout). Items trigger select, fulfilment/billing triggers init. POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete session bacp-pay required Complete (UCP complete_checkout). Verifies closed mandates, debits the rail, sends Beckn confirm. POST /sessions/{session_id}/cancel session bacp-browse required Cancel a session before an order exists (UCP cancel_checkout). No Beckn call is needed. POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff session bacp-browse (request; release before acceptance); bacp-handoff (accept, release) required Hand the session to a human (bacp.human_handoff). Requested by the agent; accepted only by a registered human support operator. POST /mandates mandate bacp-browse required Request a mandate. Returns PENDING plus a Trusted Surface link. The agent never signs or activates it. GET /mandates/{mandate_id} mandate bacp-browse — Get mandate with live status and usage (AA ConsentUse analogue) POST /mandates/{mandate_id}/relinquish mandate bacp-browse required Agent gives up its authority (agent-side revoke). Users revoke or pause on the Trusted Surface only. POST /trusted-surface/events trusted-surface bacp-ts (registry key) required Signed event from a Mandate Manager or payer PSP (mandate activated, paused, resumed, revoked, step-up result, rail event) GET /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id} trusted-surface bacp-ts (registry key) — Fetch the gateway-signed ts_render of a step-up. Only the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP may call it. GET /evidence/{transaction_id}/summary evidence bacp-browse — A human-readable summary of the evidence bundle in one language (profile in.bacp.evidence.summary.1). Informative, never evidence. GET /step-ups/{step_up_id} step-up bacp-browse — Read the state of a step-up and, once approved, the hash of the signed approval event (bacp.step_up_status). GET /orders/{order_id} order bacp-browse — Get order (Beckn status, UCP get_order). Adjustments are the append-only read model. POST /orders/{order_id}/cancel order bacp-post-order required Mandate-scoped cancel (Beckn cancel). Requires CANCEL in action_scope. POST /orders/{order_id}/returns order bacp-post-order required Mandate-scoped return (Beckn update with update_target=item). Requires RETURN in action_scope. GET /orders/{order_id}/returns/{return_id} order bacp-browse — Get return and refund status (refund receipt carries RRN/UTR) POST /issues issue bacp-post-order required Raise an IGM issue as AI_AGENT on behalf of the user (IGM issue). Requires RAISE_ISSUE in action_scope. GET /issues/{issue_id} issue bacp-browse — Issue status: the gateway's snapshot, kept current from IGM 2.0 on_issue callbacks (IGM 2.0 has no issue_status) POST /issues/{issue_id}/actions issue bacp-post-order required Complainant action (IGM 2.0 action log). ESCALATE moves ISSUE to GRIEVANCE. ODR is an out-of-protocol reference. GET /evidence/{transaction_id} evidence bacp-browse — Evidence bundle for a transaction (mandates, receipts, instruction-log chain). Access-controlled to principal, counterparties of record, GRO/ODR. POST /negotiations negotiation bacp-browse required Open a negotiation with one seller (Beckn select with bacp.negotiation capability tag) GET /negotiations/{negotiation_id} negotiation bacp-browse — Authoritative full state, offer states, transcript hashes and guard verdicts (constraint IDs only) GET /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers negotiation bacp-browse — Signed negotiation messages in this session (transcript), oldest first POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers negotiation bacp-negotiate (firm, withdraw, accept_revoke) / bacp-browse required Send offer, counter_offer, reject, withdraw, terminate, request_extension or accept_revoke POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/accept negotiation bacp-negotiate required Absolute, unqualified ACCEPT of the live offer (bacp.neg.accept, sent on Beckn init) POST /rfqs rfq bacp-browse required Publish a structured RFQ to invitees or by broadcast (one Beckn select per BPP, parent rfq_id) GET /rfqs/{rfq_id} rfq bacp-browse — RFQ state. Before close, shows only commit counts. After reveal, the landed-cost comparison set. POST /rfqs/{rfq_id}/award rfq bacp-negotiate required Award to one seller (ACCEPT of its revealed offer) and terminate the rest POST /auctions auction bacp-negotiate required Host a reverse (L1) or sealed auction through a neutral auctioneer, or register to join one GET /auctions/{auction_id} auction bacp-browse — Bidder view (current price only, own rank, never identities or sealed bids) POST /auctions/{auction_id}/bids auction bacp-negotiate required Place a bid, bid_commit, bid_reveal or bid_retract (signed, bacp-negotiate) POST /auctions/{auction_id}/standing-accepts auction bacp-negotiate required Lodge a standing accept for a Dutch auction (signed, bacp-negotiate) POST /auctions/{auction_id}/standing-accepts/{standing_accept_id}/withdraw auction bacp-negotiate required Withdraw a lodged standing accept (signed, bacp-negotiate) POST /auctions/{auction_id}/award auction bacp-negotiate required Buyer or auctioneer award of the winning bid hash (reverse_l1), or seller acceptance of the highest bid (english) GET /payment-handlers payment-handlers none (public) — The handler registry (HandlerDescriptor[]). Public, cacheable. GET /payment-handlers/{handler_id} payment-handlers none (public) — One handler descriptor, by canonical id or legacy alias POST /payment-handlers/intersect payment-handlers bacp-browse required Eligible payment handlers for a negotiation or, with in.bacp.payment_plan, a session, ordered by user preference then lowest all-in total GET /ledgers/{ledger_id} ledger bacp-browse — A credit ledger: header, chain head, balance and oldest unpaid date (in.bacp.ledger) GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries ledger bacp-browse — A page of ledger entries (after_seq, limit at most 50, status) (in.bacp.ledger) POST /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries ledger bacp-post-order required Post a payment for the principal, the debtor; only type: payment (in.bacp.ledger) POST /trade-acts trade-act bacp-post-order required Record a GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection or ledger acknowledgement after the principal approves it (in.bacp.trade_document, in.bacp.ledger) GET /orders/{order_id}/documents order bacp-browse — The trade documents recorded against an order (in.bacp.trade_document) POST /checkout-sessions ucp-checkout bacp-browse required Create a checkout in UCP shape (in.bacp.ucp_checkout; projection) GET /checkout-sessions/{id} ucp-checkout bacp-browse — Get a checkout in UCP shape PUT /checkout-sessions/{id} ucp-checkout bacp-browse required Update a checkout in UCP shape POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete ucp-checkout bacp-pay required Complete a checkout in UCP shape: one UCP instrument for each tender, each carrying a BACP closed payment mandate POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel ucp-checkout bacp-browse required Cancel a checkout in UCP shape

The status codes each operation can return are documented in the OpenAPI document. Every operation documents every status it can return, including 401, 404, 409, 413, 422, 429, 502, 503 and 504 where they apply.

docs.title: Lost-response recovery
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP Gateway
    A->>G: POST /sessions/ses_01HZXD/complete (Idempotency-Key K1)
    G--xA: response lost
    A->>G: GET /sessions/ses_01HZXD
    G-->>A: 200 status complete_in_progress, payment in_doubt
    A->>G: POST /sessions/ses_01HZXD/complete (same key K1)
    G-->>A: 409 idempotency_in_flight, Retry-After 2
    A->>G: POST /sessions/ses_01HZXD/complete (same key K1)
    G-->>A: 200 status completed, Idempotent-Replayed true

docs.title: UCP checkout projection
docs.text:
Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version 2026-10-18. Rules marked Proposed depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

BACP is not wire-compatible with the checkout of the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP); the differences are listed in BACP and other protocols. A gateway that wants a UCP-built agent to reuse its UCP response parser, status machine and totals renderer can list the optional capability in.bacp.ucp_checkout, which adds five operations that answer in the shape of the UCP checkout. This page defines that projection. A gateway that does not list the capability serves no /checkout-sessions path: a UCP client gets 404, as it did before this release.

Pinned to UCP release v2026-08-25

The projection is tested against unmodified copies of the UCP JSON Schemas of UCP's tagged release v2026-08-25 (25-08-2026, commit cd78fb3), kept under source/ucp/ (provenance and licence). The other UCP releases are v2026-04-08, v2026-01-23 and v2026-01-11 (as of 18-10-2026). Text that UCP added to its main branch after the tag (the Ask capability, a cart rule that line_items SHOULD be empty, and a registry of policy types) is not in the pinned release, and the projection does not depend on it (Q-82). A gateway MUST NOT claim UCP compatibility on any other UCP version.

docs.title: Whole or absent
docs.text:
A gateway MUST NOT list in.bacp.ucp_checkout, or claim UCP compatibility in any form, unless it passes all the entry criteria below. A partial projection is worse than none, because a UCP client would trust the parts that look right.

Criterion Rule Cases UCPF-01 A key used on /sessions/{id}/complete is replayed on /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete (and the reverse) with Idempotent-Replayed: true: the projection has the same canonical operation, so the same key space (Idempotency). BND-UCPF-01 UCPF-02 A request signed with UCP's default signature, without nonce, created or tag, is refused with 401 signature_invalid. The BACP signature profile applies unchanged. BND-UCPF-02 UCPF-03 An instrument whose credential is not of type in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate is refused with 400 invalid_request at $.payment.instruments[i].credential, with no rail call. BND-UCPF-03 UCPF-04 continue_url is only step_up.trusted_surface_url and otherwise absent, and links[] carries only typed policy links with titles from the gateway's own templates. BND-UCPF-04 UCPF-05 A complete that carries ap2.checkout_mandate is refused with 400 invalid_request at $.ap2.checkout_mandate, with no rail call. BND-UCPF-05 UCPF-06 A request that carries a UCP member of a capability that BACP does not define is refused with 400 capability_unsupported at that member, with capability set to the UCP capability id named (dev.ucp.shopping.buyer_consent, dev.ucp.common.loyalty or dev.ucp.shopping.cart), and no session is created or changed: a buyer-consent member ($.buyer.consent, UCP dev.ucp.shopping.buyer_consent), a loyalty member ($.loyalty, UCP dev.ucp.common.loyalty) or a cart reference ($.cart_id, UCP dev.ucp.shopping.cart). The paths are those of the pinned UCP schemas. The projection never declares these capabilities in its ucp envelope. BND-UCPF-06 Shape A projected checkout validates against the pinned UCP shopping/checkout.json, and a discount line is a negative integer. BND-UCP-01, BND-UCP-02

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Each operation is the same BACP operation as its /sessions twin, with the same signature tag, the same mandate checks and the same state machine; only the request and response shape differ. The UCP MCP tool names are used.

UCP operation and MCP tool REST BACP operation Signature tag create_checkout POST /checkout-sessions createSession bacp-browse get_checkout GET /checkout-sessions/{id} getSession bacp-browse update_checkout PUT /checkout-sessions/{id} updateSession bacp-browse complete_checkout POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete completeSession bacp-pay cancel_checkout POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel cancelSession bacp-browse
  • The id is the BACP session id. A request carries UCP-Agent: profile="..." as UCP requires. The gateway does not use it to authenticate or authorise: the agent is identified by its AgentCredential and its RFC 9421 signature. A gateway SHOULD NOT fetch the profile that the header names at all. A gateway that does MUST follow URL fetch hygiene, and takes nothing from the fetched profile that affects a version, an amount, a payee, a handler or a mandate.
  • A request body is the UCP body, plus a top-level bacp member that carries what BACP needs and UCP has no place for: on create_checkout, the seller (bpp_id, provider_id), transaction_id, presence and mandate_ref; on complete_checkout, the checkout mandate, checkout_hash and presence (below).
  • A response is the UCP checkout. BACP-only state is under the top-level bacp member (UCP's checkout schema allows additional members): the BACP status, checkout_hash, all_in_total, every language of every message, the step_up, plan_options and payment_plan. A UCP client ignores it.
  • The ucp envelope declares dev.ucp.shopping.checkout at version 2026-08-25 (the UCP version of the pinned release) and the session's BACP handlers as payment_handlers, each keyed by its UCP alias dev.bacp.<handler id> and carrying the BACP handler id as id and the BACP release id (for example 2026-10-18) as version, not the UCP version (Namespaces and the handler keys). It never declares dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate (No AP2).

Namespaces and the handler keys. The projection never declares an in.* id together with a schema in the profile or envelope that a UCP platform reads, and a BACP gateway MUST NOT accept or fetch a schema for an in.* id from a UCP business profile or from any other source: it logs extension_not_registered and does not activate the handler or capability. The BACP handler ids are not DNS-bound (Extensibility), whereas UCP requires the schema URL of a handler or capability to be served from the namespace authority in its name (UCP overview, Authority Binding, at release v2026-08-25). BACP holds the domain bacp.dev (owner confirmation of 18-10-2026), whose reverse-DNS authority is dev.bacp. The projection therefore applies UCP's own rule and adds no grammar to it:

  • Handler keys. The key of each entry of ucp.payment_handlers is dev.bacp.<handler id>, where <handler id> is the canonical id of the registry descriptor (dev.bacp.in.upi.circle, dev.bacp.bacp.credit_ledger). The doubled label in dev.bacp.bacp.<name> is intended: the alias is the authority dev.bacp followed by the unchanged handler id, so a reader recovers the handler id by removing the prefix dev.bacp.. UCP treats the labels after the authority as opaque, and the full handler id keeps the mapping one to one. The entry carries the BACP handler id as id and a schema of https://bacp.dev/schemas/ucp/<handler id>.json, whose host reversed (dev.bacp) is a label-aligned prefix of the key. Each schema is published in the specification repository under source/schemas/ucp/, with an unversioned $id that the build rewrites per version like every BACP schema. Each schema is self-describing as UCP asks (UCP schema-authoring, release v2026-08-25): it carries a top-level name, dev.bacp.<handler id>, and a version, the BACP release id, and an entry in the envelope carries that version. The key suffix after dev.bacp., the entry's id and the schema file name MUST be equal, otherwise the envelope is invalid; a complete that names a key which is not in the session's envelope is 400 invalid_request. A schema describes a handler entry with no config: the limits and rules of the handler are registry data, not UCP handler configuration (loss-table row 7).
  • Extension keys. The projection declares no extension today (its ucp.capabilities holds dev.ucp.shopping.checkout only). A key that BACP adds later is dev.bacp.<service>.<capability>, the shape of UCP's naming convention for capabilities, with its schema under https://bacp.dev/schemas/ucp/.
  • Old keys. A BACP handler id used as a key, as in a profile that was written before the alias, is accepted as an alias of its dev.bacp. key for the dated release that introduces the alias, and a later dated release MAY stop accepting it (versioning policy). The handler_id of a complete instrument is the BACP handler id, and the alias key is accepted there as well. The projection emits only the alias keys.
  • A gateway does not need to fetch these schemas: they are for a UCP platform that validates the envelope. The in.bacp.* capability ids do not change.

Parked UCP operations. The projection answers 404 for the UCP cart operations and for every other UCP operation that this page does not list; the cart (Q-95), account linking (Q-96), Ask (Q-97), loyalty (Q-98), catalogue lookup and variants (Q-99) and ranking parameters (Q-100) are parked, each with its controls. If the projection ever declares UCP buyer consent, it confirms granted: false, source: "platform" for every purpose unless an active marketing ConsentReceipt of the seller exists (Marketing consent); until it does, UCPF-06 refuses a buyer-consent member.

docs.title: Complete
docs.text:
complete_checkout pays with one UCP payment instrument for each BACP tender:

ucp-complete-request.gift-upi.json
{
  "payment": {
    "instruments": [
      {
        "id": "tdr_gift001",
        "handler_id": "in.ppi.gift",
        "type": "in.bacp.tender",
        "amount": 100000,
        "selected": true,
        "credential": {
          "type": "in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate",
          "token": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln"
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "tdr_upi001",
        "handler_id": "in.upi.circle",
        "type": "in.bacp.tender",
        "amount": 116000,
        "selected": true,
        "credential": {
          "type": "in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate",
          "token": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "bacp": {
    "checkout_mandate": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln",
    "checkout_hash": "sha-256:MdzPb6o2QprB1t01MqITDlt_3VlU_4O8efFu8026Jpo",
    "presence": "HNP",
    "plan_id": "plan_GIFTUPI0001"
  }
}
  • Each instrument is {id, handler_id, type: "in.bacp.tender", amount, credential}. id is the tender_id of the BACP plan, handler_id the BACP handler id, amount an integer in paise (required: an open-amount instrument is refused), and credential is {type: "in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate", token} with the BACP closed payment mandate as an attached compact JWS.
  • One instrument is a single-tender complete and equals a BACP payment_mandate. Several instruments are a BACP payment_plan, so the capability in.bacp.payment_plan is required, bacp.plan_id names an offered plan, and every rule of Wire binding of plans applies (the tenders MUST hash to an offered or Trusted-Surface-confirmed plan, one closed mandate per tender).
  • The closed checkout mandate travels in bacp.checkout_mandate, with bacp.checkout_hash and bacp.presence (and accepted_disclosures_hash, step_up_id and kb_jwt where BACP's complete takes them).
  • An instrument whose credential is of any other type is refused (UCPF-03).

Failure at complete, with a clear error. A UCP platform that does not know BACP's mandates cannot be stopped at create_checkout, because UCP has no way to make an extension mandatory at negotiation: capabilities are intersected by name, and a requirement is enforced only when complete arrives. So the projection serves create_checkout, get_checkout and update_checkout to such a platform and fails at complete: a complete that carries no BACP closed payment mandate gets 400 invalid_request at $.payment.instruments with the message code bacp_mandate_required (unrecoverable), and no rail call.

docs.title: No AP2
docs.text: The projection MUST NOT advertise dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate in the ucp envelope. BACP's closed mandate is an attached compact JWS, which is the only interoperable encoding in this version (Q-41); UCP's AP2 extension carries an SD-JWT with key binding. A later BACP release may add an SD-JWT mandate vct and only then may the projection advertise the extension. A complete that carries ap2.checkout_mandate is refused (UCPF-05).

docs.title: Escalation and links
docs.text: UCP requires a continue_url on requires_escalation, set by the business. The projection sets it only when the session has a step_up with a trusted_surface_url, and then it is exactly that URL, which the gateway mints only on an origin of the step-up's signer (Origins and delivery); with no step-up it is absent. A step-up with delivery: app_push has no link, so the projection sets no continue_url for it and the detail is in bacp.status. A seller's URL, even one a quote carries in its tags, never becomes a continue_url (UCPF-04). links[] carries only typed policy links (terms_of_service, refund_policy, privacy_policy, ...) whose title comes from the gateway's own templates, never from the seller.

docs.title: Differences that the projection keeps (normative)
docs.text:
The projection loses information. This table is normative: a gateway MUST project exactly as the second column says, and an agent that reads a projected checkout MUST read the bacp member where the third column says the UCP shape loses something. The rows are in the order in which a UCP client fails.

# BACP In the UCP projection What the UCP shape loses 1 Discount sign. A discount is a non-negative Amount of type discount A negative integer in paise: BACP discount of ₹30 is -3000. The UCP total line is all_in_total plus the operator charges, and each operator charge is a UCP totals[] line of type fee with display_text from the gateway's templates; bacp.all_in_total keeps the quote figure Nothing, if the sign is flipped; a projection with a positive discount fails the pinned schema and adds the discount to the total 2 A declined payment makes the session cancelled UCP's own rule would be incomplete with a recoverable payment_failed, but the projection reports the BACP outcome: canceled, with bacp.status: cancelled The retry that UCP offers after a decline 3 cancelled canceled. A UCP platform treats a checkout as canceled only when the business reports canceled, so the projection reports it The spelling 4 complete takes mandates (JWS) payment.instruments[] with a BACP closed payment mandate as the credential, and the checkout mandate in bacp UCP's own payment instruments and AP2 5 step_up.trusted_surface_url continue_url, only that URL, else absent Any seller-supplied handoff URL 6 human_handoff requires_escalation, with the detail in bacp.status The distinct status 7 Handlers are in the gateway profile ucp.payment_handlers, keyed by the alias dev.bacp.<handler id> with the BACP handler id as id, with no UCP config UCP handler configuration 8 Amount is {value, currency} An integer in paise, with currency at the root (INR) Nothing 9 /sessions /checkout-sessions Nothing 10 MCP tools take the body's properties, path parameters and idempotency_key UCP's tool names, with the same arguments plus UCP's id meta is not used 11 Messages carry a LangText map, and counterparty text is labelled One string in the negotiated language in UCP content, every language in bacp.messages. Counterparty text never goes in UCP content, and a UCP line_items[].item.title is seller text in a UCP field, marked as counterparty text in bacp. ai_disclosure.notice becomes a UCP warning The other languages, and the labelling of counterparty text 12 links come from the gateway Typed policy links with gateway-template titles Seller links 13 GST heads and TCS The GST heads sum to the UCP tax line, with the split in the sub-lines of that line or in namespaced total types; a TCS line never enters a buyer-facing total (whether it may is flagged to counsel, Q-83) The split of GST in a client that ignores sub-lines 14 prior_price and mrp UCP's catalogue variant.json carries a list_price ("List price before discounts"), which is not among the pinned checkout schemas. Wherever the projection states a price before discount, it takes prior_price.amount and never mrp The MRP

UCP buyer fields on create_checkout are held by the gateway and are not sent to the seller before the ConsentReceipt (Data minimisation). A payment instrument that carries a member that UCP allows and BACP does not define, for example a display or billing field, gets 400 invalid_request rather than being ignored: the projection fails closed, and this is a known delta from UCP.

docs.text:
